# Bhavisya-purana 3

## Chapter 1. Arrival of Vyasa Deva

## \|\| 3.1.1-2 \|\|

*kalyāṇāni dadātu vo gaṇapatiryasminnatuṣṭe sati kṣodīyasyapi karmaṇi prabhavituṃ brahmāpi jihmāyate \|*  
*bheje yaccaraṇāravindamasakṛtsaubhāgyabhāgyodayaistenaiṣā jagati prasiddhimagamaddevendralakṣmī rapi \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śaśvatpuṇyahiraṇyagarbharasanāsiṃhāsanādhyāsinī seyaṃ vāgadhidevatā vitaratu śreyāṃsi bhūyāṃsi vaḥ \|*  
*yatpādāmalakomalāṃgulinakha jyotsnābhirudvellitaḥ śabdabrahmasudhāṃbudhirbudhamanasyucchraṃkhalaṃ khelati \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Let the lord Ganapati bestow welfare on you, who when become dissatisfied, the strength gets squeezed and even Brahma is unable to perform the petty jobs. But the fortune of serving at his lotus like feet can be availed only by the excessively fortunate people. Therefore, I am making all the efforts to serve him, because as a result of the serving at his feet, even Indra - the lord of gods, attained the royal fortunes, besides the unparallel glory in the world. The goddess Sarasvati, who is always lodged over the tongue of Brahma and let her always shower her grace on you. He is the one from the nails of the soft toes of his feet emerges the ocean of nectar, which spreads in the spotless minds of the learned people.

## \|\| 3.1.3-7 \|\|

*namastasmai viśvodayavilayarakṣāprakṛtaye śivāya kleśaughacchidurapad padmapraṇataye \|*  
*amandasvacchandaprathitapṛthulīlātanubhṛte trivedīvācāmapyapathanijatattvasthitikṛte \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yasya gaṇḍatale bhāti vimalā ṣaṭpa dāvalī \|*  
*akṣamāleva vimalā sa naḥ pāyādgaṇādhipaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*oṃ namo vāsudevāya saśārṅgāya saketave \|*  
*sagadāya sacakrāya saśaṃkhāya namo namaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*namaḥ śivāya somāya sagaṇāya sasūnave \|*  
*savṛṣāya saśūlāya sakapālāya sendave \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śivaṃ dhyātvā hariṃ stutvā praṇamya parame ṣṭhinam \|*  
*citrabhānuṃ ca bhānuṃ ca natvā granthamudīrayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

3-7. I always offer my salutation to lord Siva, the image of welfare, who created the entire universe. It became his habit to protect and destroy the world. His lotus like feet always destroy the formations of obstructions. He takes to a universal and gigantic body. It is beyond the capacity of even the Vedas to discuss about his tattvas. Let such a lord of Ganas protect me. He is the one over whose cheeks, the lines of black wasps like the rosary of Rudraksa beads always hover. I offer my salutation to Vasudeva, the form of Omkara who carries the attributes of bow, flag, club, cakra and a conch. Similarly, I am offering my salutation to lord Siva, who is always decorated with his trident, skull and the crescent moon riding over the bull. Thus, I meditate on Siva, pray to Visnu. I also bow in reverence to Surya who also known as Citrabhanu, and Brahma as well. Thereafter, I am going to start this literary composition.

## \|\| 3.1.8-15 \|\|

*chatrābhiṣiktaṃ dharmajñaṃ dharmaputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram \|*  
*draṣṭumabhyāgatā hṛṣṭā vyāsādyāḥ parama rṣayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*mārkaṇḍeyaḥ samāṇḍavyaḥ śāṇḍilyaḥ śākaṭāyanaḥ \|*  
*gautamo gālavo gārgyaḥ śātātapaparāśarau \|\| 9 \|\|*

*jāmadagnyo bharadvājo bhṛgu rbhāgurireva ca \|*  
*uttaṃkaḥ śaṃkhalikhitau śaunakaḥ śākaṭāyaniḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pulastyaḥ pulaho dālbhyo bṛhadaśvaḥ salomaśaḥ \|*  
*nāradaḥ parvato jahurapāva suparāvasū \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tānṛṣīnāgatāndṛṣṭvā vedavedāṅgapāragān \|*  
*bhaktimānbhrātṛbhiḥ sārddhaṃ kṛṣṇadhaumyapuraḥsaraḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*yudhiṣṭhiraḥ saṃprahṛṣṭaḥ samutthāyābhivādya ca \|*  
*arghyamācamanaṃ pādyamāsanāni svayaṃ dadau \|\| 13 \|\|*

*upaviṣṭeṣu teṣveva tapasviṣu yudhiṣṭhiraḥ \|*  
*vinayāvanato bhūtvā vyāsaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 14 \|\|*

*bhagavaṃstvatprasādena prāptaṃ rājyaṃ mahanmayā \|*  
*vikramya nihataḥ saṃkhye sānubandhaḥ suyodhanaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

8-15. Once the sage Vyasa accompanied with other excellent Rsis, arrived to meet the king Yudhisthira, who was decorated with the royal emblem, the flywhisks, and was well-versed in Dharma. These Rsis included Markandeya, Mandavya, Sandilya, Sakatayana, Gautama, Galava, Gargya, Satatapa, Parasara, Parasurama, Bharadvaja, Bhrgu, Bhaguri, Uttanka, Sarikha, Likhita, Saunaka, Pulastya, Pulaha, Dalbhya, Brhadasva, Lomasa, Narada, Parvata, Jahnu, Apavasu and Paravasu. At that point of time, the Rsis who had arrived there who were quite learned and well-versed in the Vedas, were spotted by Yudhisthitra, who atonce descended from the lion throne and felt delighted with his brother. All the brothers, then making £ri Krsna to lead them with

Dhaumya, welcomed all the Rsis with respect. Then, they were made to take their seats provided to them and were offered arghya and the water for sipping. After the ascetics occupied their seats, Yudhisthira spoke to the sage Vyasa, with all humility- “O lord, I have achieved this throne by your grace. I have been able to achieve this with the destruction of Duryodhana, with all his relatives.

## \|\| 3.1.16-20 \|\|

*sarogasya yathā bhogaḥ prāpto'pi na sukhāvahaḥ \|*  
*hatvā jñātīṃstathā rājyaṃ na sukhaṃ pratibhāti me \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yatsukhaṃ pāvanaṃ prītirvanamūlaphalāśinām \|*  
*prāpya gāṃ ca hatārātiṃ na tadasti pitāmaha \|\| 17 \|\|*

*yo no bandhurgururgoptā sadā śarma ca varma ca \|*  
*sa mayā rājyalobhena bhīṣmaḥ pāpena ghātitaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*avivekamahaṃ dhāsye mano me pāpapaṅkilam \|*  
*kṣālayitvā tava girā bahudarśitavāriṇā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*saṃśrutāni purāṇāni vedāssāṃgā mayā vibho \|*  
*mamādya dharmasarvasvaṃ prajñādīpena darśaya \|\| 20 \|\|*

16-20. But like an ailing person who does not enjoy all the pleasures by getting them, similarly, I also do not relish the comforts and the kingship, after the destruction of my entire race. The comfort one enjoys by dwelling in the forest and consuming the wild roots and fruits, cannot be achieved with the destruction of all the enemies and attaining of the kingship. I had been such a sinner, that because of my greed for the kingship, I killed Bhisma - the Grandsire, who was my closest relative, protector, preceptor, who always wished well of us, with a kavaca like impregnable caught in the sinful mind. Though I have several times heard the nectar like Puranas composed by you, and also listened to all the Vedas with their parts, but О excellent one, you kindly display the supreme dharma, by excellence of your great divine knowledge.

## \|\| 3.1.21-24 \|\|

*ete sadharmagoptāro munayaḥ samupāgatāḥ \|*  
*pibato netrabhramarairbhavato mukhapaṃkajam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*arthaśāstrāṇi yāvaṃti dharmaśāstrāṇi yāni vai \|*  
*śrutāni sarvaśāstrāṇi bhīṣmādbhāgīrathīsutāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

*svargaṃ gate śāntanave bhavānkṛṣṇo'tha yādavaḥ \|*  
*suhṛttvādbandhubhāvācca nānyaḥ śikṣayitā mama \|\| 23 \|\|*

*satyaṃ satyavatīsūnurdharmarājāya vakṣyati \|*  
*viśeṣadharmānakhilānmunīnāmaviśeṣataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

21-24. The Rsis are the great warriors of Dharma. They are enjoying the nectar of your face, with black wasps like eyes. I have listened to all Arthasastra, Dharmasastra and other religious literature from the grandsire Bhisma - the son of Ganga. But after his departure to heaven, lord Krsna is my only guide, who is my teacher besides being a close relative. There is none else (on whom I could bank upon).” Thereafter, Vyasa — the son of Satyavati, spoke on all the dharmas for the sake of Dharmaraja as well as the ascetics.

## \|\| 3.1.25-30 \|\|

*vyāsa uvāca \|*  
*yadākhyeyaṃ tadākhyātaṃ mayā bhīṣmeṇa te'nagha \|*  
*mārkaṇḍeyena dhaumyena lomaśena maharṣiṇā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*dharmajño hyasi medhāvī guṇavānprā jñasattamaḥ \|*  
*na te'styaviditaṃ kiñciddharmādharmaviniścaye \|\| 26 \|\|*

*pārśvasthite hṛṣīkeśe keśave keśisūdane \|*  
*kasyacitkathane jihvā tatra saṃpari vartate \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kartā pālayitā hartā jagatāṃ yo jaganmayaḥ \|*  
*pratyakṣadarśī sarvasya dharmānvakṣyatyasau tava \|\| 28 \|\|*

*samādiśyeti kartavyaṃ bhagavānbādarāyaṇaḥ \|*  
*pūjitaḥ pāṇḍutanayairjagāma svatapovanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*svābhāṣya bhāratavidhātari saṃprayāte te kautukākuladhiyo munayaḥ praśāntāḥ \|*  
*kiṃ pṛcchati kṣapitabhāratalokaśokaḥ kiṃ vakṣyatīha bhagavānyaduvaṃśavīraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

25-30. Vyasa said- “O sinless one, whatever I intend to speak, the discussion on the same, has already been heard by you from the grandsire Bhisma. The same subject has also been highlighted by the Rsis like Markandeya, Dhaumya and I omasa. You are well-versed in dharma, learned, virtuous and highly intellectual. Therefore, you are not at all unaware of the difference between dharma as well as evil. Still because of your having been devoted to dharma and Kesava who is the killer of the demon Kasi, the tongue is desirous of singing his glory. He is the creator, preserver and destroyer of the universe, therefore, being the eye witness, he would display all the dharmas before us. Therefore, let me have your command.” Thus speaking, lord Vadarayana Vyasa, getting adored by the sons of Pandu, proceeded on to the tapovana. Thus speaking intelligently, Vyasa the great ascetic of the country of Bharata, left the place. Yudhisthira who was silently seated there and whose mind was anxious to listen to the speech of the ascetics, raised a question to the Rsis. How did lord Krsna provide the salutation?

## Chapter 2. Creation of the globe or universe

## \|\| 3.2.1-2 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*kasya pratiṣṭhā nirdiṣṭā ko hetuḥ kiṃ parāyaṇam \|*  
*kasminnaitallayaṃ yāti kasmādu tpadyate jagat \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kati dvīpāḥ samudrāśca kiyaṃto hi kulācalāḥ \|*  
*kiyatpramāṇamavanerbhuvanāni kiyaṃti ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Yudhisthira said- Whose glory or reputation always remains stable in the world? Who owns it after having been born in the world? What is the source of the origin or destruction of the world? What is the number

## \|\| 3.2.3-8 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*paurāṇaścaiva viṣayo yatpṛṣṭo'haṃ tvayānagha \|*  
*śruto'nubhūtaśca mayā saṃsāre saratā ciram \|\| 3 \|\|*

*ajāya viśvarūpāya nirguṇāya guṇātmane \|*  
*namastasmai bhagavate vāsudevāya vedhase \|\| 4 \|\|*

*atra te varṇayiṣyāmi śṛṇu pārtha purātanam \|*  
*yājñavalkyena muninā bhaviṣyaṃ bhāsvatāṃpatiḥ \|*  
*pṛṣṭo yaduttaraṃ prādādṛṣibhyastanmayā śrutam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ sarvāśubhavināśanam \|*  
*bhaviṣyottarametatte kathayāmi yudhiṣṭhira \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ekātmakaṃ tridaivatyaṃ catuḥpaṃcasulakṣaṇam \|*  
*guṇakālādibhedena sadasatsaṃpradarśitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*eka eva jagadyoniḥ pratiyoniṣu saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*ekadhā bahudhā caiva dṛśyate jalacandravat \|\| 8 \|\|*

3-8. Sri Krsna said- О sinless one, whatever has been asked by you is the subject of the Puranas, which has been experienced by me for long while living in this world, besides listening from the popular scriptures. The lord Vasudeva has been defined as the one who is same story has been heard by me from other Rsis. О Yudhisthira, the name of the story, which is full of grace, glorious, enhances life, besides being the destroyer of auspicious and inauspicious, is known as Bhavisyottara. I am going to narrate the same. It is always known as Brahman and always remains stable, besides being the soul which exists in the form of three gods, viz., Brahma, Visnu and Mahesvara, having four or five symptoms. Because of the difference in the time and virtues, sat is always displayed. That alone is the cause of the creation of the universe, which is lodged in several births and looks like a single moon appearing as many moons in the water.

## \|\| 3.2.9-17 \|\|

*brahmā viṣṇurvṛṣāṃkaśca trayo devāḥ satāṃ matāḥ \|*  
*nāmabhedaiḥ kriyābhedairbhidyaṃte nātmanā svayam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*prakriyā cānuṣaṃgaśca upoddhātastathaiva ca \|*  
*upasaṃhāra ityetaccatuṣpādaṃ prakīrtitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tarkaśca pratisargaśca vaṃśo manvantarāṇi ca \|*  
*vaṃśānucaritaṃ caiva purāṇaṃ paṃcalakṣaṇam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*eṣa vaktavyaviṣayaḥ sumahānpratibhāti me \|*  
*tathāpyuddeśato vacmi sargaṃ prati tavānagha \|\| 12 \|\|*

*mahadādiviśeṣāntaṃ savairūpyaṃ salakṣaṇam \|*  
*pañcapramāṇaṃ ṣaṭkakṣaṃ puruṣādhiṣṭhitaṃ jagat \|\| 13 \|\|*

*avyaktājjāyate buddhirmahāniti ca sā smṛtā \|*  
*ahaṃkārastu mahatastriguṇaḥ sa ca paṭhyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tanmātrāṇi ca pañcāhurahaṅkārācca sāttvikāt \|*  
*jātāni tebhyo bhūtāni bhūtebhyaḥ sacarācaram \|\| 15 \|\|*

*jalamūrtimaye viṣṇau naṣṭe sthāvarajaṃgame \|*  
*bhūtātmakamabhūdaṇḍaṃ mahattadudakeśayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sṛṣṭyāṃ śaktyā ca nirbhinnaṃ tadaṇḍamabhavaddvidhā \|*  
*bhūkapālamathaikaṃ taddvi tīyamabhavannabhaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

9-17. Brahma, Visnu and Mahesvara are the three principle gods, who happen to be eternal, who according to their names and the four stages known as procedure, comprehension, introduction and conclusion. The Sarga, Pratisarga, Vamsa (dynasty), Manvantara and Vams'acarita are said to be the five characteristics of Brahman or the Purana. O sinless one, though according to my view the subject is quite vast, still for the purpose of explaining the same, I am going to discuss the same. In this, the matter from Mahat etc. to Visesa, together with their forms as well as the symptoms have been discussed. The invisible Purusa is the presiding deity of the universe with six classes and live proofs. The intelligence emerges out of the same initially, which is also known as the great or Mahat. Out of that Mahat emerges Ahamkara (pride), Sattvika Ahamkara, besides the five subtle forms of the matter. The five bhutas emerge out of them, which become the cause of the creation of the universe. When the mobile and immobile world gets absorbed in Visnu, he sleeps in the ocean of milk, which is formed of the Sakti of the creation. Getting divided into two parts, one parts turns into Bhu or the skull or land and the other part turns into the sky.

## \|\| 3.2.18-25 \|\|

*ulbaṃ tasyābhavanmerurjarāyuḥ parvatāḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*nadyo dhamanyaḥ sañjātāḥ kledaḥ sarvatragaṃ payaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*yojanānāṃ sahasrāṇi ṣoḍaśādhaḥ pratiṣṭhita \|*  
*utsedhe caturāśītirdvātriṃśadūrdhvavistṛtaḥ \|*  
*bhūmipaṃkajavistīrṇā karṇikā merurucyate \|\| 19 \|\|*

*ādityaścādidevatvāttatrābhūttriguṇātmakaḥ \|*  
*prātaḥ prajāpatirasau madhyāhne viṣṇuriṣyate \|*  
*rudro'parāhṇasamaye sa evaikastridhāmataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*prātaḥ prajāpaterjātā munayo nava mānavāḥ \|*  
*marīciratryaṃgirasau pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ \|*  
*bhṛgurvaśiṣṭha ityaṣṭau nārado navamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*nava brahmāṇa ityeṣa purāṇe niścayaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*aṃguṣṭhāddakṣiṇāddakṣaḥ saṃjajñe kamalodbhavāt \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vāmā prasūtirudagādaṃguṣṭhāttau ca daṃpatī \|*  
*tābhyāṃ jātāstu tanayā haryaśvāste vināśitāḥ \|*  
*sṛṣṭiṃ prati samudyuktā nāradena mahātmanā \|\| 23 \|\|*

*dakṣaḥ kṣīṇānsutānvīkṣya janayāmāsa kanyakāḥ \|*  
*pañcāśaddaśa vikhyātāḥ satyāyā nāmabhiḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*dadau sa daśa dharmāya kaśyapāya trayodaśa \|*  
*kālasya nayane yuktāḥ saptarviśatimiṃdave \|\| 25 \|\|*

18-25. Its membrane is the mountain Meru and the womb happens to be the mountain. The rivers stand for the veins, while the water stands for the moisture. It expands upto sixteen thousand yojanas towards the netherworld, while it is eighty four thousand yojanas upwards. Still further, it is expanded into thirty two thousand yojanas. When the lotus like earth blossoms, its karnika is the Meru mountain. Being the eternal lord in the sky, the Sungod takes to trigunatmaka form, because in the morning he officiates as Prajapati, Visnu in the noon, while Rudra in the evening. Thus, inspite of his being the solitary Brahman, he gets divided into three parts. By the morning Prajapati, nine great Rsis were born, who were known by the names of Marici, Atri, Angira, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Bhrgu, Vasistha and Narada. Accordingly, these nine Rsis have been said to be the form of Brahman. From the big toe of the right foot of Brahma, Daksa was bom, besides his wife known by the name of Prasuti. Thereafter, the said couple produced many sons, who were destroyed by the sage Narada. At the destruction of his sons, Daksa produced fifty girls including Satya and others. Subsequently, he gave away ten of his daughters to Dharma, thirteen to Kasyapa, two to Kala - the god of death and twenty seven to Moon.

## \|\| 3.2.26-29 \|\|

*dve prādādbāhuputrāya dve kṛśāśvāya caiva hi \|*  
*rūpayauvanaśālinyaścatasro'riṣṭanemine \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ekāṃ bhṛgorbhavāyaikāṃ prādāttebhyaścarācaraḥ \|*  
*abhavatpuruṣavyāghra bhūtagrāmaścaturvidhaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*vairājamatha vaikuṇṭhaṃ kelāsamiti nāmataḥ \|*  
*meroḥ śṛṃgatrayaṃ mūrdhni brahmaviṣṇuśivālayam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*prācīdikkramayogena teṣāṃ pārśve puraḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*indrādilokapālānāṃ divyaiḥ svarllakṣaṇairyutāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

26-29. Similarly, he gave away two daughters to Kusasva, four to Aristanemi, one each to Bhrgu and Siva. This is how the mobile and immobile world was created. O lion among the humans, four types of the groups of the living beings were created on earth. The prominent gods are- BrahmA, Visnu and Mahesvara, who are lodged over the three peaks of mountain known as Vairaja, Vaikuntha and Kailasa, which are lodged over the Meru mountain. They are lodged in the eastern and other directions. For lokapalas like Indra and others, there is the heaven possessing the divine symptoms.

## \|\| 3.2.30 \|\|

*himavānhemakūṭaśca niṣadho merureva ca \|*  
*nīlaḥ śvetastathā śṛṃgī jambūdvīpe kulācalāḥ \|*  
*jambūdvīpapramāṇena sahasraguṇitaṃ śatam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. The mountains like Himavan, Hemakuta, Nisadha, Meru, Nila, Sveta, Bhrngi and Kulacala are located in the Jambudvipa, which is spread in an area of a lakh of yojanas. In the division of varsas (or continents), it has the ninth position. Out of these continents, Bharata happens to be the first one.

## \|\| 3.2.31-32 \|\|

*bhidyate navadhā so'pi varṣabhedena bhārata \|*  
*jambūśākakuśakrauñcaśālmagomeda puṣkarāḥ \|*  
*dvīpāḥ sapta samākhyātāḥ samudre saptabhirvṛtāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kṣārakṣīrekṣusurayā dadhnā caiva ghṛtena ca \|*  
*svādūdakena ca bhṛtairdviguṇairdviguṇaista thā \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. Similarly, Jamba, Saka, Kusa, Kraunca, Salmali, Gomeda and the country like Puskara were formed which have been surrounded by the seven oceans around the same. These oceans have salt water, milk, sugarcane juice, wine, curd, ghi, besides the tasteful water, which are respectively of double the size from one another.

## \|\| 3.2.33-34 \|\|

*bhūrloko'tha bhuvarlokaḥ svarmaharjjana ityapi \|*  
*tapaḥ satyaśca kathitāḥ pārtha sapta surālayāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*mahātalo bhūmitalaḥ sutalo vitala stataḥ \|*  
*rasātalaśca vijñeyaḥ saptamaśca talātalaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

33-34. O Partha, the dwelling places of the gods are known by the names of Bhuloka, Bhuvarloka, Svargaloka (heaven), Maharloka, Yamaloka, Tapaloka and Satyaloka. Similarly, Mahatala, Bhumitala, Sutala, Vitala, Rasatala, Tala and Atala Iokas are also there.

## \|\| 3.2.35 \|\|

*hiraṇyākṣaprabhṛtayo dānavendrā mahoragāḥ \|*  
*vasaṃtyeteṣu kaunteya siddhāśca ṛṣayaśca ye \|\| 35 \|\|*

35\. These happen to be the places for dwelling for the great Danavas, huge serpents. O son of Kunti, the Siddhas and Rsis also live in these

## \|\| 3.2.36-37 \|\|

*svāyaṃbhuvo manuḥ pūrvaṃ tataḥ svārociṣo'bhavat \|*  
*uttamastāmasaścaiva raivataścākṣuṣeti ṣaṭ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*vaivasvato'yamadhunā vartate manuruttamaḥ \|*  
*yasya putraiḥ prapautraiśca vibhakteyaṃ vasundharā \|\| 37 \|\|*

36-37. Among the humans, Svyyambhuva Manu happened to be the first, followed by Svarocisa, Uttama, Tamasa, Raivata, Caksusa and Vaivasvata Manu, who happened to be the seventh one and is the present descendant of the race. The sons, grandsons as well as the great grandsons of the same race divided the earth in different parts.

## \|\| 3.2.38-41 \|\|

*ādityā vasavo rudrā ekādaśa tathāśvinau \|*  
*uṣastrayaḥ samākhyātā deva vaivasvateṃ'tare \|\| 38 \|\|*

*vipracittihiraṇyākhyau daityadānavasattamau \|*  
*tayorvaṃśe tu bahavo daityadānavasattamāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*pañcāśadguṇitakoṭiyojanānāṃ mahattayā \|*  
*saptadvīpasamudrāyāḥ pramāṇamavaneḥ smṛtam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*piṇḍena ca sahasrāṇi saptatirjalamadhyataḥ \|*  
*gaurivaiṣā sumahatī bhrājate na ca līyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

38-41. During the period of the Vaivasvata Manu, the twelve Adityas, Vasus, eleven Rudras, Asvinikumaras, were known as the prominent deities. Similarly, there had been two Daitays known as- Vipracitti and Hiranyaksa. They had several of the Daitya or Danava kings. The earth comprising of the seven oceans and seven continents, is spread into fifty crores of yojanas. The earth is lodged like the globe having the size (or circumference of) seventy thousand (yojanas). Inspite of the earth being of the gigantic size, it does not get submerged into the water.

## \|\| 3.2.42-43 \|\|

*lokā lokaḥ parataraḥ parvato'gramahocchrayaḥ \|*  
*dvaitamarthaṃ sa niyato yo'sau ravirucāmapi \|\| 42 \|\|*

*naimittikaḥ prākṛtikastathaivātyantiko layaḥ \|*  
*nityaścaturtho vijñeyaḥ kālo nityāpahārakaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. The mountain named Lokaloka happens to be the best of all and is higher than the Sun. It is meant to be divided into two parts. It is indeed the place for the creation, fortunes, natural, maximum and absorption. Because of this, it has also been termed as the Kala (time) which is also called as the usurper.

## \|\| 3.2.44-45 \|\|

*utpadyate svayaṃ yasmāttattasminneva līyate \|*  
*rakṣati ca pare puṃsi bhūtānāmeva niścayaḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*yathartāvṛtuliṅgāni nānārūpāṇi paryaye \|*  
*dṛśyaṃte tāni tānyeva tathā bhāvā yugādiṣu \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. This is a definite rule with the living beings that the source from which they are born, they get absorbed in the same. Even the excellent people, after getting established, are well guarded and safe. As during the different seasons, at the time of growth, the lingas take to many forms, similarly, during the time of each one of the yugas, their feelings also became quite apparent.

## \|\| 3.2.46-49 \|\|

*pratilīneṣu bhūteṣu vibuddhaḥ sakalaṃ jagat \|*  
*vedaśabdebhya evādau nirmame sa maheśvaraḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*hiṃsrāhiṃsre mṛdukrūre dharmādharmāvṛtānṛte \|*  
*te taṃ vinā prapadyaṃte punasteṣveva karma su \|\| 47 \|\|*

*bhūrdaśaguṇena payasā saṃvṛtā tacca tejasā \|*  
*tejo'nilena nabhasā tadguṇenānilo vṛtaḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*bhūtādinā tathākāśaṃ bhūtādirmahatāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*mahānparivṛtastena puruṣeṇāvināśinā \|\| 49 \|\|*

46-49. After the destruction of the crowds of the living beings, the entire universe regains consciousness after the time of dissolution. At the time of the beginning, the Vedic words were created first of all by the lord Mahesvara. The living beings becoming pleasant and violent following dharma and adharma, the truth and falsehood, sweet and sour, follow the same type of the activities. The earth is surrounded by the water which is ten times more than its own size, similarly the water is surrounded by the lustre, the lustre is surrounded by the wind, the sky is surrounded by the wind, while the sky is surrounded by the Pahca-bhutas, while Mahat is surrounded by the great Purusa which is beyond destruction.

## Chapter 3. Display of Maya

## \|\| 3.3.1 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*kīdṛśī kṛṣṇa sā māyā viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ \|*  
*yayā vyāmohitaṃ yacca jagadetaccarācaram \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Yudhisthira said- Of what type is the Maya of Visnu, which confuses the entire world?

## \|\| 3.3.2-7 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*yena dvīpe purā viṣṇurāste cakragadādharaḥ \|*  
*vāsudevaḥ sagaruḍaḥ sacakraśca śriyā saha \|\| 2 \|\|*

*nīlotpaladalaśyāmaḥ kuṃḍalābhyāṃ vibhūṣitaḥ \|*  
*bhrājate mukuṭoddyotakeyūravanamālayā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tasya draṣṭumathābhyāgānnārado munisattamaḥ \|*  
*praṇamya stutibhirddevaṃ prāhedaṃ vismayānvitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*saṃśayaṃ paripṛcchāmi bhagavanvaktumarhasi \|*  
*kā māyā kīdṛśī māyā kiṃrūpā ca kutastathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tasyā darśaya me rūpaṃ māyāyāḥ puruṣottama \|*  
*yā ca mohayate sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ābrahmastaṃbaparyaṃtaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam \|*  
*vaikuṃṭhaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca prasādaṃ kartumarhasi \|\| 7 \|\|*

2-7. Sri Krsna said- Lord Visnu, holding the disc and club, was lodged in that continent, together with Laksmi and Garuda. Once Narada - the best of the humans, reached there in order to have a sight of lord Vasudeva, having the complexion of the blue lotus flower, adorned with kundalas in the ears and with a crown over the head. His arms were decorated with armlets and a long garland of forest flowers decorated his chest. After offering his prayer, he felt surprised and then said to the lord- “O lord, I am expressing a doubt, which may kindly be removed by you. O Purusottama, what is the thing known as Maya or an illusion? What is its form? Of what type is it? Where is it lodged? You kindly display the form of that Maya, which confuses the entire universe besides the three Iokas, from Brahma to the pillar as well as the gods, the humans, Vaikuntha as well as Vasudeva.”

## \|\| 3.3.8-10 \|\|

*evamuktastu muninā devadevo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*prahasyovāca devarṣe na kāryaṃ māyayā tvayā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*bhūyo'pi mohayāmāsa somagrāheṇa nāradam \|*  
*nāradopi mahārāja provācedaṃ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*māyāṃ darśaya me deva nānyadasti prayojanam \|*  
*athāsau viṣṇurutthāya śvetadvīpaṃ punaryayau \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. At these words of the sage, Janardana -the god of gods, smiled and said- “O divine sage, you better stop talking about Maya"' But Narada had been instigated for the purpose by serving him the Soma juice. Therefore, Narada spoke again- “O lord, you better display your Maya before me. I need nothing else. When Narada thus insisted repeatedly, lord Krsna got up from that place and proceed towards the Sveta island.

## \|\| 3.3.11-14 \|\|

*aḍulyagreṇa saṃgṛhya nāradaṃ muni puṅgavam \|*  
*tato mārgagataścakre ātmānaṃ dvijarūpiṇam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*ṛgvedasadṛśaḥ sākṣādviṣṇurbrahmavadāsthitaḥ \|*  
*vṛddhadvijottamavapuḥ saṃśayo nālpako bhavat \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śikhī kamaṃḍaludhṛto mṛgacarmopavītakaḥ \|*  
*yajñaśarmeti saṃjñāṃ ca cakre'sāvātmanaḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kṛtvāpi kuśataṃtvagrapavitrakṛta lakṣaṇam \|*  
*āyayau sa mahīpṛṣṭhe jambūdvīpaṃ cacāra ha \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. He was accompanied by Narada holding the figure of Sri Krsna. While so moving with Narada, Sri Krsna disguised himself as a Brahmana, who appeared like the Rgveda. No one could doubt (about the true personality of the Brahmana) by a look at him, because he had a tuft over his head, a kamandalu in his hand besides the deer skin. He was adorned with a sacred thread over his body. He looked like a Brahmana having the thorough knowledge of theologian. He wore a ring of kusa grass and a waistband of the sacred grass, which decorated his body. The lord in that form declared his name to be Yajna Sarma. Thus the lord, in the company of Narada, reached Jambudvipa of this earth.

## \|\| 3.3.15-17 \|\|

*vaidiśaṃ nāma nagaraṃ vetravatyāstaṭe śubham \|*  
*tasminsadodyamaparo dhanadhānyasa mṛddhimān \|\| 15 \|\|*

*gomahiṣyajasaṃpūrṇaṃ pāśupālyena saṃsthitaḥ \|*  
*halakarmavṛṣāsakto vaiśyajātiraniṃditaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*gṛhakarmaṇi tanniṣṭhaḥ sīrabhadra iti smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasyāṃtike hariḥ sākṣānnāradena sahāgataḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. While wandering in that continent, they reached the city of Vidisha which was located at the bank of the river Vetravati. They reached the house of a Vaisya known by the name of Sirabhadra. The said Vaisya always occupied himself in the household affairs, possessing a large number of the cows, buffalos, goats and other domestic animals. At that point of time, he was working in the fields with the bullocks and the plough, when

Narada with the lord reached before him. He welcomed both of them offering the seats and eatables as per his capacity. He served them well.

## \|\| 3.3.18-19 \|\|

*tenāpyāsanasanmānaiḥ samarthena kṛtādarau \|*  
*proktaṃ kenātha kiṃ tubhyaṃ sādhyamannaṃ na sādhyate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*na vāsmadīyaṃ yuṣmākaṃ rocatennaṃ tato hariḥ \|*  
*prahasya pradadau tasmai varaṃ dvijavaro mahat \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. But at the time of taking the food, he spoke with his folded hands- “O masters, what should I give you for the food? The cooked food is ready presently, but the food served by me would not be liked by you.” On hearing these words, the lord, who had guised himself as an auspicious Brahmana, smiled and bestowed a boon on the Vaisya.

## \|\| 3.3.20-24 \|\|

*unnāmya vaktraṃ covāca devasaṃstutayā girā \|*  
*saṃtu te bahavaḥ putrāḥ kṣetravyāpārabuddhayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*paśupāśagṛhāsaktāḥ śatārddhabalavāhanāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ putrāśca pautrāśca kṛṣi vṛddhipravarddhakāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*tvañca vṛttiśatairnnityaṃ varddhasva svajanāvṛtaḥ \|*  
*ityuktvā sa jagannātho vāsudevaḥ sanāradaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kṣetre gosvāmināmānaṃ dvijaṃ dadṛśatuśca tau \|*  
*daridraṃ halakarmārttaṃ methyādyopaskarārditam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*bhāgīrathyāstaṭe ramye veṇikāgrāmasannidhau \|*  
*tṛṇagulmalatācchannakṣetre ciṃtākulo hi saḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

20-24. Raising his head, the lord spoke with sweet voice- “You will get such type of sons who would be well-versed in farming and the cattle. They shall be daily engaged in household duties tirelessly. They shall have over fifty vehicles besides many sons and the grandsons. They shall increase the farming and the fields. You will always have an increase in your trade and commerce.” Thus speaking, the lord Jagannatha also known as Vasudeva, together with Narada went to a village named Venika on the bank of the river Bhagirathi or Ganga and met a Brahmana known as Gosvami, who was ploughing the field and was quite poor. He had the powder fenugreek (methi) and spices. The Brahmana was feeling worried because of the wild growth in the field and creepers.

## \|\| 3.3.25 \|\|

*tābhyāṃ saṃprārthito vipro bhojyaṃ prādācca kiṃcana \|*  
*sakāśaṃ tava saṃprāptau dūrādatithidharmiṇau \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. At the same time, both the guests reached there and asked for the food. The Brahmana somehow provided them with the food. Then both of them said- “O Brahmana, we are the guests and have arrived here before you covering a long distance.”

## \|\| 3.3.26-27 \|\|

*ityukto'sau dvijaśreṣṭho halakarma vidhāya tat \|*  
*ājagāma gṛhaṃ tūrṇaṃ tābhyāṃ saha sasaṃbhramam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*cakre caivādaraṃ bhaktyā svayamāsanasatkriyām \|*  
*pādaśaucaṃ tathābhyaṃgaṃ kṛtvātra ca susaṃskṛtam \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. On hearing these words, the Brahmana at once rushed to his abode, leaving aside his work in the field. Then he brought the food from his home. With utmost devotion, he gave them the seats. Thereafter, he gave them the water for washing their hands, feet and faces. He also offered them oil and the water for taking bath.

## \|\| 3.3.28-30 \|\|

*saha patnyā satanayo bhojyaṃ bhuktiṃ cakāra saḥ \|*  
*bhuktabhojyau ca śarvaryāṃ sukhaṃ suptau niśātyaye \|\| 28 \|\|*

*prayātau dadatuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ varaṃ tasmai dvijātaye \|*  
*mā te bhavatu gosvāminkadācidapi karṣaṇam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*mā dhānyaṃ makhasaṃtāna matprasādādvijottama \|*  
*ityuktvā jagmatustūrṇaṃ punaḥ papraccha nāradaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

28-30. He served them both with his wife and son. He served food to both of them pretty well. Subsequently, he served food to both of them during the night and served them the beds for sleeping. Thereafter, he took his food with his family. In the early morning, the lord bestowed a boon on the Brahmana, saying- “O Gosvami, by my grace, you need not have to plough your fields hereafter. You need not have such a son, who would carry out such a tradition.” Thus speaking, both of them departed from that place.

## \|\| 3.3.31-32 \|\|

*kimidaṃ vada deveśa śāparūpo varastvayā \|*  
*bhadra gosvāmine dattaḥ kiṃ ca vaiśye tathāvidhaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*ityuktaḥ prāha deveśaḥ śṛṇu nārada madvacaḥ \|*  
*paramārthaṃ pravakṣye'haṃ tava saṃśayakartanam \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. While walking during the journey, NArada said to the lord- “O god of gods, you have pronounced a curse in place of a boon to the Brahmana and the Vaisya was granted an excellent boon. What is the reason for the same.” At this question of Narada, the lord replied to Narada- “0 Narada, I am (explaining the entire situation) to you, please listen my words, which shall remove you doubt.

## \|\| 3.3.33-36 \|\|

*saṃvatsareṇa yatpāpaṃ matsyaghātī samācaret \|*  
*tadahne kena kurute lāṃgalī nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*ato'rthaṃ kṛṣipālyena narakaṃ yāti lāṃgalī \|*  
*tadabhāvānna kalpaḥ syāttena mokṣo mayi dhruvam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*mayi bhukte prasanne vā ko viśeṣo'sya nārada \|*  
*yadi svargo'tha vā mokṣo na saṃpadyeta tadvṛthā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*idānīṃ halakāluṣyaiḥ sīrabhadro viceṣṭitaiḥ \|*  
*bahupāpaprasaṃgena ghoraṃ narakameṣyati \|\| 36 \|\|*

33-36. The number of sins committed by a fisher man in a day, as compared to him, a ploughman commits much more sins in a day, while ploughing the field. Therefore, a ploughman falls in the hell. His food is essential even when he does not plough a field. In the absence of a field, he is sure to achieve the moksa. What was the special feature of my taking the food unless he achieve heaven or moksa? Since the Vaisya Sirabhadra had committed the sin by ploughing the land, therefore, because Of the excess of the number of sins, he shall have to fall in the hell.

## \|\| 3.3.37-40 \|\|

*saputrapautrasaṃtāno hṛtorthastadgṛhe mayā \|*  
*na bhuktaṃ na ca viśrāntaṃ viśrāṃtaṃ dvijaveśmani \|\| 37 \|\|*

*so'pi dvijo muniśreṣṭha saṃsārāduttariṣyati \|*  
*ityevaṃ saṃvadaṃtau ca jagmaturmārgamuttamam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*kānyakubjasya sāmīpye saraḥ śreṣṭhamapaśyatām \|*  
*haṃsakāraṇḍa vākīrṇaṃ cakravākopaśobhitam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*padminījalakahlāraraktotpalasitotpalaiḥ \|*  
*chāditaṃ padminīpatrairmatsyaiḥ kūrmairjjalodbhavaiḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

37-40. By my reaching his home, I have removed his sins as also of his sons and the grandsons. I neither took food, nor did I take the rest in his place. On the other hand, I took food and also rested at the place of the Brahmana. Therefore, O best of the sages, the Brahmana would certainly cross the ocean of the universe.” Thus both of them kept on talking, while moving on the journey and reached the city of Kanyakubhja. having a beautiful lake there, winch was crowded with the birds like swans and the ducks beside the partridges. The lake had enough of red, blue as well as white lotus flowers, besides the leaves of water lilies. There were different varieties of fish as well as the tortoises, which added to the grace of the lake.

## \|\| 3.3.41-42 \|\|

*taṭai ramyairghanairvṛkṣaiḥ ketakīkhaṇḍamaṃḍitam \|*  
*ketakīkusumāmodairllakucaistaṭamaṃḍitaiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*dātyūhaśikhibhāruṇḍacakorādyaiśca saṃkulam \|*  
*kuravaiścātakai ramyaṃ kekākulanināditam \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. The ketaki trees were grown over its bank With the fragrance of ketaki and lily flowers, the atmosphere was made quite pleasant. The buds like wood pecker, peacocks and partridges etc., moved in flocks, issuing sweet notes.

## \|\| 3.3.43-53 \|\|

*jalakukkuṭasaṃgītaṃ haṃsasārasaśobhitam \|*  
*jīvaṃjīvakahārītacakorairupaśobhitam \|\| 43 \|\|*

*vaśiṣṭhasya munernāmnā vikhyātaṃ śrīmahodayam \|*  
*asminnadya praveṣṭavyaṃ mahājanavivekinām \|\| 44 \|\|*

*sthātavyaṃ puratasteṣāṃ tasmātsnānaṃ samācaret \|*  
*ityuktvā keśavaḥ pāpaṃ sasnau prāgeva tajjalaiḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*yattīrthalokaṃ vikhyātaṃ snātvā tīraṃ samāśritaḥ \|*  
*prahare vāsudevasya nārado'pi mudā yutaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*ācamya sasnau tīrthena kṣaṇāttīrthamavāpya ca \|*  
*yāvaduttiṣṭhate toyātsnātvā ṛṣirudāradhīḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*tāvatstrītvaṃ samāpanno nāradaḥ kena varṇyate \|*  
*yasyāstu vistṛte netre vaktraṃ candropamaṃ śubham \|\| 48 \|\|*

*smarapāśopamau karṇau kapolau kanakojjvalau \|*  
*nāsikā tilasūnena kāmacāpopame bhruvau \|\| 49 \|\|*

*daśanā hīrakaistulyā vidrumābhaḥ śubhādharaḥ \|*  
*mayūrasya kalāpena tulya kacanibaṃdhanam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*śaṃkharekhātrayeṇaiva kaṃṭhadeśo virājate \|*  
*mādhavīlatayā tulyau maṃjū tasyā bhujau śubhau \|\| 51 \|\|*

*yutau raktotpalābhāsau pāṇī raktanakhāṃgulī \|*  
*pīnāvatuṃgatanudhṛtkaṭhinau kalaśopamau \|\| 52 \|\|*

*stanāvaviralau snigdhau cakravākayugopamau \|*  
*svalpakaṃ madhyadeśaṃ tu muṣṭigrāhyamasaṃśayam \|\| 53 \|\|*

43-53. The songs of the water ducks, partridges and other birds issued sweet tones, making the atmosphere quite charming. The lake belonged to Maharsi Vasistha and was known by the name of Mahodaya. Therefore, one must take a bath m this lake.” Thus speaking, lord Vasudeva himself entered the lake and had his bath in the same. After Kesava came out of the lake taking his bath, Narada too became desirous of having a bath in the same lake. Narada, before his entry into the lake, took some water in his palm and sipped it. Then, he had a dip in the water. As soon as Narada came out of the water, he found himself as a woman, whose beauty was beyond description. She had vast eyes, the face resembled the moon, the ears resembled the noose of the Kamadeva, the cheeks resembled the complexion of gold, pointed nose, the eye brows resembled the bow of Kamadeva, the teeth resembled the gems, the lips resembled the coral, the well arranged hair over the head resembled the tail of the peacock. The neck was adorned with three lines, the soft arms resembled the creeper Madhavi and the palms resembled the red lotus flowers. The nails were also of red colour. Her breasts were raised resembling the pitchers besides being beautiful. They appeared like the pair of partridge birds. Similarly, the waist could be held in a grip.

## \|\| 3.3.54-60 \|\|

*nābhimaṃḍalagāṃbhīryaṃ lāvaṇyaṃ kena varṇyate \|*  
*valitrayeṇa vikṛtā romarājirvirājitā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*nayane ca punastasyā mṛgyā iva suśobhane \|*  
*nitaṃbo biṃbaphalakā manmathāyatanaṃ śubham \|\| 55 \|\|*

*raṃbhāyugmopamāvūrū smarabāṇanibaṃdhanau \|*  
*viparītaratāyāsakhedabhārasahau dṛḍhau \|\| 56 \|\|*

*navakundalatāsārasaralaṃ sanibaṃdhanam \|*  
*jaṃghāyugaṃ mahārāja gūḍhagulpha yugaṃ tathā \|\| 57 \|\|*

*raktāṃgulīlatātalpanakhacandrakayācitam \|*  
*caraṇāraviṃdayugalaṃ saraktaṃ supratiṣṭhitam \|\| 58 \|\|*

*saivaṃvidhā tadā nārī sarvalakṣaṇapū jitā \|*  
*babhūva kṣaṇamātreṇa jagadvyāmohakāriṇī \|\| 59 \|\|*

*kṣīrodamathanottīrṇā lakṣmīmanyābhivocchritām \|*  
*dṛṣṭvāpyadarśanaṃ prāpto māyayā madhusūdanaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

54-60. No one could describe the beauty and the depth of her navel. The belly had three times of tender hair. Her eyes were as unstable as those of a doe and were graceful as a bimba fruit. Her limbs were as lovely as Rambha herself. Her thighs were like the trunks of the banana tree and as if fallen of the arrows of the god of love and could bear the weight of her body. O lord, like the fresh creeper of the lotus flowers, her feet looked charming. Thus, the damsel possessed all the excellent symbols, which were achieved by her in a moment, which could fascinate the world. By a look at that beauty, it appeared as if she was the second Laksmi having emerged out of the churning of the ocean of milk. After this event, lord Krsna suddenly disappeared from the scene by means of his own illusion.

## \|\| 3.3.61 \|\|

*saṃprāpyate ca sā kālasaṃgarāhāriṇī yathā \|*  
*āsta ekākinī mugdhā kuryāddigavalokanam \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. The beautiful damsel remained alone like a beautiful woman having arrived at a lonely place to meet her beloved. Being alone, she started looking around herself.

## \|\| 3.3.62-64 \|\|

*athājagāma taṃ deśaṃ nāmnā tāladhvajo nṛpaḥ \|*  
*saha sainyaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraṃdara ivāmaraiḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*gajārūḍhairhayārūḍhai rathārūḍhairnarottamaiḥ \|*  
*vimānayānayugmasthaistathāṃtaḥpurikājanaiḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

*dhvajātapatrakalilairanīkaiḥ parivāritaḥ \|*  
*tena sā sahasā dṛṣṭā nārī kamalalocanā \|\| 64 \|\|*

62-64. At the same time, a king named Taladhvaja arrived there with his warriors. He had been decorated like Indra. The excellent people were riding over the horses as well as the chariots. The queens of the palace were mounted in two vehicles. The army marched on with flags and umbrellas. The king suddenly spotted the lovely damsel.

## \|\| 3.3.65 \|\|

*babhūva kṣaṇamātreṇa kaṃdarpaśarapīḍitaḥ \|*  
*keyaṃ kasya kutaḥ prāptā kiṃ devī vātha mānuṣī \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. Her very sight filled him with lust and he became passionate with desire for her. He started thinking in his mind- “Who is she? Whose beloved is she? Where from has she arrived here? Is she a divine damsel or human lady?

## \|\| 3.3.66-68 \|\|

*adṛṣṭarūpāpsarasā kāciddevī samāgatā \|*  
*ahorūpaṃ surūpāyā gocare paritaḥ pumān \|\| 66 \|\|*

*mumūrṣurjāyate mohādanudigdhahato yathā \|*  
*iti saṃcintya hṛdaye rājā tāladhvajo'ntike \|\| 67 \|\|*

*uvāca nārīṃ mugdhāṃ tāṃ śṛṇu madvacanaṃ śubhe \|*  
*kā tvaṃ kasya kutaḥ prāptā deśametaṃ śucismite \|\| 68 \|\|*

66-68. It appears as if an Apsara with her unique beauty has arrived here. How attractive is her beauty? A person, by a mere look at her, feels as if dead”. Thus thinking variously, the king Taladhvaja went close to her and spoke to the charming damsel- “O auspicious one, you please listen to me. Who are you wearing a serene smile over your face? Whose beloved are you? How have you arrived here?”

## \|\| 3.3.69-70 \|\|

*ityukte sāśru cārvaṃgī prāha māṃ viddhyayonijām \|*  
*pitrā mātrā vihīnāṃ ca tathādyāpi kumārikām \|\| 69 \|\|*

*nirāśrayāṃ viditvaināṃ tato jātaḥ smarārditaḥ \|*  
*āropya hayapṛṣṭhe tāṃ tato rājāgato gṛham \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. On hearing these words, the damsel with tears flowing from her eyes, said- “I am born without a mother’s touch and have been deprived of my parents. I am a maid till now.” On hearing the words, the king thought her to be a destitute and a helpless woman. With his lustful mind, he made her ride with him over the horse. Thereafter, he moved with his horse towards his abode.

## \|\| 3.3.71-74 \|\|

*nītvā vivāhayāmāsa śāstroktavidhinā tataḥ \|*  
*reme prāsādaśṛṃgāgre paryaṃke sitayā tayā \|\| 71 \|\|*

*udyānabhavyabhūmīṣu nadīnāṃ pulineṣu ca \|*  
*parvatānāṃ nitaṃbeṣu nirjhareṣu guhāsu ca \|\| 72 \|\|*

*padmakhaṃḍeṣu phulleṣu śobhiteṣu sarassu ca \|*  
*prayāgādiṣu tīrtheṣu nadīnāmāśrameṣu ca \|\| 73 \|\|*

*divyāvasatharamyeṣu velākūleṣu pārthivaḥ \|*  
*yāvaddvādaśa varṣāṇi ekāhamapi bhārata \|\| 74 \|\|*

71-74. Reaching there, he married her according to the scriptural procedure. Thereafter, he started enjoying her over the bed covered with white bed sheet, placed over the peak of the palace. The king enjoyed her company for full twelve years in the orchards, beautiful sites, river banks, mountain caves, springs of water, caves, the lakes decorated with the beautiful lotus flowers, the holy places like Prayaga and others, the river banks or the hermitages, the divine spots, besides the sea shores. The king enjoyed her company for full twelve years.

## \|\| 3.3.75-77 \|\|

*tatastrayodaśe varṣe tasyā garbho'bhavanmahān \|*  
*etasmingarbhasaṃpūrṇe jātaṃ dīrghamalābukam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*tadbhedāhatakuṃbheṣu bījaprārohaṇānnarāḥ \|*  
*babhūvurddhātuśūnyā vai divyadehabalotkaṭāḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*paṃcāśatsaṃkhyayā jātā upasargādivarjitāḥ \|*  
*ārūḍhayauvanāḥ sarve sutāḥ saṃgrāmakovidāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

75-77. She conceived during the thirteenth year. After the completion of the duration of the pregnancy, a pinda resembling a pumpkin emerged out of her womb. In that fruit, several seeds were sprouting which resembled the human figures with divine bodies, but were immensely strong. They were fifty in number. When they became youthful, they became great warriors.

## \|\| 3.3.78-83 \|\|

*teṣāṃ putrāśca pautrāśca babhūvuḥ surasattamāḥ \|*  
*yuyudhuḥ śarasaṃghātaiścakraśūlāsipaṭṭiśaiḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

*hayairanyairgajairanyaiḥ krodhāṃdhāḥ kauravā iva \|*  
*pāṃḍavaiḥ saha saṃgrāme yuyudhuḥ kṣayamaṃjasā \|\| 79 \|\|*

*sapadātigajārohāḥ sāṃtaḥpurayugecchayā \|*  
*vineśurabdhimāsādya siṃdhūnāṃ pravahā iva \|\| 80 \|\|*

*sāsisabalavistārāḥ sadarpāḥ samahocchrayāḥ \|*  
*indralokopamaṃ sarvaṃ kulaṃ naṣṭaṃ kṣaṇaṃ tadā \|\| 81 \|\|*

*saṃdṛśya nāradīyaiṣā vinaṣṭaṃ svakulaṃ raṇe \|*  
*ruroda snehasaṃyuktai rasaiḥ kaluṣayā girā \|\| 82 \|\|*

*hā daiva hā vidhe pāpa hā kṛtānta namaskṛta \|*  
*darśayitvā vidhānaṃ me punarnetre hṛte tvayā \|\| 83 \|\|*

78-83. Their sons and the grandsons were similarly strong and valorous. They were quite intelligent and the best of the humans. Subsequently, all of them were filled with arrogance like the Kauravas. Mounting their vehicles, carrying their weapons like bows and arrows, discs, swords, pattisa and other weapons, they reached in the battlefield to wage a war against the Pandavas. Reaching there, getting enraged, they started fighting a terrific war with the Pandavas. Subsequently, all of them, mounting over their horses and the elephants together with their warriors, they went on killing the enemies, reached the middle of the battleground. Ail of them, having been surrounded by the enemies from all the sides, like a river in space gets absorbed in the oceanic water, all of them were destroyed. In the war, all their weapons, strength, pride, vehicles, soldiers, etc. were all destroyed. At that point of time, the divine lady got the news about the destruction of her entire family. She, then getting upset (because of the love for family), started crying and lamenting. She cried- “O destiny, О fate, you are the remover of the sins. Even the god of death bows in reverence to you. You have taken out both the eyes, after giving them to me.”

## \|\| 3.3.84-86 \|\|

*ityuktvā svamurohastairjaghāna bhṛśaduḥkhitā \|*  
*bhūmau mūrcchāturā bhūtvā punaḥ prāptā vicetanam \|\| 84 \|\|*

*so'pi rājā viṣaṇṇo'sau nirviṇṇaḥ śokasāgare \|*  
*bhūmau nipatito duḥkhādruroda bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ \|\| 85 \|\|*

*viṣaṇṇo maṃtribhiḥ sārdhaṃ vṛddhaśokena saṃyutaḥ \|*  
*etasminnaṃtare viṣṇurājagāma dvijaiḥ saha \|\| 86 \|\|*

84-86. Thus lamenting, feeling extremely painful, she started beating her head. With the striking of her own head, she fell down unconscious on the ground. On regaining consciousness, she started beating her head again. At the same time, the ministers of the king also feeling grieved, tried to console the king, getting confused at the same time. By about the same time, lord Visnu disguised as an old Brahmana reached there in the king’s court.

## \|\| 3.3.87-88 \|\|

*dvijaveṣaparicchanna upaviṣṭaḥ sukhāsane \|*  
*tataḥ purassaro bhūtvā cakre dharmārthadarśanam \|\| 87 \|\|*

*kiṃ rodanena bahunā yuvayoḥ kleśakāriṇā \|*  
*śrūyatāṃ viṣṇumāyaiṣā svapnadṛṣṭadhanopamā \|\| 88 \|\|*

87-88. The ministers, offering salutation to him, lodged him over the throne. Thereafter, he asked the king and the queen, the cause of their miserable condition. On coming to know of the reason for misery of both the king and the queen, lord Visnu disguised as a Brahmana, started delivering discourse to them on dharma.

## \|\| 3.3.89-93 \|\|

*śobhane yādṛśaḥ śokaḥ kṛtaḥ saṃsārasāgare \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ pariṇāmoyamīdṛśaḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*puraṃdarasahasrāṇi cakravartiśatāni ca \|*  
*nirvāpitāni kālena pradīpa iva vāyunā \|\| 90 \|\|*

*kuryuśca karayugmena cūrṇaṃ meruṃ mahītale \|\| 91 \|\|*

*ūddhartuṃ dharaṇīsaṃjñāṃ grahītuṃ candrabhāskarau \|*  
*praviṣṭāste tu kālena kṛtāṃtavadanaṃ tadā \|\| 92 \|\|*

*durgastrikūṭaḥ parikhāḥ samudrā rakṣāṃsi yodhā dhanadācca vittam \|*  
*maṃtraśca yasyauśanasā praṇītaḥ sa rāvaṇo daivavaśādviṣaṇṇaḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

89-93. He said- “0 king! Both of you getting so upset are crying immensely. There is no benefit for so doing. To the contrary, it adds to the misery. All of you should listen to my words. The universe, its wealth and the family emerge out of the Maya of Visnu and are dream like. O excellent one, while moving in the ocean of the universe, it would not be proper for you to grieve like this. Because whosoever is born in this world, has to face such a situation, one day or the other. So much so that the powerful Kala, consumes all like the fire in thousands of Indras, hundreds of the Cakravarti kings, unrooting them completely. The aquatic animals and other living beings or creatures can be destroyed by him. Even the oceans can be dried up by the same. He is the one who can reduce to dust the Meru mountain. He can rescue the earth (from water of the ocean). Even those who can capture the sun and the moon, get vanished with moves of the destiny and meet with their end. As a move of the destiny, even Ravana had to meet with his end, though he was lodged in the Trikuta mountain surrounded by the ocean, had Raksasas as his warriors, the wealth of Kubera with him and the advice of Sukracarya with him.

## \|\| 3.3.94-95 \|\|

*saṃgrāme gajaturagasamākule'pi vādādagnau vā gatavivare mahodadhau vā \|*  
*sarvairvā saha vasatāmudīrṇakopairnābhāvyo bhavati kadācideva nāśaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*pātālamāviśatu yātu surendralokamārohatu kṣitidharādhipatiṃ sumerum \|*  
*maṃtrauṣadhipraharaṇaiśca karotu rakṣāṃ yadbhāvi tadbhavati nātha vibhāvito'smi \|\| 95 \|\|*

94-95. Even when one is surrounded by elephants, horses and others in the battlefield, or is surrounded by the fire, netherworld, the mountain top or when a person hides himself in the deep oceanic water or remains present before all the people, or tries to escape himself from the fury of the death, this is not possible. O master, the netherworld, the heaven or the peak of the Sumeru mountain or even when one is protected by the mantras or the herbs, but whatever is destined to happen, it does happen. This is well known to me.

## \|\| 3.3.96-98 \|\|

*roditi kaścidathāśrudhautānanagurutaraśokavihvalaḥ \|*  
*pravikaṭacaraṇavānapi nṛtyati kaściddharmādivigrahaḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

*gāyati hṛdayahāri sukhanirbharamāyatavistṛtā'dharo'dhikam \|*  
*sāra eṣa raṃgodaragatanaṭapaṭahākāma evāyam \|\| 97 \|\|*

*ityevaṃ dharmamuddiśya viṣṇuḥ saṃsāraceṣṭitam \|*  
*tūṣṇīṃ babhūvānupadaṃ tataste dvijapuṅgavāḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

96-98. Suffering immensely with grief in the world some one cries like this as a result of which his face gets washed with the tears. Some religious minded person dances even in extremely unfavourable circumstances. Someone expresses delight with comfort. Some one is dancing and singing. Therefore, the gist of the matter is that in the theatre, the music attracts the listeners, and keeps them occupied. Similar is the case with the universe. The universe should be viewed in the same way.” Thus pronouncing the worldly discourse, lord Visnu disguised as the Brahmana kept silent.

## \|\| 3.3.99 \|\|

*uttiṣṭha snāhi putrāṇāṃ prakuruṣvaurdhvadehikam \|*  
*mā śokaṃ viṣṇumāyaiṣā viṣṇunā nirmitā svayam \|\| 99 \|\|*

99\. O best of the Brahmanas, thereafter, all of them were advised to go and have a bath, performing the last rites of the dead sons. It was all the Maya or the illusion of lord Visnu, which has been produced by him.

## \|\| 3.3.100-103 \|\|

*ityuktā cārusarvāṃgī sa babhūvācalaḥ pumān \|*  
*sa eṣa sadṛśākāro nāradastatkṣaṇe'bhavat \|\| 100 \|\|*

*so'pi rājā dadarśātha taṃ samaṃtripurohitaḥ \|*  
*sāṃtaḥpuramidaṃ sarvamiṃdrajālopamaṃ kṣaṇāt \|\| 101 \|\|*

*nāradaṃ muniśārdūlaṃ jaṭābhārabhayānakam \|*  
*gauravarṇaṃ jvalaṃtaṃ ca brāhamyā lakṣmyā virājitam \|\| 102 \|\|*

*śikhā kamaṇḍaludharaṃ vīṇādaṇḍakaraṃ tathā \|*  
*brahmasūtreṇa śubhreṇa kaupīnācchādanena ca \|*  
*pādukābhyāṃ sthitaṃ tīre saraso brāhmaṇāsane \|\| 103 \|\|*

100-103. The beautiful damsel, after taking the bath, appeared like Narada. Thereafter, the courtiers, the priest with the king, besides the queens of the palace witnessed everything like the magic that Narada was present there with matted locks of hair over his head, having fair complexion, adorned with Brahman-Laksmi as well as the tuft, vina, the sacred thread, Kaupina as well as the scarf. Not only that, on the bank of the lake, the sandals of the Brahmanas were also found.

## \|\| 3.3.104-107 \|\|

*saṃpragṛhya karāgreṇa jagāmādarśanaṃ hariḥ \|*  
*ambareṇa suraiḥ sārddhaṃ tasmāddeśādyudhiṣṭhira \|\| 104 \|\|*

*śvetadvīpamathāsādya prāha devo muniṃ nṛpa \|*  
*devarṣe yattvayā pṛṣṭaṃ pūrvaṃ māyākathāṃ prati \|\| 105 \|\|*

*māyā yayedṛśī māyā yatsvarūpā yadātmikā \|*  
*sā te māyā mayā brahmanvaiṣṇavī saṃpradarśitā \|\| 106 \|\|*

*evamuktvā munivaraṃ devadevo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*babhūvāntarhitassadyo devarṣestasya paśyataḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

104-107. Lord Visnu was also present there, holding the finger of Narada. O Yudhisthira, Janardana - the god of gods, also reached the Svetadvipa, by aerial way. The lord then said to Narada-“O divine sage, you had earlier questioned me about Maya of Visnu and I have displayed its form. Thus, lord Janardana - the god of gods, released Narada from that female form with the help of his Maya.

## Chapter 4. Blemishes of the world

## \|\| 3.4.1-5 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*devatvaṃ mānuṣatvaṃ ca tiryaktvaṃ kena karmaṇā \|*  
*prāpnoti puruṣaḥ kena garbhavāsaṃ sudāruṇam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*garbhasthaśca kimaśnāti kathamutpadyate punaḥ \|*  
*dattotthānādikāndoṣānkathaṃ tarati dustarān \|\| 2 \|\|*

*bālabhāve kathaṃ puṣṭiḥ syādyuvā kena karmaṇā \|*  
*kulīnaḥ kena bhavati surūpaḥ sudhanaḥ katham \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kathaṃ dārānavāpnoti gṛhaṃ sarvaguṇairyutam \|*  
*paṃḍitaḥ putravāṃstyāgī syādā mayavivarjitaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*kathaṃ sukhena mriyate kathaṃ bhuṃkte śubhāśubham \|*  
*sarvamevāmalamate gahanaṃ pratibhāti me \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Yudhisthira said- O lord, how does a person is born as a god, a human, bird or other creatures? What does he consume in pregnancy period? How is he born after remaining in the womb? How does he bear the pain like toothache? How does he grow during infancy and how does he reach the youthful age? By which deeds, one achieves the youthful age, and the wife of high race, with beauty, well built body besides being virtuous? How does a person discards a body with sons, free from ailments while living comfortably. How does he face the evil and the auspicious deeds? I am feeling these subjects to be quite deep.

## \|\| 3.4.6-7 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*śubhairdevatvamāpnoti miśrairmānuṣatāṃ vrajet \|*  
*aśubhaiḥ karmabhirjjaṃtustiryagyoniṣu jāyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

*pramāṇaṃ śrutirevātra dharmādharmaviniścaye \|*  
*pāpaṃ pāpena bhavati puṇyaṃ puṇyena karmaṇā \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Sri Krsna said- By performing the noble deeds, one becomes a god or a Deva. With the performing of the mixed deeds, one is born as a human and with the performing of (he evil deeds, one is born as a bird or other such species. It is the Vedas alone which distinguish between the good or the evil deeds. It is recorded therein that with the performing of the evil deeds, one achieves the evil result, while with the performing of the noble deeds, one achieves the good results.

## \|\| 3.4.8-13 \|\|

*ṛtukāle tadā bhuktaṃ nirdoṣaṃ yena saṃsthitam \|*  
*tadā tadvāyunā spṛṣṭaṃ strīraktenaikatāṃ vrajet \|\| 8 \|\|*

*visargakāle śukrasya jīvaḥ karaṇasaṃyutaḥ \|*  
*bhṛtyaḥ praviśate yoniṃ karmabhiḥ svairnniyojitaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tacchukraraktamekasthamekāhātkalalaṃ bhavet \|*  
*pañcarātreṇa kalalaṃ buhudā kāratāṃ vrajet \|\| 10 \|\|*

*budbudaṃ saptarātreṇa māṃsapeśī bhavettataḥ \|*  
*dvisaptāhādbhavetpeśī raktamāṃsadṛḍhāṃcitaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*bījasyevāṃkurāḥ peśyāḥ pañcaviṃśa tirātrataḥ \|*  
*bhavaṃti māsamātreṇa pañcadhā jāyate punaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*grīvā śiraśca skandhaśca pṛṣṭhavaṃśastathodaram \|*  
*māsadvayena sarvāṇi kramaśaḥ saṃbhavaṃti ca \|\| 13 \|\|*

8-13. In case a sinless person, during the period of menses, unites with the woman innocently, then at the time of the fall of his semen, the jiva like a servant, as a result of the deeds performed by him, reaches the appropriate yoni or birth. At that point of time, the semens of the man and the woman getting united, gets ripened for a day. After a week, it starts turning into the flesh. In two weeks period, the blood (or semen) becomes a solid flesh. It then becomes the seed and starts sprouting. On the arrival of the twenty fifth night, the five limbs of the body via., neck, head, shoulder, back bone and the belly, start their formation. Similarly in two months, the process of the formation of the limbs as started above, is completed.

## \|\| 3.4.14-18 \|\|

*tribhirmāsaiḥ prajāyaṃte sadravyāṃkurasaṃdhayaḥ \|*  
*māsaiścaturbhiraṃgulyaḥ prajāyaṃte yathākramam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*mukhaṃ nāsā ca karṇau ca jāyante pañca māsakaiḥ \|*  
*daṃtapaṃktistathā guhyaṃ jāyaṃte ca nakhāḥ punaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*karṇau ca raṃdhrasahitau ṣaṇmāsābhyaṃtareṇa tu \|*  
*pāyurmeḍhramupasthaśca nābhiścāpyupa jāyate \|\| 16 \|\|*

*saṃdhayo ye ca gātreṣu māsairjāyaṃti saptabhiḥ \|*  
*aṅgapratyaṃgasaṃpūrṇaḥ śiraḥ keśasamanvitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vibhaktāvayavaḥ puṣṭaḥ punarmāsāṣṭakena ca \|*  
*paṃcātmakasamāyuktaḥ paripakvaḥ sa tiṣṭhati \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18. During the third month, the joints start sprouting. In the fourth month, the hands and the fingers start the formation. During the fifth month of the pregnancy, the face, nose and both the ears are formed. During the sixth month, the gums, anus, nails and holes of ears, are formed. During the seventh month, sinew, testicles, penis and the joints are formed. During the eight month, the formation of all the limbs, the hair of the head, and other limbs are grown separately. O son of the race of Bharata, during the ninth month, the pregnancy is matured with all the limbs.

## \|\| 3.4.19-21 \|\|

*māturāhāravīryeṇa ṣaḍvidhena sa tiṣṭhati \|*  
*rasena pratyahaṃ bālo vardhate bharatarṣabha \|\| 19 \|\|*

*tatte'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi yathāśrutamariṃdama \|*  
*nābhisūtranibandhena varddhate sa dinedine \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tataḥ smṛtiṃ labhejjīvaḥ saṃpūrṇe'smiñcharīrake \|*  
*sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ vijānāti nidrāsvapnaṃ purā kṛtam \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. Then, the food-semen of the mother, which is formed with the six types of juices, makes the pregnancy to grow. I am describing the matter as has been heard by me. The jiva during pregnancy grows daily through the navel and during this period, he is reminded of his earlier birth. It is because, at that point of time, his body is fully developed. He is fully aware of the comforts and pleasures enjoyed by him earlier. During the pregnancy, he becomes aware of the pleasure, pain and dreams, quite well.

## \|\| 3.4.22-25 \|\|

*mṛtaścāhaṃ punarjāto jātaścāhaṃ punarmṛtaḥ \|*  
*nānāyoni sahasrāṇi mayā dṛṣṭāni tāni vai \|\| 22 \|\|*

*adhunā jātamātro'haṃ prāptasaṃskāra eva ca \|*  
*etacchreyaḥ kariṣyāmi yena garbhe na saṃśrayaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

*garbhasthaściṃtaye devamahaṃ garbhādviniḥsṛtaḥ \|*  
*adhyeṣye caturo vedānsaṃsāravinivartakān \|\| 24 \|\|*

*evaṃ sa garbhaduḥkhena mahatā paripīḍitaḥ \|*  
*jīvaḥ karmavaśādāste mokṣopāyaṃ viciṃtayan \|\| 25 \|\|*

22-25. During the same pregnancy, he becomes aware of his earlier birth and how did he meet with his death in the past birth? He gets also aware of the fact that he has to die after his birth besides the fact that he after taking thousands of births, has entered the present pregnancy- “Soon after my present birth after due initiation, I shall perform the noble deeds, in order to avoid my re-entry in the womb of my mother. Because of my present condition in the womb, I am thinking like this, but soon after my birth, I shall study all the four Vedas in order to achieve moksa.”

## \|\| 3.4.26-29 \|\|

*yathā girivarākrāṃtaḥ kaścidduḥkhena tiṣṭhati \|*  
*tathā jarāyuṇā dehī duḥkhe tiṣṭhati ceṣṭitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*patitaḥ sāgare yadvadduḥkhairāste samākula \|*  
*garbhodakena siktāṃgastathāste vyākulaḥ pumān \|\| 27 \|\|*

*lohakuṃbhe yathā nyastaḥ pacyate kaścidagninā \|*  
*tathā sa pacyate jaṃturgarbhasthaḥ pīḍitodaraḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*sūcībhiragnivarṇābhirvibhinnasya niraṃtaram \|*  
*yadduḥkhamupajāyeta tadgarbhe'ṣṭaguṇaṃ bhavet \|\| 29 \|\|*

26-29. Accordingly, as a result of his earlier deeds, the jiva immensely suffers from the pain of pregnancy and always thinks of the means for his redemption. As a person suffers getting pressed under the weight of a mountain, similarly, the jiva suffers in the womb of the mother. As a person suffers and feels painful in the oceanic water, similarly, getting soaked in the water of the womb, the Jiva also feels painful. As a person when put in a pitcher of iron and then cooked in fire, the jiva has to suffer the pain of remaining in the womb. The pain of suffering in the womb is eight times more, then getting pierced with needles heated in the fire.

## \|\| 3.4.30-31 \|\|

*garbhavāsātparo vāsaḥ kaṣṭo naivāsti kutracit \|*  
*dehināṃ duḥkhavadrājansughoro hyatisaṅkaṭaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*ityetadgarbhaduḥkha hi prāṇināṃ parikīrtitam \|*  
*carasthirāṇāṃ sarveṣātmāmagarbhānurūpataḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

30-31. O king, the jiva does not have to suffer the terrific pain as compared to the jiva’s living in the mother’s womb, because the womb is full of many miseries. Thus, I have narrated to you the pain of the womb. The birth of other mobile and immobile beings should also be understood accordingly.

## \|\| 3.4.32-38 \|\|

*garbhātkoṭiguṇaṃ duḥkhaṃ yoniyaṃtraprapīḍanāt \|*  
*saṃmūrcchitasya jāyeta jāyamānasya dehinaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*śaravatpīḍyamānasya yaṃtreṇeva samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*śirasi tāḍyamānasya pāpamudgarakeṇa ca \|\| 33 \|\|*

*garbhānniṣkampamāṇasya prabalaiḥ sūtimārutaiḥ \|*  
*jāyate sumahadduḥkhaṃ paritrāṇamaviṃdataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*yaṃtreṇa pīḍitā yadvanniḥsārāḥ syustilekṣavaḥ \|*  
*tathā śarīraṃ niḥsāraṃ yoniyaṃtraprapīḍitam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*asthimajjātvacāmāṃsasnāyubaṃdhena yaṃtritam \|*  
*raktamāṃsamṛdā yuktaṃ viṇmūtradravalepanam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*keśalomatṛṇācchannaṃ rogāyatanamāturam \|*  
*vadanaikamahaddvāraṃ daṃtoṣṭhakavibhūṣitam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*oṣṭhadvayakapāṭaṃ ca dantajihvārgalānvitam \|*  
*nāḍīsvedapravāhaṃ ca kaphapittapariplutam \|\| 38 \|\|*

32-38. Not only this, the pain which the jiva has to suffer at the time of coming out of the womb is crores of time more than his remaining in the womb. The jiva at the time of birth faints because of the pain with which he suffers. At that point of time, he suffers pain over his entire body as if having been shot with arrows by which all his limbs feel painful. At that same time, the sins attack him with club over the head. He feels extremely painful even with the touch of his body with the air, while coming out of the womb and there is no one to protect him in such a situation. As the dregs of oil seeds come out of the oil mill, with the crushing of the sesamum seeds, similarly, the jiva facing similar pain emerges out of the womb. At that point of time, the body of the jiva is smeared with bones, marrow, skin, flesh, sinews, blood, flesh besides urine and the refuse; besides there are hair on the head and body as well. His lips are like doors, with teeth and the tongue in the same. Besides perspiration, cough etc. flow from his body.

## \|\| 3.4.39-41 \|\|

*jarāśokasamāviṣṭaṃ kālacakrānale sthitam \|*  
*kāmakrodhasamākrāṃtaṃ vyasanaiścopamarditam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*bhogatṛṣṇāturaṃ mūḍhaṃ rāgadveṣavaśānugam \|*  
*saṃvartitāṃgapratyaṃgaṃ jarāyupariveṣṭitam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*saṃkaṭenāviviktena yonidvāreṇa nirgatam \|*  
*viṇmūtraraktasiktāṃgaṃ patkeśācca samudbhavam \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. He also has to suffer from various attacks from air etc., by which he feels extremely painful. There is no one there to help him. With the attack of passions, anger and blemishes, he becomes painful. He becomes restless because of lust, desire, attachment, jealousy. All his limbs are covered with membranes. Getting surrounded with the hidden dangers, he emerges out of the womb, soaked in refuse, urine with red and white feet.

## \|\| 3.4.42 \|\|

*iti dehagṛhaṃ proktaṃ nityasyānityamā tmanaḥ \|*  
*aviśuddhaṃ viśuddhasya karmabaṃdhavinirmitam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In this way, I have described the inauspicious body of the eternal jivatma and how does he achieves the same. This is the inauspicious form of the auspicious soul in the form of the bondage of karmas (deeds).

## \|\| 3.4.43-49 \|\|

*śukraśoṇitasaṃyogāddehaḥ saṃjāyate yataḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ viṇmūtrapūrṇaśca tenāyamaśuciḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*yathāṃtarviṣṭhayā pūrṇaḥ śuciḥ syānna bahirghaṭaḥ \|*  
*yatnataḥ śodhyamāno'pi deho'yamaśucistathā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*saṃprāpyātra pavitrāṇi paṃcaga vyahavīṃṣi ca \|*  
*aśucitvaṃ kṣaṇāccāpi kimanyadvastubiṃdavaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*dehaḥ saṃśodhyamāno'pi pañcagavyakuśāṃbubhiḥ \|*  
*ghṛṣyamāṇa ivāṃgāro nirmalatvaṃ na gacchati \|\| 46 \|\|*

*srotāṃsi yasya satataṃ pravahaṃti gireriva \|*  
*kaphamūtrapurīṣādyaiḥ sa dehaḥ śuddhyate katham \|\| 47 \|\|*

*sarvāśucinidhānasya śarīrasya na vidyate \|*  
*śucirekaḥ pradeśo'pi viṭpūrṇaḥ syaṃdate kila \|\| 48 \|\|*

*kāyaḥ sugaṃdhadhūpādyairyatnenāpi tu saṃskṛtaḥ \|*  
*na jahāti svakaṃ bhāvaṃ śvapu cchamiva nāmitam \|\| 49 \|\|*

43-49. The body emerges out of the combination of blood and semen, filled with retuse and urine. Thus, it is always inauspicious. As by placing the refuse behind the doors, it cannot be purified by any means, similarly, the inauspicious body never gets purified, inspire of purifying it again and again. The pancagavya is formed by the cow’s milk, ghi, curd, urine and the dung. With the use of the same pancagavya, the body is purified in a moment. Because these five things have enough of purity. Even when the coal is rubbed, it cannot becomes bright. Similarly, the body, even after purifying it with pancagavya and kusa cannot be purified. How could the body generating cough, urine and refuse be purified? Because of the effect of refuse (and urine), it could not be pure. Even when the same is provided with the fragrance of incense etc., the body does discard its nature like the tail of a dog (which cannot be straightened).

## \|\| 3.4.50-54 \|\|

*yathā jātyaiva kṛṣṇo hi na śuklaḥ syādupāyataḥ \|*  
*saṃśodhyamānā'pi tathā bhavenmūrtirna nirmalā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*jighrannapi svadurgaṃdhaṃ paśyannapi malaṃ svakam \|*  
*na virajjati loko'yaṃ pīḍayannapi nāsikām \|\| 51 \|\|*

*aho mohasya māhātmyaṃ yena vyāmohitaṃ jagat \|*  
*jighranpaśyansvakaṃ doṣaṃ kāyasya na virajyate \|\| 52 \|\|*

*evametaccharīraṃ hi nisargādaśuci dhruvam \|*  
*tvaṅmātrasāraṃ niḥsāraṃ kadalīsārasaṃnibham \|\| 53 \|\|*

*garbhasthasya smṛtiryāsītsā jātasya praṇaśyati \|*  
*saṃmūrcchitasya duḥkhena yoniyaṃtraprapīḍanāt \|\| 54 \|\|*

50-54. As the black blanket cannot be made bright by any means, similarly, the body cannot be purified by any means. It is quite strange that the jlvatma or the individual soul do not develops detachment inspite of experiencing bad smell, besides the foul smell of refuse. The entire universe has thus been confused, that a person inspite of witnessing the impurity of the body, do not develops detachment. The events which are remembered during the pregnancy, the said memory is lost soon after the birth because the pain caused to the individual soul at the time of pregnancy makes the infant fainted.

## \|\| 3.4.55-61 \|\|

*bāhyena vāyunā cāsya mohasaṃjñena dehinaḥ \|*  
*spṛṣṭamātreṇa ghoreṇa jvaraḥ samupajāyate \|\| 55 \|\|*

*tena jvareṇa mahatā mahāmohaḥ prajāyate \|*  
*saṃmūḍhasya smṛtibhraṃśaḥ śīghraṃ saṃjāyate punaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*smṛtibhraṃśāttu tasyeha pūrvakarmavaśena ca \|*  
*ratiḥ saṃjāyate tūrṇaṃ jaṃtostatraiva janmani \|\| 57 \|\|*

*rakto mūḍhasya loko'yamakārye saṃpravartate \|*  
*na cātmānaṃ vijānāti na paraṃ vindate ca saḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*na śrūyate paraṃ śreyaḥ sati cakṣuṣi nekṣate \|*  
*same pathi śanairgacchanskhalatīva padepade \|\| 59 \|\|*

*satyāṃ buddhau na jānāti bodhyamāno budhairapi \|*  
*saṃsāre kliśyate tena rāgalobhavaśānugaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*garbhasmṛterabhāvena śāstramuktaṃ maharṣibhiḥ \|*  
*tadduḥkhamathanārthāya svargamokṣaprasādhakam \|\| 61 \|\|*

55-61. While coming out of the womb, the soul is touched with the air and he suffers from high fever, as a result of which he develops a great illusion. The person then is deprived of the entire memory. With the loss of the memory of the earlier birth, the jiva develops attachment to his new birth. Then he engages himself in performing the deeds afresh. At that point of time, he neither has any information about himself nor does he know about the Brahman. He does not care for the beneficial words, when they are spoken by others. He does not see inspite of his having the eyes. Even when he walks over the plain ground, he falls at every step. Inspite of possessing wisdom, he does not listen to the learned people. He is overpowered by attachment and greed, he has to face enormous miseries in the world. Though the tales about the stay in the womb of the mother are forgotten, but for the overpowering of the miseries, the ascetics have composed the religious treatises, which lead one to achieve the heaven and the moksa.

## \|\| 3.4.62-63 \|\|

*ye saṃtyasminpare jñāne sarvakāmārthasādhake \|*  
*na kurvaṃtyātmanaḥ śreyastadatra mahadbhutam \|\| 62 \|\|*

*avyakteṃdriyavṛttitvādbālye duḥkhaṃ mahatpunaḥ \|*  
*icchannapi na śaknoti kartuṃ vaktuṃ ca satkriyām \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. How surprising it is in this world that inspite of possessing the excellent knowledge, a human hardly cares for his own welfare. During the childhood, though one is not quite conscious about the sense organs and inspite of being desirous of something, it is beyond his capacity to say or do something according to his will. During the childhood, therefore, a person has to face painful situations.

## \|\| 3.4.64-65 \|\|

*daṃtotthāne mahadduḥkhaṃ maulena vyādhinā tathā \|*  
*bālarogaiśca vividhaiḥ pīḍā bālagrahairapi \|\| 64 \|\|*

*tṛḍbubhukṣāparītāṃgaḥ kaścittiṣṭhati rāraṭan \|*  
*viṇmūtrabhakṣaṇamapi mohādbālaḥ samācaret \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. At the time of the growing of the teeth, he has to suffer from the pain in the gums. He also has to face many child-diseases, besides hunger and thirst and for these types of pains, he cries often. The children, out of contusion, sometimes also consume urine and retuse as well.

## \|\| 3.4.66-88 \|\|

*kaumāre karṇavedhena mātāpitrośca tāḍanāt \|*  
*akṣarādhyayanātpuṃsāṃ duḥkhaṃ syādguruśāsanāt \|\| 66 \|\|*

*prasanneṃdriyavṛttiśca kāmarāgaprapīḍanāt \|*  
*rogoddhatasya satataṃ kutaḥ saukhyaṃ ca yauvane \|\| 67 \|\|*

*īrṣyayā ca mahadduḥkhaṃ mohādraktasya jāyate \|*  
*netrasya kupitasyaiva rāgo duḥkhāya kevalam \|\| 68 \|\|*

*na rātrau viṃdate nidrāṃ kopāgniparipīḍitaḥ \|*  
*divā vāpi kutaḥ saukhyamarthopārjanaciṃtayā \|\| 69 \|\|*

*strīṣvāyāsitadehasya ye puṃsaḥ śukrabiṃdavaḥ \|*  
*na te sukhāya maṃtavyāḥ svedajā iva biṃdavaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*krimibhistudyamānasya kuṣṭhinaḥ kāminastathā \|*  
*kaṇḍūyanāgnitāpena yadbhavetstrīṣu taddhi tat \|\| 71 \|\|*

*yādṛśaṃ viṃdate saukhyaṃ gaṃḍānvayavinirgame \|*  
*tādṛśaṃ strīṣu maṃtavyaṃ nādhikaṃ tāsu vidyate \|\| 72 \|\|*

*gaṃḍasya vedanā yadvatsphuṭitasya nivartate \|*  
*tadvatstrīṣvapi maṃtavyaṃ na saukhyaṃ paramārthataḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

*viṇmūtrasya samutsargātsukhaṃ bhavati yādṛśam \|*  
*tādṛśaṃ teṣu vijñeyaṃ mūḍhaiḥ kalpitamanyathā \|\| 74 \|\|*

*nārīṣvaśucibhūtāsu sarvadoṣāśrayāsu ca \|*  
*nāṇumātrakamapyevaṃ sukhamasti vicārataḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*sanmānamapamānena viyogena susaṃgamaḥ \|*  
*yauvanaṃ jarayā grastaṃ kiṃ saukhyamanupadravam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*valīpalitakhālityaiḥ śithilīkṛtavigraham \|*  
*sarvakriyāsvaśaktaṃ ca jarayā jarjarīkṛtam \|\| 77 \|\|*

*strīpuṃsayornnavaṃ rūpaṃ tadānyonyaṃ priyaṃ purā \|*  
*tadeva jarayā grastamubhayorapi na priyam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*apūrvavatsvamātmānaṃ jarayā parivartitaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ paśyannapi rajyeta ko'nyastasmādacetanaḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*jarābhibhūtaḥ puruṣaḥ patnīputrādibāṃdhavaiḥ \|*  
*aśaktatvāddurācārairbhṛtyaiśca paribhūyate \|\| 80 \|\|*

*dharmamarthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca na jarī yataḥ \|*  
*śaktaḥ sādhayituṃ tasmāccharīramidamātmanaḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*vātapittakaphādīnāṃ vaiṣamyaṃ vyādhirucyate \|*  
*tasmādvyādhimayaṃ jñeyaṃ śarīramidamātmanaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*vātādyavyatiriktatvādvyādhīnāṃ pañjarasya ca \|*  
*rogairnānāvidhairyāni dehaduḥkhānyanekadhā \|*  
*tāni ca svātmavedyāni kimanyatkathayāmyaham \|\| 83 \|\|*

*ekottaraṃ mṛtyuśatamasmindehe pratiṣṭhitam \|*  
*tatraikaḥ kālasaṃyuktaḥ śeṣāścāgantavaḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*ye tvihāgaṃtavaḥ proktāste praśāmyaṃti bheṣajaiḥ \|*  
*japahomapradānaiśca kālamṛtyurna śāmyati \|\| 85 \|\|*

*yadi cāpi na mṛtyuḥ syādviṣamadyādaśaṃkitaḥ \|*  
*na saṃti puruṣe tasmādapamṛtyuvibhītayaḥ \|\| 86 \|\|*

*vividhā vyādhayaḥ śastraṃ sarpādyāḥ prāṇinastathā \|*  
*viṣāṇi jaṃgamādyāni mṛtyordvārāṇi dehinām \|\| 87 \|\|*

*pīḍitaṃ sarvarogādyairapi dhanvantariḥ svayam \|*  
*svasthīkartuṃ na śaknoti prāptamṛtyuṃ ca dehinam \|\| 88 \|\|*

66-88. During the childhood, the rite of piercing of the ears is performed, then punishment from the parents on doing mischief, the punishments from the preceptor, while engaged in the studies, one is punished. Similarly, during the youthful age, one has the external effect because of his satisfaction for the sake of the sense organs. According, becoming more passionate, he becomes upset with lust and desire. Because of his being excessively passionate, one attracts grave ailments. Therefore, one cannot enjoy the least comfort during the youthful age. A passionate person has to face several miseries because of the jealousy. Attachment towards an angry person also becomes the cause of misery. Because inflamed in anger, the attraction towards him is the cause of misery. While burning in the fire of anger, a person cannot sleep during the night. When a person is upset for the earning of the wealth, he is deprived of the comfort even during the day. Becoming passionate for the women, the drops of semen which are ejected while uniting with her, they should also not be considered as pleasant, like the drops of perspiration when the leprosy germs bite, one feels somewhat relieved after scratching that particular limb. Similarly, when the man is bitten by semen germs, the semen falls with a man’s union with a woman. By so doing, the scratching of the man gets subsided. When the boils are burst out, one feels comfort, similarly, by uniting with the woman, one earn the similar type of comfort and no more. The passions are then subsided. No other spiritual comfort is achieved by the act. By easing or by dropping refuse, one feels relieved and the same comfort is felt at the time of the drop of the semen. But the fools have thought about it in a different direction. Thus, by uniting with a woman, which is short lived and is the storehouse of all the blemishes, results in no comfort or pleasure, in case one thinks about deeply. During the youthful age, a person respectfully indulges with a tight embrace with a woman. But when the youthful age is eclipsed by the old age, it is followed by disturbances. Therefore, there is no comfort in that faith or belief. During the old age the human body gets shattered and the skin starts hanging. The entire body gets weak and it becomes unable to perform many of the activities. The beauty and the form of the body which always looks pleasing and refreshing in the youthful age, the same body is not so attractive during the old age. On reaching the old age, one becomes weak, the sons, the wife and the wicked relatives besides the servants also insult the old man. A person achieves dharma, artha, kama and moksa with his own efforts. Therefore, he should make all the efforts to achieve the same, because there is never any chance of getting blemish in making such efforts. When the cough, wind and the bile get disproportioned in the body, one attracts ailment. Therefore, the human body is known to be the storehouse of ailments. Similarly, there are several other ailments besides those generated by wind. Many types of pains are generated in the ribs, the body has enough of ailments, which are experienced by the people. There is nothing else to be spoken, nor am I going to speak. A hundred and one ailments are always lodged in this body, which can cause death any time. One out of them is the kala, while the other diseases are attracted (from others). But the disease which are attracted from others, they can be subsided with the use of the herbs or with the performing of japam or the charities. But the death which is destined can never be averted. Had there been a possibility to avert the death, then the people could fearlessly have consumed the poison. But this is impossible among the humans. They have to face several types of ailments, strike with weapon or snake bite, or by other means and face death. He has to face all types of diseases. At the time of the death of a person even when Dhanvantri appears in person and treats him with the best of the herbs, even then, he cannot be cured.

## \|\| 3.4.89-90 \|\|

*nauṣadhaṃ na tapo dānaṃ na maṃtrā na ca bāṃdhavāḥ \|*  
*śaknuvaṃti paritrātuṃ naraṃ kālena pīḍitam \|\| 89 \|\|*

*rasāyanatapojapyairyogasiddhairmahātmabhiḥ \|*  
*kālamṛtyurapi prājñaistīryate nālasairnnaraiḥ \|\| 90 \|\|*

89-90. When a person is overshadowed by kala, the herbs, tapas, charities, mantras as well as the kiths and kins, cannot save him. The yogis who are well-versed in yogic practices and make use of alchemy, besides performing tapas and japam, can defeat even the kala-mrtyu or the definite death. But the lethargic people can never do so.

## \|\| 3.4.91 \|\|

*nāsti mṛtyusamaṃ duḥkhaṃ nāsti mṛtyusamaṃ bhayam \|*  
*nāsti mṛtyusamastrāsaḥ sarveṣāmeva dehinām \|\| 91 \|\|*

91\. There is no grief greater than the death, there is no danger worse than the death; there is no fear greater than the death, in the bodies of all the people.

## \|\| 3.4.92-100 \|\|

*sadbhāryāputramitrāṇi rājyaiśvaryadha nāni ca \|*  
*abaddhāni ca vairāṇi mṛtyuḥ sarvāṇi kṛntati \|\| 92 \|\|*

*he janāḥ kiṃ na paśyadhvaṃ sahasrasyāpi madhyataḥ \|*  
*janāḥ śatāyuṣaḥ pañca bhavaṃti na bhavaṃti ca \|\| 93 \|\|*

*aśītikā vipadyante kecitsaptatikā narāḥ \|*  
*paramāyuṣaṃ sthitaṃ ṣaṣṭistaccaivāniścitaṃ punaḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*yasya yāvadbhavedāyurdehināṃ pūrvakarmabhiḥ \|*  
*tasyārddhamāyuṣo rātrirharate mṛtyurūpiṇī \|\| 95 \|\|*

*bālabhāvena mohena vārddhakye jarayā tathā \|*  
*varṣāṇāṃ viṃśatiryāṃti dharmakāmārthavarjitā \|\| 96 \|\|*

*āgaṃtukerbhayaiḥ puṃsāṃ vyādhiśokairanekadhā \|*  
*bhakṣyate'rddhaṃ ca tatrāpi yaccheṣaṃ tacca jīvati \|\| 97 \|\|*

*jīvitāṃte ca maraṇaṃ mahāghoramavāpnuyāt \|*  
*jāyate janmakoṭīṣu mṛtaḥ karmavaśātpunaḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*dehabhedena yaḥ puṃsāṃ viyogaḥ karmasaṃkṣayāt \|*  
*maraṇaṃ tadvinirdiṣṭaṃ nānyathā paramārthataḥ \|\| 99 \|\|*

*mahātapapraviṣṭasya cchidyamāneṣu marmasu \|*  
*yadduḥkhaṃ maraṇe jaṃtorna tasyehopamā kvacit \|\| 100 \|\|*

92-100. The timely death destroys even the chaste wife, sons, friends, kingdom and the riches. О graceful listeners, do you not visualize that out of the thousands of people, even five of them do not reach the age of a hundred years? Some of them die at the age of eighty years, some die at the age of seventy, some have the age of sixty years, but death for them even is uncertain, because of the deeds of the several births, half of his prescribed age is usurped by the nights. Besides during the childhood and old age due to confusion, twenty years of their lives are simply wasted. During this period, there is no activity like dharma, artha and kama. Besides several of the contagious disease which attracts him, reduce half of his age. He therefore, remains alive for a very short period. At the end of the life, one has to face the terrific death and then face the tradition of rebirth. A person, according to his deeds, reaches the prescribed yoni and with the exhausting of the related deeds, his life is ended. Thehe reaches another yoni and develops a body. This is therefore, the process of achieving a new body and separation from it by means of death. But in this process nothing is spiritual. There is no mention, anywhere of a person who is a great tapasvi suffering from pain in anyone of his limbs. No such example is available.

## \|\| 3.4.101 \|\|

*hā tāta mātaḥ kāṃteti rudannevaṃ hi duḥkhitaḥ \|*
