*maṃḍūka iva sarpeṇa grasyate mṛtyunā janaḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

101\. At the time of death, feeling painful, a person cries and calls for his father, mother, husband and other relatives. But that person gets destroyed as a frog gets destroyed, having been swallowed by a snake.

## \|\| 3.4.102-103 \|\|

*bāṃdhavaiḥ saṃpariṣvaktaḥ priyaiḥ sa parivāritaḥ \|*  
*niḥśvasandīrghamuṣṇaṃ ca mukhena pariśuṣyati \|\| 102 \|\|*

*krandate caiva khaṭvāyāṃ parivartanmuhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*saṃmūḍhaḥ kṣipate'tyarthaṃ hastapādāvitastataḥ \|\| 103 \|\|*

102-103. His dear relatives at that point of time, try to remove his pain surrounding him from all the sides. But he continues to have deep breathing. Because of this, his mouth is dried up. Lying over the bed he cries with pain. Regaining consciousness, he moves his hands and feet, here and there from the bed to the ground and from ground to the bed.

## \|\| 3.4.104-105 \|\|

*khaṭvāto kāṃkṣate bhūmiṃ bhūmeḥ khaṭvāṃ punarmahīm \|*  
*vivaśastyaktalajjaśca mūtraviṣṭhānulepitaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*yācamānaśca salilaṃ śuṣkakaṇṭhoṣṭhatālukaḥ \|*  
*ciṃtayānaśca vittāni kasyaitāni mṛte mayi \|\| 105 \|\|*

104-105. He desires to remain in the bed. Then, he getting compelled, becomes shameless and his body is plastered with refuse and urine. The neck, the lips and pallet are swallowed. He asks for water repeatedly and he thinks about his wealth alone as to who would inherit his wealth after his death.

## \|\| 3.4.106-109 \|\|

*pañcāvaṭānkhanyamānaḥ kālapāśena karṣitaḥ \|*  
*mriyate paśyatāmeva janānāṃ ghurghurasvanaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

*jīvastṛṇajalaukeva dehāddehaṃ viśetkramāt \|*  
*saṃprāpyottarakālaṃ hi dehaṃ tyajati paurvakam \|\| 107 \|\|*

*maraṇātprārthanāduḥkhamadhikaṃ hi vive kinaḥ \|*  
*kṣaṇikaṃ maraṇāduḥkhamanaṃtaṃ prārthanākṛtam \|\| 108 \|\|*

*jagatāṃ patirarthitvādviṣṇurvāmanatāṃ gataḥ \|*  
*adhikaḥ ko'parastasmādyo na yā syati lāghavam \|\| 109 \|\|*

106-109. Having been caught with the noose of kala, he starts snoring and the person like a straw, according to his deeds, departs from one body and enters into another body. Thus, kala makes one to discard the earlier body and achieves the future body. But the Jiva feels more painful than death, when he has to beg from someone. Because by the death, one feels painful for a moment and while begging, one has to feel painful many times.

## \|\| 3.4.110 \|\|

*jñātaṃ mayedamadhunā mataṃ bhavati yadguru \|*  
*na paraṃ prārthayedbhūyastṛṣṇā lāghavakāraṇam \|\| 110 \|\|*

110\. For the sake of begging, Visnu had to patronize a dwarfish body. Therefore, no one should beg from anyone. It is said that the greed is the only cause to become little by a person. Because of this, a person has to face always the miseries, at the time of birth or the death. This tradition of suffering becomes a habit with the people.

## \|\| 3.4.111-116 \|\|

*ādau duḥkhaṃ tathā madhye duḥkhamaṃte ca dāruṇam \|*  
*nisargātsarvabhūtānāmiti duḥkhaparaṃparā \|\| 111 \|\|*

*vartamānānyatītāni duḥkhānyetāni yāni tu \|*  
*narā na bhāvayaṃtyajñā na virajyati tena te \|\| 112 \|\|*

*atyāhārānmahadduḥkhamanāhārānmahattamam \|*  
*tulitaṃ jīvitaṃ kaṣṭaṃ manye'pyevaṃ kutaḥ sukham \|\| 113 \|\|*

*bubhukṣā sarvarogāṇāṃ vyādhiḥ śreṣṭhatamaḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*sa cānnauṣadhilepena kṣaṇamātraṃ praśāmyati \|\| 114 \|\|*

*kṣudvyādhivedanātulyā niḥśeṣabalakartanī \|*  
*tayābhibhūto mriyate yathānyairvyādhibhirna hi \|\| 115 \|\|*

*tadrasopi hi kāmādvā jihvāgre parivartate \|*  
*tatkṣaṇādvārddhakālena kaṃṭhaṃ prāpya nivartate \|\| 116 \|\|*

111-116. A person never thinks of the basic cause of the past and the present miseries. Due to this ignorance, he does not develop detachment from the miseries. The rich diet, which a person considers to be the best and in case he takes more diet of the same, he has to suffer great pain. At the same time, he also cannot discard it as well. Thus, in case the life is unbalanced, it becomes troublesome. How could he achieve pleasure in the same? The hunger or the desire to eat is the medicine for all the ailments. It gets pacified in a moment in preference to the other medicines. The pain of the disease like hunger destroys the entire strength, and is said to be the best. Because, like an ailing person, a person suffeting front hunger also has to meet with his end. By placing the tasteful food in the mouth, its taste is found by the tongue, but the same reaches the belly through the throat.

## \|\| 3.4.117-118 \|\|

*iti kṣudvyādhitaptānāmannamauṣadhavatsmṛtam \|*  
*na tatsukhāya mantavyaṃ paramārthena paṃḍitaiḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

*mṛtopamo yaścekṣeta sarvakāryavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*tatrāpi ca kutaḥ saukhyaṃ tamasācchāditātmanaḥ \|\| 118 \|\|*

117-118. Accordingly, the people who suffer from hunger, for them the food is surely a medicine. But the comfort so achieved, is not at all spiritual, according to the view of the learned people. A person, who discarding everything, starvs like a dead person only, he cannot achieve even a little comfort in his life, because his knowledge as well as the soul is always covered by darkness.

## \|\| 3.4.119-125 \|\|

*prabodhe'pi kutaḥ saukhyaṃ kāryairupahatātmanaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣigorakṣavāṇijyasevādhvādipariśramaiḥ \|\| 119 \|\|*

*prātarmūtrapurīṣābhyāṃ madhyāhne tu bubhukṣayā \|*  
*tṛptāḥ kāmena bādhyante jaṃtavo'pi vinidrayā \|\| 120 \|\|*

*arthasyopārjane duḥkhamarjitasyāpi rakṣaṇe \|*  
*āye duḥkhaṃ vyaye duḥkhamarthebhyaśca kutaḥ sukham \|\| 121 \|\|*

*caurebhyaḥ salilādagneḥ svajanātpārthivādapi \|*  
*bhayamarthavatāṃ nityaṃ mṛtyoḥ prāṇabhṛtā miva \|\| 122 \|\|*

*khe yātaṃ pakṣibhirmāṃsaṃ bhakṣyate śvāpadairbhuvi \|*  
*jale ca bhakṣyate matsyaistathā sarvatra vittavān \|\| 123 \|\|*

*vimohayati saṃpatsu tāpayaṃti vipattiṣu \|*  
*khedayaṃtyarjanākāle kadā hyarthāḥ sukhāvahāḥ \|\| 124 \|\|*

*yathārthapatirudvigno yaśca sarvārthaniḥspṛhaḥ \|*  
*yataścārthapatirduḥkhī sukhī sarvārthaniḥspṛhaḥ \|\| 125 \|\|*

119-125. Even after becoming conscious, he does not get interested in the farming trade and the job of serving others, nor does he follow the same path. Since he is disinterested in following the path of making all the efforts, how could he able to enjoy the comforts? This is the way of the people, that in the early morning, they perform purification rites. In the noon, they subside their hunger by taking food. After taking the food, when they get satisfied, then they enjoy sex with their wives. Thereafter, they are overpowered by sleep. A person has to face many painful situations while earning his living or wealth. Even after earning the wealth, he has to face many difficulties in saving it and also spending the same. Then how can he enjoy the comforts? Like a person being panic stricken from death, even a wealthy person remains apprehensive of thieves, flood of waters, fire, danger from own kith and kins, besides the king. As the wild birds which consume the flesh, while flying in the sky consume the same, but when the same flesh falls on the earth, it is eaten by the dogs and when the same falls in the water, it serves as the food to the fish. Similarly, a rich person is looked with greed by all the other people. A person, inspite of being wealthy, remains absorbed in his riches and similarly, suffers at the time of adversities. He remains upset even at the time of the earning of the wealth. Therefore, it is difficult to say as to when the wealth can make a person comfortable, but the people who disown the wealth are found to be more peaceful. Because a wealthy person always remains uncomfortable and the one without wealth feels more peaceful.

## \|\| 3.4.126 \|\|

*śītena duḥkhaṃ hemaṃte grīṣme tāpena dāruṇam \|*  
*varṣāsu vātavarṣābhyāṃ kāle'pyevaṃ kutaḥ sukham \|\| 126 \|\|*

126\. In the winter season, the cold is there and during the summer season, one has to face heat. During the rainy season, one has to face the rains which cause enormous misery. Therefore, the people never feel comfortable even during the different seasons.

## \|\| 3.4.127 \|\|

*vivāhavistare duḥkhaṃ tadgarbhodvahane punaḥ \|*  
*prasave'patyadoṣaiśca duḥkhaṃ duḥkhādikarmabhiḥ \|\| 127 \|\|*

127\. Similarly, what type of comfort is achieved by a householder? Because at the time of the arranging of the marriage and concluding of the same, one has to face many troubles. Then the woman has to carry the pregnancy, which is quite painful.

## \|\| 3.4.128-131 \|\|

*dantākṣiraugaiḥ putrasya hā kaṣṭaṃ kiṃ karomyaham \|*  
*gāvo naṣṭāḥ kṛṣirbhagnā vṛṣāḥ kvāpi palāyitāḥ \|\| 128 \|\|*

*amī prāghūrṇakāḥ prāptā bhaktacchede ca me gṛhe \|*  
*bālāpatyā ca me bhāryā kaḥ kariṣyati raṃdhanam \|\| 129 \|\|*

*pradānakāle kanyāyāḥ kīdṛśaśca varo bhavet \|*  
*iti cintābhibhūtānāṃ kutaḥ saukhyaṃ kuṭubinām \|\| 130 \|\|*

*kuṭuṃbaciṃtākulitasya puṃsaḥ śrutaṃ ca śīlaṃ ca guṇāśca sarve \|*  
*apakvakuṃbhe nihitā ivāpaḥ prayāṃti dehena samaṃ vināśam \|\| 131 \|\|*

128-131. After the infant is born, he has to face many ailments, including the teething trouble. The woman has to face the painful situation, while carrying the pregnancy. Then, when he comes in conflict with other children, one feels painful with the suffering of one’s own child, a person becomes somewhat confused. He always says- “I am suffering badly, what should I do, where should I go? I know not where my cow has gone? She could not be traced inspite of the best efforts. The crop has been completely destroyed during the year. I know not who has stolen my bullock? The guests have arrived in my house. Who will cook the food for them? My wife has a small infant in her lap. One feels worried at the time of his daughter’s marriage. Wherefrom shall we get a suitable groom for her.” A person their remains surrounded by such type of worries. Not only this, a person gets shattered (with domestic problems) inspite of his getting well educated, nobility and virtues, but still he gets broken like the pitcher filled with water.

## \|\| 3.4.132-134 \|\|

*rājyepi ca mahadduḥkhaṃ saṃdhivigrahaciṃtayā \|*  
*putrādapi bhayaṃ yatra tatra saukhyaṃ hi kīdṛśam \|\| 132 \|\|*

*sajātīyādvadhaḥ prāyaḥ sarveṣāmeva dehinām \|*  
*ekadravyābhilāṣitvācchunāmiva parasparam \|\| 133 \|\|*

*nāpradhṛṣyabalaḥ kaścinnṛpaḥ khyātosti bhūtale \|*  
*nikhilaṃ yastiraskṛtya sukhaṃ tiṣṭhati nirbhayaḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

132-134. When a person becomes a king, he has to worry for compromise, strife etc. always. At times, he becomes fearful from his own sons even. Then how can he be comfortable, none can say. Because it is generally observed that when being desirous of one and the same thing, like the fighting deeds, one meets with his end by the people of his own caste. There is no peaceful king on earth, who lives comfortably, discarding all his belongings.

## \|\| 3.4.135 \|\|

*ā janmanaḥ prabhṛti duḥkha mayaṃ śarīraṃ karmātmakaṃ tava mayā kathitaṃ narendra \|*  
*dānopavāsaniyamaiśca kṛtaistadeva sarvopabhogasukhabhāgbhavatīha puṃsām \|\| 135 \|\|*

135\. O Narendra, I have spoken to you about achieving of the body and the type of deeds which start from the birth and last till the end and make the life troublesome. All these have been well discussed. But with the giving away of the charities, by fasting, besides the observing of the rules, all the pleasures are bestowed (by the lord) with comfort.

## Chapter 5. Description of the sins and their division

## \|\| 3.5.1 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*adhodhaḥ patanaṃ puṃsāmadhaḥkarma prakīrtitam \|*  
*narakārṇavaghoreṣu yātanā pāpamucyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sri Krsna said- The reasons for the fall of a person happen to be his degraded deeds, by which a person reaching the hells, has to suffer the torture there.

## \|\| 3.5.2-3 \|\|

*adharmabhedā vijñeyāścittavṛttiprabhedataḥ \|*  
*sthūlāḥ sūkṣmāḥ susūkṣmāśca koṭi bhedairanekadhā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*tatra ye pāpanicayāḥ sthūlā narakahetavaḥ \|*  
*te samāsena kathyaṃte manovākkāyasādhanāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Accordingly, there are the divisions in adharma (or the sinful ways) according to the feelings in one’s mind. There are crores of divisions, viz., gross, subtle and extremely subtle etc. But the gross sinful deeds among them, which lead one to the terrific hell, are being described by me. Such deeds are performed mentally, by speech, as well as by the body, because of which one achieves the horrible hell. I am going to speak about them.

## \|\| 3.5.4 \|\|

*parastrīṣvatha saṃkalpaścetasāniṣṭaciṃtanam \|*  
*akāryābhiniveśaśca caturdhā karma mānasam \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. These include desire for other’s wife, the desire to unite or sleep with her. Such are the deplorable deeds, which are committed mentally and are of four types.

## \|\| 3.5.5-6 \|\|

*anibaddhapralāpitvamasatyaṃ cāpriyaṃ ca yat \|*  
*parāpavādapaiśunyaṃ caturdhā karma vācikam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*abhakṣyabhakṣaṇaṃ hiṃsā mithyā kāmasya sevanam \|*  
*parasvānāmupādānaṃ caturddhā karma kāyikam \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. The irrelevant conversation, falsehood, harsh words and the back biting of others are the four types of sins committed by speech. The four evil deeds- taking of the prohibited food, killing of others, falsely uniting (with other females) and stealing of the wealth of others, are the four types of deeds which are committed by the body.

## \|\| 3.5.7 \|\|

*ityetaddvādaśavidhaṃ karma proktaṃ sasādhanam \|*  
*teṣāṃ bhedaṃ punarvacmi yeṣāṃ phalamanaṃtakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. Thus, I have spoken to you about the twelve types of the deeds, besides the sources for the same. But now, I am going to repeat about their divisions, which have been said to bestow enormous merits.

## \|\| 3.5.8 \|\|

*ye dviṣaṃti mahādevaṃ saṃsārārṇavatāraṇam \|*  
*samastapātakopetāste yānti narakāgniṣu \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Lord Mahadeva - the redeemer of the universe, and the one who becomes envious of him, then inviting all the sins, he falls in the fire of the hell.

## \|\| 3.5.9 \|\|

*brahmaghnaśca surāpaśca steyī ca gurutalpagaḥ \|*  
*mahāpātakinaścaite tatsaṃsargī ca paṃcamaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The committing of Brahmahatya, drinking of wine, to unite with the spouse of the preceptor etc., are said to be the five grave sinners.

## \|\| 3.5.10 \|\|

*krodhāddveṣādbhayāllobhādbrāhmaṇaṃ viśasaṃti ye \|*  
*prāṇāṃtiko mahādoṣo brahmaghnāste prakīrtitāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A person, who under the influence of anger, jealousy, fear and the greed, kills a Brahmana while exercising control over him, he is called as the killer of the Brahmana (Brahmaghati).

## \|\| 3.5.11 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaṃ ca samāhūya yācamānamakiñcanam \|*  
*paścānnāstīti taṃ brūyātsa caivaṃ brahmahā smṛtaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. When a Brahmana is called for giving away to him a small thing by someone, and is later refused to be given the same, he is termed to be the killer of a Brahmana.

## \|\| 3.5.12 \|\|

*yastu vidyābhimānena nityaṃ jayati vai dvijān \|*  
*samāsīnaḥ sabhāmadhye brahmahā so'pi kīrtitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A person, who getting proud of his high education, getting disinterested in an assembly, insults a Brahmana, then he has also been also termed as the killer of a Brahmana.

## \|\| 3.5.13 \|\|

*mithyāguṇaiḥ svamātmānaṃ nayatyutkarṣaṇaṃ balāt \|*  
*gurūṇāṃ ca viruddho yaḥ sa caiva brahmahā smṛtaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. When a Brahmana who suffers from hunger and thirst, begs for food, but is refused by the householder or if he creates some obstruction to give him the food, he also is termed as the killer of the Brahmana. The usurping of riches, kidnapping of a man or a woman, elephant, horse, a cow, the land, silver, gems, medicines, sandalwood, agaru, musk of a deer, the garments and the trust money, are the crimes equivalent to the stealing of the gold.

## \|\| 3.5.14-23 \|\|

*kṣuttṛṭsaṃtaptadehānāṃ dvijānāṃ bhoktumicchatām \|*  
*samācarati yo vighnaṃ tamāhurbrahmaghātakam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*piśunaḥ sarvalokānāṃ chidrānveṣaṇatatparaḥ \|*  
*udvegajananaḥ krūraḥ sa caiva brahmahā smṛtaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*gavāṃ tṛṣṇābhibhūtānāṃ jalārthamupasarpatām \|*  
*samācarati yo vighnaṃ sa caiva brahmahā smṛtaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*paradoṣamabhijñāya nṛpakarṇe karoti yaḥ \|*  
*pāpīyānpiśunaḥ kṣudraḥ sa caiva brahmahā smṛtaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*devadvijagavāṃ bhūmiṃ pūrvabhuktā harettu yaḥ \|*  
*pranaṣṭāmapi kālena tamāhurbrahmaghātakam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*dvijavittāpaharaṇe nyāyataḥ samupārjite \|*  
*brahmahatyā samaṃ jñeyaṃ pātakaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*agnihotraparityāgo yastu yājñikakarmaṇām \|*  
*mātāpitṛparityāgaḥ kūṭasākṣyaṃ suhṛdvadhaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*gavāṃ mārge vane cāgniṃ pure grāme ca dīpayet \|*  
*iti pāpāni ghorāṇi surāpānasamāni tu \|\| 21 \|\|*

*hīnasvaharaṇe cāpi narastrīgajavājinām \|*  
*gobhūrajataratnānāmauṣadhīnāṃ rajasya ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*caṃdanāgarukarpūrakastūrīkhaṇḍavāsasām \|*  
*haste nyasyāpaharaṇaṃ rukmasteyasamaṃ smṛtam \|\| 23 \|\|*

14-23. One who indulges in back biting of one and all, or is in the habit of finding fault with others, incites others, is of cruel nature, or obstructs a thirsty cow moving for the drinking of water, those who complain to the king learning about the faults of others, those who usurp the land given for the use of the Brahmanas, gods and the cows and the one who gets destroyed in a short time or the one who steals the riches of a Brahmana which had been earned by him by judicious means, he is to be termed as the killer of the Brahmana. There is no doubt about it. Those who stop the performing of Agnihotra and yajna, disown the parents, give false evidence in the court, kill the frien , cows, elephants, besides burning fire in a forest, a city, a village, all of them earn the sin of drinking of wine.

## \|\| 3.5.24-25 \|\|

*kanyānāṃ varayogyānāmadānaṃ sadṛśe vare \|*  
*putramitrakalatreṣu gamanaṃ bhaginīṣu ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kumārīsāhasaṃ ghoramantyajastrīniṣevaṇam \|*  
*avarṇāyāśca gamanaṃ gurutalpasamaṃ smṛtam \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. When a girl of marriageable age is not given over to her groom, union with the daughter-in-law, the wife of a friend or a sister, taking liberty with the unmarкшed girls, union with a low caste woman, or a woman fallen from her caste, are the sins equivalent to the uniting of a person with the wife oа a preceptor.

## \|\| 3.5.26 \|\|

*mahāpātakatulyāni pāpānyuktāni yāni tu \|*  
*tāni pātakasaṃjñāni tadvadāmyupapātakam \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. Thus, I have talked about the grave sins and those equivalents to the same. Now, I am talking about the inferior sins.

## \|\| 3.5.27 \|\|

*dvijārthaṃ ca pratijñāya na prayacchati yaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tasmānnarapate vighnatulyaṃ tadupapātakam \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. O lord of the people, when a word is given to a Brahmana, which is denied later on, it is said to be an inferior sin. The violation of the religious tradition by a Brahmana is also a minor sin.

## \|\| 3.5.28-44 \|\|

*dvijadravyāpaharaṇaṃ maryādāyā vyatikramaḥ \|*  
*atikopaśca mānaśca dāṃbhikatvaṃ kṛtaghnatā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*atyaṃtaviṣayāsaktiḥ kārpaṇyaṃ śreṣṭhamatsaraḥ \|*  
*paradārāpaharaṇaṃ sādhukanyāvidūṣaṇam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*parivittiḥ parīvettā yayā ca parividyate \|*  
*tayorddānaṃ ca kanyāyāstayoreva ca yājanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*putramitrakalatrāṇāmabhāve svāminastathā \|*  
*śiṣṭānāṃ caiva saṃnyāsaḥ sahajānāṃ tapasvinām \|\| 31 \|\|*

*bhaṃgaśca dharmakṛtyānāṃ sahāyānāṃ vināśanam \|*  
*pīḍāmāśramasaṃsthānānnācarettvalpikāmapi \|\| 32 \|\|*

*svabhṛtyaparivargasya paśudhānyadhanasya ca \|*  
*kupyadhānyapaśusteyamayācyānāṃ ca yācanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*gavāṃ kṣatriyaveśyānāṃ strīśūdrāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*yajñārāmataḍāgānāṃ dārāpatyasya vikrayaḥ \|*  
*tīrthayātropavāsānāṃ vratāyatanakarmaṇām \|\| 34 \|\|*

*strīdhanānyupajīvaṃti strībhiratyaṃtanirjitāḥ \|*  
*arakṣaṇaṃ ca nārīṇāṃ madyapastrīniṣevaṇam \|\| 35 \|\|*

*ṛṇānāmapradānaṃ ca dhānyavṛddhyupajīvinām \|*  
*niṃditācca dhanādānamapaṇyānāṃ ca vikrayaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*viṣamāraṇamaṃtrāṇāṃ prayogo mūlakarmaṇām \|*  
*uccāṭanāvicāraśca garavidveṣaṇakriyā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*jihvāsamupabhogārthaṃ yasyārambhaḥ svakarmasu \|*  
*mūlyenādhyāpayedyaśca mūlyenādhīyate ca ye \|\| 38 \|\|*

*vrātyatā vratasaṃtyāgaḥ sarvāhāraniṣevaṇam \|*  
*asaddārābhigamanaṃ śuṣkatarkāvalaṃbanam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*devāgnisādhusādhvīnāṃ niṃdā gobrāhmaṇasya ca \|*  
*pratyakṣaṃ vā parokṣaṃ vā rājñāṃ maṇḍalikāmapi \|*  
*duḥśīlā nāstikāḥ pāpāḥ sarvaśūnyasya vādinaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*parvakāle divā caiva viyonau paśuyoniṣu \|*  
*rajasvalānāṃ yonau ca maithunaṃ ca samācaret \|\| 41 \|\|*

*strīputramitrasaṃprīte grāsānnacchedakāśca ye \|*  
*janasyā priyavaktāro dhūrtāḥ samayabhedinaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*bhettā taḍāgacakrāṇāṃ saṃkramāṇāṃ rathasya ca \|*  
*ekapaṃktisthitānāṃ ca pākabhedaṃ karoti yaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

*ityetaiste narāḥ pāpairupapātakinaḥ smṛtāḥ \|*  
*yuktāstadūnakaiḥ kṣudraiḥ pāpaiḥ pāpatarāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

28-44. Usurping the wealth of a Brahmana, the violation of the religious tradition, to become extremely angry, to become proudy, deceitfulness, ungratefulness, excess of sex with a woman, miserliness, to be envious with the elders, kidnapping of other’s wife, making a girl inauspicious, to marry the younger girl when the elder girl is still unwed, or make her participate in the performing of the yajna, to desecrate the wives of the sons in the absence of their husbands, to torture the noble ascetics or the disciples in the performing of the religious activities, even to slightly torture the sages of the asrama, to usurp the riches of one’s own servant or his animals, to beg from an unsuitable person, to sell the cows; Ksatriyas, whores and the Sudras particularly those who are engaged in yajnas, selling of the wife or the son, who proceed to pilgrimage, who perform all the vratas observing all the rules, the one who makes the living out of the riches of the wife, one who is defeated by the wife, one who canno protect the wife, one who unites with a woman who drinks wine, one who does not repay the loan taken by him, one who cannot protect the woman, one who makes a living by the increase of cereals, the one who receives the money from a degraded person, one who sells the household goods, one who uses the poison, mantra for killing of others, one who possesses polluted ideas, to work for the pleasing of one’s own tongue, to import education in lieu of the wealth, one who is of hybrid birth and has discarded performing the vratas, one who consumes all types of eatables, one who unites with a degraded woman, one who enters into useless discussion, one who denounce the Devas, ascetics, auspicious woman, the cow, Brahmana. besides the king of the entire region openly or secretly, one who is not noble, an unbeliever, sinful, one who denounces all at the time of festivities, one who unites with woman during the day or with animals or the woman in period, one who destroys the morsel of a woman, his son and the friend, the one who is unpopular orator, wicked, creates differences at all the times, the one who breaks the tank or the wheel of the moving chariot, one who creates differences among the people who are seated in the same time, are the deeds which fall under the category of the minor sins. Such a person is said to be a minor sinner. There arc other sinners, who commit still smaller or petty sins.

## \|\| 3.5.45 \|\|

*ye gobrāhmaṇakanyānāṃ svāmimitratapasvinām \|*  
*aṃtaraṃ yāṃti kāryeṣu te narā nārakāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. They happen to those who committ petty sins like creating obstructions in the activities of cows, Brahmana girls, master, friend and the ascetics. Such persons have been described as Narakis or those heading for the hell.

## \|\| 3.5.46-60 \|\|

*paraśriyā ye tapyaṃte ye paradravyasūcakāḥ \|*  
*paravyāpāraniratāḥ parastrīnaradūṣakāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*dvijāya duḥkhaṃ yaḥ kuryātprakārairbahubhiḥ sadā \|*  
*sevate yo dvijaḥ śūdrāṃ surāṃ jighrati kāmataḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*ye pānābhiratāḥ krūrā ye ca hiṃsāpriyā narāḥ \|*  
*vittārthaṃ ye ca kurvaṃti dānayajñādikāṃ kriyām \|\| 48 \|\|*

*goṣṭhāgnijalarathyāsu tarucchāyāmaṭheṣu ca \|*  
*tyajaṃtyamedhyaṃ puruṣā ārāmāyataneṣu ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

*madyapānaratā nityaṃ gānavādyaratā narāḥ \|*  
*kelīkalābhujaṃgāśca raṃdhrānveṣaṇatatparāḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*vaṃśeṣu kāśakāṣṭhaiśca śubhaiḥ śaṃkubhireva vā \|*  
*ye mārgānsamupaghnaṃti parastrīrāharaṃti ca \|\| 51 \|\|*

*kūṭaśāsanahartāraḥ kūṭakarmakriyāratāḥ \|*  
*kūṭayuddhāśca śastreṇa kūṭasaṃvyavahāriṇaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*dhanuṣāṃ śalyaśastrāṇāṃ yaḥ kartā yaśca vikrayī \|*  
*nirdayo'tīva bhṛtyeṣu paśūnāṃ damakaśca yaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*mithyā pravadato vākyamākarṇayati yaḥ śanaiḥ \|*  
*svāmimitragurudrohī māyāvī capalaḥ śaṭhaḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*ye bhāryāputramitrāṇi bālavṛddhakṛśāturān \|*  
*bhṛtyānatithibandhūṃśca prabādhante bubhukṣayā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*yaḥ svayaṃ miṣṭamaśnāti viprāyānyatprayacchati \|*  
*vṛthāpākaḥ sa vijñeyo brahmavādiṣu garhitaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*niyamānsvayamādāya ye tyajaṃtyajiteṃdriyāḥ \|*  
*pravrajyāvāsino ye ca rahasyānāṃ ca bhedakāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*tāḍayaṃti ca vegādye śapaṃti ca muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*durbalāṃśca na puṣṇaṃti punastānvāhayaṃti ca \|\| 58 \|\|*

*pīḍayaṃtyatibhāreṇa sakṣatānvāhayaṃti ca \|*  
*sārddhayāmāduparitaḥ saṃyukteṣu ca bhuṃjate \|\| 59 \|\|*

*ye bhagnakṣatarogārtānsvagorūpānbubhukṣayā \|*  
*na pālayaṃti yatnena te goptā nārakā narāḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

46-60. Those who feel jealous by observing the wealth of other people, those who talk about the wealth of others here and there, those who patronize the caste and dharma of others, those who pollute the wives of others, besides those who tease the Brahmanas variously, those who drink wine, unite with the Sudra women, patronize the cruel torture, those who out of greed for wealth, perform the yajnas and other religious practices, besides who pollute the cowpeтs, the fire, water, the tree branches and the shades of the trees, besides polluting the hermitages, orchards, the temples, those drinking wine daily and singing and playing on musical instruments, those who are the destroyers of the sports, search the loopholes of others, fix the bamboo or wood to obstruct the path, those who kidnap the wives of others, the destroyers of the destroyers of the false rulers, those who keep on performing the cruel deeds, those who resort to falsehood by quoting the false scriptures, those who make the bows and other weapons and sell them, who are cruel over their servants, are cruel on the animals, who listen to the people indulging in falsehood, quite slowly who prove untrue to friends and the preceptors, those who are illusory, talkative, wicked, those who upset the wives, friends, children as well as the aged persons, the servants, the guests and the relatives, starving them at the same time, those do not give sweets to the Brahmanas, but consume them themselves. Inspite of following all the rules, they lose control over the sense organs, there are the recluses who inspite of their being so, they live at one place for long time, they unfold the secrets, and pronounce the curses repeatedly, inspite of punishing repeatedly with force, they pronounce the curses repeatedly. Instead of feeding the weak people, they instead load them with excessive burden. Inspite of their having performed their duty for long, they do not relive them for rest, those who take food after a prahara and a half, they get shattered, ailing, they also do not give the fodder to the cows in time. Such people have also been termed as those belonging to the hell.

## \|\| 3.5.61 \|\|

*vṛṣāṇāṃ vṛṣaṇānyeva pāpiṣṭhā gālayaṃti ye \|*  
*vāhayaṃti ca gāṃ vadhyāṃ te mahānārakāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

61\. Those who take out the testicles of the bulls and piercing the nose of the cows who load them with burden, are known as the people who belong to the hell.

## \|\| 3.5.62 \|\|

*āśramaṃ samanuprāptaṃ kṣuttṛṣṇāśramapīḍitam \|*  
*ye'tithiṃ nābhimanyaṃte te vai nirayagāminaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

62\. When a guest suffering from hunger and thirst arrives in an asrama, those, who do not serve him, proceed surely to the hell.

## \|\| 3.5.63 \|\|

*anāthaṃ vikalaṃ dīnaṃ bālaṃ vṛddhaṃ kṛśāturam \|*  
*nānukaṃpaṃti ye mūḍhāste yānti nirayārṇavam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Those who are not kind to orphans, upset ones, poor, children, old people and ones who are lean and thin, they are the fools and fall in the hell.

## \|\| 3.5.64 \|\|

*ajāviko māhiṣikaḥ sāmudro vṛṣalīpatiḥ \|*  
*śūdraviṭkṣatravṛttiśca nārakī syāddvijādhamaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Those of the Brahmanas who employ the sheep, goats, buffaloes, those who go on sea voyage, marry the Sudra woman, and take to the jobs of the Ksatriyas or the Vaisyas or the Sudras, are surely the degraded ones and fall in the hell.

## \|\| 3.5.65 \|\|

*śilpinaḥ kārukā vaidyā hemakārā naṭā dvijāḥ \|*  
*kṛtakaukṣeya sayuktāstathānye nārakāḥ smṛtāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

65\. The artisans, the masons, the physicians, the goldsmiths and those who resort to performing dance to fill their bellies, they surely fall in the hell.

## \|\| 3.5.66 \|\|

*yaścoditamatikramya svecchayā vā haretkaram \|*  
*narake tu sa pacyeta yaśca daṃḍarucirbhavet \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Those who discard all the rules and move as per their own wish and those who are interested in giving punishment, they keep on boiling in the hell.

## \|\| 3.5.67-68 \|\|

*utkocakairadhikṛtaistaskaraiśca prapīḍyate \|*  
*yasya rājñaḥ prajā ruṣṭā pacyate narakeṣu saḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*ye dvijāḥ pratigṛhṇaṃti nṛpasyānyāyavartinaḥ \|*  
*prayāṃti tepi ghorāṇi narakāṇi na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. Those, who during their life time, accepting bricks, always suffer from the offices as well as the thieves, similarly, a king whose people remain always dissatisfied with him, then that king as well as those Brahmanas who accept the charities of such a king, fall in the terrific hell, facing the torture there. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.5.69-70 \|\|

*pāradārikacaurāṇāṃ yatpāpaṃ pārthivasya tat \|*  
*bhavedarakṣatastasmādghorastasya pratigrahaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*acauraṃ cauravatpaśyeccoraṃ vā'caurarūpavat \|*  
*avicārya nṛpastasmāddhātayannarakaṃ vrajet \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. Like a person who steals the wife of others, he earns the sin no doubt, but the king of the place also has to share the related sin as well, because he is unable to govern the people well. Therefore, accepting of the charities from him is totally prohibited. A king, who thoughtlessly makes an honest person a thief and a thief an honest, and punishes accordingly, he proceeds to the hell.

## \|\| 3.5.71-74 \|\|

*ghṛtatailānnapānāni madhumāṃsasurāsavam \|*  
*guḍekṣukṣāraśākāni dadhimūlaphalāni ca \|\| 71 \|\|*

*tṛṇaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ puṣpapatramauṣadhaṃ kāṃsyabhājanam \|*  
*upānacchatraśakaṭamāsanaṃ śayanāṃbaram \|\| 72 \|\|*

*tāmraṃ sīsaṃ trapuṃ kācaṃ śaṃkhādyaṃ ca jalodbhavam \|*  
*vārkṣaṃ vā vaiṇavādyaṃ vā gṛheṣūpaskarāṇi ca \|\| 73 \|\|*

*ūrṇākārpāsakauśeyabhaṃgapaṭṭodbhavāni ca \|*  
*sthūlasūkṣmāṇi vastrāṇi ye ca lobhāddharaṃti ca \|\| 74 \|\|*

71-74. The persons who steal the food cooked in ghi or the oil, consume drinks and meat or juices, sugarcane balls, sugarcane, saltish things, vegetables, curd, the basic fruit, straw, wood, milk, leaves, bronze vases, the shoes, umbrellas, or sleeping in a vehicle, copper, lead, zinc, glass, conch and other aquatic things, the musical instruments made of wood or bamboos, the wooden, silk, cotton textiles, which could be quite fine or thick or any other things, surely falls in the hell.

## \|\| 3.5.75-78 \|\|

*evamādīni cānyāni dravyāṇi vividhāni ca \|*  
*narakāṇi dhruvaṃ yāṃti narā vā nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

*yadvā tadvā paradravyamapi sarṣapamātrakam \|*  
*apahṛtya naro yāti narakaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

*evamādyai्rnaraḥ pāpairutkrāṃteḥ samanaṃtaram \|*  
*śarīraṃ yātanārthāya pūrvākāramavāpnuyāt \|\| 77 \|\|*

*yamalokaṃ vrajettena śarīreṇa yamājñayā \|*  
*yamadūtairmahāghorairnīyamānaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

75-78. A person, who steals the salt as well as mustard seeds or other things, surely falls in the hell. Similarly, those who commit other types of sins, they discarding the present body, achieve another body and travel to the place of Yama with the same (changed) body. Thereafter, at the command of Yama, the messengers of Yama severely punish the said person.

## \|\| 3.5.79 \|\|

*tiryaṅmānuṣadehānāmadharmaniratātmanām \|*  
*dharmarājaḥ smṛtaḥ śāstā sughorairvividhairvadhaiḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. The humans and the birds having the bodies, who are engaged in the committing ol the crimes, are variously punished by Dharmaraja.

## \|\| 3.5.80 \|\|

*vinayācārayuktānāṃ pramādātskhalitātmanām \|*  
*prāyaścitterguruḥ śāstā na ca tairdṛśyate yamaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

80\. Those who are quite humble and follow the good conduct when indulge in improper manner out of pride, for them the punishment is said to be prescribed by their preceptors for repentance.

## \|\| 3.5.81 \|\|

*pāradārikacaurāṇāmanyāyavyavahāriṇām \|*  
*nṛpatiḥ śāsakasteṣāṃ pracchannānāṃ ca dharmarāṭ \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. When it is so done, they do not have to suffer at the hands of Yama. The king is their controller. For one who enjoys the wives of others, the king is the Dharmaraja for such a person invisibly.

## \|\| 3.5.82 \|\|

*tasmātkṛtasya pāpasya prāyaścittaṃ samācaret \|*  
*nābhuktasyānyathā nāśaḥ kalpakoṭiśatairapi \|\| 82 \|\|*

82\. Therefore, a person must do repentance for the crimes or sins committed by him, because without such a repentance, such a person cannot be redeemed even in the crores of the kalpas.

## \|\| 3.5.83 \|\|

*yaḥ karoti svayaṃ karma kārayedvāpi moda yet \|*  
*kāyena manasā vācā tasya cādhogatiḥ phalam \|\| 83 \|\|*

83\. One who commits a sin mentally, by speech or physically or supports the crimes of others, he surely achieves the degraded position.

## \|\| 3.5.84 \|\|

*iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktāḥ pāpabhedāḥ sasādhanāḥ \|*  
*kathyate gatayaścitrā narāṇāṃ pāpakarmaṇām \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. Thus, I have narrated to you the divisions of the sins and the sources for the same. Now, I shall speak about the condition of the sinful people.

## \|\| 3.5.85 \|\|

*vākkāyacittajanitairbahubhedabhinnaiḥ kṛtyaiḥ \|*  
*śubhāśubhaphalodayahetubhūtaiḥ bhāsvatsureśabhuvanaṃ \|*  
*narakānanekānsaṃprāpnuvaṃti manujā manujeṃdracandra \|\| 85 \|\|*

85\. Thereafter, Yudhisthira said- “O Indra among the humans, the auspicious or inauspicious deeds committed mentally, by speech or physically and the divisions thereof, have been spoken by you, with the committing of such sins, the people have to fall in the terrific hells.”

## Chapter 6. Reward of the auspicious and inauspicious deeds

## \|\| 3.6.1-3 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*athaibhiḥ pātakairyāṃti yamalokaṃ caturvidhaiḥ \|*  
*saṃtrāsajananaṃ ghoraṃ vivaśāḥ sarvadehinaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*garbhasthairjāyamānaiśca bālaistaruṇamadhyamaiḥ \|*  
*puṃstrīnapuṃsakairvṛddhairjñātavyaṃ sarvajaṃtubhiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*śubhāśubhaphalaṃ tatra dehināṃ pravicāryate \|*  
*citraguptādibhiḥ sabhyairmadhyasthaiḥ sarvadarśibhiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Sri Krsna said- All the people having been compelled by four types of sins, achieve the extremely painful hells. The assessment of the deeds or misdeeds performed by the men, women, eunuchs as well as the old people after their birth from the womb, the good or bad deeds committed by them during childhood, and youthful age are weighed by the judges like Citragupta and others, who happen to be quite civilized and impartial.

## \|\| 3.6.4-5 \|\|

*na te'tra prāṇinaḥ saṃti ye na yāṃti yamakṣayam \|*  
*avaśyaṃ hi kṛtaṃ karma bhoktavyaṃ tadvidhāritam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tatra ye śubhakarmāṇaḥ saumyacittā dayānvitāḥ \|*  
*te narā yāṃti saumyena pathā yamaniketanam \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. No one is born on earth who does not have to reach the abode of Yama, because one has to face the result of the deeds performed by him. Those who perform the auspicious deeds and possess the noble heart, they travel to the Yamaloka by the pleasant path.

## \|\| 3.6.6 \|\|

*yaḥ pradadyāddvijendrāṇāmupānatkāṣṭhapādukām \|*  
*sa varāśvena mahatā sukhaṃ yāti yamālayam \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. Those who give the shoes or the wooden sandals to the Brahmanas, they riding on the beautiful horses, move towards the Yamaloka, with comforts.

## \|\| 3.6.7-9 \|\|

*chatradānena gacchaṃti yathā chatreṇa dehinaḥ \|*  
*divyavastraparīdhānā yāṃti vastrapradāyinaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*śibikāśvapradānena tatastena sukhaṃ vrajet \|*  
*śayyāsana pradānena sukhaṃ yāṃti yamāśrayam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ārāmakartā chāyāsu śītalāsu sukhaṃ vrajet \|*  
*yāṃti puṣpakayānena puṣpārāmapradāyinaḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Those who give away in charity the umbrellas, the costumes, they travel in palanquin, and those who give away a horse in charity, they reach the place of Yama with comfort. Those who give away a bed or a seat in charity besides the orchards, providing the cool shade to the people and also give away the sandals, they are taken to the abode of Yama with great respect.

## \|\| 3.6.10-11 \|\|

*devāyatanakartā ca yatīnāmāśramasya ca \|*  
*anāthamaṃḍapānāṃ ca krīḍanyāti gṛhottamaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*devāgniguruviprāṇāṃ mātāpitrośca pūjakāḥ \|*  
*pūjyamānā narā yāṃti kāmikena pathā sukham \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Those who build the temples, hermitages for the poors and helpless people and playfully make the abodes of the gods or the temples for the gods, fire, the Brahmanas and worship the parents, they get respected and are honorably carried through a noble path.

## \|\| 3.6.12 \|\|

*dyotayaṃto diśaḥ sarvā yāṃti dīpapradāyinaḥ \|*  
*pratiśrayapradānena sukhaṃ yāṃti gṛhaṃ svayam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. The giving away of the lamps or providing shelter to the deserving people, such people, illuminating all the directions, move comfortably as if moving in their ov/n houses.

## \|\| 3.6.13-15 \|\|

*sarva kāmasamṛddhena pathā gacchaṃti gopradāḥ \|*  
*ye na pāpāni kurvaṃti te tṛptā yāṃti nānyathā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ārtauṣadhapradātāraḥ sukhaṃ yāṃti nirākulāḥ \|*  
*viśrāmyamāṇā gacchaṃti guruśuśrūṣaṇe ratāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*pādaśaucapradānena śītalena pathā vrajet \|*  
*pādābhyaṃgaṃ ca yaḥ kuryādaśvapṛṣṭhena sa vrajet \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Those who give away the cows in charity, they move by the path in which all the desires are fulfilled. They reach their quite contented. Those who distribute free medicines to the poor, or those who surely serve the preceptors, etc., and travel while taking rest, they move by the way by which the water for the washing of the feet is found available. The Brahmanas get all for application over their feet. They move riding over the horses. Those who serve the cool water to the people, move by the most comfortable path.

## \|\| 3.6.16-21 \|\|

*hemaratnapradānena yāti durgāṇi nistaran \|*  
*yānavāhanadānena narayānena gacchati \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sarvakāmasamṛddhātmā bhūmidānena gacchati \|*  
*annapānapradānena pibankhādaṃśca gacchati \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ityevamādibhirdānaiḥ sukhaṃ yāṃti yamakṣayam \|*  
*svargepi vipulānbhogānprāpnuvaṃti narottama \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sarveṣāmeva dānānāmannadānaṃ paraṃ smṛtam \|*  
*sadyaḥ prītikaraṃ divyaṃ balabuddhivivarddhanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*trayāṇāmapi lokānāṃ jīvitaṃ hyudakaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*pavitramamṛtaṃ divyaṃ śuddhaṃ sarvarasāyanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*annaṃ pānaṃ ca govastrabhūśayyācchatramāsanam \|*  
*paraloke praśastāni dānānyaṣṭau viśeṣataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

16-21. Those who donate jewels and the vehicles, they move riding over a beautiful vehicle. One who donates land, has all his desires fulfilled; those who donate food, reach their enjoying eatables on the way. O best of the humans, thus, by giving away the charities, after completing the journey to the place of Yama comfortably, the people reach the heaven and enjoy enormous pleasures of all the charities. The giving away of the food is the best, because it suddenly increases love, divine strength and intelligence. The water is said to be the life in all the three worlds, which is quite auspicious, nectar like, pure and the essence of all the juices. In the realm of the donation of food, the cooked food, betel, cow, costumes, land, bed, umbrella and the seat are the eight types of charities, which are said to be praiseworthy.

## \|\| 3.6.22 \|\|

*annadānaṃ viśeṣeṇa dharma rājapure narāḥ \|*  
*yasmādyāṃti sukhenaiva tasmāddharmaṃ samācaret \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Particularly with the giving away of the food, a person arrives comfortably in the place of Dharmaraja. Therefore, this particular type of dharma viz., giving away of food must be performed.

## \|\| 3.6.23 \|\|

*ye punaḥ krūrakarmāṇaḥ pāpā dānavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*te ghoreṇa pathā yāṃti dakṣiṇena svamālayam \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. The people, who are cruel and sinful, they travel to the abode of Yama, by the southern path and reach Yamaloka.

## \|\| 3.6.24-25 \|\|

*ṣaḍaśītisahasrāṇi yojanānāmatītya yat \|*  
*vaivasvatapuraṃ jñeyaṃ nānārūpavyavasthitam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*samīpasthamivābhāti narāṇāṃ śubhakarmaṇām \|*  
*pāpānāmatidūrasthaṃ pathā raudreṇa gacchatām \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. At a distance of eighty six yojanas from this place, one reaches the well organized part of the place of Yama which is quite close for the people who perform the noble deeds. The sinful people who move by the horrible path, it looks as if at a far off distance.

## \|\| 3.6.26 \|\|

*tīvrakaṃṭakayuktena śarkarānicitena ca \|*  
*kṣuradhārānibhaistīvraiḥ pāṣāṇairnicitena ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. On the path of the sinful persons, they come across sharp thorns, sandy ground. At places, the ground has sharp edged stones leaped together.

## \|\| 3.6.27-28 \|\|

*kvacitpaṃkena mahatā duruttāraiśca khātakaiḥ \|*  
*lohasūcīnibhairdarbhaiḥ saṃchannena pathā kvacit \|\| 27 \|\|*

*taṭaprapātaviṣṭaṃbhaiḥ parvatairvṛkṣasaṃkulaiḥ \|*  
*prataptāṃgārayuktena yāṃti mārgeṇa duḥkhitāḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. At places, there are muddy swamps and at places one finds the kusa grass with needle like sharp edges. At places, the path is obstructed with the fall of rocks obstructing flow of water from the river. At places, the path is obstructed with thick trees. At places, the road is full of burning coal, which make the walking there quite painful.

## \|\| 3.6.29-40 \|\|

*kvacidviṣamagartaiśca kvacilloṣṭaiḥ supicchilaiḥ \|*  
*prataptavālukābhiśca tathā tīkṣṇaiśca śaṃkubhiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*anekatāpairvitatairvyāptaṃ vaṃśavanaṃ kvacit \|*  
*kvacidvālukayā vyāptaṃ kaṣṭenaiva praveśanam \|\| 30 \|\|*

*kvaciduṣṇāṃbunā vyāptaṃ kvacitkārīṣavahninā \|*  
*kvacitsiṃhairvṛkairvyāptaṃ daṃśaiḥ kīṭaiśca dāruṇaiḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kvacinmahājalaukābhiḥ kvaciccājagaraiḥ punaḥ \|*  
*makṣikābhiśca raudrābhiḥ kvacitsarpairviṣolbaṇaiḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*mattamātaṃgayūthaiśca balonmattaiḥ pramāthibhiḥ \|*  
*paṃthānamullikhadbhiśca tīkṣṇaśṛṃgairmahāvṛṣaiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*mahāviṣāṇairmahiṣairuṣṭrairmattaiśca khādakaiḥ \|*  
*ḍākinībhiśca raudrābhirvikarālaiśca rākṣasaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vyādhibhiśca mahāghoraiḥ pīḍyamānā vrajaṃti ca \|*  
*mahādhūlīvimiśreṇa mahācaṇḍena vāyunā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*mahāpāṣāṇavarṣeṇa hanyamānā nirāśrayāḥ \|*  
*kvacidvidyutprapātena dīryamāṇā vrajaṃti ca \|\| 36 \|\|*

*mahatā bāṇavarṣeṇa vidhyamānāśca sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*patadbhirvajrasaṃghātairulkāpātaiśca dāruṇaiḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*prataptāgāravarṣeṇa dahyamānā vrajaṃti ca \|*  
*taptena pāṃśuvarṣeṇa pūryamāṇā rudaṃti ca \|\| 38 \|\|*

*mahāmegharavairghorairvitrāsyaṃte muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*niśitāyudhavarṣeṇa cūryamāṇā narairvṛtāḥ \|*  
*mahākṣārāmbudhārābhiḥ sicyamānā dravaṃti ca \|\| 39 \|\|*

*mahāśītena marutā tīkṣṇena paruṣeṇa ca \|*  
*samaṃtātpīḍyamānāste śuṣyaṃte saṃkucaṃti ca \|\| 40 \|\|*

29-40. At places, there are terrific pits, slippery soil, the burning sand, sharp thorns and the bamboo forests, which cause immense pain. At places, one has to enter the hot water (springs), at some other places one faces the terrible fire. Some places are infested with the wild animals like lions, wolves, the terrible germs, which obstruct the path. At places one finds terrific leeches, pythons, the terrific carnivores, poisonous serpents, intoxicated wild elephants, digging the earth with their strong tusks, which obstructs the path of the bulls. At places, one finds the male buffaloes with huge horns. At times one finds the wild female robbers, the horrible demons. Then suffering from horrible ailments, covered with dust, facing the rain of stones, with blowing of the forceful winds, the traveler has no means of escape. Becoming shelterless with the fall of lightning, the travelers feels injured and painful. At places, the soul has the rain of stones over it which injures all his limbs, causing extreme pain. At places, the person has to face the shower of sharp arrows, as a result of which all his limbs feel painful. At places, he is injured with the comets or the vajras. At places, he is burnt with fire flames. Having been burnt with the heated sand, he starts crying, he gets terrified with thunder of the clouds while walking. He moves forward with the attack of the terrific weapons. T 1 hereafter, getting soaked with the waves of the saline water, he has to face the terrific cold and sharp winds which shatter the limbs of the body. As a result of which all his limbsi are squeezed.

## \|\| 3.6.41-43 \|\|

*itthaṃ mārgeṇa raudreṇa pāṃthairvi rahitena ca \|*  
*nirālaṃbena durgeṇa nirjalena samaṃtataḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*aviśrāmeṇa mahatā nirgatāpāśrayeṇa ca \|*  
*tamorūpeṇa kaṣṭena sarvaduḥkhāśrayeṇa ca \|\| 42 \|\|*

*nīyaṃte dehinaḥ sarve ye mūḍhāḥ pāpakarmiṇaḥ \|*  
*yamadūtairmahāghoraistadājñākāribhirbalāt \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. In this way, by travelling over the dangerous path, where no eatable could be found on the way, crossing the shelterless fort, having no place for shelter or the water tanks, the path which is full o f darkness, the sinful person is carried by the dangerous messengers of Yam a, who are horrible to look at. At that point of time, the commands of those messengers have to be obeyed per force, because the jiva is alone there and there is no one to help him.

## \|\| 3.6.44 \|\|

*ekākinaḥ parādhīnā mitrabaṃdhuvivarjitāḥ \|*  
*śocaṃtaḥ svāni karmāṇi rudaṃtaśca muhurmuhuḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Even he is discarded by the friend i s as well as the kiths and kins. Reaching there, he feels painful for the evil deeds performed by him and cries out again and again.

## \|\| 3.6.45-47 \|\|

*pretabhūtā vivastrāśca śuṣkakaṇṭhoṣṭhatālukāḥ \|*  
*kṛśāṅgā bhītabhītāśca dahyamānāḥ kṣudhāgninā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*baddhāḥ śṛṃkhalayā keciduttānāḥ pādayornarāḥ \|*  
*ākṛṣyaṃte ghṛṣyamāṇā yamadūtairbalotkaṭaiḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*punaścādhomukhāścānye ghṛṣyamāṇāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ \|*  
*keśapāśanibaddhāśca kṛṣyaṃte rajjubhirnarāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

45-47. At that point of time, he remains in the form of a goblin, with no clothes on his body. His neck, lips and palate dry up. He being quite lean and thin, feels extremely fearful, and suffers from hunger. He is hung upside down by binding his feet with cha ins. The powerful messengers of Yama frighten some of the people there by dragging then at the same time. By so doing, the person has to suffer immensely. The rope is tied to the hair of the head of someone and he is dragged on I the ground.

## \|\| 3.6.48-52 \|\|

*lalāṭe cāṃkuśaistīkṣṇairbhinnāḥ kṛṣyaṃti dehinaḥ \|*  
*uttānā raṭamānāśca kvacidaṃgāravartmanā \|\| 48 \|\|*

*pāścādbāhvaṃsabaddhāśca jaṭhare ca prapīḍitāḥ \|*  
*pūritāḥ śṛṃkhalābhiśca hastayośca prakīlitāḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*grīvāyāmarddhacandreṇa kṣipyamāṇā itastataḥ \|*  
*śiśne ca vṛṣaṇe baddhvā nīyaṃte carmarajjunā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*vibhinnā udare cānye taptaśṛṃkhalayā narāḥ \|*  
*kṛṣyaṃte karṇayoścānye bhinnāśca cibukopari \|\| 51 \|\|*

*chinnāgrapādahastāśca chinnakarṇauṣṭhanāsikāḥ \|*  
*saṃchinnaśiśnavṛṣaṇāśchinnabhinnāṃgasaṃdhayaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

48-52. The sharp goads are pierced into the forehead of some of them. Some of them are dragged while lying supine as a result of which they cry aloud. Sometimes, he is placed over the burning coal. The hands of some of them are bound, causing excessive pain. Some of them are bound with a chain and the nails are fixed in the hands. Then inserting a hand in his mouth, the chest is dragged, here and there. The linga and testicles of some of them are tightly bound with leather and they are then dragged. The belly of some is torned out with a heated chain. Someone is dragged severing his nose. The chin, hands, ears, lips and the nose are severed. The linga and testicles of someone are cut off, while the joints of someone are dismembered and then they are tortured with spears, arrows and dragged. When the limbs are shattered, with the use of the weapons, he cries aloud. Feeling helpless, he runs here and there, but the messengers of Yama at that point of time, beat him with clubs of iron and the rods again and agai

## \|\| 3.6.53 \|\|

*pratudyamānāḥ kuṃtaiśca sāyakaiśca tatastataḥ \|*  
*bhidyamānāḥ pradhāvaṃti krandamānā nirāśrayāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. Someone is beaten with the iron lashes or is hurt with bhindapalas as a result of which the streams of puss and blood start flowing from his body.

## \|\| 3.6.54-57 \|\|

*mudgarairllohadaṇḍaiśca hanyamānā muhurmuhuḥ \|*  
*kaśaiśca vividhaighorairjvalitāgnisamaprabhaiḥ \|\| 54 \|\|*

*bhiṃdipālairvibhidyaṃte sravaṃtaḥ pūyaśoṇitam \|*  
*māṃse kṣatāśca kṛmibhirnīyaṃte vivaśā narāḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*yācamānāśca salilamannaṃ cāpi bubhukṣitāḥ \|*  
*chāyāṃ prārthayamānāśca śītārtā bahuvāyunā \|\| 56 \|\|*

*dānahīnāḥ prayāṃtyevaṃ yāvaṃto vimukhā narāḥ \|*  
*gṛhītadānapātheyāḥ sukhaṃ yāṃti yamālayam \|\| 57 \|\|*

54-57. Someone’s flesh is cut off and then beaten with the lashes. One getting upset with thirst and suffer from hunger and the jiva asks for food and water again and again. Similarly, he, suffering from cold and hailstorm, begs to have a shelter, but since he had never resorted to any charity, he has to end his journey with disappointment. Those who give away charities, it serves as the food for the journey, which makes their travel comfortable. The one who has charity of giving food to his credit, it serves him as the food for the journey and he reaches the abode of Yama with comfort.

## \|\| 3.6.58-61 \|\|

*evaṃ pathātikaṣṭena prāptā yamapuraṃ tadā \|*  
*prajñāpitāstadā dūtairniveśyaṃte yamāgrataḥ \|\| 58 \|\|*

*tatra ye śubhakarmāṇastāṃśca saṃmānayedyamaḥ \|*  
*svāgatāsanadānena pādyārgheṇa priyeṇa ca \|\| 59 \|\|*

*dhanyā yūyaṃ mahātmāna ātmano hitakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*yena divyasukhārthāya bhavadbhiḥ sukṛtaṃ kṛtam \|\| 60 \|\|*

*idaṃ vimānamāruhya divyastrībhogabhūṣitam \|*  
*svargaṃ gacchadhvamatulaṃ sarvakāmasamanvitam \|\| 61 \|\|*

58-61. A person who has no charity to his credit, has to suffer. At that point of time, the messengers of Yama in the form of Yama welcome the arrival of the person with nobility. On seeing him, the Yama atonce gets up from the throne, welcomes the auspicious men with respect. He is then made to sit over a seat and offered with padya and arghya. Welcoming the guest, Yama then addresses him- “You - the noble soul, is quite graceful, because, you being the well-wishers of the soul, for the achieving of your own divine comfort, have performed the noble deeds. Therefore, you be seated over the beautiful plane, which is decorated with the divine damsels. It fulfills all the desires and belongs to the beautiful heaven. Therefore, for the fulfillment of all your desires, you better board the plane and proceed on to the heaven.

## \|\| 3.6.62-63 \|\|

*tato bhuktvā mahābhogānaṃte puṇyasya saṃkṣayāt \|*  
*yatkiñcidalpamaśubhaṃ punastadiha bhokṣyatha \|\| 62 \|\|*

*te cāpi dharmarājānaṃ narāḥ puṇyānubhāvataḥ \|*  
*paśyaṃti saumyavadanaṃ pitṛbhūtamivātmanaḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

62-63. Enjoying all the comforts there and ultimately with the decline of all the merits whatever unpresent is left out, you face it here.” At that pint of time, the auspicious soul, because of his auspicious merits, witnesses Dharmaraja in his beautiful form, who appears to him like his own father.

## \|\| 3.6.64-66 \|\|

*ye punaḥ pāpakarmāṇaste paśyaṃti bhayānakam \|*  
*pāpāviśuddhanayanā viparītātmabuddhayaḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*daṃṣṭrākarālavadanaṃ bhrukuṭīkuṭilekṣaṇam \|*  
*ūrdhvakeśaṃ mahāśmaśruprasphuradadharottaram \|\| 65 \|\|*

*aṣṭādaśabhujaṃ kruddhaṃ nīlāṃjanacayopamam \|*  
*savāryudhodyatakaraṃ brahmadaṇḍena tarjakam \|\| 66 \|\|*

64-66. But the sinful persons visualize him as a terrific god. Because of inauspicious sight, adverse type of wisdom, the sinful person visualize Dharmaraja as a horrific personality, with horrible teeth, terrific face, curved eyebrows, long hair, wildly grown beard and moustaches, the lips fluttering with anger, possessing eighteen arms, the body resembling the mountain, holding all the weapons in his hands as attributes, beating (the sinners) with Brahma-danda.

## \|\| 3.6.67 \|\|

*mahāmahiṣamārūḍhaṃ dīptāgnisamalocanam \|*  
*raktamālyāmbaradharaṃ mahāmerumivocchritam \|\| 67 \|\|*

67\. He has a gigantic body, mounted over a he-buffalo. He eyes resemble the burning fire. He is clad in red garments. He wears a garland around his neck and is tall like the Meru mountain.

## \|\| 3.6.68 \|\|

*pralayāṃbudanirghoṣaṃ pibaṃtamiva sāgaram \|*  
*grasaṃtamiva lokānāmudgiraṃtamivānalam \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. He thunders like the clouds of the time of dissolution. He appears like drinking the entire water of the ocean or swallowing the people or vomiting fire flames.

## \|\| 3.6.69-70 \|\|

*mṛtyuśca tatsamīpasthaḥ kālānalasamaprabhaḥ \|*  
*kālaścāṃjanasaṃkāśaḥ kṛtāṃtaśca bhayānakaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*mārī cogrā mahāmārī kālarātriḥ sudāruṇā \|*  
*vividhā vyādhayaḥ kaṣṭā nānārūpabhayāvahāḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

69-70. The death with black complexion, having the lustre of the burning fire, also accompanies him. Kala like a black mountain, the terrible Krtanta (death), the terrific Marica, epidemic and horrible Kalaratri with many diseases, always remain present in his court, who are always horrible and torture the people variously.

## \|\| 3.6.71-72 \|\|

*śaktiśūlāṃkuśadharāḥ pāśacakrāsidhāriṇaḥ \|*  
*vajradaṇḍadharā raudrāḥ kṣudratūṇīdhanurdharāḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*asaṃkhyātā mahāvīryāḥ krūrāścāñjanasaṃprabhāḥ \|*  
*sarvāyudhodyatakarā yamadūtā bhayānakāḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. He holds the weapons like Sakti, Sula, goad, noose, disc, sword, vajradanda, horrible bow and quiver. He is accompanied by lakhs of his attendants holding these weapons. The messengers of Yama are also innumerable in number, highly valorous, cruel, having black complexion, resembling the lustre of a black mountain. All of them appear there equipped with all the weapons.

## \|\| 3.6.73-76 \|\|

*anena parivāreṇa mahāghoreṇa saṃvṛtam \|*  
*yamaṃ paśyaṃti pāpiṣṭhāścitraguptaṃ ca bhīṣaṇam \|*  
*nirbhartsayataṃ cātyantaṃ yamaṃ sadupakāriṇam \|\| 73 \|\|*

*citraguptaśca bhagavāndharmavākyaiḥ prabodhayan \|*  
*bhobho duṣkṛtakarmāṇaḥ paradravyāpahāriṇaḥ \|*  
*garvitā rūpavīryeṇa paradāravimardakāḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*yatsvayaṃ kriyate karma tatsvayaṃ bhujyate punaḥ \|*  
*tatkimātmopaghātārthaṃ bhavadbhirduṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*idānīṃ kiṃ pratapyadhvaṃ pīḍyamānāḥ svakarmabhiḥ \|*  
*bhuñjadhvaṃ svāni karmāṇi nātra doṣo'sti kasyacit \|\| 76 \|\|*

73-76. The horrible looking Citragupta is also spotted by the sinner, who addresses Yama in a noble way. Lord Citragupta with his religious discourses, addresses the sinners- “O sinners, you have usurped the riches of others. Getting proud of your beauty and strength, you enjoyed the wives of others. One has to reap the harvest of his own deeds. Therefore, why did all of you, like killing your ownself followed the evil ways? Presently you have to suffer for your own misdeeds. Why do you feel painful now, whatever deeds you had performed, you shall have to reap the reward for the same. No one is to be blamed for the same.”

## \|\| 3.6.77-80 \|\|

*ete ca pṛthivīpālāḥ saṃprāptā matsamīpataḥ \|*  
*svakīyaiḥ karmabhirghorairduṣprajñā balagarvitāḥ \|\| 77 \|\|*

*bhobho nṛpā durācārāḥ prajāvidhvaṃsakāriṇaḥ \|*  
*alpakālasya rājyasya kṛte kiṃ duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam \|\| 78 \|\|*

*rājyalobhena mohādvā balādanyāyataḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*yatpīḍitāḥ phalaṃ tasya bhuṃjadhvamadhunā nṛpāḥ \|\| 79 \|\|*

*kṛtaṃ rājyaṃ kalatraṃ ca yadarthamaśubhaṃ kṛtam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ saṃparityajya yūyamekākinaḥ sthitāḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

77-80. Subsequently, addressing the rulers, he says “O rulers of the earth, getting intoxicated of your own strength and wisdom, you people have arrived here because of your own deeds. You destroyed your people, by your own misdeeds. Because of your greed for ruling the kingdom, which was to be short lived, why did you act in such a way? Because for the greed of the kingdom, now you have to face the reward for your misdeeds. For the sake of the kingdom and the woman, you have done all (those misdeeds) and all of you are facing the reward of the same.

## \|\| 3.6.81 \|\|

*paśyāma tadbalaṃ tubhyaṃ yena vidhvaṃsitāḥ prajāḥ \|*  
*yamadūtaistāḍyamānā adhunā kīdṛśaṃ bhavet \|\| 81 \|\|*

81\. Getting blinded by the pride or arrogance, all of you destroyed your own people, how do you feel when you are personally get punished at the hands of the messengers?

## \|\| 3.6.82-83 \|\|

*evaṃ bahuvidhairvākyairupālabdhā yamena te \|*  
*śocaṃtaḥ svāni karmāṇi tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭhaṃti pārthiva \|\| 82 \|\|*

*iti dharmaṃ samādiśya nṛpāṇāṃ dharmarāṭ punaḥ \|*  
*tatpāpapaṃkaśuddhyarthamidaṃ vacanamabravīt \|\| 83 \|\|*

82-83. O king, many similar words are then spoken by (the Citragupta to) all those present there, hearing which they are filled with remorse and repentance, and remain silent. Then the Dharmaraja, after delivering the discourse to the kings, speaks to his messengers, for getting the sinners relieved of their sins.

## \|\| 3.6.84 \|\|

*bhobhoścaṇḍa mahācaṇḍa gṛhītvā nṛpatīnimān \|*  
*viśodhayadhvaṃ pāpebhyaḥ krameṇa narakāgniṣu \|\| 84 \|\|*

84\. He says- “O Canda and Mahacanda, you setter throw these rulers in the fire of the hell, in order to get them relieved of their sins.”

## \|\| 3.6.85-86 \|\|

*tataḥ śīghraṃ samutthāya nṛpānsaṃgṛhya pādayoḥ \|*  
*bhrāmayitvātivegena vikṣipyordhvaṃ vigṛhya ca \|\| 85 \|\|*

*sarvaprāṇena mahatā sutapte tu śilātale \|*  
*ā sphālayaṃti tarasā vajreṇeva mahādrumam \|\| 86 \|\|*

85-86. On hearing these words, the messengers start immediately, holding the rulers by their feet, rotate them and then throw them. Catching hold of them in the mid way, they strike them against the mountain slabs, and then throw them off forcefully like a log of wood.

## \|\| 3.6.87 \|\|

*tataḥ sa raktasrotobhiḥ sravate jarjarīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*sa niḥsaṃjñastadā dehī niśceṣṭaḥ saṃprajāyate \|\| 87 \|\|*

87\. Then, the blood starts flowing from their bodies like the flow of streams. With the pain of such a strike, the person is fainted atonce and appears as if has become lifeless.

## \|\| 3.6.88-91 \|\|

*tataḥ sa vāyunā spṛṣṭaḥ śanairujīvate punaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ pāpaviśuddhyarthaṃ kṣipyate narakārṇave \|\| 88 \|\|*

*aṣṭāviṃśatirevādhaḥ kṣiternarakakoṭayaḥ \|*  
*saptamasya talasyāṃte ghore tamasi saṃsthitāḥ \|\| 89 \|\|*

*rauravaprabhṛtīnāṃ ca narakāṇāṃ śataṃ smṛtam \|*  
*catvāriṃśatsamadhikaṃ mahānarakamaṃḍalam \|\| 90 \|\|*

*yeṣu pāpāḥ prapacyaṃte narāḥ karmānurūpataḥ \|*  
*yātanābhirvicitrābhirākarmaprakṣayādbhṛśam \|\| 91 \|\|*

88-91. But with the touch of the wind, he regains his consciousness and life back. Subsequently, for the purification of his body of the sins, the messengers of Yama, put the body in twenty eight altars of hell, which are as vast as the ocean and are lodged quite deep below the earth. At the end of the seventh Ioka known as Tala, then he has to pass through various horrible hells known as Raurava and others. These are known to be a hundred and forty in number. The sinful person suffers in those hells.

## \|\| 3.6.92-93 \|\|

*ā malaprakṣayādyadvadagnau dhāsyaṃti dhātavaḥ \|*  
*tathā pāpakṣayātpāpāśśodhyaṃte narakāgniṣu \|\| 92 \|\|*

*sugāḍhahastayā bāḍhaṃ taptaśṛṃkhalayā narāḥ \|*  
*mahāvṛkṣāgraśākhāyāṃ laṃbyaṃte yamakiṃkaraiḥ \|\| 93 \|\|*

92-93. Upto the time the filth is there, similarly, till the deeds get exhausted, the person has to suffer from torture with the decline of the sins, like the metals burning in the fire. Someone is thrown into the fire of hell. Someone is bound with the heated chains and hanged with vast branch of a tree by the messengers of Yama.

## \|\| 3.6.94 \|\|

*tataste sarpayaṃtreṇa kṣiptā dolyaṃti kiṃkaraiḥ \|*  
*dolyaṃtaścātivegena niḥsaṃjñā yāṃti yojanam \|\| 94 \|\|*

94\. After torturing him there for long, he is tortured by sarpa-yantra. The person, at that point of time, rushes with great force and then gets fainted.

## \|\| 3.6.95-99 \|\|

*aṃtarikṣasthitānāṃ ca lohabhāraśataṃ tataḥ \|*  
*pādayorbadhyate teṣāṃ yamadūtairmahābalaiḥ \|\| 95 \|\|*

*tena bhāreṇa mahatā bhṛśamātardditā narāḥ \|*  
*dhyāyaṃtaḥ svāni karmāṇi tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭheti vihvalāḥ \|\| 96 \|\|*

*jvālābhiragnivarṇābhirllohadaṃḍaiḥ sakaṃṭakaiḥ \|*  
*hanyaṃte kiṃkarairghoraiḥ samaṃtātpāpakāriṇaḥ \|\| 97 \|\|*

*tataḥ kṣāreṇa dīptena vahnerapi viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*samaṃtataḥ pralipyaṃte kṣatāṃgā jarjarīkṛtāḥ \|\| 98 \|\|*

*punarvidārya cāṃgeṣu śirasaḥprabhṛti kramāt \|*  
*vṛntākavatprapacyaṃte taptatailakaṭāhake \|\| 99 \|\|*

95-99. At the time of his running in space, the messengers bind iron of excessive weights to his feet. With weight of the same, the person feels extremely painful and laments for the misdeeds committed by him earlier but has to bear the entire torture silently. The messengers of Yama struck them with huge barbed rods of iron. Again with the fire flames, his body limbs are burnt out as a result of which all his limbs get shattered. Thereafter, his head and other limbs of the body are torn out often. The messengers of Yama, first put the person in apan filled with boiling oil like a bunch of fruit, in which he groans.

## \|\| 3.6.100-103 \|\|

*viṣṭhāpūrṇe tataḥ kūpe kṛmīṇāṃ nicaye tataḥ \|*  
*medastvakpūyapūrṇāyāṃ vāpyāṃ kṣipyaṃti te punaḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

*bhakṣyaṃte krimibhistīkṣṇairlohatuṇḍaiśca vāyasaiḥ \|*  
*śvabhirdaṃśairvṛkairghorairvyāghrairapyatha vānaraiḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*pacyaṃte māṃsavaccāpi pradīptāṃgārarāśiṣu \|*  
*protāḥ śūleṣu tīkṣṇeṣu narāḥ pāpena karmaṇā \|\| 102 \|\|*

*tilapiṃḍairivākramya ghoraiḥ karmabhirātmanaḥ \|*  
*tilavatsamprapīḍayante cakrākhye narake tathā \|\| 103 \|\|*

100-103. Then they drop him in altars filled with refuse and germs, marrow, skin and puss. The flesh of the sinners is bitten by the germs or insects which bite him with the sharp end beaks. Then the crows and other birds peak the bodies of the sinners with their sharp beaks. Similarly, the flesh of some people is consumed by dogs, kites, wolves and tigers. Sometimes their flesh is cooked like the meat. At places, these persons are tortured with spears and tridents. The jiva has to suffer like the ball of sesamum seeds, because of his deeds. As the sesamum seeds are crushed in the oil mill, he is crushed.

## \|\| 3.6.104-105 \|\|

*bhidyaṃte cāpi talpeṣu lohabhrāṣṭreṣvanekadhā \|*  
*tailapūrṇakaṭāheṣu sutapteṣu punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*bahuśaḥ pīḍyate jihvā yā'satyapriyavādinī \|*  
*saṃdaṃśena sutaptena prapīḍyante ca pādayoḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

104-105. Some one is pushed from a high building, some one is thrown in the oil oven, (someone is cut into pieces and the) pieces of his body are poured in the boiling oil. Thus, he is tortured repeatedly. The tongue which speaks the falsehood is tortured variously. It is made to be bitten by the creatures which bite or is tortured by the boiling oil. His feet are tortured.

## \|\| 3.6.106-108 \|\|

*mithyāgamapravaktuśca dvijihvasya ca nirgatā \|*  
*jihvārddhakrośavistīrṇā halaistīkṣṇaiśca bādhyate \|\| 106 \|\|*

*nirbhartsayaṃti ye krūrā mātaraṃ pitaraṃ gurum \|*  
*teṣāṃ vakṣa ulūkābhirmukhamāpūrya sevyate \|\| 107 \|\|*

*tataḥ kṣāreṇa dīptena tāmreṇa tu punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*hatenāpūryate'tyarthaṃ taptatailaiśca tanmukham \|\| 108 \|\|*

106-108. Those who denounce the Sastras as untrue are placed in the sarpa-yantra. Then his tongue is injured. Those who denounce his parents, the preceptors, his chest is pecked by the birds like owl and others, with their sharp beaks. Thereafter, making use of thorns, burning copper and other weapons, he is killed. When he is alive, the burning or boiling oil is poured into his mouth.

## \|\| 3.6.109-110 \|\|

*itastataḥ punarvaktraṃ bhṛśamāpūrya hanyate \|*  
*viṣṭhābhiḥ kṛmibhiścāpi suvarṇaharaṇairnaraḥ \|\| 109 \|\|*

*pariṣvajati cātyugrāṃ pradīptāṃ lohaśālmalīm \|*  
*hanyate pṛṣṭhadeśe ca punastīkṣṇairmahāghanaiḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

109-110. When he moves his mouth here and there, then oil is poured into his mouth repeatedly. Those who steal the gold are thrown in the tanks filled with refuse and the insects, and they are made to suffer. Their palates are injured with roads of iron. Then, they are forced to embrace the heated iron rods. Thereafter, he is injured at the back with the big hammers.

## \|\| 3.6.111 \|\|

*daṃtureṇātikūṭena krakacena balīyasā \|*  
*śiraḥ prabhṛti pādāṃtaṃ ghoraiḥ karmabhirātmajaiḥ \|*  
*khādyate svāni māṃsāni pāyate śoṇitaṃ svakam \|\| 111 \|\|*

111\. Some of the people are sawn with saw having sharp teeth, from the head to feet. Some of the people are cut off from head to foot.

## \|\| 3.6.112-114 \|\|

*annaṃ pānaṃ na dattaṃ yairmūḍhairnāpyanumoditam \|*  
*ikṣuvatte prapīḍyante jarjarīkṛtamastakāḥ \|\| 112 \|\|*

*asitālavane ghore cchidyaṃte khaṃḍakhaṃḍaśaḥ \|*  
*sūcībhirbhinnasarvāṃgāstaptaśūlapraropitāḥ \|*  
*saṃbādhyamānā vivaśāḥ kliśyaṃte na mriyaṃti vai \|\| 113 \|\|*

*dehādutsādyamāṃsāni bhidyaṃte'sthīni mudgaraiḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭirākṛṣyate tūrṇaṃ yamadūtairbalotkaṭaiḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

112-114. Some of the people because of their own deeds, eat their own flesh and drink their own blood. Such of the fools who never gave away the food in charity, nor have they supported the giving away of the food in charity, they are crushed by putting them in the oil mill like crushing of the sugarcane. In the horrible palm grove, the leaves of which are as sharp as the sword, the limbs of the living being are cut off with the coming in contact with them. The limbs of some of them are pierced through like the needle. Someone is injured with the spear. Perforce the living being has to bear the pain and the punishment, because the life does not depart out of his body. The powerful messengers of Yama take out the flesh from the body and the bones of some of them are being broken with the use of clubs. Someone is being dragged after taking out his eyes.

## \|\| 3.6.115 \|\|

*nirastāste nirucchvāsāstiṣṭhaṃti narake dhruvam \|*  
*ucchvasaṃti sadā śvāsairvālukāvadanāvṛtāḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. Bearing all these sufferings, the living being remains in the hell. It is difficult to have even a deep sigh there, because at the time of so doing, the messengers of Yama insert the sand in their mouth.

## \|\| 3.6.116-121 \|\|

*raurave rodamānāśca pīḍyante vividhaiḥ śaraiḥ \|*  
*mahārauravapīḍābhirmahatībhistadaṃtike \|\| 116 \|\|*

*padorāsye gude caiva pārśve corasi mastake \|*  
*nikhanyaṃte ghanaistīkṣṇaiḥ sutaptairlohaśaṃkubhiḥ \|\| 117 \|\|*

*sutaptavālukāyāṃ ca praluṭhyante punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*jatupaṃke bhṛśaṃ tapte kṣiprā krandaṃti vistaram \|\| 118 \|\|*

*tenatenaiva rūpeṇa hasante pāradārikam \|*  
*gāḍhamāliṅgyate nārīṃ jvalaṃtīṃ lohanirmitām \|\| 119 \|\|*

*pūrvākāraṃ ca puruṣaṃ prajvalaṃtaṃ samaṃtataḥ \|*  
*duścāriṇīḥ striyo gāḍhamāliṃgaṃti vadaṃti ca \|\| 120 \|\|*

*kiṃ pradhāvasi vegena te na mokṣo'sti sāṃpratam \|*  
*laṃghitaste yathā bhartā pāpaṃ bhuṃkṣva tathādhunā \|\| 121 \|\|*

116-121. In case, the living beings are hurt by several types of arrows in the Raurava hell, they cry aloud. At the same spot where the living being is badly suffering from the horrible pain of the terrific hell, close to him the hot iron nails are being fixed over the feet, mouth, anus, chest, heart and the head of a person, who had united with the wife of others. These nails are quite hard and sharp. Then, he is dragged in the hot sand and is thrown in the heated mud in an iron vase. As a result of which, he always goes on crying. With all the tortures made by the messenger of Yama, who finding him upset, laughs at him. Then, they make him embrace the hot iron image of his beloved, which remains burning like the fire. Similarly, the wicked woman also, is made to embrace the burning and hot iron image of her beloved quite tightly. The messengers of Yama speak to her at that point of time- “Why are you running here and there, the way you desecrated the tradition and honour of your husband, you better face the reward for the same personally, after which you would be released.”

## \|\| 3.6.122 \|\|

*lohakumbhe tathā kṣiptāḥ savidhānaiḥ śanaiḥśanaiḥ \|*  
*mṛdvagninātha pacyaṃte svapāpaireva mānavāḥ \|\| 122 \|\|*

122\. As the stuff after putting it in the iron pitcher is cooked up slowly in the fire, similarly, a person is cooked by means of his sins there.

## \|\| 3.6.123-124 \|\|

*kvaṇaṃtyudūkhale sāsrāḥ prakṣipyaṃte śilāsu ca \|*  
*kṣipyaṃte cāṃdhakūpeṣu daśyaṃte bhramarairbhṛśam \|\| 123 \|\|*

*kṛmibhirbhinnasarvāṃgāḥ śataśo jarjarīkṛtāḥ \|*  
*sutīkṣṇakṣārakūpepu kṣipyaṃte tadanaṃtaram \|\| 124 \|\|*

123-124. Someone is pounded by placing him in the mortar, someone is thrashed over the stone slab, someone is thrown in the dry well, where the black wasps eat up his flesh. He gets completely shattered having been torn out by the insects. He is thrown in the well with salt water.

## \|\| 3.6.125 \|\|

*mahājvāle ca narake pāpāḥ phūtkārayaṃti ca \|*  
*itastataśca dhāvaṃti dahyamānāstadarcciṣā \|\| 125 \|\|*

125\. Reaching the hell having been filled with high flames, the sinful person issues the hissing sound. Suffering from the fire flames, he rushes here and there.

## \|\| 3.6.126-129 \|\|

*pṛṣṭhe cānīya jaṃghe dve vinyaste skandhayoḥ sthite \|*  
*tayormadhyena cākṛṣya bāhupṛṣṭhena gāḍhataḥ \|*  
*baddhvā parasparaṃ sarvaṃ sudṛḍhaṃ gāḍharajjubhi \|\| 126 \|\|*

*pīḍayaṃti susaṃrabdhā bhramarāstīkṣṇalohajāḥ \|*  
*mānināṃ krodhināṃ caiva purā pāpasya saṃśayāt \|\| 127 \|\|*

*pāpānāṃ narake puṃsāṃ ghṛṣyate caṃdanaṃ yathā \|*  
*śarīrābhyaṃtaragataṃ taruṇānāṃ ca dāruṇam \|\| 128 \|\|*

*piṃḍabaṃdho smṛto yāmyo mahājvāleṣu yātanāḥ \|*  
*rajjubhirveṣṭitāṃgāśca praliptāḥ kardamena ca \|*  
*karīṣarūkṣavahnau ca pacyaṃte na mriyaṃti ca \|\| 129 \|\|*

126-129. Both the thighs are turned backwards and then bound for some one. Then both the arms are also stretched backwards and are bound quite tightly. Then he is tortured with the iron rod with thorns. They rub a person who is arrogant and filled with rage, he is thrown in the hell for the washing away of his sins. Sometimes, the youthful people have to face extreme pain in their bodies. Observing such sights, one should always keep in mind the city (of Yama) in the south which is the form of the burning flame. Several types of tortures are extended to the people. The limbs of someone are tightly bound with the rope. The limb over which the mud is plastered is cooked in the fire of the cowdung cakes. But he still fails to die.

## \|\| 3.6.130 \|\|

*sutīkṣṇakṣāratoyena śarkarāsu śilāsu ca \|*  
*ā pāpasaṃkṣayātpāpā ghṛṣyaṃte caṃdanaṃ yathā \|\| 130 \|\|*

130\. Someone is rubbed over the salty sand stone according to his sins. The insects sometimes enter into the body of someone and eat up his flesh with their sharp mouths.

## \|\| 3.6.131-137 \|\|

*śarīrābhyantaragataiḥ prabhūtaiḥ kṛmibhirnarāḥ \|*  
*bhakṣyaṃte tīkṣṇavadanairādehaprakṣayāṭ bhṛśam \|\| 131 \|\|*

*kṛmīṇāṃ nicaye kṣiptāḥ pūtimāṃsasya rāśiṣu \|*  
*tiṣṭhantyudvignahṛdayāḥ parvatābhyāṃ ca pīḍitāḥ \|\| 132 \|\|*

*sutaptavajralepena śarīramanulipyate \|*  
*adhomukhordhvapādāśca dhṛtāstapyaṃti vahniṣu \|\| 133 \|\|*

*vadanāṃte pravinyastaṃ sutaptāyomayaṃ guḍam \|*  
*te khādaṃti parādhīnā hanyamānāstu mudgaraiḥ \|\| 134 \|\|*

*ye śivāyatanārāmavāpīkūpamaṭhāṃga ṇāt \|*  
*abhidravaṃti pāpiṣṭhā narāstatra vasaṃti ca \|\| 135 \|\|*

*vyāyāmodvartanābhyaṃgasnānamāpānabhojanam \|*  
*krīḍanaṃ maithunaṃ dyūtamāca raṃti ramaṃti ca \|\| 136 \|\|*

*te bādhairvividhairghorairikṣuyantrādipīḍanaiḥ \|*  
*nirayāgniṣu pacyaṃte yāvadācandratārakam \|\| 137 \|\|*

131-137. The living being with heaps of puss and flesh are bitten by the insects. Getting upset, he gets anxious to flee, but his body gets plastered with a hot plaster. Someone is hanged upside down in the fire altar. Thereafter, the iron balls are inserted in his mouth in place of the sugarcane balls, as a result of which getting fed up, he has to consume the same. In case he does not do so, he is belaboured with the clubs. A person, who after destroying the abode of Siva, an orchard, the step-well, well and a hermitage, makes use of the related land for the purpose of his own living or these places are used for making exercise or using it for the smearing of oil over the body or for the plastering of the body or for bathing, eating, sports, performing of the sex act, or for the purpose of gambling, then he has to suffer torture of various kinds. He has also to suffer similarly to the crushing from the oil mill. Then, he has to suffer till the moon remains with the stars.

## \|\| 3.6.138-141 \|\|

*ye śṛṇvaṃti gurorniṃdāṃ teṣāṃ karṇaḥ prapūryyate \|*  
*agnivarṇairayaḥkīlaistaptatāmrādibhirdrutaiḥ \|\| 138 \|\|*

*trapusīsārakūṭādyaiḥ kṣāreṇa jatunā punaḥ \|*  
*kramādāpūryate karṇo narakeṣu ca yātanāḥ \|*  
*anukrameṇa sarveṣu bhavaṃtyetāḥ samaṃtataḥ \|\| 139 \|\|*

*sarveṃdriyāṇāmapyevaṃ kramātpāpena yātanāḥ \|*  
*bhavaṃti ghorāḥ pratyekaṃ śarīre tatkṛtena ca \|\| 140 \|\|*

*sparśalobhena ye mūḍhāḥ saṃspṛśaṃti parastriyam \|*  
*teṣāṃ tvagagnivarṇābhiḥ sūcībhiḥ pūryate bhṛśam \|\| 141 \|\|*

138-141. Those who listen to the denouncement of their own preceptor, their ears are first filled with the small iron pieces, heated in fire, heated copper, pieces of lead and then the hot iron is inserted in them. Thus, their entire body feels painful. Because of the torture, all their sense organs get shattered. Similarly, each and every sinner has to face the pain of torture. A foolish person, who with the desire of having a union with the wife of others, the skin of his body is scratched with the tip of the needles.

## \|\| 3.6.142 \|\|

*tataḥ kṣārādibhiḥ sarvaiḥ śarīramanulipyate \|*  
*yātanā ca mahākaṣṭā sarveṣu narakeṣu ca \|\| 142 \|\|*

142\. Thereafter, the saltish and other materials are plastered over his body and they make him move in all the types of hells.

## \|\| 3.6.143-146 \|\|

*guroḥ kurvaṃti bhrukuṭiṃ krūraṃ cakṣuśca ye narāḥ \|*  
*paradārāṃśca paśyaṃti lubdhāḥ snigdhena cakṣuṣā \|\| 143 \|\|*

*sūcībhiragnivarṇābhisteṣāṃ netraṃ prapūryate \|*  
*kṣārādyaiśca kramātsarvairdehe sarvāśca yātanāḥ \|\| 144 \|\|*

*devāgniguruviprāṇāṃ ye'nivedya prabhuṃjate \|*  
*lohakīlaśataistaptaistajjihvāsyaṃ prapūryate \|\| 145 \|\|*

*tataḥ kṣāreṇa dīptena tailatāmrādibhiḥ kramāt \|*  
*śarīre ca mahāghorāścitrā narakayātanāḥ \|\| 146 \|\|*

143-146. A person who looks at his preceptor with contempt or looking with a passionate intention at the wife of the others, the burning needle is inserted in his eye. One who takes food without offering the same to the gods, fire, preceptors or the Brahmanas, his tongue is pierced with hundreds of hot nails. Thereafter, the application of saltish matter is made over his body, he is made to suffer with the saltish material and is thrown in the oil tank, besides causing other torture.

## \|\| 3.6.147-148 \|\|

*ye śivārāmapuṣpāṇi lobhātsaṃgṛhya pāṇinā \|*  
*jighraṃti mūḍhamanasaḥ śirasā dhārayaṃti ca \|\| 147 \|\|*

*āpūryate śirasteṣāṃ sutaptairlohaśaṃkubhiḥ \|*  
*nāsikā cātibahuśastataḥ kṣārādibhiḥ punaḥ \|\| 148 \|\|*

147-148. The people who smell the flowers, after plucking them from the orchards of the gods, or decorate their heads with them, their bodies are pierced with the iron nails. Similarly, pinching the nose, his body is plastered with the saltish matter.

## \|\| 3.6.149-155 \|\|

*ye niṃdaṃti mahātmānamācāryaṃ dharmadeśikam \|*  
*śivabhaktāṃśca ye mūḍhāḥ śivadharmaṃ ca śāśvatam \|\| 149 \|\|*

*teṣāmurasi kaṃṭhe ca jihvāyāṃ daṃtasaṃdhiṣu \|*  
*tālukoṣṭhe ca nāsāyāṃ mūrdhni sarvāṃgasaṃ dhiṣu \|\| 150 \|\|*

*agnivarṇāḥ sutaptāśca triśikhā lohaśaṃkavaḥ \|*  
*ākhanyaṃte subahuśaḥ sthāneṣveteṣu mudgaraiḥ \|\| 151 \|\|*

*tataḥ kṣāreṇa taptena tāmreṇa trapuṇā punaḥ \|*  
*taptatailādibhiḥ sarvairāpūryaṃte samaṃtataḥ \|\| 152 \|\|*

*kṣāratāmrādibhirdīptairdahyaṃte bahuśaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*narakeṣu ca sarveṣu vicitrā dehayā tanāḥ \|\| 153 \|\|*

*bhavaṃti bahuśaḥ kaṣṭāḥ pāṇipādasamudbhavāḥ \|*  
*śivāyatanaparyaṃte śivārāme ca kutracit \|\| 154 \|\|*

*samutsṛjaṃti ye pāpāḥ purīṣaṃ mūtrameva vā \|*  
*teṣāṃ liṃgaṃ savṛṣaṇaṃ cūrṇyate lohamudgaraiḥ \|\| 155 \|\|*

149-155. A person who denounces dharma, the Acaryas and saints of the country, besides the devotees of Siva or Saivisim, gets pierced with the trident at heart, neck, tongue, teeth, joints, palate, lips, nose, head and all the limbs. Thereafter, his body is struck with the clubs. And the heated saltish matter, copper, lead or its pieces, and the boiling oil are poured in all the sense organs and then he is made to suffer from the pain of the hells, as a result of which his hands, feet and other limbs feel painful. A sinful person who eases himself in the complex of a Siva temple, his linga and the testicles are pounded with the clubs of iron.

## \|\| 3.6.156-158 \|\|

*sūcībhiragnivarṇābhistataścāpūryate punaḥ \|*  
*lohadaṇḍaśca sumahānagnivarṇaḥ sakaṃṭakaḥ \|*  
*ākhanyate gude teṣāṃ yāvanmūrdhni vinirgataḥ \|\| 156 \|\|*

*tataḥ kṣāreṇa mahatā tāmreṇa trapuṇā punaḥ \|*  
*drutenāpūryate gāḍhaṃ gudaṃ śiśnaṃ hi dehinām \|\| 157 \|\|*

*manaḥ sarvendriyāṇāṃ ca yasmāduktaṃ pravarttakam \|*  
*tasmādindriyaduḥkhena jāyate tatsuduḥkhitam \|\| 158 \|\|*

156-158. With the heated needle, a hole is made. Then, the heated iron rod with nails is inserted in his anus and is taken out from the mouth. Thereafter, the saline matter, pieces of copper and lead are inserted in his anus and the linga. At that point of time, his mind, which is under control of the sense organs, feels painful at the miserable condition of the sense organs, and begs for redemption.

## \|\| 3.6.158-161 \|\|

*manaḥ sarvendriyāṇāṃ ca yasmāduktaṃ pravarttakam \|*  
*tasmādindriyaduḥkhena jāyate tatsuduḥkhitam \|\| 158 \|\|*

*dhane satyapi ye dānaṃ na prayacchaṃti tṛṣṇayā \|*  
*atithiṃ cāvamanyaṃte kālaprāptaṃ gṛhāśrame \|\| 159 \|\|*

*te lohatoraṇe baddhā hastapādāvatāḍitāḥ \|*  
*vidāritāṃgāḥ śuṣyaṃte tiṣṭhaṃtyabdaśataṃ narāḥ \|\| 160 \|\|*

*hastapādalalāṭeṣu kīlitā lohaśaṃkubhiḥ \|*  
*nityaṃ ca nīvṛtaṃ vaktraṃ kīlakadvayanāḍitam \|\| 161 \|\|*

158-161. Inspite of his being rich, a person, who out of greed does not give the riches in charity, does not serve the guest who arrives at his home in time, the hands and feet of such a person are bound with the iron wire and his body is shattered. Such type of pain has to be borne by a defaulter for hundreds of years. Therefore, the iron nails are fixed in the hands, feet and the head for long. Then two nails are also inserted in his mouth regularly.

## \|\| 3.6.162-168 \|\|

*kṛmibhiḥ prāṇibhiścograirlohadaṃḍaiśca vāyasaiḥ \|*  
*upadravairbahuvidhaiḥ sarpairmukharakaistataḥ \|\| 162 \|\|*

*āpīḍyaṃte jihvāmūle nibadhya śṛṃkhalāḥ punaḥ \|*  
*tiṣṭhaṃti laṃbamānāśca lohabhāraprapīḍitāḥ \|\| 163 \|\|*

*snigdhe ca vṛṣaṇe naddhe lohabhāradvayaṃ punaḥ \|*  
*tiṣṭhate laṃbamānaṃ ca bahubhāracaturguṇam \|\| 164 \|\|*

*tataḥ svamāṃsamutkṛtya tilamātrapramāṇataḥ \|*  
*bhojanaṃ dīyate teṣāṃ sūcyagreṇa saśoṇitam \|\| 165 \|\|*

*yadā nirmāṃsatāṃ prāptāḥ kālena mahatā punaḥ \|*  
*tataḥ kṣāreṇa dīptena vapusteṣāṃ pralipyate \|\| 166 \|\|*

*sicyaṃte varṣadhārābhiḥ śoṣyaṃte vāyunā punaḥ \|*
