*yathā śākhāpraśākhābhirvistṛtāsi mahītale \|*  
*tathā mamāpi saṃtānaṃ dehi tvamajarāmare \|\| 13 \|\|*

*evameṣā purā pārtha pūjitā tridaśottamaiḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ patnīvadhūbhiśca bhaginībhi stathaiva ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*pūjitābhyarhitā vācā gauryā rājañchriyā tathā \|*  
*martyaloke vedavatyā damayaṃtyāpi sītayā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sukeśyā ca ghṛtācyā ca raṃbhayā ca sukeśayā \|*  
*sahanyā kāmakaṃdanyā menakorvaśikādibhiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*strībhirevārcitā dūrvā saubhāgyasukhadāyinī \|*  
*snātābhiḥ śuci vastrābhiḥ sakhībhiḥ sasuhṛjjanaiḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dattvā dānāni viprebhyaḥ phalaṃ dattvārcayetprabhoḥ \|*  
*tilapiṣṭakagodhūmasaptadhānyāni pāṃḍava \|\| 18 \|\|*

*bhakṣayitvā suhṛnmitrasaṃbaṃdhisvajane tathā \|*  
*yā nāryo vicariṣyaṃti vratametatpurātanam \|\| 19 \|\|*

4-19. Sri Krsna said- In ancient times, for the churning of the ocean of milk, lord Visnu had held the Mandaracala mountain over his thighs. With the moving of the mountain with force, his hair were removed and carried by the oceanic waves to far off places, where they took the form of tender grass, which came to be known as Durva. Thus, at the birth of the moon faced Durva and when it was placed over the moon, the nectar emerged out of it. When the kalasas of nectar were carried by the Devas, Danavas, Gandharvas, Yaksas and Vidyadharas, some drops of the same had fallen from the kalasa on the grass as a result of which it got sanctified and was adored by the gods. Therefore, on that particular eighth moon day, Durva should be worshipped offering fruits, flowers, date palm, coconut, grapes, wall nuts, catechu, wild fruit, Artocarpus laucha, orange, silk cotton fruit, mango, myrobalan, lemon, pomegranate, curd, unbroken rice, flowers, besides the eatables, and the same should be adored. I am speaking out the process for the same, saying- “O Durva, you were born out of the nectar and you have been adored by the gods as well as the asuras, therefore, bestowing fortunes as well as children, make all my efforts successful. O Durva, you are eternal and as you have spread in many branches on earth, similarly, my wife, the daughter-in-law, sisters, besides Sarasvati, Gauri, Laksmi in the heaven, and on earth the chaste ladies like Vedavati, Damayanti, Sita, Sukesi, Ghrtaci, Rambha, Sukesa, Sahanya, Kamakandanya, Menaka and Urvasi, besides the other woman have worshipped Durva, which bestows fortunes and pleasures.” After taking a bath and getting clad in auspicious garments, together with the handmaids as well as the relatives, she should give away charities to the Brahmanas. Thereafter, the gods should be worshipped. The powder of the sesamum seeds, wheat and seven cereals should be given away in charity and one should take food with his friends and relatives.

## \|\| 3.56.20-22 \|\|

*dūrvāṣṭamīti vikhyātaṃ puṇyaṃ saṃtānakārakam \|*  
*tāḥ sarvāḥ sukhasaubhāgyaputrapautrādibhistathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*martye loke ciraṃ sthitvā tataḥ svargaṃ gatāḥ punaḥ \|*  
*devairānaṃditāstatra bhartṛbhiḥ saha bāṃdhavaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vasaṃti ramamāṇastā yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. This Durvastami is therefore auspicious, bestows children and a woman who performs this vrata, she achieves comforts, fortunes, sons, grandsons and enjoy all the comforts on earth for a long time and finally proceed on to the heaven. Reaching there, she enjoys all the pleasures with her husband. They are attended to by the gods and enjoy life upto the time of dissolution.

## \|\| 3.56.23 \|\|

*meghāvṛteṃbaratale harite vanāṃte yā sāṣṭamī śubhaphalā saphalā nabhasye \|*  
*dūrvāphalākṣatatilaiḥ pratipūjya yoṣiddūrveva vṛddhimupayāti sutaiḥ suhṛdbhiḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thus, on the days of bright eighth moon day of the month of Bhadrapada, when the sky is overcast with clouds, in the green gardens when the vrata of Durvastami is concluded, the lady with all her relatives attain wisdom like Durva.

## Chapter 57. Krsnastami Vrata

## \|\| 3.57.1-4 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṣṭamīvrataṃ pārtha śṛṇu pāpabhayāpaham \|*  
*dharmasaṃjananaṃ loke rudraprītikaraṃ param \|\| 1 \|\|*

*māsi mārgaśire prāpte daṃtadhāvanapūrvakam \|*  
*upavāsasya niyamaṃ kuryānnaktasya vā punaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*aśaktaśaktabhedena gṛhānniṣkramya bāhyataḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ varṣamekaṃ guruṃ pṛṣṭvā vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*brahmacārī jitakrodhaḥ śivārcanajape rataḥ \|*  
*tato'parāhṇasamaye snātvā nadyāṃ viśuddhadhīḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Sri Krsna said- Now, I am going to speak you about this Krsnastami vrata, which is the destroyer of the sins, creator of dharma and bestows the light of Rudra. You please listen. In the month of Margasirsa on the day of dark eighth moon day, cleaning the teeth with the brushing of them with tooth stick, taking a vow for keeping a fast which should continue during the night itself, one should complete it properly. In case, one is unable to do so, he should go to his preceptor and accepting his command with respect, he should observe Brahmacarya (sanctity) for a year, besides discarding anger and should absorb himself in the worship of Siva. In the forenoon, he should go to a river and take his bath with pure water.

## \|\| 3.57.5 \|\|

*śivaliṅgaṃ samabhyarcya sumanobhiḥ sugaṃdhibhiḥ \|*  
*gugguluṃ ca śubhaṃ dagdhvā dadyānnaivedyamuttamam \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Thereafter, he should worship the Sivalinga with fragrant flowers lovingly. The incense of guggulu and sweet eatables should be offered to Siva with respect.

## \|\| 3.57.6-7 \|\|

*tato devasya purato homaṃ kuryāttilai rguru \|*  
*mārgaśīrṣe śubhe māsi śaṃkarāyeti pūjayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

*gomūtraprāśanaṃ kṛtvā svapyādbhūmau tato niśi \|*  
*atirātrasya yajñasya phalamāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Thereafter, he should perform the homa before the Sivalinga, offering the sesamum seeds and raw sugar, through his priest. The worship of lord Siva should be carried out in the month of Margasirsa, breaking his fast by consuming cow’s urine and sleep on the ground during the night. By so doing, a person achieves the meit of performing the Atiratra sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.57.8 \|\|

*evaṃ puṣyepi saṃpūjya śaṃbhuṃ nāma maheśvaram \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ ghṛtaṃ prāśya vājapeyaphalaṃ bhajet \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Similarly, on the dark eighth moon day of the month of Pausa, Sambhu name of Mahesvara should be recited, while performing the worship. Then he should break his fast consuming the ghi. By so doing, one attains the merit of performing Vajapeya sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.57.9 \|\|

*māghe māheśvaraṃ nāma kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ prapūjayet \|*  
*niśi pītvā gavāṃ kṣīraṃ gomedhāṣṭakamāpnuyāta \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. On the dark month moon day of the month of Magha, the lord should be worshipped as Mahesvara. The fast should be broken with the payasam of cow’s milk and by so doing, one achieves the merit of performing eight sacrifices.

## \|\| 3.57.10 \|\|

*phālgune ca mahādevaṃ saṃpūjya prāśayettilān \|*  
*rājasūyasya yajñasya phalamaṣṭaguṇaṃ bhajet \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Lord Siva should be worshipped in the month of Phalguna as Mahadeva and the fast should be broken by consuming the sesamum seeds and by so doing, one achieves the merit of performing eight Rajasuya sacrifices.

## \|\| 3.57.11 \|\|

*caitre ca sthāṇunāmānaṃ kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ śivaṃ yajet \|*  
*yavāhārośvamedhasya yajñasya phalamāpnuyāt \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. On the dark moon day of the month of Caitra, with the performing of vrata, one achieves the merit of performing the Sthanu sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.57.12 \|\|

*vaiśākhe śivanāmānamiṣṭvā rātrau kuśodakam \|*  
*pītvā puruṣamedhasya phalaṃ daśaguṇaṃ bhajet \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. In the month of Vaisakha, the lord has to be adored by the name of Siva. The fast has to be broken at night by drinking the water of kusa grass. By so doing, one achieves the merit of performing the Naramedha sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.57.13 \|\|

*jyeṣṭhe paśupatiṃ pūjya gavāṃ śṛṅgodakaṃ pibet \|*  
*gavāṃ lakṣapradānasya naraḥ phalamavāpnuyāt \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Lord Siva has to be adored in the month of Jye$tha by the name of Pasupati or the water of Gosrnga. By so doing, a person achieves the merit of donating a lakh of cows.

## \|\| 3.57.14 \|\|

*āṣāḍhe cogranāmānamiṣṭvā saṃprāśya gomayam \|*  
*varṣāṇāṃ niyutaṃ sāgraṃ rudraloke mahīyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. During the month of A$adha, 3iva has to be adored in the form of Ugra and the fast has to be broken with the consuming of the cowdung. By so doing, a person is respected in the Rudraloka for ten thousand years.

## \|\| 3.57.15 \|\|

*śrāvaṇe śarvanāmānamiṣṭvārkaṃ niśi bhakṣayet \|*  
*bahusvarṇasya yajñasya naraḥ phalamavāpnuyāt \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. In the month of Sravana, Siva has to be adored as Sarva and the fast should be broken by consuming Mandara (swallow wart) at night, and by so doing, a person achieves the merit of performing a yajna of enormous gold.

## \|\| 3.57.16 \|\|

*māsi bhādrapade'ṣṭamyāṃ tryaṃbakaṃ nāma pūjayet \|*  
*bilvapatraṃ niśi prāśya annadīkṣāphalaṃ bhajet \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. During the month of Bhadrapada, one should adore Siva as Trayambaka. During the night, the fast should be broken with the wood apple fruit. By so doing, a person earns the merit of giving away of Annadiksa.

## \|\| 3.57.17 \|\|

*bhavanāmāśvine pūjyaḥ prāśayettaṃḍulodakam \|*  
*pauṇḍarīkasya yajñasya phalaṃ śataguṇaṃ bhajet \|\| 17 \|\|*

17\. During the month of Asvina, Siva has to be adored by the name of Bhava. The fast at night has to be broken by taking rice water. The one who does so earns the merit of performing a hundred Paundarika sacrifices.

## \|\| 3.57.18 \|\|

*kārtike rudranāmānaṃ saṃpūjya prāśayeddadhi \|*  
*agniṣṭomasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. During the month of Kartika, Siva has to be adored in the form of Rudra. By breaking the fast by taking curd, a person earns the merit of performing the Agnistoma sacrifice.

## \|\| 3.57.19-20 \|\|

*abdāṃte bhojayedviprāñchivabhaktiparāyaṇān \|*  
*pāyasaṃ madhu saṃyuktaṃ ghṛtena samabhiplutam \|*  
*śaktyā hiraṇyavāsāṃsi bhaktyā tebhyo nivedayet \|\| 19 \|\|*

*satilā kṛṣṇakalaśā bhakṣyabhojyena saṃyutāḥ \|*  
*dvādaśātra pradātavyāśchatropānadyugānvitā \|*  
*nivedayati rudrāṇāṃ gāṃ ca kṛṣṇāṃ payasvinīm \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Thus, at the end of the vrata, the payasam cooked with ghi and honey should be served to the Brahmanas who should be fully satisfied. Thereafter, as per one’s means, one should also give away the costumes, gold, twelve black pitchers filled with sesamum seeds, several items of eatables, umbrellas, shoes and mulching black cows should also be given with respect, according to one’s means.

## \|\| 3.57.21 \|\|

*varṣamekaṃ caredevaṃ nairantaryyeṇa yo naraḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṣṭamīvrataṃ bhaktyā tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Thus for a lull one year, the vrata of the dark eighth day of the Moon should be completed. The merit one earns for so doing is going to be stated by me. You please listen.

## \|\| 3.57.22-23 \|\|

*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ sarvaiśvaryasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*modate bhūpavannityaṃ martyaloke śataṃ samāḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*anena vidhinā devāḥ sarve devatvamāgatāḥ \|*  
*devī devītvamāpannā guhaḥ skaṃdatvamāgataḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Getting relieved of all the sins, the performer enjoys all the royal comforts like a king for a hundred years. By performing this vrata, the gods and goddesses of the heaven achieved their respective divinity including Guha and Skanda.

## \|\| 3.57.24 \|\|

*brahmā brahmatvamāpanno hyahaṃ viṣṇutvamāgataḥ \|*  
*indraśca devarājatvaṃ gāṇapatyaṃ gaṇo gataḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. Brahma achieved Brahmatva, I myself achieved Vaisnava grace, similarly, Indra achieved lordship of the heaven, Ganapati achieved the leadership of the Sivaganas.

## \|\| 3.57.25-28 \|\|

*nārī vā puruṣo vāpi kṛtvā kṛṣṇāṣṭamīvratam \|*  
*akhaṃḍitaṃ mahārāja puṇyaṃ prāpnotyanuttamam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sūryakoṭipratīkāśairvimānaiḥ sarvakāmikaiḥ \|*  
*rudrakanyāsamākīrṇairhaṃsasārasasaṃyutaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*nṛtyavāditrasaṃyuktairutkṛṣṭadhvanināditaiḥ \|*  
*dodhūyamānaścamaraiḥ stūyamānaḥ surāsuraiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*trinetraḥ śūlapāṇiśca śivaiśvaryasamanvitaḥ \|*  
*āste śivapure tāvadyāvatkalpeṣu cāṣṭakam \|\| 28 \|\|*

25-28. O great kings, with the performing of this dark eighth moon day vrata, irrespective of being a man or a woman, the person achieves the imperishable merits. Thereafter, enjoying all the pleasures, boarding a plane issuing the lustre of a crores of suns, surrounded with the Rudra-girls, decorated swans and the crane which issue the sound of dancing, singing and music from the place, he achieves the place of Siva. Waving the flywhisks, the Gods and the Asuras serve him. Achieving all the fortunes of Siva - the holder of trident having three eyes, he enjoys all the comforts and lives there for eight kalpas.

## \|\| 3.57.29 \|\|

*ityetatte samākhyātaṃ pārtha kṛṣṇāṣṭamīvratam \|*  
*yacchrutvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. O Partha, I have thus spoken to you the method of performing the vrata of the dark astami or the eighth moon day of the dark fortnight, by listening to which, a person is relieved of all the sins. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.57.30 \|\|

*kṛṣṇāṣṭamīvratamidaṃ śivabhāvitātmā satyāśanairuditanāmayutairupoṣya \|*  
*kṛṣṇāndadāti kalaśānsatilānnayuktānyosau prayāti padamuttamamindumauleḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. One who performs vrata of this astami which bestows welfare, observing the fast and at the end of the year gives away twelve pitchers filled with sesamum seeds, he achieves the best place of lord Candramauli.

## Chapter 58. Anaghastami Vrata

## \|\| 3.58.1-2 \|\|

*tena dattena loke'smindattaṃ rājyaṃ mahītale \|*  
*kārtavīryāya kauṃteya yogābhyāsaḥ savistaraḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*tayoḥ kālena mahatā jātaḥ putro mahā tapāḥ \|*  
*datto nāma mahāyogī viṣṇoraṃśo mahītale \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Sri Krsna said- Atri - the son of Brahma, had been a great Rsi besides being illustrious. His chaste wife was known as Anasuya. After the lapse of a long period, with the union of both of them, an immensely illustrious son known by the name of Datta was born who was the form of lord Visnu himself. He had also been a great yogi.

## \|\| 3.58.3-4 \|\|

*dvitīyo nāma lokesminnanaghaśceti viśrutaḥ \|*  
*tasya bhāryā nadī nāma babhūva sahacāriṇī \|\| 3 \|\|*

*aṣṭaputrā jīvavatsā sarvabrāhmaguṇairvṛtā \|*  
*anayorviṣṇurūpeṇa lakṣmīścaiva nadī smṛtā \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. At the same time, another great tapasvi Rsi known by the name of Anagha, was also there. His noble wife had eight sons and a daughter. He had all the virtues of a Brahmana. Anagha was the form of Visnu and the his wife was the form of Laksmi.

## \|\| 3.58.5-9 \|\|

*evaṃ tasya sabhāryasya yogābhyāsaratasya vā \|*  
*ājagmuḥ śaraṇaṃ devāḥ śuṃbhadaityena pīḍitāḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*brahmalabdhaprasādena drutaṃ gatvāmarāvatīm \|*  
*saṃruddhāṃ jaṃbhadaityena divyavarṣaśataṃ nṛpa \|\| 6 \|\|*

*daityadānavasaṃyoge pātālādetya bhārata \|*  
*tasya sainyamasaṃkhyeyaṃ daityadānavarākṣasaiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tena nirṇāśitā devāḥ seṃdracaṃdramarudgaṇāḥ \|*  
*tyājitāḥ svāni dhiṣṇyāni tyaktvā jagmurdiśo daśa \|\| 8 \|\|*

*agrataḥ pralayaṃ yāṃtaḥ sendrā devā bhayārditāḥ \|*  
*pṛṣṭhatonu vrajaṃti sma daityā jaṃbhapuraḥsarāḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

5-9. He used to perform the yogic exercises with his wife. The gods who had been tortured by a daitya reached before the great Rsi Anagha and prayed to him- “Getting a boon from Brahma, the daitya atonce proceeded to Amaravati and surrounded it from all the sides. He enjoyed all the pleasures for a divine hundred years. O Bharata, the countless armies of Daily as, Danavas and the Raksasas reached the heaven and they defeated the armies of gods besides Indra, the Moon and the Marudganas, besides wounding them. Thereafter, the Gods deserting their abodes, started fleeing from the heaven. While moving in the other directions, the Gods were destroyed by the Raksasas.

## \|\| 3.58.10-12 \|\|

*yudhyaṃtaḥ śarasaṃghātairgadāmusalamudgaraiḥ \|*  
*nardanto vṛṣabhārūḍhāḥ kecinmahiṣavāhanāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*śarabhairgaṃḍakairvyāghrairvānarai rabhasairdrutāḥ \|*  
*muñcanto yāṃti pāṣāṇācchataghnīstomarāñcharān \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yāvadvindhyagiriṃ prāptāstattasyāśramamaṇḍalam \|*  
*anaghaścānadī caiva dāṃpatyaṃ yatra tiṣṭhati \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. In the great battle, the demons equipped with weapons like arrows, clubs, mortars, as well as the mudgaras and other weapons, used the bulls, male buffaloes, rhinoceros, tigers and the monkeys as their vehicles, and attacked the enemy with force. They followed the gods showering on them the stones and stone-bails, reached close to the Vindhyagiri mountain. The gods while on flight, reached the asrama where Anagha and Nadi were leading the life of a householder and spending their time in the performing of the yogic practices.

## \|\| 3.58.13-22 \|\|

*tayoḥ samīpaṃ saṃprāptāste narāḥ śaraṇārthinaḥ \|*  
*anagho'pi ca tāndevāṃllīlayaiva savāsavān \|\| 13 \|\|*

*abhyaṃtare praviśyātha tiṣṭhadhvaṃ vigatajvarāḥ \|*  
*tatheti nāma te kṛtvā sarve tuṣṭiṃ samāsthitāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*daityā api drutaṃ prāptā ghnaṃtaḥ praharaṇairarīn \|*  
*ityūcurulbaṇā ghorā gṛhṇīdhvaṃ brāhmaṇīṃ muneḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*drutaṃ drumānākṣipadhvaṃ puṣpopagaphalopagān \|*  
*athāropyānaghaṃ mūrdhni daityā jagmustadāśramān \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tatkṣaṇāccāpi daityānāṃ śrīrbabhūva śirogatā \|*  
*dattakenāpi te dṛṣṭā naṣṭā dhyānāgninā kṣaṇāt \|*  
*nistejaso babhūvurhiḥ niḥśrīkā madapaṃḍitāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*devairapi gṛhītāste daityāśca haraṇe raṇe \|*  
*rudaṃtī nistanaṃtaśca niśceṣṭā brahmakaṃṭakāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*ṛṣṭibhiḥ karaṇaiḥ śūlaistriśūlaiḥ parighairghanaiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ te pralayaṃ jagmustatprabhāvānmunestadā \|\| 19 \|\|*

*asurā devaśastraughairjitā indreṇa ghātitāḥ \|*  
*devā api svarāṣṭreṣu tasthuḥ sarve yathā purā \|*  
*surairapi munestasya devarṣermahimā'bhavat \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tataḥ sa sarvalokānāṃ bhavāya satatotthitaḥ \|*  
*karmaṇā manasā vācā śubhānyeva samācarat \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kāṣṭhakuḍayaśilābhūta ūrdhvabāhurmahātapāḥ \|*  
*brahmottaraṃ nāma tapastepe suniyatavataḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

13-22. They sought refuge with the Rsi. On hearing their prayer, Anagha secured their safety in a mountain cave and then said to them- “You lead here the life of comfort and joy.” The gods accepted the words of Anagha and started living there with comfort. On the other hand, the daityas torturing the gods with their attacks, issued harsh and poisonous words for the sage, saying- “You better catch hold of the wife of the sage and carry her away. Besides that, you also uproot the trees diadem with fruits and conceal them.” Thereafter, the daityas uprooted a number of trees and making a bundle of it, threw it over the head of the sage Anagha and left for their own place. At the same time, Sri or fortune of the daityas, left their crown and at the same time, in full view of all, Dattaka jumped into the fire flames and was reduced into ashes. Thereafter, the foolish daityas, who had been deprived of Sri or Laksmi, were captured by the gods. Then they were attacked by the gods who attacked the daityas with their swords, spears, tridents, parighas and other weapons, besides with influence of the Rsi, all the daityas were destroyed, who started crying pathetically and were fainted and became inactive. Thus, with the attack by the weapons shot by Indra and other gods, the daitays were completely destroyed and all the gods returned to their respective countries, and started enjoying all the comforts as before. When the glory of the sage so came to light in the context of the gods, he started doing good for the welfare of the people with his body and speech, becoming stable like the wood or the stone slabs, the great ascetic, remaining disciplined, started performing tapas, known as Brahmottara by raising his hands.

## \|\| 3.58.23-26 \|\|

*netre hyanimiṣe kṛtvā bhruvormadhye vilokayan \|*  
*trīṇi varṣasahasrāṇi divyānīti hi naḥ śrutam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tathorddhvaretasastasya sthitasyānimiṣasya hi \|*  
*yogābhyāsaprayatnasya māhiṣmatyāḥ patiḥ prabhuḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*ekāhāddrutamabhyetya kārtavīryorjuno nṛpaḥ \|*  
*śuśrūṣāṃ vinayaṃ cakre divārātramataṃdritaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*gātrasaṃvāhanaṃ pūjāṃ manasā ciṃtitaṃ tathā \|*  
*sampūrṇe niyame vṛtte dṛḍhatuṣṭyā samanvitaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

23-26. Fixing his gaze, without winking his eyes over the middle of the eyebrows, he performed sever tapas for three thousand years. Raising both his arms, fixing his gaze with the concentration of mind, the Maharsi became absorbed in tapas. (Then the king of Mahismati known as) Sahasrabahu once reached before the sage. With all humility, he remained in service of the sage throughout the day and night. He himself worshipped the Maharsi and took good care of him. Then he started pressing his hands and feet and other parts of the body.

## \|\| 3.58.27-30 \|\|

*tasyai dadau varānpuṣṭāṃścaturo bhūritejasaḥ \|*  
*pūrvaṃ bāhusahasraṃ tu sa vavre prathamaṃ varam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*adharmāddhīyamānasya sadbhistasmānnivāraṇam \|*  
*dharmeṇa pṛthivīṃ jitvā dharmeṇaivānupālanam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*saṃgrāmānsubahūñjitvā hatvā vīrānsahasraśaḥ \|*  
*saṃgrāme yudhyamānasya vadho me syāddhareḥ karāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

*cakravartipadaṃ caiva aṣṭasiddhisamanvitam \|\| 30 \|\|*

27-30. Thus completely following all the rules when the tapas was completed, the Maharsi feeling delighted, bestowed four boons on the king of Mahismati known as Sahasrabahu- (i) There should be no religious study by the unnoble people, (ii) The land should be taken by religious ideology and it should be ruled as per the scriptures, (iii) When a large number of warriors are killed in the war, one should meet with his end at the hands of the lord, (iv) After getting the boons, the wicked person had given over the kingdom to the sage. The Maharsi then expanded his yogic practices making use of the eight siddhis, and the king achieved the position of an emperor.

## \|\| 3.58.31-34 \|\|

*tenāpi pṛthivī kṛtsnā saptadvīpā saparvatā \|*  
*sasamudrākaravatī dharmeṇa vidhinā jitā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*tasya bāhusahasraṃ tu prabhāvātkila dhīmataḥ \|*  
*yāgādratho dhvajaścaiva prādurbhavati māyayā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*daśayajñasahasrāṇi teṣu dvīpeṣu saptasu \|*  
*nirargalāni vṛttāni svayaṃ vai tasya pāṃḍava \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sarve yajñā mahābāho prasannā bhūridakṣiṇāḥ \|*  
*sarve kāñcanavedikyāḥ sarve yūpaiśca kāñcanaiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

31-34. Thereafter, Sahasrabahu conquered the entire earth by religious means. Initially, a thousand arms were grown over the body of the king. Thereafter, with an illusion, a flag and a chariot emerged out of the sacrifice. Then Sahasrabahu performed ten thousand yajnas in the seven continents, in an appropriate manner. These yajnas were spread in a vast area and in these yajnas, huge sums were given as daksina (to the Brahmanas) who were pleased. The pillars and fire altars of these yajnas were made in gold and were well decorated. Narmada. Thus while indulging in the water sport, inspite of his remaining quite delightful, the river Narmada remained always comprehensive and did not raise high waves. With his thousand arms, the ocean was disturbed as a result of which Asuras of the netherworld felt miserable. Keeping silent and finding that the ocean was being disturbed with two thousand hands, the extremely poisonous serpent Sesa attacked the king. But inspite of that, he held his head quite static and like the part of a banana trunk, he thought himself as thrown and defeated. With the use of his five sharp arrows, he confused the ten faced Ravana - the lord of Lanka, caught him, and overpowered him. He brought him in Mahismati and imprisoned him with bondages.

## \|\| 3.58.35-38 \|\|

*sarvadevairmahābhāgairvimānasthairalaṃkṛtāḥ \|*  
*gaṃdharvairapsarobhiśca nityamevopaśobhitāḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tasya yajñe jagurgāthāṃ gaṃdharvā nāradastathā \|*  
*caritaṃ rājasiṃhasya mahimānaṃ nirīkṣya te \|\| 36 \|\|*

*na nūnaṃ kārtavīryasya gatiṃ yāsyanti pārthivāḥ \|*  
*yajñairdānaistapobhirvā vikrameṇa śrutena ca \|\| 37 \|\|*

*dvīpeṣu saptasu sa vai khaḍgacarmaśarāsanī \|*  
*vyacaracchyenavadyo vai dūrādārādavaikṣata \|\| 38 \|\|*

35-38. At that point of time, all the gods remained in their respective planes and were well adorned. The Apsaras were always engaged in singing and dancing. Narada and the Gandharvas sung the story of the king. Thus, witnessing the enormous glory of the king, it becomes evident that by following his footsteps, you would also achieve the glory of Sahasrabahu. He is the sequence of the performing of sacrifices, charities, tapas etc., with your strength and the grace of the Vedas, you would also rule the earth with all the seven continents. You will carry the sword, shield, bow and arrow, and roam about in all the directions freely.

## \|\| 3.58.39-40 \|\|

*anaṣṭadravyatā cāsya na śoko na ca vai klamaḥ \|*  
*prabhāveṇa mahīrājorakṣaddharmeṇa ca prajāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*pañcāśītisahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ vai narādhipa \|*  
*samudravasanāyāṃ sa cakravartī babhūva ha \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. He could be seen from close quarters as well as from distant places. His riches never declined, nor did he attract anxiety or grief. 0 best of the humans, thus he saved the people by all religious means and he ruled the earth for eighty five thousand years upto the seashore. He became an emperor or a Cakravarti king.

## \|\| 3.58.41 \|\|

*sa eva paśupālobhūtkṣetrapālaḥ sa eva ca \|*  
*sa eva vṛṣṭyāṃ parjanyo yogitvādarjuno'bhavat \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. He was also declared as Pasupata and Ksetrapala. By means of clouds, be became the rain and by means of his excellence in the yogic practices, he became Arjuna as well.

## \|\| 3.58.42 \|\|

*sa vai bāhusahasreṇa jyāghātakaṭhinatvacā \|*  
*vāti raśmisahasreṇa kṣobhyamāṇe mahodadhau \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Making use of his thousand arms, which had been turned hard with the use of the string of the bow, he achieved enormous glory and disturbed the great ocean.

## \|\| 3.58.43-49 \|\|

*na hi nāgamanuṣyaistu māhipmatyāṃ mahādyutiḥ \|*  
*karkoṭāheḥ sutāñjitvā puri tatra nyaveśayat \|\| 43 \|\|*

*sa vai patnīṃ samudrasya prāvṛṭkāleṃbujekṣaṇām \|*  
*krīḍate ca madonmattaḥ pratisrotaścakāra ha \|\| 44 \|\|*

*lalitaṃ krīḍatā tena phalaniṣpandamālinī \|*  
*ūrmībhrukuṭimatyeva śaṃkitāsyeti narmadā \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tasya bāhusahasreṇa kṣobhyamāṇe mahodadhau \|*  
*bhavaṃtyālīnaniśceṣṭāḥ pātālasthā mahāsurāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*tūṣṇīkṛto mahābhāga līnāhīnamahāmatiḥ \|*  
*cakārottuṅgakṣubdhormi doḥsahasreṇa sāgaram \|\| 47 \|\|*

*krāṃtā niścalamūrddhāno babhūvuśca mahoragāḥ \|*  
*sāyāhne kadalīkhaṇḍānnirdhā tanihatā iva \|*  
*jitā dhanurdharāḥ sarve sutyaktaiḥ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*laṅkādhipaṃ mohayitvā sabalaṃ rāvaṇaṃ balāt \|*  
*nirjitya vaśamānīya māhiṣmatyāṃ babaṃdha ca \|\| 49 \|\|*

43-49. Once the extremely illustrious Sahasrabahu gained the daughter of the great serpent Karkotaka in a victory competition and brought her in the city of Mahismati. During the rainy season, while enjoying the water sport with his beloved girl, the Rsi created another river. The said sage getting arrogant, usually enjoyed the water sport in the river

## \|\| 3.58.50-52 \|\|

*tatobhyetya pulastyastu arjunaṃ saṃprasādayan \|*  
*mumoca rakṣaḥ paulastyaṃ paulastyenānugāminā \|*  
*tasya bāhusahasrasya babhūva jyātalasvanaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*kṣudhitena kadācitsa prārthitaścitrabhānunā \|*  
*saptadvīpāṃ citrabhānoḥ prādādbhikṣāṃ mahīmimām \|\| 51 \|\|*

*kuṃḍeśayastato'dyāpi dṛśyate bhagavānhariḥ \|*  
*niṃbādityaśca pratyakṣo jāgratsaṃstasya veśmani \|*  
*babhūva duhiturhetoḥ śarado'dyāpi tiṣṭhati \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. Then, Pulastya reached before Sahasrarjuna and pleasing the king, got his grandson freed. Once the string of his bow was caught in his arms, which created a huge sound. When Citrabhanu begged for food from the king getting hungry, he gave always in charity all the seven continents with the earth in arms and the lord who resided in the altar and slept there, can still be seen. In the same house, for the sake of the daughter, Nimbadi can still be seen in the form of Sarada.

## \|\| 3.58.53-57 \|\|

*sa evaṃ guṇasaṃyukto rājābhūdarjuno bhuvi \|*  
*anaghasya prasādena yogācā ryasya pāṃḍava \|\| 53 \|\|*

*teneyaṃ varalabdhena kārtavīryeṇa yoginā \|*  
*pravartitā martyaloke prasiddhā hyanaghāṣṭamī \|\| 54 \|\|*

*aghaṃ pāpaṃ smṛtaṃ loke taccāpi trividhaṃ bhavet \|*  
*yasmādaghaṃ nāśayati tenāsāvanaghā smṛtā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*tasyāṣṭaguṇamaiśvaryaṃ vinodārthaṃ vibhāvyate \|*  
*aṇimā mahimā prāptiḥ prākāmye laghimā tathā \|\| 56 \|\|*

*īśitvaṃ ca vaśitvaṃ ca sarvakāmāvasāyitā \|*  
*ityaṣṭau yogasiddhasya siddhayo mokṣalakṣaṇāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

53-57. Thus, because of the extreme grace of the sage Anagha, the said king became a monarch possessing all the virtues on earth. Having been blessed with the boons by him, Sahasrarjuna popularized the Anaghastami in the world. The scriptures interpreted Agha as sins, which are of three types on earth. The person who destroys the sins is called Anagha. For his pleasure, the fortunes with eight gunas always remain present with him. They are known as- Anima, Mahima, Prapti, Prakamya, Laghima, Isitva, Vasitva besides others, which fulfill all the desires. These are also said to be the yogas siddhis and all of them have the symptoms of achieving moksa.

## \|\| 3.58.58 \|\|

*samutpannā dattakasya loke pratyayakārakāḥ \|*  
*yātrāsamāptau saṃgṛhya yadaghāni tathaiva vā \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. For the firm knowledge of the universe, the siddhis were bestowed for the donor and these had been collected by him at the end of his journey.

## \|\| 3.58.59 \|\|

*jagatsamastamanaghaṃ kuryādasmādato'naghā \|*  
*madaṃśo madgataprāṇo loke sminnṛtako dvijaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. In order to relieve the entire world of the sin, the Brahmana came to be known by the name of Anagha. The related eight moon day also came to be known as Anagha. A Brahmana who belongs to my family and is absorbed in my thought alone, is popularly known as Vrttaka or a simple person.

## \|\| 3.58.60 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*kīdṛśaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa sa vai rājārjuno vratam \|*  
*cakre vā triṣu lokeṣu kairmantraiḥ samayaiśca kaiḥ \|*  
*kasminkāle tithau kasyāmetanme vada keśava \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Yudhistira said- O lord with lotus like eyes, how did that king perform this vrata, at what time and using which one of the mantra, he popularized it in the three worlds? 0 Kesava, you also speak out the related moon day also for the same.

## \|\| 3.58.61-62 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāṃ mārgaśīrṣe daṃpatī darbhanirmitau \|*  
*anaghaṃ cānaghāṃ caiva bahuputraiḥ samanvitām \|\| 61 \|\|*

*purā kṛtīkṛtau śāṃtau bhūmibhāge sthitau śubhau \|*  
*snātvaivamarcayetpuṣpaiḥ sasugandhairyudhiṣṭhira \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. Sri Krsna said- O Yudhisthira, on the dark eighth day of the month of Margasirsa, a figure of Anagha should be prepared with the kusa grass, with several of his sons, and should be consecrated over an auspicious land. It should be worshipped with offering it a bath, fragrant flowers etc.

## \|\| 3.58.63-66 \|\|

*ṛgvedoktaṛcā vipro viṣṇuṃ dhyātvā mamāṃśajam \|*  
*anaghaṃ vāsudevenānaghāṃ lakṣmīṃ vrajāṃ tanum \|*  
*pradyumnādiputravargaṃ harivaṃśe yathoditam \|\| 63 \|\|*

*oṃ ato devā avaṃtu no yato viṣṇurvicakrame \|*  
*pṛthivyāḥ saptadhāmabhiḥ \|*  
*idaṃ viṣṇurvicakrame tredhā nidadhe padam \|*  
*samūḷhamasyapāṃsure \|*  
*trīṇi padā vicakrame viṣṇurgopā adābhyaḥ \|*  
*ato dharmāṇi dhārayan \|*  
*viṣṇoḥ karmāṇi paśyata yato vratāni paspaśe \|*  
*iṃdrasya yujyaḥ sakhā \|*  
*tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyaṃti sūrayaḥ \|*  
*divīva cakṣurātatam \|*  
*tadviprāso vipanyavo jāgṛvāṃsaḥ samiṃdhate \|*  
*viṣṇoryatparamaṃ padam \|*  
*lokodbhavaiḥ phalaiḥ kandaiḥ śṛṃgārairbadaraiḥ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*vittaiśca dhānyaiḥ puṣpaiśca gaṃdhadhūpaiḥ sadīpakaiḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

*yaḥ pūjayedbhaktiyuktaḥ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|*  
*tato dvijānbhojayecca suhṛtsaṃbaṃdhibāṃdhavān \|\| 65 \|\|*

*vratāvasāne gṛhṇīyātkaścideko naro vratam \|*  
*teṣāṃ madhye dṛḍhāścakruranaghavratapāragāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

63-66. Thereafter, a Brahmana should be worshipped as my own Amsa, Anagha and Vasudeva, besides Laksmi as Anagha. Then as per the provision of the Harivamsa, Pradyumna and my sons should also be meditated upon. Then uttering the reds from Rgveda, the adoration should be done. The seasonal fruits, roots, decoration, wealth, cereals, flowers, fragrance, incense and lamp should be offered. One who worships them with devotion, he is relieved of all the sins. Thereafter, one should be seated with Brahmanas and all his relatives, and serve food to them.

## \|\| 3.58.67-69 \|\|

*idaṃ jīvanaghātī cetsatyaṃ tu samayoṣitam \|*  
*varṣamekaṃ tataḥ svecchā idaṃ tavānaghavratam \|\| 67 \|\|*

*tatropekṣaṇakaṃ kāryaṃ naṭanartakagāyakaiḥ \|*  
*prabhāte tu navamyāṃ taṃ toyamadhye visarjayet \|\| 68 \|\|*

*evaṃ yaḥ kurute yātrāṃ varṣevarṣe ca harṣitaḥ \|*  
*bhaktiyuktaḥ śraddhayā ca sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 69 \|\|*

67-69. At the end of the vrata, a member of the family should come forward to patronize this vrata for future. The son expert in the performing of the Anagha vrata does not cause harm to the body but to the contrary, it makes the human life as the best, because this Anagha vrata has been faithfully performed with devotion for a full one year. Thereafter, on the ninth moon day, accompanied with song and music besides dancing, one should go to a lake or a river and consign the material in the water. Thus a person who completes this vrata every month, all his sins get destroyed. When lord Visnu id delighted, there is the expansion in the family, one attained good health. After enjoying all the comforts on earth, he attains the highest place in the heaven. This vrata is the remover of the sins and its glory has been spoken by me.

## \|\| 3.58.70 \|\|

*kuṭuṃbaṃ varddhate tasya yasya viṣṇuḥ prasīdati \|*  
*ārogyaṃ sapta janmāni tato yāṃti parāṃ gatim \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. When lord Visnu is pleased, there is expansion of the family for seven generations. There are no ailments for seven births and the performer achieves final beatitude.

## \|\| 3.58.71 \|\|

*etāmaghaughaśamanāmanaghāṣṭamīṃ ca kauṃteya saṃprati mayā kathitā hitāya \|*  
*kurvaṃtyananyamanasaḥ svayaśobhivṛddhyai ṛddhiṃ prayāṃti kṛtavīryasutānurūpām \|\| 71 \|\|*

71\. This Anaghasami vrata is the destroyer of sins and its glory has been spoken by me. Who so ever performs this vrata with devotion, he achieves all riches, beautiful form and the desired success.

## Chapter 59. Somastami Vrata

## \|\| 3.59.1-2 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*athānyatsaṃpravakṣyāmi vrataṃ śreyaskaraṃ param \|*  
*śivalokapradaṃ puṇyaṃ vidhivanme nibodhatām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*vāre some sitāṣṭamyāṃ pakṣe somaṃ samarcayet \|*  
*vidhinā candracūḍālaṃ prāpyametatsa candrakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Sri Krsna said- I am going to tell you about an extremely beneficial vrata, with the observing of which, one achieves the auspicious Sivaloka. You listen about it quite carefully. On the eighth bright moon day falling on monday, one should worship the Moon as well as Siva who is known as Candracuda. Thus, vrata should be observed appropriately.

## \|\| 3.59.3-5 \|\|

*dakṣiṇārdhe hariṃ dhyātvā madhye tu paritaḥ prabhum \|*  
*pañcāmṛtādinā devaṃ sthāpayitvā yatavratī \|\| 3 \|\|*

*candanenenduyuktena dakṣiṇārdhaṃ vilepayet \|*  
*harabhāgaṃ nīlaraktaṃ śivasyopari mauktikam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*paścātpuṣpaiḥ samabhyarcya sitaṃ raktairanuttamaiḥ \|*  
*nīrājanaṃ punaḥ kuryātpañcaviṃśatidīpakaiḥ \|*  
*atha siddhaiḥ śubhairbhakṣyainevadyaṃ vinivedayet \|\| 5 \|\|*

3-5. Lord Hari should be shown on the right (other deities should be placed in the centre and around the main image). The images should thereafter be bathed with pancamrta. Thereafter, Yatavrati should be lodged to his right half and that part of Siva should be decorated with sandal paste and brown colour, besides the gems and beads. Thereafter, using the white and red flowers of excellent type, the worship should be performed, burning twenty five lamps, with separate wicks and the arati should be performed. Then for the removal of the sins, sweet and auspicious food should be served.

## \|\| 3.59.6-8 \|\|

*evaṃkṛtopavāsastu prabhāte pūrvavacchivam \|*  
*sampūjyājyaṃ tilairmiśraṃ juhuyājjātavedasi \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vratino brāhmaṇānpaścādbhojayitvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*mithunāni tu sambhojya yathāśaktyanupūjayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

*āvartya pitarāvarcya vidhinā tena suvrata \|*  
*saṃvatsarāṃte kartavyaṃ yattatsarvaṃ nibodha me \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. In the way, after the spending of night by fasting, during the morning time, the adoration of lord Siva should be performed as before. He should make the offerings of ghi in the fire flames and the performer of the vrata should please the Brahmanas by serving food. 0 Suvrata, Brahmana couple should be given the costumes and ornaments as per one’s means. He should again worship Siva and Siva while concluding the vrata. At the end of the year, the active ties which are to be performed are being spoken by me. You please listen.

## \|\| 3.59.9-10 \|\|

*prāgukvavidhinā pūjyā sitapītayugadvayam \|*  
*dadyādvitānakaṃ caiva patākāṃ ghaṭakīṃ tathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dhūpagaṃdhārasī cāpi dīpavṛkṣaṃ suśobhanam \|*  
*evamādīni yojyāni pūrvavadbhojyamācaret \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. According to the set procedure, after performing the puja, the canopy of white and yellow colour, besides banner, bell, incense, fragrance, juice, and the lamps for both of them (Siva and Siva) should be decorated and all the rites should be performed as before, offering the food etc.

## \|\| 3.59.11-12 \|\|

*caturasraṃ trikoṇaṃ ca maṇḍalaṃ kārayettataḥ \|*  
*trikoṇe pārvatīṃ dhyāyeccaturasre maheśvaram \|\| 11 \|\|*

*saṃkalpya dvijadāṃpatyaṃ vāsobhirbhūṣaṇaistathā \|*  
*pūjayitvā yathāśaktyā kuryānnīrājanaṃ śubhaiḥ \|*  
*dīpakaiḥ pañcaviṃśadbhirbhojayitvā visarjayet \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Thereafter, square and triangular mandalas should be drawn. In the triangle, Parvati should be lodged, while Mahesvara should be lodged in the square orb. Thereafter, the Brahmana couple should be presented with various types of costumes and ornaments. They should be worshipped appropriately and then the arati should be performed with lamps with twenty five wicks. The food should then be served to them. Thereafter, they should be gracefully sent off.

## \|\| 3.59.13-15 \|\|

*abdapañcakamekaṃ vā evaṃ yaḥ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*ubhābhyāṃ lokamāsādya padaṃ yāsyatyanāmayam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*ā dehapatanādyastu nityametatsamācaret \|*  
*ihaiva sa hariḥ sākṣānnararūpo vibhāvyate \|\| 14 \|\|*

*na spṛśaṃtyāpadastasya na duḥkhī bhavati kvacit \|*  
*jvaragrahādibhirnaiva pīḍyate'sau kadācana \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. Thus, by performing five vratas or completing the vrata in a particular year, the performer, enjoying all the comforts in both the worlds, achieves the excellent place. A person who performs this vrata throughout the life, he is considered to be Visnu incarnate on earth. He does not have to face any opposition, distress or pain of the planets.

## \|\| 3.59.16-18 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*atha vā tena mārgeṇa tāmavehi sitāṣṭamīm \|*  
*saṃprāpyādityayogena prāgvidhānena cābhyaset \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kiṃtu dakṣiṇataṃtrasthaṃ bhāskaraṃ vārcayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*padmarāgeṇa divyena suvarṇena ca pārvatīm \|\| 17 \|\|*

*kuṃkumena samālabhya candanena śivaṃ tathā \|*  
*abhāve sarvaratnānāṃ hema sarvatra yojayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. Sri Krsna said- In case the same type of the bright eighth moon day falls on Sunday, then performing worship as per the aforesaid procedure on astami (eighth day of the moon) regularly, one should worship the Sungod according to the tantric mantras. Parvati should be decorated with the ornaments of ruby or gold offering the vermilion also to her. Siva should be adored offering the sandal paste. In the absence of the gems, the gold should be used everywhere.

## \|\| 3.59.19-20 \|\|

*rudrabījaṃ paraṃ pūtaṃ priyaṃ rudrasya sarvadā \|*  
*raktamālyāṃbaradharaṃ naivedyaṃ ghṛtapācitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*śeṣaḥ pūrvavidhānena kartavyo vidhivistaraḥ \|*  
*tithau pūrṇe ca kurvīta gavyenānagha pāraṇam \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Since the Ruraksa seeds are dear to lord Siva, the same may be offered to him. The goddess Uma should be worshipped offering the red costumes and the red garments. Thereafter, the food made of ghi should be offered to them, satisfying them at the same time. О sinless one, performing the worship as has been described earlier, at the end of the vrata (or astamti), he should break his fast consuming the cow ’s ghi.

## \|\| 3.59.21 \|\|

*etatprākca vidhāyābdaṃ pañcābdānevameva ca \|*  
*kṛtvā sūryādilokeṣu bhuktvā bhogānvrajetparam \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Observing this vrata for a year, in case a person do so for another five years, he enjoys all the comforts in Suryaloka and other places in the heaven, and finally achieves the supreme position.

## \|\| 3.59.22 \|\|

*pataṃgavatpratāpī syādadīnaśca jana priyaḥ \|*  
*asminrogo na bādheta dhanavānputravānbhavet \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. Such a person shines and becomes resplendent like the Sun, becomes fortunate and a popular figure in the world. He never suffers from any ailment. He always has enough of riches and progeny.

## \|\| 3.59.23 \|\|

*yadyaṣṭamī bhavati somayutā kadācidarkeṇa vā kurukulodvaha tāmupoṣya \|*  
*pūjyo mayā saha haraṃ hariṇāṃkacihnaṃ bhaktyāyuṣāṃ padamupaiti padaṃ purāreḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. О son of the race of Kuru, in case the bright eighth moon day falls on monday or Sunday, and on that day a person worships Siva and Parvati with me, besides the Moon, he achieves the position of Murari.

## Chapter 60. Sri Vrksanavami Vrata

## \|\| 3.60.1 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*samutpanneṣu ratneṣu kṣīrodamathane purā \|*  
*daityānāṃ mohanārthāya yoṣidbhūte janārdane \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Sri Krsna said- In earlier times, with the churning of the ocean of milk, fourteen gems emerged. With a wish of possessing all the gems, by confusing the daityas, lord Janardana took to the form of a lady known as Mohini.

## \|\| 3.60.2 \|\|

*bilve vṛkṣe kṣaṇaṃ śrāṃtā viśrāṃtā kamalālayā \|*  
*yāmevamiti vānyonyaṃ yuyudhurdevadānavāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. In order to confuse the daityas, Mohini rested for a while under the wood apple tree. As a result of this, there was a terrific war, which was fought between the gods and the daityas.

## \|\| 3.60.3 \|\|

*jitāḥ sarve purā pārtha yuddhe kṛṣṇena cakriṇā \|*  
*pātālaṃ gamitā daityāḥ saśrīkaḥ svayamāyayau \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. O Partha, Sri Krsna - the holder of cakra, had already defeated the daityas therefore, together with Sri, he arrived there and the daityas proceeded on to the nether world.

## \|\| 3.60.4-7 \|\|

*śrīḥ samāvāsitā yasmācchrīvṛkṣastu tataḥ smṛtaḥ \|*  
*tasmādbhādrapadasyaiva śuklapakṣe kurūttama \|\| 4 \|\|*

*navamyāmarcayedbhaktyā īṣatsūryodaye nagam \|*  
*śrīvṛkṣaṃ vividhaiḥ puṣpairanagnipācitaiḥ phalaiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tilapiṣṭānnagodhūmairdhūpagandhasragaṃbaraiḥ \|*  
*īṣadbhānukarātāmratāmrīkṛtanabhastale \|\| 6 \|\|*

*maṃtreṇānena rājendra kṛtvā brāhmaṇabhojanam \|*  
*tato bhuñjīta maunena tailakṣāravivarjitaḥ \|*  
*anagnipākaṃ bhūpātre dadhipuṣpaphalaiḥ śubham \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. Because of the momentary stay of the lord (as Mohini) there, the tree came to the known as Sri-Vrksa. Therefore, on the bright moon day of the month of Bhadrapada, at the time of the sunrise, the tree should be worshipped with devotion. O Rajendra, several types of flowers, auspicious fruits, sesamum seed’s powder, wheat flour, incense, fragrance and garland should be offered, while worshipping the tree. The Brahmana should be served with food, after performing the puja. Thereafter, one should take food which is cooked without oil or sour materials. It should include the flowers and curd which should be placed in a Bhupatra or the leaves.

## \|\| 3.60.8-9 \|\|

*evaṃ yaḥ kurute pārtha śrīvṛkṣasyārcanaṃ naraḥ \|*  
*nārī vā duḥkhaśokābhyāṃ mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*saptajanmāṃtaraṃ yāvatsukhasaubhāgyasaṃyutā \|*  
*śrīmatī phalinī dhanyā martyaloke mahīyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. O Partha, a man or a woman who worships the tree like this, does not have to face any grief. There is no doubt about it. The woman, who performs this vrata, becomes fortunate and has enough of sons and grandsons in this world and is ultimately honoured everywhere.

## \|\| 3.60.10 \|\|

*śrīvṛkṣamakṣataphalaṃ vasitaṃ navamyāṃ naivedyapuṣpaphalavastravicitradhānyaiḥ \|*  
*pūjyaḥ prabhātasamaye puruṣottameṣṭaḥ saṃprāpnuvaṃti puruṣāḥ puruṣendravandyām \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thus, on the ninth moon day at the time of the sunrise, the eatables, flowers, fruits, costumes and several types of cereals should be offered to the tree. The offering of the fresh fruits is liked by Purusottama very much. When the tree is so appropriately worshipped, the people achieve the highest position.

## Chapter 61. Dhvaja-Navami Vrata

## \|\| 3.61.1-2 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*mahiṣāsure vinihate bhagavatyā mahāsuraiḥ \|*  
*pūrvavairamanusmṛtya saṃgrāmā bahavaḥ kṛtāḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*nānārūpadharā devī avatīrya punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya nijaghne daityasattamān \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Sri Krsna said - After the goddess Jagadambika killed the demon Mahisasura, he remembering the same enmity together with other asuras, fought several times (in other births). But the goddess also, for the upholding of the dharma, took to many forms and repeatedly killed those asuras in many forms.

## \|\| 3.61.3-4 \|\|

*atha raktāsuro nāma mahiṣasya suto mahān \|*  
*āsīttena tapastaptaṃ varṣāṇāṃ niyutāni ṣaṭ \|*  
*tasmai dadau caturvaktro rājyaṃ trailokyamaṇḍale \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tena labdhaṃ vareṇātha melayitvā danoḥ sutān \|*  
*prārabdhaṃ saha śakreṇa yuddhaṃ gatvā'marāvatīm \|\| 4 \|\|*

3-4. Thereafter, the valorous Raktasura - the son of Mahisa, performed tapas for sixty thousand years as a result of which Brahma again bestowed on him the kingship of the three worlds. After getting the boon from Brahma, the Raksasa uplifted the Danu dynasty and got them under his fold. Thereafter, together with countless warriors, he reached Amaravati and started fighting with Indra.

## \|\| 3.61.5-6 \|\|

*taddṛṣṭvā dānavabalaṃ sannaddhātyuddhatadhvajam \|*  
*yuyudhe dānavaiḥ sārddhaṃ suraiḥ śakrapurassaraiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tatra prāvartata nadī śoṇitaughataraṃgiṇī \|*  
*khaḍgamatsyagadāgrāhavasunaṃdakakacchapā \|*  
*vahaṃtī pitṛlokāya surāsurabhayānakā \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Observing the terrific army of the danavas, the gods, making Indra to lead them started fighting a terrific battle with the danavas, who held their flag quite high. As a result of the war, a river of blood started flowing, in which the clubs, fishes, crocodiles, vasu and swords looked like the tortoises, who took to terrific forms and started dispatching the gods to Pitrloka.

## \|\| 3.61.7-10 \|\|

*atha raktāsuro roṣādyuyudhe vibudhaiḥ saha \|*  
*te hanyamānā vibudhā raktākṣeṇa mahāraṇe \|\| 7 \|\|*

*bhraṣṭāḥ svargaṃ parityajya tyaktapraharaṇā drutam \|*  
*karacchatrāṃ purīṃ prāptā yatrāste bhavavallabhā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*durgā cāmuṇḍayā sārdhaṃ navadurgāsamanvitā \|*  
*ādyā tāvanmahālakṣmīrnaṃdā kṣemakarī tathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*śivadūtī mahāruṇḍā bhrāmarī rudramaṃgalā \|*  
*revatī harasiddhistu navaitāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*etāsāṃ te stutiṃ cakrustridaśāḥ praṇatānanāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. Subsequently, with sharp attacks of Raktasura, the gods were injured. The gods then threw away their weapons and they not only fled away from the battleground, but also from the heaven. All of them then took refuge with the goddess in the city of Karacchatra. The great goddesses Durga with all her nine forms resided there. They are known by the names of- Mahalaksmi, Ksemakari, Sivaduti, Mahatunda, Nanda, Bhramari, Candramandala, Revati and Harasiddhi. Reaching there, with all humility, the gods started offering prayer to the goddess.

## \|\| 3.61.11-12 \|\|

*amarapatimukuṭacumbitacaraṇāṃbujasakalabhuvanasukhajananī \|*  
*jayati jagadīśavaṃditā sakalāmalaniṣkalā durgā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vikṛtanakhadaśanabhūṣaṇarudhiravaśācchuritakṣatakhaḍgahastā \|*  
*jayati naramuṃḍamuṃḍitapiśita surāhārakṛccaṇḍī \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. They said- “Victory to the goddess who bestows comforts to all the people of the world. Victory to the same goddess whose feet arc always kissed by the crown of Indra. Like the spouse of Jagadisa, she has everlasting beautiful form, she is the absolute one, she wears the garland of human heads, consumes the flesh and blood of the Raksasas, and is known as the goddess Candi, victory to you. O goddess, she is the one who devours the Raksasas and drinks their blood, victory to the goddess Candi.

## \|\| 3.61.13-15 \|\|

*pracchāditaśikhigaṇodbalavikaṭajaṭābaddhacandramaṇiśobhā \|*  
*jayati digaṃbarabhūṣā siddhavaṭeśā mahālakṣmīḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*karakamalajanitaśobhā padmāsanabaddhapadmavadanā ca \|*  
*jayati kamaṇḍaluhastā naṃdā devī natārtiharā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*digvasanā vikṛtamukhā phetkāroddāma pūritadiśaughā \|*  
*jayati vikarāladehā kṣemaṃkarī raudrabhāvasthā \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. She holds a sword which shines like the deformed nails and teeth, with the flowing of the stream of blood and shatters the limbs. She has no clothes on her, she is adored by the Siddhas, let victory be to such a goddess Laksmi. She looks graceful with the gems knitted in the locks of her hair. She is surrounded by the peacocks. She holds a kamandalu in her hand, the goddess Nanda is the remover of the sorrow of her devotees, victory to her. She looks graceful with the lotus flower held in her hand being seated over a lotus seat, besides has a lotus like face. The goddess Ksemakari, who is without the garments, has deformed face, is breathing heavily in anger, with the flames emerging out of her breathing. She has a terrific body, who appears on her horrible form, victory to her.

## \|\| 3.61.16-17 \|\|

*krośitabrahmāṃḍodarasuravaramukharahuṃkṛtaninādā \|*  
*jayati madātimihastā śivadūtī prathamaśivaśaktiḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*muktāṭṭahāsabhairavaduḥsahataracakitasakaladikcakrā \|*  
*jayati bhujagendramaṇiśobhitakarṇā mahātuṇḍā \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Sivaduti, who happens to be the half of the Sakti of Siva, victory to her. She is the one who subsides the arrogance of Indra simply with a humkara. Getting extremely intoxicated, she holds a fish in her hand. Let the goddess Mahatunda who bound the lord of serpents in her ear, be victorious. She is the one who with her unbearable loud laugh, surprises all the directions.

## \|\| 3.61.18 \|\|

*paṭupaṭahamurajamardalajhallarijhaṅkāranartitāvayavā \|*  
*jayati madhuvratarūpā daityaharī bhrāmarī devī \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Let the goddess Bhramari be victorious, who using the kettle drums, muraja, drum and jhalari (musical instruments) as ornaments, dances with seven limbs of the body. She is the killer of the daitya named Madhu. Victory to such a goddess known as Bhramari.

## \|\| 3.61.19-20 \|\|

*śāṃtā praśāṃtavadanā siṃhavarā dhyānayogata nniṣṭhā \|*  
*jayati caturbhujadehā candrakalā candramaṇḍalā devī \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pakṣapuṭacaṃcughātaiḥ saṃcūrṇitavividhaśatrusaṃghātā \|*  
*jayati śitaśūlahastā bahurūpā revatī bhadrā \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Victory to the goddess Candramandala, having four arms, decorated with the digits of the moon. She is of peaceful nature, having the feeling of calmness over her face and is mounted over an excellent lion. She gets absorbed in meditation. The goddess Revati has a gentle form, victory to her. She kills many of her enemies with the attack of her wings as well as the beak. Holding a sharp trident in her hands, she takes to many forms.

## \|\| 3.61.21 \|\|

*paryaṭati jagati haṣṭā pitṛvananilayeṣu yoginīsahitā \|*  
*jayati harasiddhināmnī harasiddhirvaṃditā siddhaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. Similarly, the goddess Harasiddhi, who is served by the Siddhas, let she also attain victory. When feeling delighted, together with other yoginis, she moves freely in the forests of her father Himalaya.

## \|\| 3.61.22-25 \|\|

*iti navadurgāsaṃstavamanupamamāryābhirapararāṭ kṛtvā \|*  
*idamūce saha devaistrāhyasmānsarvabhītibhyaḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*punaḥpunaḥ praṇamyocurbhavānīṃ siṃhavāhinīm \|*  
*asmākaṃ bhayabhītānāṃ śaraṇye śaraṇaṃ bhava \|\| 23 \|\|*

*devānāṃ tadvacaḥ śrutvā dattvā tebhyo'bhayaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*siṃhārūḍhā vinirgatya durgābhiḥ sahitā purā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*yuyudhe dānavaissārdhaṃ mahāsamaradurdinam \|*  
*kumārī viṃśatibhujā ghanavidyullatopamā \|\| 25 \|\|*

22-25. Thus offering prayers with the Aryametres, after adoring the Navadurgas, Indra also told the goddess- “I pray that you protect us against all the dangers.” Thereafter, bowing in reverence, speaking humbly, he said to the goddess seated over her vehicle lion- “O goddess, you are the refuge of all of us who are frightened.” Then riding over the lion, together with are her majesty, the goddesses provided refuge to the gods. She went out of the city and started a great war with the daityas. At that point of time, the maiden goddess had twenty arms and she possessed the lustre of the lightning emerging from the clouds.

## \|\| 3.61.26-30 \|\|

*te'pi tatrāsurāḥ prāptāḥ pracaṃḍā rudrarūpiṇaḥ \|*  
*sarve labdhavarāḥ śūrāḥ sutaptatapasastathā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*mahāgrāhaparākrāṃtā duṣṭamāyāvinaṣṭaye \|*  
*abrāhmaṇyāddhṛdyamiṣā nāmataśca nijodyatāt \|\| 27 \|\|*

*indramārī asatkleśaḥ pralaṃbo narakaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*kuṣṭhaḥ pulomā śarabha śaṃbaro duṃdubhiḥ kharaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*ilvalo namucirbhaumo vātāpi dhenukaḥ kaliḥ \|*  
*māyāvṛtau balau bandhurmadhukaiṭabhakālajit \|\| 29 \|\|*

*rahaḥ pauṃḍūाdidaityendrāḥ prādhānyena prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*phanagobhirjanāḥ sarve sannaddhāḥ svāgrato dhvajaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

26-30. The daityas also in the battlefield, who were quite valorous and had achieved the boon after performing hard tapas, displayed their awful and horrible forms. For the destruction of the illusion (Maya) of the wicked demons, the goddess, taking to the form of Mahagraha, attacked the daityas who were known by the names of- Indramari, Asatklesa, Pralamba, Ku$tha, Puloma, Sarabha, Sambhara, Dundubhi, Khara, Davala, Namuci, Bhauma, Vatapi, Dhenuka, Kali, Mayavi, both the brothers Madhu and Kaitabha, Kalajit besides Praundra and others who were quite well known. Spreading their arms, all of them were ready for the war.

## \|\| 3.61.31-34 \|\|

*rūpato varṇitāścaiva dhvajāsteṣāṃ pṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*pratyadṛśyaṃta rājendra jvalitā iva pāvakāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kāñcanāḥ kāñcanā pīḍāḥ kāñcanasragalaṃkṛtāḥ \|*  
*patākā vividhairvālairucchritā lakṣaṇānvitāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*nīlyaḥ pītāḥ sitā raktāḥ kṛṣṇāsrāḥ pañcavarṇakāḥ \|*  
*tatra paṭṭapaṭīsautrāḥ kṛtabudbudakarburāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*patākākāntiranalā nartakya iva śobhanāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

31-34. Those daityas, who ate inauspicious meat and flesh, had collected there with all the materials. Their forms have been described. They had individual flags, which looked like the fire flames. All of them were adorned with individual flags which were adorned with gold. The high symptoms were surpassed on them. The flags were of blue, yellow, white, red, and black colours and were quadrangular in shape and had been beautifully painted. Beautiful female dancers were painted over them in an attractive manner.

## \|\| 3.61.35-36 \|\|

*tato halahalārāvaṃ cakruste dānavottamāḥ \|*  
*prāsphālayaṃta paṇavabherījharjharagomukhān \|*  
*nyavādayaṃtānakānye śaṃkhāḍaṃbaraḍiṃḍimān \|\| 35 \|\|*

*evaṃ te samayudhyaṃta bhavānīṃ daityadānavāḥ \|*  
*samājaghnuḥ śaraiḥ śūlaiḥ parighaiḥ śaktitomaraiḥ \|*  
*karṇakairīṣaṇaiḥ kuntaiḥ śataghnīkūṭamudgaraiḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

35-36. Suddenly, a terrific sound was raised from the camp of the danavas, which was issued with the playing upon of the small drums, kettle drums, cymbals, conch shells, conches, big drums, war trumpets, besides the small drums. Thereafter, the war between the goddess and the daityas started, in which the weapons like arrows, spears, parighas, tomaras, saktis, karnaka, kuntas, satagni and kuta-mudgaras were used in attacks.

## \|\| 3.61.37-38 \|\|

*āhatya mānaroṣeṇa jajvaluḥ samare'dhikam \|*  
*siṃhārūḍhā drutaṃ devī raṇamadhye pradhāvitā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*ācchidyācchidya cihnāni dhvajānnānāvidhāṃstathā \|*  
*balātkāreṇa daityānāmanāthasamare ruṣā \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Then getting fed up with the attacks, the goddess was highly enraged. Then mounting over the lion, she attacked in the battlefield and forcibly deprived the daityas of their chatras, symbols, several types of flags and banners, which were handed over to the gods.

## \|\| 3.61.39-40 \|\|

*cihnakāni dadau tuṣṭā devebhyaḥ śīghracāriṇī \|*  
*surairapi gṛhītāni jaya devīti vādibhiḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*aṃbikā tu bhṛśaṃ tuṣṭā teṣāṃ cakre kṣaṇātkṣayam \|*  
*kālarātrī dānavānāṃ mārīva nipapāta sā \|*  
*jīvitāni ca jagrāha daityānāṃ devanaṃdinī \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. With the grant of the auspicious symptoms to the gods by the fast moving goddess, they accepted them gradually and the gods then raised the slogans of victory. The goddess Ambika then feeling delighted, at once killed all the daityas who lay there on the ground. The goddess then killed the daityas like an epidemic. The goddess, who was the delight of the gods, caught hold of the daityas and swallowed them alive.

## \|\| 3.61.41-42 \|\|

*atha raktāsuraṃ kaṃṭhe gṛhītvāpātya bhūtale \|*  
*devī jaghāna tīkṣṇena triśūlena bhṛśaṃ divi \|\| 41 \|\|*

*sa bhinnahṛdayaḥ paścādbhūmau tatra prapothitaḥ \|*  
*tathāpi devyā nihataḥ papāta ca mamāra ca \|\| 42 \|\|*

41-42. The goddess, then using her sharp trident, pierced the neck of Raktasura and tossed him up in the sky. On his falling on earth, his heart was shattered and he still tried to recompose himself. But the goddess again attacked him, as a result of which he fell again, never to get up again and the life parted out of his body.

## \|\| 3.61.43-44 \|\|

*devāstānasurāñjitvā gatvā śatrupuraṃ jitam \|*  
*dadṛśuste raṇaprāṃte laṃbamānānmahādhvajān \|*  
*yātrāṃ cakruḥ saṃprahṛṣṭā navamyāṃ dhvajacihnitām \|\| 43 \|\|*

*atodyāpīha bhūpālairjayalabdhīcchayādṛtaiḥ \|*  
*upoṣyate narairbhaktairnārībhiścaiva pāṃḍava \|\| 44 \|\|*

43-44. Thereafter, the gods captioned the dwelling places of the enemies. They found that such types of flags had been raised there, which looked quite high even up to the end of the war. О Pandava, getting extremely delighted, on the ninth day of the moon, the gods started their journey with the marked flag. Because of this, all the rulers desirous of victory, besides the men and the women, should observe fast on that particular day.

## \|\| 3.61.45 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*kīdṛgvidhānaṃ tasyāstu navamyā brūhi me prabho \|*  
*sarahasyaṃ samaṃtraṃ ca yena tuṣyati caṃḍikā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Yudhisthira said- О lord, on that particular ninth moon day, how the fast is to be observed and what is the procedure for the same, you kindly tell me, by following which and with the reciting of the mantras, the goddess gets pleased.

## \|\| 3.61.46-48 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*pauṣasya śuklapakṣe yā navamī saṃpariśrutā \|*  
*tasyāṃ snātvā śubhaiḥ puṣpairarcanīyā hareḥ svasā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*kumārī subhagā devī siṃhasyaṃndanagāminī \|*  
*dhvajānnānāvidhānkṛtvā purastasyāśca pūjayet \|*  
*mālatīkusumairddīpairgandhadhūpavilepanaiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*balibhiḥ paśubhirmedhyaiḥ surāmāṃsāsṛgambaraiḥ \|*  
*dadhicandanacūrṇaiśca bhagnaiścānagnipācitaiḥ \|*  
*maṃtreṇānena kauṃteya brahmaṇopyathavā nanu \|\| 48 \|\|*

46-48. Sri Krsna said - On the bright ninth moon day of the month of Pausa, after taking bath, the fragrant and pleasant flowers should be offered to the goddess, who happens to be the sister of lord Hari, while worshipping her. The maiden goddess mounting over a lion should be consecrated with flags and banners. The jasmine flowers, lamp, fragrance, incense, sandal paste and animal sacrifice should be offered to her with devotion, which is said to be quite glorious. O Kaunteya! The performer should make Brahmanas to recite various Devi mantras.

## \|\| 3.61.49-56 \|\|

*bhadrāṃ bhagavatīṃ kṛṣṇāṃ viśvasya jagato hitām \|*  
*saṃveśinīṃ saṃyamanīṃ grahanakṣatra mālinīm \|\| 49 \|\|*

*prapannohaṃ śivāṃ rātrī bhadre pāraya me vratam \|*  
*sarvabhūtapiśācebhyaḥ sarvasatvasarīsṛpaiḥ \|*  
*devebhyo mānuṣebhyaśca bhayebhyo rakṣa māṃ sadā \|\| 50 \|\|*

*tataścāropayedrājā devīnāṃ bhavane tathā \|*  
*bhojayeta kumārīṃ ca praṇipatya kṣamāpayet \|\| 51 \|\|*

*upavāsena kurvīta ekabhaktena vā punaḥ \|*  
*bhaktyā bhūpālapañcāsya bhaktistasyā garīyasī \|\| 52 \|\|*

*evaṃ ye pūjayiṣyaṃti dhvajairbhagavatīṃ narāḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ durgā durgamārge coravyālāgni saṃkaṭe \|\| 53 \|\|*

*raṇe rājakule gehe yuddhamadhye jale sthite \|*  
*rakṣāṃ karoti satataṃ bhavānī sarvamaṃgalā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*asyāṃ babhūva vijayo navamyāṃ pāṃḍunaṃdana \|*  
*bhagavatyāstu tenaiṣā navamī satataṃ priyā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*dhanyā puṇyā pāpaharā sarvopadravanāśanī \|*  
*anuṣṭheyā prayatnena sarvānkāmānabhīpsubhiḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

49-56. Goddess Bhagavati provides benefaction to all the people in this world. She is the embodiment of patience and all the planets and constellations are like her necklace. She is the protector of all gods as well as humans. Thus, with the use of the flags, a person who worships the goddess, even when facing miseries on the harsh path, the goddess Sarvamangala protects him completely from the thieves, ghosts, Pisacas, serpents, fire, calamity, battlefield, while facing trouble from the king or in the water and protects him always. 0 son of Pandu, the day of that particular navami has been known as a victory day, this particular day enjoys immense favour with the goddess. Therefore, for the fulfillment of all the desires, the anusthana and prayers should be held on that particular day, which is quite auspicious, remover of the sins, and subsides all the disturbances.

## \|\| 3.61.57 \|\|

*devyarcanāhitamatirmanujo navamyāṃ hemasrajaṃ dhvajavaraṃ sa hi ropayedyaḥ \|*  
*bhogānavāpya manasobhimatānprakāmaṃ dehaṃ vihāya samupaiti sa vīralokam \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. A person who gets absorbed in the worship of the goddess with devotion and on the day of navami, offers a garland of gold to the goddess, he enjoying all the pleasures on earth, achieves the place of the goddess.

## Chapter 62. Ulka-Navami Vrata

## \|\| 3.62.1-3 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*ulkākhyaṃ navamīṃ rājankathayāmi nibodha tām \|*  
*yā kāśyapena kathitā tārakasyārtināśinī \|\| 1 \|\|*

*aśvayukchuklapakṣe yā navamī lokaviśrutā \|*  
*nadyāṃ snātvā samabhyarcya pitṛdevīṃ yathāvidhi \|\| 2 \|\|*

*paścātsaṃpūjayeddevīṃ cāmuṇḍāṃ bhairavapriyām \|*  
*puṣpairdhūpaissanaivedyairmāṃsamatsyasurāsavaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Sri Krsna said- Now, I am speaking about the procedure for the observing of the vrata of Ulkanavami, which had been told by Brhaspati to get rid of the sufferings of Taraka. You please listen. On the bright ninth day of the month of Asvina, one should take his bath in the river and after offering oblation for the gods, the goddess Camunda - beloved of lord Bhairava, should be worshipped with the offering of flowers, incense, eatables, drink, meat, and fish.

## \|\| 3.62.4-5 \|\|

*pūjayitvā stavaṃ kuryānmantreṇānena mānavaḥ \|*  
*samāropyāñjaliṃ mūrdhni jānubhyāmavanīṃ gataḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*mahiṣaghni mahāmāye cāmuṇḍe muṇḍamālini \|*  
*dravyamārogyavijayau dehi devi namo'stu te \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. The person should kneel down before the goddess, place both the hands over his head in the form of an anjali (handcups). Then he should offer various types of prayers, saying-“O killer of Mahisasura, you wear the garland of human skulls, I offer salutation to you again and again, O excellent one. You bestow on me the good fortunes and the victory. I offer my salutation to you again and again.”

## \|\| 3.62.6-7 \|\|

*kumārīrbhojayetpaścānnavanīlasukaṃcukaiḥ \|*  
*paridhānairbhūṣaṇaiśca bhūṣayitvā kṣamāpayet \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sapta pañcāpyathaikāṃ vā cittavittānurūpataḥ \|*  
*śraddhayā tuṣyate devī iti vīrānuśāsanam \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. Thereafter, the young girls should by served with food and offered ornaments as well as the blouse and other costumes of blue colour and ornaments. Then as per one’s own mind, one should beg forgiveness seven, five or even once. By so doing, the goddess gets pleased. It has been ordained.

## \|\| 3.62.8-10 \|\|

*abhyukṣya maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā gomayena śucismitaḥ \|*  
*dattāsane copaviśetpātraṃ ca purato nyaset \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tataḥ susiddhamannaṃ yattatsarvaṃ pariveṣayet \|*  
*saghṛtaṃ pāyasaṃ cāpi sthāpayetpātrasa nnidhau \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tṛṇāni ṣaṣṭimādāya cādāya dhamanīṃ tathā \|*  
*prajvālayettatto bhojyaṃ yāvajjvalati pāvakaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. Sprinkling water over the earth, the mandala should be plastered with the cowdung and he should be seated over an asana and siddha food should be placed before him and the fire should be ignited. Till the fire flames last, he should take food of payasam mixed with ghi. When the flames subside, he should discard the food.

## \|\| 3.62.11 \|\|

*praśāṃte bhojanaṃ tyaktvā samācamya prasannadhīḥ \|*  
*cāmuṃḍāṃ hṛdaye dhyātvā gṛhakṛtyaparo bhavet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. Then he should rinse his mouth with delight. Devoting his mind towards Camunda he should engage himself in the household work.

## \|\| 3.62.12-13 \|\|

*anena vidhinā sarvaṃ māsimāsi samācaret \|*  
*tataḥ saṃvatsarasyāṃte bhoja yitvā kumārikāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*vastrairābharaṇaiḥ pūjya praṇipatya kṣamāpayet \|*  
*suvarṇaṃ śaktito dadyādgāṃ ca viprāya śobhanām \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. Thus observing the same process every month, at the end of the year, the young maid girls should be served the food, after which the costumes and ornaments should also be given to them and then humbly beg forgiveness. The Brahmana should be given the gold as per one’s means, and a cow in charity.

## \|\| 3.62.14-15 \|\|

*ya evaṃ kurute pārtha puruṣo navamīvratam \|*  
*na tasya śatravo nārtiḥ sa rājā naṣṭataskaraḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*bhūtāḥ pretāḥ piśācā no janayaṃti bhayaṃ gṛhe \|*  
*samudyateṣu śastreṣu haṃtā tasya na vidyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. A person who performs this navami vrata gets free form the anger of the king or the danger from the thieves. He also gets free from the danger of goblins, pretas, besides the pisacas. He also cannot be killed even with the use of arms.

## \|\| 3.62.16-17 \|\|

*taṃ rakṣati sadodyuktā sarvāsvāpatsu caṃḍikā \|*  
*naro vā yadi vā nārī vratametatsamācaret \|*  
*ulkāvatsa sapatnānāṃ jvalannāste sadā hṛdi \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tāṃ śuṣkakoharamukhīṃ prakaṭorudaṃṣṭrāṃ kāpālinīṃ samavalaṃbitamuṇḍamālām \|*  
*uktavrateṣu puruṣo navamīṣu caṇḍīṃ saṃpūjya kasya hṛdaye na ca śaṃ karoti \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. He is saved from all the misfortunes by the goddess Candika. A lady who completes this vrata, she burns like a comet in the hearts of her co-wives. Accordingly, on the day of navami, one who adores the goddess Candika having a dry face, thighs and teeth, decorated with the garland of skulls, she can win over the hearts of one and all the people who get anxious to seek her favour.

## Chapter 63. Ten Incarnations

## \|\| 3.63.1-8 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*pūrvaṃ kṛtayugasyādau bhṛgorbhāryā mahāsatī \|*  
*divyārāmāśrame ramyā gṛhakāryaikatatparā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*babhūva sā bhṛgornityaṃ hṛdayepsitakāriṇī \|*  
*tasyāṃ munirmahātejā agnihotraṃ nidhāya ca \|\| 2 \|\|*

*viṣṇostrāsāddānavānāṃ kulatrāṇasamākulam \|*  
*muktvā yuddhasthitaṃ pārśve samarpya munipuṅgavaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dattvā nikṣepakaṃ sarvaṃ divyāyai sumahātapāḥ \|*  
*jagāma himavatpārśve haraṃ toṣayituṃ rahaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*saṃjīvanīkṛte nityaṃ kaṇairdhūmamadhomukhaḥ \|*  
*papau dānavarājasya vijayāya purohitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*ājagāma gate tasmingaruḍenāśrito hariḥ \|*  
*abhyetya jalpanaṃ cakre cakraṇotkṛttakaṃdharam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*galadrudhirasaṃpannaṃ lohitārṇavavasaṃnibham \|*  
*dṛṣṭvāsurabalaṃ sarvaṃ nihataṃ viṣṇunā tadā \|*  
*divyā saṃśaptukāmābhūdviṣṇuṃ sāsrāvilekṣaṇā \|\| 7 \|\|*

*yāvannoccarate vācaṃ cakreṇa kṛttakaṃdharam \|*  
*tāvannipātayāmāsa śirastasyāḥ sakuṇḍalam \|\| 8 \|\|*

1-8.Sri Krsna said- In earlier times, during the start of Krta-yuga, Divya - an immensely chaste woman and the wife of the Rsi Bhrgu, while staying in her hermitage, completed her household work quite efficiently, as a result of which she became the beloved of her husband. Once the great sage, who also stopped the daityas v/ho were afraid of Visnu to stop further war, entrusted the care of his wife to them and went to Himalaya in order to meditate upon lord Siva. His aim was to achieve the Sanjivani lore. For that purpose, he started performing hard tapas. He stood upside down and consumed the sun rays and started tapas. For the victory of the king of danavas, when the priest Bhrgu was performing hard tapas in the forest, lord Visnu arrived at his hennitage, mounting over Garuda. Lord Visnu talked with the danavas who were guarding the place and wounded their shoulders with the use of his cakra. Divya - the wife of Bhrgu, found the danava guards having been injured and streams of blood were flowing from their bodies. Thus finding the daitya army getting so destroyed, with tears flowing from her eyes, Divya was turned into a horrible form. She got ready to pronounce a curse on Visnu. Before she could utter a word from her mouth, Visnu cut off her head with her ears adorned with kundalas.

## \|\| 3.63.9 \|\|

*prāpya saṃjīvanīṃ vidyāṃ yāvadāyātyasau muniḥ \|*  
*tāvatsa daityānnāpaśyatpaśyati sma nipātitam \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. Subsequently, after achieving the knowledge of Sanjivani lore, the sage Bhrgu returned home and found the destruction of the daityas besides his own wife’s destruction.

## \|\| 3.63.10-11 \|\|

*roṣācchaśāpa ca hariṃ bhrukuṭīkuṭilānanaḥ \|*  
*avaśyabhāvabhāvitvādviśvasya hitakāraṇāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

*yasmāttvayā hatā daityā brahmaṇo matparigrahāḥ \|*  
*tasmāttvaṃ mānuṣe loke daśa vārāngamiṣyasi \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. His eyebrows were curved and in great rage, he pronounced a curse on Visnu, this was destined to happen and no one could avert it. “O Visnu, being Brahman yourself, you have destroyed daityas as also my family, therefore, you shall have to be born on earth ten times.”

## \|\| 3.63.12-13 \|\|

*ato'rthaṃ mānuṣe loke rakṣārthaṃ ca mahīkṣitām \|*  
*avatāraṃ cakārāhaṃ bhūyobhūyaḥ pṛthagvidham \|\| 12 \|\|*

*pūrvoktaiḥ kāraṇaiḥ pārtha avatīrṇaṃ mahītale \|*  
*māṃ narā ye'rcayiṣyaṃti teṣāṃ vāsastriviṣṭape \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. O Partha, therefore, I incarnates on earth again and again in order to protect the noble kings. Because of the aforesaid reasons, I have presently incarnated on earth. Therefore, such of the people who worship me, surely get a place in the heaven.

## \|\| 3.63.14 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*vrataṃ daśāvatārākhyaṃ kṛṣṇa brūhi savistaram \|*  
*samaṃtraṃ sarahasyaṃ ca sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Yudhisthira said- O Krsna, you kindly enlighten me on the performing of the Dasavatara vrata, which removes all the sins, in detail. You also kindly enlighten me about the relevant mantra.

## \|\| 3.63.15-17 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*proṣṭhapade site pakṣe daśamyāṃ niyataḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*snātvā jalāśaye svacche pitṛdevāditarpaṇam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kṛtvā kurukulaśreṣṭha gṛhamāgatya mānavaḥ \|*  
*gṛhṇīyāddhānyacūrṇasya dvihastaprasṛti trayam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*krameṇa pāvayettāṃ tu puṃsaṃjñaṃ ghṛtasaṃśritam \|*  
*varṣe varṣe dine tasminyāvadvarṣāṇi vai daśa \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Sri Krsna said- On the tenth bright moon day of the month of Bhadrapada, getting disciplined, one should go to an auspicious lake and purify himself by taking a bath. The oblations for the gods and the pitrs should be offered thereafter and one should return home. Then, the ghi should be mixed in the powder of cereals measuring ten anjalis, which should be use as naivedya and the same should be used for the whole year.

## \|\| 3.63.18-20 \|\|

*prathame pūrikānvarṣe dvitīye ghṛtapūrakān \|*  
*tṛtīye śuklakāsāraṃ caturthe modakāñchubhān \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sohālakānpañcame'bde ṣaṣṭhe'bde khaṇḍaveṣṭakān \|*  
*saptame'bde kokarasānapūpāṃśca tathāṣṭame \|\| 19 \|\|*

*navame karṇaveṣṭāṃstu daśame khaṇḍakāñchubhān \|*  
*daśa dhenūrdaśahare daśaviprāya dāpayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. During the first year the fried cakes; during the second year the sugar; during the third the white kamsara (barley powder mixed with raw sugar and gid); the sweet balls in the fourth year; Sohala (an eatable) in the fifth year; then fried cake in the sixth year; the wild paint in the seventh year; sweet cakes in the eighth year; karnavesta (an eatable) in the ninth year and the raw sugar in the tenth year, should be offered to lord Visnu. Besides ten Brahmanas should be served with food and ten cows should be given in charity.

## \|\| 3.63.21-25 \|\|

*krameṇa bhakṣayitvā ca yathoktaṃ bharatarṣabha \|*  
*arddhārddhaṃ piṣṭayedevamarddhārddhaṃ vā dvijātaye \|*  
*svata evārdhamaśnīyādgatvā ramye jalāśaye \|\| 21 \|\|*

*daśāvatārānabhyarcya puṣpadhūpavilepanaiḥ \|*  
*maṃtreṇānena medhāvī harimabhyukṣya vāriṇā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*matsyaṃ kūrmaṃ varāhaṃ ca narasiṃhaṃ trivikramam \|*  
*śrīrāmaṃ rāma kṛṣṇau ca buddhaṃ caiva sakalkinam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*gato'smi śaraṇaṃ devaṃ hariṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum \|*  
*praṇato'smi jagannāthaṃ sa me viṣṇuḥ prasīdatu \|\| 24 \|\|*

*chinattu vaiṣṇavīṃ māyāṃ bhaktyā jāto janardanaḥ \|*  
*śvetadvīpaṃ nayasyasmānsamātmani nivedayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

21-25. The performer should complete the vrata consuming the aforesaid eatables. O son of Bharata, initially, the eatable powder should be divided in four parts. One fourth each of it should be given over to the gods and the Brahmanas. The remaining half should be carried over the bank of a river or a lake and should be taken by the performer. In this way, the illustrious person, using flowers, paste etc., should worship the ten incarnations of Visnu. The lord should be consecrated reciting the mantra- O Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Narasimha, Vamana, Sri Rama, Ramakrsna, Budha, Kalki, Narayana (are the ten incarnations of Visnu), 1 take refuge with them. Let lord Visnu be pleased with me. I offer prayer with devotion that let lord Janardana free me from the Vaisnavi bondage. I am offering prayer myself, that I should be sent to the Svetadvipa.

## \|\| 3.63.26 \|\|

*evaṃ yaḥ kurute pārtha vidhinānena suvrata \|*  
*daśāvatāranāmākhyaṃ tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. O Partha, when this Dasavatara-vrata is concluded appropriately, the merit one earns, is being revealed by me.

## \|\| 3.63.27-28 \|\|

*śrūyate yāstvimālocya puruṣāṇāṃ daśā daśa \|*  
*tāśchinatti na saṃdehaḥ śakrapraharaṇairhariḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*saṃsārasāgare ghore majjata tatra māṃ hariḥ \|*  
*śvetadvīpaṃ nayatvāśu vratenānena toṣitaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. Making use of the weapons of Indra, Lord Visnu separate the ten incarnations, there is no doubt about it. Getting pleased with my vrata, rescuing me from the ocean of the universe, lord Visnu should rapidly send me to the Svetadvipa.

## \|\| 3.63.29-31 \|\|

*kiṃ tasya na bhavelloke yasya tuṣṭo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*so'haṃ janārdano rājankālarūpī dharāsutaḥ \|*  
*martyaloke svayaṃ pārtha bhūbhārottārakāraṇam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*yā strī vratamidaṃ pārtha cariṣyati mayoditam \|*  
*sā lakṣmyā'calayā yuktā bhartṛputrasamanvitā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*martyaloke ciraṃ sthitvā viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|*  
*viṣṇulokādrudralokaṃ tato yāti paraṃ padam \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. When lord Janardana is pleased, which desire of a devotee cannot be fulfilled? I am the same Janardana, who has incarnated on earth to relieve her of her burden. O Partha, a woman who performs this vrata, which has thus been revealed by me, she possessing ali the riches, together with her husband and sons, after enjoying all the pleasures on earth for long, is respected in Visnuloka. From Visnuloka, she goes to Rudraloka and finally achieves the highest position.

## \|\| 3.63.32 \|\|

*ye pūjayaṃti puruṣāḥ puruṣottamasya matsyādikāṃstu daśamīṣu daśāvatārān \|*  
*martyā daśasvapi daśāsu sukhaṃ vihṛtya te yāṃti yānamadhiruhya sureśalokān \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. Thus on the day of Dasami, one who worships the ten incarnations of Visnu, he also enjoying all the pleasures, reaches the Devaloka, boarding a divine plane.

## Chapter 64. Description of Asa-Dasami

## \|\| 3.64.1-3 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*pārtha pārthivavṛndānāṃ mukhapaṅkajasadrave \|*  
*śṛṇuṣvāvahito vacmi tavāśādaśamīvratam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*nalanāmābhavatpūrvaṃ niṣadheṣu mahīpate \|*  
*sa bhrātrā nirjito rājye puṣkareṇeti naḥ śrutam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*akṣairdyūtena rājendra niryayau bhāryayā saha \|*  
*vanaṃ pratibhayaṃ śūnyaṃ jhillīkagaṇanāditam \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Sri Krsna said- I am now telling you the process for the observing of the Asadasi vrata, which is the form of the Sun, for the shining of the faces of the rulers. You please listen to the same, with apt attention. In the earlier times, in the Nisadha country, a king named Nala was there, who had been a glorious king. He started playing the game of gambling with his brother known as Puskara. As a result of this, he was deprived of his kingdom, and then leaving his kingdom together with his wife -DamayantI, he had to retire to a great and dense forest which was infested with wild forests and the forest tribes.

## \|\| 3.64.4-6 \|\|

*sa gatvā pratyahorātraṃ jalamātreṇa vartayan \|*  
*dadarśa vanamadhyasthāñchakunīnkāṃcanacchavīn \|\| 4 \|\|*

*grahītumicchaṃstānrājansamācchādya svavāsasā \|*  
*khamāpetuḥ khagāstūrṇaṃ gṛhītvā vasanaṃ śubham \|\| 5 \|\|*

*āsasāda samāḥ kāściddhṛtavāsāḥ suduḥkhitaḥ \|*  
*damayaṃtīṃ samāprāpya nidrayāpahṛtāṃ tadā \|*  
*duḥkhādutsṛjya gatavānbhāgyataḥ prāgdhaneśvaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

4-6. Reaching there, they had to spent their night relying on water only. Once they sighted two birds with golden wings in the centre of the forest. In order to capture them, Nala tried to spread his cloth over them. But the birds, carrying his costume, flew away and disappeared in the sky. Thus having been deprived of the costumes, Nala with DamayantI went to some other place and started resting there. Leaving DamayantI in a precarious condition, with the move of the destiny, he proceeded on to the city of Ayodhya.

## \|\| 3.64.7 \|\|

*gate tu naiṣadhe bhaimī prabuddhai vāñcitānanā \|*  
*apaśyaṃtī nalaṃ vīraṃ vīra bhīmasutā vane \|*  
*itaścetaśca babhrāma hāheti rudatī muhuḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. After the departure of Nala, the moon faced Damayanti - the daughter of the king Bhima, when could not find Nala there, she went in search of him in the forest, crying and lamenting at the same time.

## \|\| 3.64.8-14 \|\|

*duḥkhaśokasamākrāṃtā naladarśanalālasā \|*  
*āsasāda dine kaiścitsā caidyapuramaṃjasā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*unmattavatparivṛtā śiśubhiḥ kautukākulaiḥ \|*  
*sā dṛṣṭā cedirājasya jananyā janaveṣṭitā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*candralekheva patitā bhūmau bhāsitadiṅmukhā \|*  
*āropya sā svabhavanaṃ pṛṣṭā kā tvaṃ varānane \|\| 10 \|\|*

*uvāca bhaimī savrīḍaṃ sairaṃdhrīṃ māṃ nibodhatām \|*  
*na dhāvayeyaṃ caraṇau nocchiṣṭaṃ bhakṣayāmyaham \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yadi prārthayate kaściddaṃḍyaste sāṃprataṃ bhavet \|*  
*pratijñayānayā devi tiṣṭheyaṃ tava veśmani \|*  
*evamastvanavadyāṃgi rāja mātāpyuvāca tām \|\| 12 \|\|*

*evaṃvidhā tadbhavane kaṃcitkālamaniṃditā \|*  
*uvāsa vasanārddhena pravṛttāṃte kila dvijaḥ \|*  
*ānayāmāsa mudito damayaṃtīṃ gṛhaṃ pituḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*mātrā pitrā samāyuktā sutairbhrātṛbhireva ca \|*  
*damayaṃtī tathāpyāste duḥkhaṃ naiṣadhavarjitā \|\| 14 \|\|*

8-14. She was suffering with grief and with the desire to search for Nala, bearing the pain of the journey, she reached the city of Vaidya, where she started looking like an insane person.
