From the first dhyana, one achieves auspicious merit; from Rudra-dhyana, one gets unique birth; with the performance of Dharma-dhyana, one achieves Devaloka after death; and by meditating in Sukla-dhyana, one achieves birth free from death. Therefore, Suklatara-dhyana, which relieves one of the ailments of the birth and death, is extremely beneficial, carries on the world and removes all the blemishes.

## \|\| 3.126.48 \|\|

*samāḥ sahasrāṇi tu sapta vai jale daśaikamagnau pavane ca ṣoḍaśa \|*  
*gavāṃ gṛhe ṣaṣṭiraśītirāhave anāśane bhārata cākṣayā gatiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

48\. The people with learnings should try to get the same. О Bharata, abstinence from hunger is seven thousand times, eleven times in the fire, sixteen in the wind, sixty in the cows and in the purified matter, there are eighty thousand of them.

## Chapter 127. Construction of wells, tanks and step-wells

## \|\| 3.127.1-3 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*taḍāgotsarjane deva vidhiṃ vidhividāṃ vara \|*  
*kathayasva mahābhāga mama devakinaṃdana \|\| 1 \|\|*

*vāpīkūpodakānāñca ke maṃtrāḥ parikīrtitāḥ \|*  
*ke ṛtvijotra ke yūpāḥ kartavyāḥ kuṇḍamaṇḍape \|\| 2 \|\|*

*dānaṃ kimatra nirdiṣṭaṃ balayaḥ ke prakīrtitāḥ \|*  
*kasminkāle kathaṃ kuryādityetatsakalaṃ vada \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Yudhisthira said – О Deva, you are the best among those who are well-versed in the moves of the destiny. Therefore, you let me know the method of digging a tank. О son of Devaki, what are the mantras prescribed for the construction of step-wells, the wells and the tanks? How should the Rtvija and Yupa-stambha be installed in the kunda-mandapa or the pavilion of the altar? What types of charities are prescribed for the same? What type of sacrifice is made therefore? How should it be done and at what time should it be done? You kindly enlighten me on the subject in an exhaustive manner.

## \|\| 3.127.4-7 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*sādhusādhu mahābāho yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi \|*  
*taḍāgavāpīkūpānāmutsargaṃ kathayāmi te \|\| 4 \|\|*

*niṣpanne baddhapālīke sarvodbhedavivarjite \|*  
*sopānapaṃktisahite pāṣāṇaiḥ sarvataścite \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tasminsalilasaṃpūrṇe kārtike vā viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*taḍāgasya vidhiḥ kāryaḥ sthiranakṣatrayogataḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*munayaḥ kecidicchaṃti vyatīte cottarāyaṇe \|*  
*na kālaniyamo hyatra pramāṇaṃ salilaṃ yataḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О valorous one, whatever is being asked by you to me is indeed a noble question. Therefore, I am going to tell you about the construction o f a tank, a well and a step-well. You please listen. While constructing a tank, the land should be dug upto the surface of the water and then a circular brick wall should be constructed, which should be without the contact of the trees. The stone steps should then be built on all the sides, the secretion of water from the well should be made especially in the month of Kartika during a stable constellation. Some of the sages give opinion that after the passing of the Uttarayana period, the consecration ceremony should be performed. But because of the presence of the water there, no specific rules for the purpose have been prescribed.

## \|\| 3.127.8-9 \|\|

*taḍāgapālaśīrṣe tu maṃḍalaṃ kārayecchubham \|*  
*daśadvādaśahastaṃ ca caturdvāraṃ suvistṛtam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*toraṇāni tu catvāri caturdikṣu vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*aśvatthoduṃbaraplakṣavaṭaśākhāmayāni ca \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. At the prominent side of the tank, an auspicious mandala should be created, which should be twenty two cubits in length, with a door of four cubits and quite wide. It should have toranas or arches on all the four sides and decorated with the branches of wild fig tree, udumbara, plaksa and vata.

## \|\| 3.127.10-11 \|\|

*nānāvarṇāstu paritaḥ patākāḥ parikalpayet \|*  
*madhye mahādhvajaḥ kāryaḥ pañcavarṇaḥ suśobhanaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*caturhastā bhavedvedī madhye pañcakarātha vā \|*  
*yajamānapramāṇena madhye yūpena śobhitā \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. Decorated with various gems, a flag should be installed. A big flag decorated with five gems should be lodged in the center of the well. Then, an altar of four hands length along with а yupa of any length should be built.

## \|\| 3.127.12-14 \|\|

*kadaṃbāśvatthapālāśavaikaṃkatamayaḥ śubhaḥ \|*  
*brāhmaṇasyāsya nirdiṣṭo yūpaḥ śrutivicakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*nyagrodhabilvajaḥ proktaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca khādiraḥ \|*  
*vaiśyasyoduṃbaramayo madhvarjunasamudbhavaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*bibhītakoduṃbarajaḥ śākaśālmalisaṃbhavaḥ \|*  
*śūdrasya yūpo nirdiṣṭaḥ sāradārumayo'tha vā \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. The trees like kadamba, asvattha, paldsa and vaikamkata are considered to be auspicious. Yupa should be designed as per the advice of a Brahmana who is well-versed in Vedas. Nyagrodha and bilva trees are prescribed for Brahman as; Khadira tree for Ksatriyas; Udumbara and arjuna for Vaisyas and the internal part of a silk cotton tree has been prescribed for the construction of yupas for Sudras.

## \|\| 3.127.15-19 \|\|

*lokapālāṣṭakaṃ tatra rajasā ca vilekhayet \|*  
*brahmāviṣṇuśca rudraśca kamalā cāmbikā tathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*sāvitrī sahitā kāryā puṣpadhūpairathārcayet \|*  
*kuryātkuṃḍāni catvāri caturdikṣu vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*mekhalātrayayuktāni hastamātrāṇi sarvataḥ \|*  
*hemālaṃkāriṇaḥ kāryā hotāraḥ ṣoḍaśāṣṭa vā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ahatāṃbarasaṃvītāḥ srakcandanavibhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*sthāpakāścātra vihitā vedavedāṅgapāragāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*itihāsapurāṇajñāḥ priyavāco'nasūyakāḥ \|*  
*mṛnmayāni ca pātrāṇi tāmrāṇi sruksruvaṃ tathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

15-19. Thereafter, the Asta-Lokapalas like Brahma, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Kamala (Laksmi), Ambika and Savitri should be worshipped with incense and flowers. Four tanks or the pools of water should be constructed on all the four sides, three mekhalas of a cubit length each besides the gold ornaments should decorate them. In the auspicious activity, there should be sixteen or eight sacrificial priests, who should be decorated with new clothes, garlands as well as the sandal paste, besides being well-versed in the Vedas, Purdrias and the other scriptures. They should possess a sweet tongue and should be blissful Acaryas. All the vases in the yajna should be made of pottery or of the copper.

## \|\| 3.127.20-21 \|\|

*vyaṃjanāni ca kāryāṇi homārthaṃ samidhastilāḥ \|*  
*grahayajñavidhānena homaḥ kāryo vijānatā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*vedyādhivāsitānāṃ ca surāṇāṃ homa iṣyate \|*  
*vāruṇaistu tathā maṃtrairhotavyaṃ puṣṭivarddhanam \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. The ladles should be made in wood for performing homa. Besides the sacrificial sticks, condiments and sesamum seeds for making offerings in the fire, should also be arranged. This process of the performing of the sacrifice and for this purpose, a pedestal should be constructed. The gods should be established in the pedestal and the relevant mantras should be recited.

## \|\| 3.127.22-23 \|\|

*indrādilokapālānāṃ pūrvādikramayogataḥ \|*  
*baliṃ dadyācca talliṅgairmantraissarvārthasiddhaye \|\| 22 \|\|*

*dvāreṣu kalaśāndadyātsahiraṇyānsapallavān \|*  
*aśvatthapallavaiḥ kāryāḥ śubhāścandanamālikāḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Thereafter, offerings should be made to Indra and other Lokapalas, reciting the mantras. For the purpose of achieving all round success, the doors should be decorated with gold. The fresh shoots of the trees should be made to decorate the pitchers. They should further be decorated with sandal paste as well as the flower garlands.

## \|\| 3.127.24-25 \|\|

*sauvarṇaṃ kārayetkūrmaṃ tāmreṇa makaraṃ tathā \|*  
*rajatena tathā matsyaṃ trapuṇā darduraṃ tathā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*śiśumārajalaukāñca rajatenaiva kārayet \|*  
*sarvānapi yathāsthānaṃ tāmrapātryāṃ nidhāpayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

24-25. A tortoise should be made of gold, the crocodile should be made of copper and fish should be made of silver, while the frogs should be made of lead. The porpoise, the leeches, should be made in silver and placed in a copper plate.

## \|\| 3.127.26-27 \|\|

*eṣā pratiṣṭhā nāmeti mantreṇāmaṃtrayecca tān \|*  
*yūpapratiṣṭhā kartavyā vedoktavidhinā tataḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*kuṃkumena samālabhya puṣpairdhūpaiḥ samarcayet \|*  
*vastrayugmena saṃpūjya naivedyādi yathākramam \|\| 27 \|\|*

26-27. Thereafter, with the recitation of the mantras – “Esa pratistha” and others, invoking should be done. According to the provision of the Vedas, the yupa should be fixed and while so doing, the vermilion, flowers, incense, two costumes, besides the eatables etc. should also be offered.

## \|\| 3.127.28 \|\|

*tato dvijātipravaraḥ śrapayitvā caruṃ navam \|*  
*tataścāgnyāhutīrdadyādbhūrbhuvaḥsvariti kramāt \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. All these things should then be given to a learned Brahmana. Thereafter, the fresh caru should be used for making the offerings. Uttering – “Bhurbhuvah Svah”, the same should be made in the fire.

## \|\| 3.127.29-31 \|\|

*tataścāvāhayeddevaṃ varuṇaṃ saritāṃ patim \|*  
*vāditraghoṣaigītaiśca gandhamālyānulepanaiḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

*śvetenaiva tu vastreṇa śiroveṣṭaṃ tu kārayet \|*  
*ādāya tāmrapātrīṃ tu brahmaghoṣapuraḥsaraḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*apramāṇaṃ jalaṃ gatvā varuṇāya nivedayet \|*  
*tvaṃ varuṇa iti maṃtreṇa jala madhye pravāhayet \|\| 31 \|\|*

29-31. Then Varuna – the lord of the rivers, should be invoked with the playing of the musical instruments. The garlands, paste and a turban of: white cloth should be given to the Brahmana, who should be worshipped at the same time. The Brahmana who leads the ceremonies, holding the copper vase, after entering the deep water, should hand over the vase to Varunadeva with respect and uttering the mantra, he should consign the same in the water.

## \|\| 3.127.32 \|\|

*yaccānyadvastrabījāni tatsarvaṃ majjayejjale \|*  
*tārayecca tato dhenuṃ dakṣiṇāyā udagvrajet \|\| 32 \|\|*

32\. All other materials including the cloth etc. should be dropped in the same water and then cross over to the south with cow.

## \|\| 3.127.33 \|\|

*gośiroveṣṭanaṃ kuryātsati vastre tu buddhimān \|*  
*lāṃgalasyāgramādāya avatīrya tato jalam \|\| 33 \|\|*

33\. At that point of time, the head of the cow should be covered with the cloth. Then he should hold the end of the tail and following the cow, he should cross over to the other side.

## \|\| 3.127.34-38 \|\|

*jñātibhiḥ sahitaḥ kartā sabhāryaścāvagāhayet \|*  
*tato'vatīrya salilāddattvā gāṃ brāhmaṇāya tām \|*  
*śaktyā ca dakṣiṇāṃ dadyādevaṃ viprānvisarjayet \|\| 34 \|\|*

*sāmānyaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo mayā dattamidaṃ jalam \|*  
*evaṃ jalāñjaliṃ kṣiptvā pūjayejjalamātaraḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*toṣyāḥ karmakarāḥ sarve kuddālāni ca pūjayet \|*  
*avāritaṃ tu dātavyaṃ mantrapūrvaṃ dinatrayam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*ekāhaṃ ca yathāśaktyā vittaśāṭhyaṃ na kārayet \|*  
*gosahasraṃ tadardhaṃ vā tasyārdhamathavāpi vā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*śatamardhaśataṃ vāpi pañcaviṃśatimeva ca \|*  
*tāsāmabhāve gāṃ dadyātsavatsāṃ kāṃsyadohanām \|\| 38 \|\|*

34-38. Thereafter, the performer, together with his relatives and the wife, after the crossing of the water by the priest, should give away the appropriate daksina to the Brahmanas, who should then be sent off. Thereafter, he should say – “I am making the water available for the use of all the living beings.” Thus speaking, he should drop the water in his hand cups. Thereafter, he should adore the water mothers besides the working labourers. Then he should worship the instruments like axes etc. At that time, he should distribute charities for one or three days as per his means, whole heartedly and he should not be miserly in the distribution of charities. One should also give away in charity a thousand or half of the number or hundred or fifty, twenty five or alternatively a single cow with a calf should be given away together with a milk pot of bronze.

## \|\| 3.127.39-43 \|\|

*eṣa rājaṃstaḍāgasya vidhiste parikīrtitaḥ \|*  
*vāpīkūpavidhānaṃ ca kathayāmi tathā param \|\| 39 \|\|*

*kuṇḍamaṇḍapasaṃbhārabhūṣaṇācchādanādikam \|*  
*taḍāgavidhivatkuryādyūpagotaraṇādikam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*akālamūlānkalaśānvāpīkoṇeṣu dāpayet \|*  
*tīrthodakasamāyuktānsitacandanacarcitān \|\| 41 \|\|*

*sitavāsoyugacchannānsamālyānratnagarbhiṇaḥ \|*  
*śrapayitvā caruṃ tatra yāvanmātro yathāvidhi \|\| 42 \|\|*

*catasra āhutīrdadyādbhūrbhuvaḥ svariti kramāt \|*  
*grahahomaṃ prakurvīta śāṃtipuṣṭivivarddhanam \|\| 43 \|\|*

39-43. O king, I have thus spoken about the digging of a tank. I am now speaking about the construction of a well or a step-well. The method of the establishment of a kunda in the step-well, the mandapa or a pavilion, the method of construction on the paraphernalia are the same besides the method of decorating it with a pavilion and ornaments. In addition to the erecting of a pillar, the cow, the arch etc., resemble those with the construction of the tank. The same method is followed. In a comer of the step-well, the pitchers should be established, which should be filled with the holy water of the sacred places. These pitchers should be plastered with the white sandal paste, each covered with two white costumes, decorated with garlands, besides having gems in the same. All formalities should be observed as prescribed for the tanks. The havi should be made as per the prescribed method and four offerings, uttering bhur bhuvah and svah should be dropped in the fire for achieving peace and development.

## \|\| 3.127.44 \|\|

*varuṇāya baliṃ dadyāllokapālebhya eva ca \|*  
*vāruṇāni ca sūktāni paṭheyurddhijasattamāḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. Thereafter, for the sake of Varuna and the lokapalas, the sacrifice should be made reciting the Varuna-sakta by the Brahmanas. The sacrifice should then be completed.

## \|\| 3.127.45 \|\|

*vedīmadhye maṃḍalaṃ ca padmamatra praśasyate \|*  
*tanmadhye pūjaye cchaṃbhuṃ brahmāṇaṃ keśavaṃ tathā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. Again in the middle of the pedestal, a lotus should be formed and Siva, Brahma and Viṣṇu should be lodged therein.

## \|\| 3.127.46-50 \|\|

*matsyakamaṭhamaṇḍūkānvedyā madhye'dhivāsayet \|*  
*mitramitro'si bhūtānāṃ dhanado dhanakāṃkṣiṇām \|\| 46 \|\|*

*vaidyo rogābhibhūtānāṃ śaraṇyaḥ śaraṇārthinām \|*  
*anenaiva hi maṃtreṇa varuṇāya visarjayet \|\| 47 \|\|*

*ādau cāvāhayeddevamanenaiva viśeṣataḥ \|*  
*namaste viśvaguptāya namo viṣṇo apāṃpate \|\| 48 \|\|*

*sānnidhyaṃ kuru deveśa samudre yadvadatra vai \|*  
*tatastu dakṣiṇā deyā brāhmaṇānāṃ narādhipa \|\| 49 \|\|*

*gauḥ sthāpakāya dātavyā bhojanaṃ cānivāritam \|*  
*sarveṣāmeva dātavyameṣa paurāṇiko vidhiḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

46-50. In the middle of the pedestal, a fish, a frog and tortoise should be lodged. For the sake of all the living beings, you are Mitra, Kubera for those who desire for wealth and a physician for an ailing person. You are the refuge for the refugees. Reciting this mantra, he should beg forgiveness and then send off lord Varunadeva – “Salutation to you. Salutation to Varuna – the lord of waters. You kindly dwell in this step-well, as you do in the ocean.” Thus speaking, he should be sent off. Then while distributing daksina to the Brahmanas, the fodder should be given to the cow and the other people should be served with the food, pleasing them at the same time. This is said to be the initial procedure. This is the method prescribed in the Puranas.

## \|\| 3.127.51-52 \|\|

*śarāyā āgataṃ toyaṃ sāmudraṃ prathamaṃ smṛtam \|*  
*nipāne vā taḍāge vā saṃsthitaṃ tadbhavecchuci \|\| 51 \|\|*

*vāpīkūpataḍāge vā sthitaṃ tu prathamaṃ jalam \|*  
*apeyaṃ tu bhavetsarvaṃ tajjalaṃ sūtikāsamam \|\| 52 \|\|*

51-52. О king of the people, the oceanic water should be placed in a pottery vase, which is called the initial water. Close to a well, in case this water is placed in another step-well, a tank or others reservoirs, their waters get purified. Because the water of a well, step-well, a tank when taken out for the first time is said to be unfit for drinking, like a woman having just delivered a child.

## \|\| 3.127.53 \|\|

*samudro'pi hi kauṃteya devayonirapāṃpatiḥ \|*  
*kuśāgreṇāpi rabhasā na spṛṣṭavyastvasaṃskṛtaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

53\. О son of Kunti, similarly, the water of the ocean, which is called as Devayoni or Jaladhisvara, is devoid of the samskaras and is unfit to be touched by the tip of the kusa grass.

## \|\| 3.127.54-56 \|\|

*agniśca tejo mṛḍayātha dehe retodhā viṣṇuramṛtasya nābhiḥ \|*  
*evaṃ bruvanpāṃḍava satyavākyaṃ tatovagāheta patiṃ nadīnām \|\| 54 \|\|*

*vaiṣṇave māsi saṃprāpte nakṣatre vāruṇe tathā \|*  
*arghyaṃ pradadyādbhaktyā tu tasminkāle mahodadheḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*snātvā tu vidhivanmaṃtraiḥ sāgare tu samāhitaḥ \|*  
*phalamūlākṣatairbhakṣyaistathārghyaṃ saṃprakalpayet \|\| 56 \|\|*

54-56. Uttering the mantra- “Agnisca tejo mrdayatha dehe retodhavisnurmrtasya nabhi,” the samskara should be performed and the water of the ocean should be immersed. On the Vaisnava month in the Satabhisa constellation, the oblation should be offered to the ocean with devotion. After reciting the mantras, taking a bath in an appropriate manner, with a careful mind, the fruits and roots, besides the eatables and the unbroken rice should be used, while offering oblation.

## \|\| 3.127.57 \|\|

*api janmasahasraṃ tu yatpāpaṃ kurute naraḥ \|*  
*mucyate sarvapāpebhyaḥ snātvā tu lavaṇāṃbhasi \|\| 57 \|\|*

57\. A person who commits sins in his thousands of births, he is freed from all of them with the letting of a bath in salt water of the ocean.

## \|\| 3.127.58 \|\|

*vidhijñena tu kartavyaṃ brāhmaṇena yathāvidhi \|*  
*kartā kārayitā caiva ubhau tu svargagāminau \|\| 58 \|\|*

58\. When a Brahmana who is well-versed in the procedure, performs this as per the prescribed procedure, the performer as well as the one who makes others to perform this, both of them reach the heaven.

## \|\| 3.127.59 \|\|

*vidhiṃ tvenamajānāno yaḥ kuryādarthamohitaḥ \|*  
*kartā kārayitā caiva ubhau narakagāminau \|\| 59 \|\|*

59\. Those who are not well-versed with the procedure, when get this act performed just for the greedy riches, then the performer as well as the priest, both fall in the hell.

## \|\| 3.127.60 \|\|

*yo na kārayate śāṃtiṃ taḍāgādyeṣu karmasu \|*  
*tasya tanniṣphalaṃ sarvamuptaṃ bījamivoṣare \|\| 60 \|\|*

60\. Therefore, during the consecration of a tank or a step-well, in case the Santi rites are not performed, then it becomes infructuous like the seeds sown in the barren land.

## \|\| 3.127.61-62 \|\|

*sarvaratnamayaṃ divyaṃ candrārkasadṛśaprabham \|*  
*vimānaṃ tejasā yuktamārohetpuṇyakarmakṛt \|\| 61 \|\|*

*kaścitpibati tattoyaṃ nipānasthaṃ tato'ñjalim \|*  
*brāhmaṇo vā yatirgaurvā yena kartā na sīdati \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. A person who performs the auspicious deeds (like digging of a step-well), graces such a plane which is studded with all the divine gems, having the lustre of the Sun and the Moon, and always remains shining. Thereafter, the water of the step-well should be used first by a mendicant or a cow for a bath and by so doing, the performer should not face any difficulty.

## \|\| 3.127.63 \|\|

*utsṛṣṭe kṛtakṛtyastu suhṛtkuryānmahotsavam \|*  
*mahābhojyaṃ mahotsargaṃ yajamāno dināṣṭakam \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. Thus with the completion of an excellent deed, the celebrations should be made which should continue for eight days.

## \|\| 3.127.64-65 \|\|

*kārakāḥ karmaṇo vāpi sūtradhārādayo narāḥ \|*  
*iṣṭāpūrtena dharmeṇa te'pi svargaṃ prayāṃti hi \|\| 64 \|\|*

*khanyamāne mahībhāge prāṇino ye kṣayaṃ gatāḥ \|*  
*citre vā devakūṭārthe te sarve tridivaṃ gatāḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. This is Istapurti yajna, performing which all the big or the small workers of the step- well achieve the heaven. At the time of the chiseling out of the auspicious step-well or during the making of images of the gods, the people who are lost, all of them reach the heaven.

## \|\| 3.127.66-69 \|\|

*dhenostu romakūpāṇi yāvantīha narottama \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi varṣakoṭiśatāni ca \|\| 66 \|\|*

*koṭiryugasahasrāṇāṃ svarge tiṣṭhettaḍāgakṛt \|*  
*cettasyapitaraḥ kecinnarakaṃ samupāgatāḥ \|\| 67 \|\|*

*tāṃstu tārayate sarvānātmānaṃ ca mahīpate \|*  
*āsphoṭayaṃti pitaro valgaṃti prapitāmahāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

*api naḥ sa kule jāto yastaḍāgaṃ kariṣyati \|*  
*sarvasvenāpi kauṃteya bhūmiṣṭhamudakaṃ kuru \|\| 69 \|\|*

66-69. О best of the humans, a person who constructs a tank, he earns for the stay in the heaven for the number of yugas equivalent to the hair on the body of a cow, multiplied by a thousand crores. In case, some of his manes are lodged in the hell, he gets instrumental in redeeming them as well, besides he himself is also redeemed. The manes of the builder of the tanks, realizing this that a son having been born in my race, would surely build a tank, challenge the opponent with the putting of their thighs, while the grandfather is filled with delight. Therefore, О son of Kunti, you get a tank built on earth, spending all your riches.

## \|\| 3.127.70-71 \|\|

*kulāni tārayetsapta yatra gaurvitṛṣī bhavet \|*  
*evaṃ varṣaśatenāpi kṛttikā viharīvane \|\| 70 \|\|*

*māsaṃ cetāgṛhe koṭikṣaṇadhvaṃsidhanasya hi \|*  
*taḍāgaṃ devabhavanaṃ vāpīvṛkṣoghanacchadaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

70-71. By so doing, when the thirst of a cow is quenched, the seven generations get redeemed. Realizing well that the wealth is short lived, for the stable riches of the house, one should construct the tanks, temples, step-wells, besides planting the trees of thick shade. By doing all these, one surely earns moksa.

## \|\| 3.127.72-74 \|\|

*caturthakaṃ phalaṃ prāptaṃ kārite'smiṃścatuṣṭaye \|*  
*yathā mātuḥ samācaṣṭe putraḥ śīlaṃ svakairguṇaiḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

*tathā svādena ca jalaṃ kartuḥ sarvaṃ śubhāśubham \|*  
*ataḥ śubhāgataṃ dravyaṃ taḍāgādiṣu lāpayet \|\| 73 \|\|*

*dhanyasya pāṃthāḥ saṃprāpya taḍāgaṃ vṛkṣamaṃḍitam \|*  
*pītvāpaḥ pādapatale viśramaṃti ramaṃti ca \|\| 74 \|\|*

72-74. As a son with his personal qualities projects the nobility of his parents, therefore riches earned with the performing of the noble deeds, should be spend in the building of the tanks, reservoirs etc. Graceful are the people who build the tanks which are surrounded by the several shady trees and the travelers by drinking the water of the same, rest in the thick shade of the trees, feeling blissful.

## \|\| 3.127.75-77 \|\|

*mārutodbhūtavīcyagraiḥ karaiḥ kamalamaṃḍitam \|*  
*abhyāgatāya sudhiyā taḍāgādyaṃ prakalpitam \|\| 75 \|\|*

*sāmānyaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo yena bhūmigataṃ jalam \|*  
*tāritaṃ kāritaṃ tena suputreṇa kuladvayam \|\| 76 \|\|*

*mūrtaṃ svabhāvataḥ siddhamiṣṭaṃ mantrapradarśitam \|*  
*iṣṭāpūrte kṛte rājankṛtakṛtyaḥ pumānbhavet \|\| 77 \|\|*

75-77. The tanks have beautiful waves which disturb the lotus flowers. A son who builds a water tank for the welfare of the common man, then while so doing, he redeems both his races. Thus the yajna known as Ista-purti when completed by a person, he becomes fully successful in his life.

## \|\| 3.127.78-84 \|\|

*unnatā vātha nimnā vā kīrtiryena prakāśitā \|*  
*tena trailokya candreṇa jananī pārtha putriṇī \|\| 78 \|\|*

*tritayaṃ nighnatāṃ neyaṃ tritayaṃ connatiṃ parām \|*  
*taḍāgamatha yo bhūmau deva devālayaṃkṛtī \|\| 79 \|\|*

*yaḥ kārayati loke'sminkīrtistasyāmalā bhavet \|*  
*sa jīvati sa evaikaḥ sa bhavedajarāmaraḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*upetānāmapi divaṃ sa nibandhavidhāyinām \|*  
*āsta eva nirātaṃkaṃ tasya kīrtimayaṃ vapuḥ \|\| 81 \|\|*

*tāvatsvarge sa ramate yāvatkīrtiranaśvarā \|*  
*tāvattvilāyāmadhyāste sukṛtī vaibudhaṃ padam \|\| 82 \|\|*

*haṃsāsyakṣiptanīlyagraṃ padminīkhaṇḍamaṇḍitam \|*  
*pīyamānaṃ mahāgrāmairdhanyāḥ paśyaṃti svaṃ saraḥ \|\| 83 \|\|*

*ghaṭairañjalibhirvaktrairyasya vāṭīpuṭairjalam \|*  
*pibaṃti jaṃtavaḥ sarve kimanyattasya varṇyate \|\| 84 \|\|*

78-84. O Partha, a person who has earned the high or low grace, with such a moon of the world and a person who adorns a race accordingly, he should construct the tank with high walls, because a person who builds such a type of tank, his glory is spotless and everlasting. Such a person lives forever after his death. A person who builds the steps in a tank, he enjoys his undisturbed stay in the heaven and his body earns fame and glory. Such a glorious person stays in the heaven for unlimited time and enjoys the position of a god there. Graceful is the person who can have a look at a tank so built by him, in which the swans carry in their beaks the blue lotus with their stalks and which is decorated with the blossoming lotus flowers and is good enough for the use of a common man. The water of such a tank is consumed by the hand cups, pitcher or by sipping. The glory or the importance of the same cannot be described in any way.

## \|\| 3.127.85-86 \|\|

*taḍāgaṃ nagaropāṃte dhanyasya kila jāyate \|*  
*ubhayorarthasaṃsiddhirdṛṣṭā karturjanasya ca \|\| 85 \|\|*

*yeṣāṃ devakulaṃ tattu niṣpadyeta sarastaṭe \|*  
*abhīṣṭadevatāyuktaṃ teṣāṃ pārtha kimucyate \|\| 86 \|\|*

85-86. The graceful people build the tanks close to the cities, because the purpose of the people is served in both the ways. Close to such a tank, all the gods appear what could be spoken about them? The time upto which the bricks or the small boats remain at the same level as the earth, for an equal time the builder of the said temple is honoured in the heaven.

## \|\| 3.127.87-89 \|\|

*na bhavaṃtīṣṭikā yāvaddroṇī vā bhūmisannibhā \|*  
*svarge mahīyate tāvatkārako devaveśmanaḥ \|\| 87 \|\|*

*bhogyasthāne kṛtaḥ kūpaḥ susvādusalilastathā \|*  
*dṛḍharajjusamāyuktaḥ punātyāsaptamaṃ kulam \|\| 88 \|\|*

*yasya svādujalaṃ kūpe pibaṃti satataṃ janāḥ \|*  
*kiṃ tena na kṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ savasattvopakāriṇā \|\| 89 \|\|*

87-89. The place which is of the common interest to all, a well of the tasty water should be constructed and by so doing, the seven generations of the builder get redeemed. The tasty water of such a well is consumed by all at all times. The merits earned by such a person who is beneficial for all, cannot be earned by anyone else.

## \|\| 3.127.90-91 \|\|

*yaḥ prāsādānracayati śubhāndevatānāṃ taḍāge kīrtistasya bhramati vipulā vaṃśamārgānuyātā \|*  
*divyānbhogānbhajati ca sadā kārakaścāprameyānbhuktvā saukhyaṃ punarapi ca bhaveccakravartī pṛthivyām \|\| 90 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ taḍāgāni bahūdakāni kūpāśca yūpāśca pratiśrayāśca \|*  
*annapradānaṃ madhurā ca vāṇī yamasya te nirvacanī bhavaṃti \|\| 91 \|\|*

90-91. A person who builds a room or a temple at the bank of the tank or a well, earns enormous glory and his family traditions always remain alive. Enjoying several types of everlasting pleasures in the world, he becomes a Cakravarti king on earth who builds many of the tanks, wells, pillars, alms-houses (for the use of pilgrims). The charities are always given by him. His tongue is always sweet. Such people are beyond description by Yama.

## Chapter 128. Completion of religious rites for planting of trees etc.

## \|\| 3.128.1 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*vṛkṣāropaṇamāhātmyaṃ vada devakinandana \|*  
*udyāpanavidhiṃ caiva sarahasyaṃ samāsataḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Yudhisthira said- О son of Devaki, what is the importance of the planting of the trees? You also kindly reveal the secrets.

## \|\| 3.128.2-6 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*varaṃ bhūmiruhāḥ pañca nagakāṣṭharuhā daśa \|*  
*patraiḥ puṣpaiḥ phalairmūlaiḥ kurvaṃti pitṛtarpaṇam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*bahubhirmṛtakiñjātaiḥ putrairdharmārthavarjitaiḥ \|*  
*varameke pathitaruryatra viśramate janaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*prāṇinaḥ prīṇayaṃti sma cchāyāvalkalapallavaiḥ \|*  
*ghanacchadāḥ sutaravaḥ puṣpairdevānphalaiḥ pitṝn \|\| 4 \|\|*

*puṣpapatraphalacchāyāmūlavalkaladārubhiḥ \|*  
*dhanyā mahīruhā yeṣāṃ viphalā yāṃti nārthinaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*putrāḥ saṃvatsarasyāṃte śrāddhaṃ kurvaṃti vā na vā \|*  
*pratyahaṃ pādapāḥ puṣṭiṃ śreyo'rthaṃ janayaṃti hi \|\| 6 \|\|*

2-6. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – The planting of five trees on earth and ten trees over the mountain are said to be the best, because the trees with their fruits, roots, flowers, as well as the leaves, please the manes. What could be the benefit for the sons, who are devoid of dharma and who are like the dead ones, while remaining alive? A single tree planted over the path is considered to be the best in the cool shade of which traveler enjoys the comfort. The excellent trees with thick shade make the people and the manes delightful with their barks, shade, the leaves and the flowers. The persons who plant the trees, these trees serve the people with their leavers, flowers, fruits, roots, the bark and the wood, and serve the living beings. Therefore, these trees are quite graceful, because they do not disappoint the supplicants, whether a son does the sraddha after the year or not, it is not at all certain, but the cluster of trees always feeds the people and make them comfortable.

## \|\| 3.128.7-8 \|\|

*na tatkarotyagnihotraṃ sukhaṃ yadyoṣitaḥ sutaḥ \|*  
*yatkaroti ghanacchāyaḥ pādapaḥ pathi ropitaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sacchāyā ca sapuṣpā ca saphalā vṛkṣavāṭikā \|*  
*kulayoṣeva bhavati bhartṛlokadvayānugā \|\| 8 \|\|*

7-8. A son bom of one’s own married life, who performs the fire sacrifices, provides comforts in future. But the comforts cannot reach the place where the shady trees are being planted on the path. The beautiful shade, the flowers and the fruits growing in an orchard, provide comforts to both the races like a chaste wife who makes both the races delightful.

## \|\| 3.128.9 \|\|

*aśokaphalāvakarā tilakālaṃkṛtānanā \|*  
*sarvopabhoga veśyeva vāṭikā rasikā sadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

9\. The orchard decorated with the Asoka fruits is made spotless. Besides the orchard in which the trees are grown, looks like a decorated whore, who is used by all.

## \|\| 3.128.10 \|\|

*sadā sa tīrthī bhavati sadā dānaṃ prayacchati \|*  
*sadā yajñaṃ sa yajate yo ropayati pādapam \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A person who plants the trees, always remains shining like the Sun, always gives charities and always performs the yajnas.

## \|\| 3.128.11 \|\|

*aśvatthamekaṃ picumaṃdamekaṃ nyagrodhamekaṃ daśa ciñciṇīkān \|*  
*kapitthabilvāmalakītrayaṃ ca pañcāmravāpī narakaṃ na paśyet \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. One who plants a tree, each of the species of plpala, nima and banyan, then three trees each one of tamarind, feronia elephantum, wood apple, myrobalan, five mango trees, besides the one who digs a step-well, can never fall in the hell.

## \|\| 3.128.12 \|\|

*puṣpopagaṃdhāḍhyaphalopagandhaṃ yaḥ pādapaṃ sparśayate dvijāya \|*  
*sa strīsamṛddhaṃ vahuratnapūrṇaṃ labhedvimānapratimaṃ gṛhaṃ vai \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. A person who gives away a tree laden with fruits, flowers and fragrance, he flourishes with his wife and achieves a house which is filled with a large number of gems and which resembles a plane.

## \|\| 3.128.13-14 \|\|

*pratiśrayāśrānta samāśrayatvātsamīhitaṃ tatra phalaṃ bubhukṣoḥ \|*  
*apatyamekaṃ paralokahetorvimṛśyatāṃ kiṃ taravo na ropitāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*na khānitāḥ puṣkariṇyo ropitā na mahīruhāḥ \|*  
*māturyauvanacaureṇa tena jātena kiṃ kṛtam \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. Such of the people who are desirous of eating the fruit, it is to be said to them that the trees provide home like comforts and are also beneficial for the other world, why did you not plant such trees? Because a person who has not constructed a tank and has also not planted a tree, what is the use of the birth of such a person, who simply stole the youth of his mother?

## \|\| 3.128.15 \|\|

*chāyāmanyasya kurvaṃti tiṣṭhaṃti svayamātape \|*  
*phalaṃti ca parārtheṣu na svārtheṣu mahādrumāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. The great trees themselves stand in the sunshine and provide their shade for the sake of others. They always blossom, bear fruit for the sake of others and not for selfish use.

## \|\| 3.128.16-18 \|\|

*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi vṛkṣasyodyāpane vidhim \|*  
*sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ sarvakīrtivivarddhanam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*aputrayā purā pārtha pārvatyā mandarācale \|*  
*aśokaḥ śokaśamanaḥ putratve parikalpitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*jātakarmādikāstasya yāḥ kriyāḥ kila buddhiman \|*  
*carakātripurāṇoktāstāḥ śṛṇuṣva yudhiṣṭhira \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. Hereafter, I am going to speak out the religious rites at the time of the planting of the trees which remove all the sins and bestows fourfold glory to a person. О Partha, while living over the Mandaracala mountain, when Parvati was childless, she planted an Asoka tree and imagined the same to be her son. She performed the name giving ceremony of the tree as well performed the other rites. This has been prescribed by Caraka and the other Puranas. О Yudhisthira, you please listen.

## \|\| 3.128.19-21 \|\|

*tato mūle ghanadalo valgucchāyāṃgapallavaḥ \|*  
*śītavātātapasahaḥ saṃskāryastaruṇastaruḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*strīnāmakaṃṭakīkubjakīṭavṛścikakoṭaraḥ \|*  
*nodyāpyaḥ pādapaḥ pārtha śiṣṭānāṃ yo na saṃmataḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*ālavāle suvihite śubhe baddhacatuṣkike \|*  
*śodhayitvā tamuddeśaṃ suguptaṃ kārayettataḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. The samskaras of such a youthful tree should be performed. It should have the roots, thick leaves, pleasant shade and the tender shoots and should be able to face the cold, storms and the sun rays. Such of the trees which have the feminine names, are thorny, hunch backed and in the hollows of which the insects or scorpions are filled, they should not be consecrated. Only the trees which are recommended by the learned people alone should be consecrated. A basin should be made round the tree, besides a circular pedestal and the place should then be protected.

## \|\| 3.128.22-24 \|\|

*sadaivodyāpanaṃ pārtha pādapānāṃ praśasyate \|*  
*śubhe'hni viprakathite grahanakṣatrasaṃyute \|\| 22 \|\|*

*patākālaṃkṛtaṃ vṛkṣaṃ pūrvedyuradhivāsayet \|*  
*raktavastraiḥ samācchādya raktasūtreṇa veṣṭayet \|\| 23 \|\|*

*piṣṭātakenāvakiretsarvauṣadhyā ca pādapam \|*  
*sthāpayetpūrṇakalaśāṃścaturdikṣu vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

22-24. О Partha, the consecration of the trees is a praiseworthy activity. Therefore, in consultation with a Brahmana and during an appropriate constellation, an auspicious flag should be raised close to the tree. The Adhivasa ceremony should be performed initially, coiling a red cloth round it with a red cord. Then the tree should be plastered with the red paste. Four pitchers should be placed on all the four sides of the tree.

## \|\| 3.128.25 \|\|

*pallavālaṃkṛtamukhānsitacandanacarcitān \|*  
*sitavāsoyugacchannānsakalānratnagarbhiṇaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

25\. The upper portion of the pitchers should be covered with the tender leaves. The sandal paste should be applied to them and they should be covered with the four clothes. The gems should be poured into each one of them.

## \|\| 3.128.26 \|\|

*patākālaṃkṛtāḥ sarve kāryāstatsannidhau drumāḥ \|*  
*mūlavinyastakalaśā raktasūtrāvaguṇṭhitāḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. All the flags near them should be well decorated. At the base of all of them, the pitchers with red threads placed around their necks should be placed on all the sides.

## \|\| 3.128.27-32 \|\|

*raktapītasitācchādaiścarcitāḥ sumanoharaiḥ \|*  
*kaladhautamayānyatra phalāni daśa paṃca vā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tāmrapātryāṃ sabījāni saralānyadhivāsayet \|*  
*tūryamaṅgalaghoṣeṇa caturdikṣu kṣipedbalim \|\| 28 \|\|*

*indrādilokapālebhyo bhūtebhyo maṃtravidguruḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prabhāte vimale kuṃḍaṃ kṛtvā samekhalam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*grahayajñavidhānena śāṃtikarma samārabhet \|*  
*suvarṇālaṃkṛtānkṛtvā brāhmaṇānvedapāragān \|\| 30 \|\|*

*caturo'ṣṭau yathāśaktyā vāsobhirabhipūjayet \|*  
*tilājyena ca homaḥ syāttuṣṭipuṣṭikaraḥ sadā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*mātaraṃ sthāpayitvāgre pūjayetkusumākṣataiḥ \|*  
*śrapayitvā caruṃ samyakpāyasādyapariplutam \|\| 32 \|\|*

27-32. The pitchers should be of red, white and yellow colours. Delicious five to ten fruits should also be placed in a copper vase and Adhivasana should be performed for them. Blowing the trumpets and other auspicious music should be played upon, in all the directions. The offerings should be made for Indra and other Lokapalas. Thereafter, on the next day, during the auspicious day break, a kunda with a chain should be built and with the performance of yajna, the ceremony of peace should be performed. In the sacrifice, four or eight Brahmanas, as per one’s means, should be offered with gold ornaments as well as the costumes. For increase in the satisfaction and the growth, while performing homa with sesamum seeds and ghi, the Matrkas should be lodged in a line and should be worshipped with the offering of the flowers and unbroken rice. Thereafter, the offering of payasam mixed with ghi should be made in the fire.

## \|\| 3.128.33-35 \|\|

*homādau jātakarmādi godānaṃ yāvadeva tu \|*  
*pādapaṃ snāpayitvā tu samaṃtraistīrthavāribhiḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*jātakaṃ nāmakaraṇamannaprāśanameva ca \|*  
*suvarṇasūcyā kurvīta karṇavedhaṃ vidhānavit \|\| 34 \|\|*

*jātarūpakṣureṇātra cūḍākāryā yathākramam \|*  
*badhnīyānmekhalāṃ mauñjīṃ vāsaśca paridhāpayet \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. At the start of homa, the names to the trees should be given, besides the cows should also be given over in charity. While performing the same, the mantras should be recited initially and the trees should be bathed with the water of the holy places, followed by the ceremonies of giving names to each one of them, tasting of food, piercing of the ear with the golden needle and shaving of the hair with the golden blade. All these ceremonies should be performed adequately. Besides the mekhala or the waist band of munja grass should also be tied, besides offering the costumes.

## \|\| 3.128.36 \|\|

*yajamānastataḥ snātaḥ śuklāṃbaradharaḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*puṣpāñjaliḥ samabhyetya maṃtrametamudīrayet \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The yajamana should then take his bath and clad himself in white clothes. Purifying himself, carrying the cup full of flowers, he should beg forgiveness, reciting the mantras.

## \|\| 3.128.37-38 \|\|

*ye śākhinaḥ śikhariṇāṃ śirasā vibhūṣā ye nandanādiṣu vaneṣu kṛtapratiṣṭhāḥ \|*  
*ye kāmadāḥ suranaroragakinnarāṇāṃ te me natasya duritārtiharā bhavaṃtu \|\| 37 \|\|*

*etairdvijairvidhivaraprahuto hutāśaḥ paśyatyasāvahimadīdhitiraṃbarasthaḥ \|*  
*tvaṃ vṛkṣa putraparikalpanayā vṛto'si kāryaṃ sadaiva bhavatā mama putrakāryam \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. “О trees, you are lodged over the mountain peaks. Decorating them, you are well established in the Nandana and other forests. You fulfill the desires of the gods, humans, serpents, besides the kinnaras, you remove all my misfortunes. The offerings which have been dropped by these excellent Brāhmaṇas in an appropriate manner, the fire flames getting ignited have reached the sky as if observing us all. О tree, we have symbolized you as a son. Therefore, you should perform all the duties which are desired of a son.”

## \|\| 3.128.39-41 \|\|

*ityevamuktvā taṃ vṛkṣaṃ lālayitvā punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*ghṛtapātre svavadanaṃ dṛṣṭvāśiṣamudīrayet \|\| 39 \|\|*

*aṅgādaṅgātsaṃbhavasi hṛdayādabhijāyase \|*  
*ātmā vai putranāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śatam \|\| 40 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇānāṃ tato deyā dakṣiṇā hṛṣṭamānasaiḥ \|*  
*sthāpakāya śubhāṃ dhenuṃ dattvā kuryānmahotsavam \|\| 41 \|\|*

39-41. Thus speaking and seeing the tree tenderly, one should see his own face in a vase filled with ghi. Then he should say – “Your limbs have emerged out of my limbs, because one’s own soul becomes popular as the son. Therefore, you enjoy the life of hundreds of years.” Thereafter, feeling delighted, the Brahmanas should be given the daksina and the Acdrya should be given over the cows.

## \|\| 3.128.42 \|\|

*dīnānāthajanānāṃ ca bhojanaṃ cānivāritam \|*  
*itareṣāṃ pradātavyaṃ saṃtuṣṭena surāsavam \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. In these celebrations, the poor, the orphans and the deprived people should essentially be served the food, while the beverages should be served to the other people.

## \|\| 3.128.43 \|\|

*jñātibandhujanaiḥ sārddhaṃ svayaṃ bhuñjīta kāmataḥ \|*  
*preṣyāḥ karmakarāḥ sarve pūjanīyāḥ svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. Other friends and relatives should also be served with food. The workers and the labourers should be pleased as per the means of a person.

## \|\| 3.128.44 \|\|

*ya evaṃ kurute pārtha vṛkṣāṇāṃ mahadutsavam \|*  
*sarvakāmānavāpnoti ihaloke paratra ca \|\| 44 \|\|*

44\. О Partha, those who perform the consecration ceremony of the trees, they have their desires fulfilled during this world and beyond even.

## \|\| 3.128.45 \|\|

*putrairvinā śubhagatirna bhavennarāṇāṃ duṣputrakairiti tathobhayalokanāśaḥ \|*  
*etadvicārya sudhiyā paripālya vṛkṣānputrāḥ purāṇavidhinā parikalpanīyā \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. It has been ordained in the Sastras that one does not achieve the highest position without a son and by having a wicked son, both the lokas get destroyed. Realizing this, the learned people should plant the trees like the son and should take care of them accordingly.

## Chapter 129. Method of Devapuja

## \|\| 3.129.1 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*ye mānavāstridaśamūrtiniketanāni kurvaṃti sādhujanadṛṣṭimanoharāṇi \|*  
*teṣāṃ mṛte'tha paramārthamaye śarīre loke paribhramati kīrtimayaṃ śarīram \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – Such of the people who build the temples for the consecration of the images of the deities, which allure or entice the minds of the noble people, after the shedding away of the human bodies, their glorious and immortal bodies always keep on roaming about.

## \|\| 3.129.2-3 \|\|

*yaḥ kārayeddvārasitābhragauramuttuṃgasaudhadhavalāyatanaṃ surāṇām \|*  
*caṃdrāvadātabhavane divi labdhasaukhyo rājyaśriyaṃ sa bhuvi bodhayutāmupaiti \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ye kārayaṃti surasadmasu devatānāmarcāḥ suvarṇarajatāyasaśailatāmrāḥ \|*  
*sāmaṃtamaulimaṇiraśmisamamarcitāste siṃhāsane'ṅgadakirīṭabhṛto'vabhāṃti \|\| 3 \|\|*

2-3. Like the white clouds which are devoid of the water, the white gates and like the high white buildings, when the temples are built, then those people are treated like the lunar rays of the heaven, enjoying the best of comforts in the heaven, descend on the earth with goddess Laksmi on earth, when they possess enough of riches. People who make the images of gods in gold, silver, iron, stone and copper, are adorned with the kirita crown as well as the armlets and are established over the throne, who is adorned by his courtiers always.

## \|\| 3.129.4 \|\|

*ye merumaulisurasaṃghakṛtābhiṣekāḥ pañcāmṛtaiḥ suravarānabhiṣecayaṃti \|*  
*te divyakalpamabhidhārya sureśvaratvaṃ rājyābhiṣekamatulaṃ punarāpnuvaṃti \|\| 4 \|\|*

4\. The gods who dwell over the peaks of the Mem mountain and a person who performs the abhiseka for them, he enjoys the comfort of a god (in the heaven) for a period of the divine kalpa and is then himself established as a great monarch.

## \|\| 3.129.5 \|\|

*ye śailarājamalayodbhavacaṃdanena satkuṃkumena ca surānanulepayaṃti \|*  
*te divyagandhapaṭavāsasugaṃdhidehā naṃdaṃti naṃdanavaneṣu sahāpsarobhiḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. The people who offer paste of the sandalwood trees which are grown in the Malayagiri – the lord of the mountain, they achieve a divine body, clad in divine costumes, having the divine fragrance and they play with the Apsaras in the Nandanavana.

## \|\| 3.129.6 \|\|

*gaṃdhāḍhyajātikamalotpaladivyapuṣpairdevānnavairanudinaṃ nanu ye'rcayaṃti \|*  
*puṣpottamairnarapatitvamavāpya te'pi yāsyaṃti kuṃdadhavalāmacireṇa siddhim \|\| 6 \|\|*

6\. With the offering of the fragrant jasmine flowers and the divine flowers of the blue lotus, a person who adores the deities, he achieves the position of a king and then attains the spotless glory very shortly.

## \|\| 3.129.7 \|\|

*āmodibhirhimaturuṣkasugandhadhūpairye mānavāḥ suravarānapi dhūpayaṃti \|*  
*karpūradhāranibhagandhavarā bhirāme svarge vimānavati te bhavane ramaṃte \|\| 7 \|\|*

7\. The snow, incense, benzoic and fragrant flowers when offered to the gods by a person, then like the stream of camphor, they always stay in the buildings which are filled with divine fragrance in the heaven.

## \|\| 3.129.8-9 \|\|

*dodhūyate kanakadaṃḍavirājitaiśca saccāmarairdhavalakuṇḍalasundarībhiḥ \|*  
*divyāṃbarasraganulepanabhūṣi tāṅgāṃ kṛtvā sureśabhavanāṃbaravastrapūjām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dedīpyate dinakarojjvalapadmarāgaratnaprabhācchuritahemamaye vimāne \|*  
*divyāṃganāparivṛto nayanābhirāmaḥ prajvālya dīpamamalaṃ bhavane surāṇām \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. The damsels adorned with the strong earrings serve the people there with the flywhisks having the grips of gold. Such people are clad in divine garments, garlands, paste, who worship also the temples of the gods. They have the lustre resembling the Sun and they are seated over the planes, which are decorated with rubies issuing the enormous lustre. Those who give away the lamps in the temples, such donors are also serving as the delight of the people’s eyes.

## \|\| 3.129.10 \|\|

*yo jāgaraṃ suravarābhimato dadāti caitrotsavādidivaseṣvapi tūryanādaiḥ \|*  
*vīṇāsuveṇumadhurasvarabhāṣi ṇībhiḥ saṃgīyate ca sa kṛśodarakinnarībhiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. During the months of Caitra and others, on the days of the festivities, playing on the musical instruments besides the blowing of the trumpets, one who resorts to the awakening before the gods, he enjoys company of the kinnaras in the heaven, who have sweet speech, with slender waists and who play on vina and flute.

## \|\| 3.129.11-13 \|\|

*kurvati ye sadupalenadhāturāgasaṃmārjanaṃ suravarāyatane'nuraktāḥ \|*  
*muktākalāpamapi kāṃcanabhakti citrairvaiḍūryakṛṭṭimatale divi te vasaṃti \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dadyācca yaḥ paramabhaktiyutaḥ surāṇāṃ ghaṇṭāvitānavaracāmaramātapatram \|*  
*keyūrahāramaṇikuṇḍalabhūṣi tosau ratnādhipo vasati bhūtalacakravartī \|\| 12 \|\|*

*abhyarcayetprativacaḥ kusumairvicitrairdevādhidevaparisaṃstutapādapadmān \|*  
*bhaktyā prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ praṇamaṃti devāṃste bhūrbhuvaḥ svarmahimāptaphalā bhavaṃti \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. The people who decorate the temples with various types of colours besides brooming them regularly, they in turn earn their stay in the heaven. Such of the people who make beautiful drawings filled with gold and lapiz lazuli on the walls as well as the floor, and also give away a bell, canopies, excellent flywhisks besides the umbrella for the sake of the gods, such people getting adorned with waist-lets, armlets, garlands, gems and earrings, become the Cakravarti kings over the earth. Those, who offering the flowers of different kinds, offer their salutation at the lotus like feet of the gods with love and devotion, they becoming blissful, achieve the fruit of bhur bhuvah svah.

## Chapter 130. Method of giving away the lamp

## \|\| 3.130.1-2 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*bhagavankena tapasā vratena niyamena vā \|*  
*dānena kena vā loke projjvaltvaṃ prajāyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

*atitejo mahaddīptaṃ dīptāṃśukiraṇojjvalam \|*  
*śarīraṃ jāyate yena tanme vaktumathārhasi \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Yudhisthira said – О lord, by which types of tapas, vrata or the charities, one achieves the unprecedented brightness. You kindly let me know the method by which the extremely illustrious bright body shining like the sun rays, could be achieved on earth. You kindly tell me the way out.

## \|\| 3.130.3-7 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*mathurāyāṃ purā pārtha piṅgalo nāma tāpasaḥ \|*  
*āgataḥ sa ca me patnyā jāmbavatyā prapūjitaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*praṣṭaśca praśramevaitaṃ sa cāvocadyathātatham \|*  
*tayāpi me samākhyātaṃ tatsarvaṃ te vadāmyaham \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yadāyadā nṛpaśreṣṭha puṇyakālaḥ prapadyate \|*  
*saṃkrātau sūryagrahaṇe candraparvaṇi vaidhṛtau \|\| 5 \|\|*

*uttare tvayane prāpte dakṣiṇe viṣuve tathā \|*  
*ekādaśyāṃ śuklapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ dinakṣaye \|\| 6 \|\|*

*saptamyāmatha vāṣṭamyāṃ snātvā vrataparo naraḥ \|*  
*nārī vā bhūmidevebhyaḥ prayacchetprayatāṃgaṇe \|*  
*ghṛtakuṃbhena dīpena prajvalaṃtaṃ pradīpakam \|\| 7 \|\|*

3-7. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О Partha, in earlier times, once a mendicant named Pingala arrived before me in Mathura. He was adored by my beloved Jambavati. On her enquiry from the mendicant, whatever reply she got from him, the same is being repeated by me, because thereafter, Jambavati narrated everything to me verbatim. О best of the rulers, on the auspicious time like the first day of the month during the solar or lunar eclipses, on the conclusion of ayana or the six months, the equinox, bright eleventh moon day of the month, dark fourteenth day of the fortnight, seventh moon day and on the eighth moon day, while taking his bath and performing the vrata, one should place a lamp of ghi in the middle of the courtyard of the house for the sake of the earth goddess. The vrata should be performed by both a man and a woman.

## \|\| 3.130.8 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭir uvāca \|*  
*bhūmidevā iti proktaṃ yattvayā madhusūdana \|*  
*kimetatkautukaṃ me'sti saṃśayaṃ chettumarhasi \|\| 8 \|\|*

8\. Yudhisthira said – О Madhusudana, what type of the sport has been stated by you with the mentioning of the Earth goddess? You kindly remove my doubt.

## \|\| 3.130.9-13 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*purā kṛtayugasyādau triśaṃkurnāma pārthivaḥ \|*  
*sa svargaṃ gantukāmo'bhūccharīreṇa narottama \|*  
*tataścaṇḍālatāṃ nīto vaśiṣṭhena mahātmanā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*triśaṃkuḥ sarvamācakhyau viśvāmitrāya dhīmate \|*  
*so'pi manyuvaśādyajñaṃ cakārāhūya devatāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*na tā haviḥ pratyagṛhṇaṃstataḥ kruddhaḥ kuśātmajaḥ \|*  
*viśvāmitrastu kopena cakārānyānsurottamān \|\| 11 \|\|*

*śṛṃgāṭakā nnālikerānpacanānānajauḍakān \|*  
*medhārathadavārtākatārikūṣmaṇḍakodravān \|\| 12 \|\|*

*uṣṭrānmanujadevāṃśca krodhānmuniravāsṛjat \|*  
*cakārānyānsapta ṛṣīnpratimāsaṃ surottamān \|\| 13 \|\|*

9-13. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – O best of the humans, in earlier times, during the Krtayuga, there had been a king known by the name of Trisanku, who was desirous of reaching the heaven with the human body that he possessed on earth. Because of his insisting for the same, the sage Vasistha pronounced a curse on him to become а Candala. When he was turned into a Candala, he expressed his desire to the Maharsi Visvamitra. On hearing his words, Maharsi Visvamitra also getting enraged, started performing a yajna invoking the gods. But the gods refused to accept their respective parts of havi. Visvamitra on his part, getting enraged, started invoking another set of gods. In utter rage, Visvamitra also created thorny fruit or water chestnut, coconut, cucumber, Anajaudaka, Medharatha, Vartaki, Tari, water melon, small grains, camels, humans besides die gods.

## \|\| 3.130.14-17 \|\|

*tataḥ śakraḥ samāgamya viśvāmitraṃ prasādya vai \|*  
*sṛṣṭiṃ nivārayāmāsa ye sṛṣṭāste tathāpi ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*martya loke ca te sarve devā devakuleṣvatha \|*  
*maṃtrairnibaddhāḥ piṇḍīṣu sthitā mūrtibhṛto yathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*brahmā viṣṇustathā rudro ye cānye devatāgaṇāḥ \|*  
*lokānāmupakārāya martyalokamupāgatāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*pratimāsu sthitāḥ śaśvadbhogānbhuñjati śāśvatān \|*  
*varapradāśca bhaktānāmiti te guhyamīritam \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. Observing the creation of the Saptarsis and the gods every month, Indra came to him and pleaded Visvamitra and dissuaded him from further creation. But the gods who had already been created, they are lodged on earth like the images. Thus, all the gods like Brahma and others were lodged in the images with the reciting of the mantras. Similarly, Brahma, Viṣṇu and Rudra, besides the other gods, remained on earth for the welfare of the people, getting enshrined in the images and enjoy all the pleasures there, besides bestowing boons to their devotee. This is the secret story which had been revealed by Narada.

## \|\| 3.130.18-20 \|\|

*tebhyaḥ purastāddātavyo dīpyamānaḥ pradīpakaḥ \|*  
*sūryāya raktavastreṇa pūrṇavartiṃ ghṛtairyutām \|*  
*catuḥprasthaiḥ prajvalantīṃ maṃtreṇānena dāpayet \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tadvi ṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyaṃti sūrayaḥ \|*  
*divīva cakṣurātatam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pītavastreṇa kṛṣṇāya śvetavastreṇa śūline \|*  
*kausuṃbhavastreṇāḍhyena gaurīmuddiśya dāpayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. The burning lamps are placed before the images of those gods, besides the red cloth, and four prasthas of ghi in which wick should keep on burning. It should be placed before Viṣṇu, reciting the mantras. The said form of Viṣṇu is always meditated upon by the learned people. Then reciting the mantras, lord Kṛṣṇa should be offered a yellow garment, Siva should be offered the white garment and the goddess Gauri should be offered the costumes of the colour of flowers.

## \|\| 3.130.21-22 \|\|

*lākṣāraktena durgāyai pūrṇavarti prabodhayet \|*  
*nīlavastreṇa kāmāya gaṇanāthāya khādiraiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*nāgebhyaḥ kṛṣṇavastreṇa grahebhya iṣikā yudhām \|*  
*devāṃganā pitṛbhyastu pitṛvartiṃ prabodhayet \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. Durga should be offered a cloth of red colour. For her, a complete wick should be made. Similarly, the blue cloth should be given over to Kamadeva. Gananatha should be offered the cloth of maroon colour, while the serpents should be offered the black cloth. Such of the planets who have Isikayudha with them, for the divine damsels as well as for the manes, the wick should be lighted. I am also revealing some speciality, you please listen.

## \|\| 3.130.23-24 \|\|

*viśeṣaṃ śṛṇu sūryāya pūrṇavartirnigadyate \|*  
*śivāyeśvaravartīti bhogavartirjanārdane \|\| 23 \|\|*

*padmavartirviriṃcāya gauryyai saubhāgyavartikā \|*  
*nāgebhyo nāgavartīti grahavartiryudhiṣṭhira \|\| 24 \|\|*

23-24. The wick which is to be offered to the sun is called the Purnavarti (full wick); the wick which is to be given to lord Siva is known as Isvaravarti, the one which is meant for Janardana is said to be the Bhogavarti; the one which is to be offered to Brahma is known as the Padmavarti; the one which is to be given to the goddess Gauri is known as Saubhagyavarti. For the one which is to be offered to the serpents, is known as Nagavarti and the one which is to be given to the planets, it is known as Grahavarti.

## \|\| 3.130.25-30 \|\|

*netrapaṭṭena madhunā ghṛtena madhukuṃḍake \|*  
*arcite carcite caiva lalitāyai prabodhayet \|\| 25 \|\|*

*maṃtreṇānena rājendra tanniśāmaya vaidikam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*1 agre tvāṃ kāmyayā girā tubhyaṃ tā girasastu viśvāḥ \|*  
*sukṣitayaḥ pṛthakpṛthak \|\| 27 \|\|*

*2 agne kāmāya jegire agnipriyeṣu dhāmasu \|*  
*kāmo bhūtasya bhavyasya samrāḍeko virājati tābhyāṃ nāma svāhā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*evametena vidhinā yaḥ prayacchati dīpakam \|*  
*vistīrṇe vipule pātre ghṛtakumbhe niyojitam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*yāṃti te brahmasadanaṃ vimānenārkavarcasā \|*  
*tiṣṭhaṃti dyotamānāste yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 30 \|\|*

25-30. О Yudhisthira, a bondage of cloth should be well soaked in ghi and for offering it to the goddess Lalita, the relevant mantras are being spoken by me. You please listen, which are said to be – “Agne tvam kamyaya gira tubhyamta girasastu visvah, suksitayah prthakprthaka. Agne kamaya jegire agni-priyesu dhamasu. Kamo bhutasya bhavyasya samradeko virajati tabhyam nama svaha.” О Rajendra, with the following of this process, a vast vase filled with ghi, when offered as the lamp to the Sungod, they looking graceful being illustrious, finally achieve the abode of Brahma. Even at the time of the great dissolution, they feel comfortable in the sky.

## \|\| 3.130.31-32 \|\|

*sadīpe tu yathā deśe cakṣūṃṣi balavanti hi \|*  
*tathā dīpasya dātāro bhavaṃti saphalekṣaṇāḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*yathaivordhvaṃ gatirnityaṃ rājandīpaśikhāsu vai \|*  
*dīpadātustathaivordhvaṃ gatirbhavati śobhanā \|\| 32 \|\|*

31-32. By placing a lamp at an appropriate place, the person who does so, he possesses the healthy and successful eyes. О king, as a long flame always bums upwards, similarly, a person who gives away a lamp in charity, he always attains the graceful higher position.

## \|\| 3.130.33-35 \|\|

*ghṛtena dīpo dātavyo rājaṃstailena vā punaḥ \|*  
*vasāmajjādibhirdeyo na tu dīpaḥ kathañcana \|\| 33 \|\|*

*dīpastailena kartavyo na tu karma vijānatā \|*  
*nirvāpaṇaṃ ca dīpasya hiṃsanaṃ ca vigarhitam \|\| 34 \|\|*

*yaḥ kuryātkarmaṇā tena syādasau puṣpitekṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*dīpahartā bhavatyaṃdhaḥ kāṇo nirvāpako bhavet \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. О king, besides the lamp, the lamp with oil can also be donated. But the lamp filled with fat or marrow, should never be donated. A learned and an active person should not extinguish the lamp which amounts to terror because the people who do so, are likely to lose their eyesight. A person who steals the lamp becomes blind, while who extinguishes it becomes blind of one eye.

## \|\| 3.130.36 \|\|

*padmasūtrodbhavāṃ vartiṃ gaṃdhatailena dīpitām \|*  
*virogaḥ subhagaścaiva dattvā bhavati mānavaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

36\. The use of lotus stalk as the wick, when lighted and given over to a deity, the donor becomes free from ailment besides getting fortunes.

## \|\| 3.130.37 \|\|

*prajvālya devadevasya karpūreṇa tu dīpakam \|*  
*aśvamedhamavāpnoti kulaṃ caiva samuddharet \|\| 37 \|\|*

37\. In case the lamp of camphor is offered to the god of gods, one earns the merit of performing the Asvamedha sacrifice, besides his entire family gets redeemed.

## \|\| 3.130.38 \|\|

*etanmayoktaṃ tava dīpadānaphalaṃ samagraṃ kuruvaṃśacandra \|*  
*śrutvā yathāvatsatataṃ hi deyā dīpāstvayā viprasurālayeṣu \|\| 38 \|\|*

38\. О moon of the race of Kuru, I have spoken to you about the donation of lamps and its importance, listening to which you should always donate lamps in the abode of the Brahmanas as well as the temples.

## \|\| 3.130.39 \|\|

*atrāpyudāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam \|*  
*dīpadānāllalitayā yadavāptaṃ purā'nagha \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. О sinless one, I am going to speak out to you an event of old history in which the goddess Lalita gave away in charity the lamps and the related merit she earned therefrom, in considerable detail.

## \|\| 3.130.40-41 \|\|

*āsīccitrarathonāma vidarbheṣu mahīpatiḥ \|*  
*tasya putraśataṃ rājño jajñe pañcadaśottaram \|\| 40 \|\|*

*ekaiva kanyā tasyāsīllalitā nāma nāmataḥ \|*  
*sarvalakṣaṇasampannā rūpeṇāpratimā bhuvi \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. There had been a king named Citraratha of Vidarbha country, who had a hundred and fifteen sons, besides a daughter named Lalita. She possessed all the noble and auspicious symptoms, besides being extremely beautiful.

## \|\| 3.130.42-43 \|\|

*tāṃ dadau kāśirājāya cārvaṃgīṃ cārudharmaṇe \|*  
*śatānyanyāni bhāryāṇāṃ trīṇyāsaṃścārudharmaṇaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tāsāṃ madhye'gramahiṣī lalitā sāpyathābhavat \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. Such a beautiful daughter was given over by the king of Vidarbha to the king of Kāśī in marriage. Kāśīraja had already a hundred and three beautiful queens, out of whom Lalita became the chief queen.

## \|\| 3.130.44-46 \|\|

*viṣṇorāyatane sā tu sahasraṃ paridīpakān \|*  
*prajvālayantyanudinaṃ divārātramanirvṛtam \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tāmisramāśvayukpakṣaṃ śuklapakṣaṃ ca kārttikam \|*  
*tasyāḥ prajvalito dīpa uccasthānakṛtaḥ śubhaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*tasminkāle tathā nityaṃ brāhmaṇāvasathe ca sā \|*  
*vyagrā bhavati sāyāhne dīpapreṣaṇatatparā \|\| 46 \|\|*

44-46. She used to light thousands of lamps in the temple of Viṣṇu, daily. These lamps burnt throughout the day and night. The light of her lamps was spread in the sky during both the fortnights of the month of Kartika. During those days, she lighted the lamps in the abodes of the Brahmanas as well as the temples, in which she had to spend enough of riches.

## \|\| 3.130.47-50 \|\|

*catuṣpatheṣu rathyāsu devatāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*caityavṛkṣeṣu goṣṭheṣu parvatānāṃ ca mūrddhasu \|\| 47 \|\|*

*pulineṣu nadīnāṃ ca kūpamūleṣu pāṃḍava \|*  
*tāṃ sapatnyo'tha saṃgamya papracchuridamādṛtāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*lalite vada bhadraṃ te lalitaṃ vacanaṃ tathā \|*  
*na tathā balipuṣpeṣu na tathā dvijapūjane \|\| 49 \|\|*

*bhavatyāḥ sumahānyatno dīpaprajvālane yathā \|*  
*tadetatkathayāsmākaṃ lalite kautukaṃ param \|\| 50 \|\|*

47-50. The lamps were burnt near the crossings, streets, temples, below the pipala tree, cowpens, mountain peaks and river banks. The pedestals were used for the burning of the lamps. Once her co-wives went to Lalita and respectfully asked her – “O Lalita, let you meet with welfare, your body is extremely charming. You make all efforts in burning the lamps, the same interest is not found in the offering of bali, flowers and adoration of the Brahmanas. Therefore, О Lalita, you kindly toy to tell us the secret behind it. Because all of us do believe that you must be aware of the importance of the giving away of the lamps in charity.”

## \|\| 3.130.51-54 \|\|

*manyāmahe tvayāvaśyaṃ dīpadānaphalaṃ śrutam \|*  
*lalitovāca \|*  
*nāhaṃ matsariṇī bhadrā na ca rāgādidūṣitā \|\| 51 \|\|*

*ekapatyāśritāḥ sādhvyo bhavatyo mama mānadāḥ \|*  
*apṛthagdharmacaraṇāḥ śṛṇvantu gaditaṃ mama \|\| 52 \|\|*

*mayaitaddīpadānasya yatheṣṭaṃ bhujyate phalam \|*  
*hiraṇyadayitā bhāryā śailarājasutā varā \|\| 53 \|\|*

*umādevīti madreṣu devikā sā saridvarā \|*  
*narāṇāmanukampārthaṃ brahmaṇā hyavatāritā \|*  
*śrutā kiṃ bhavatībhiḥ sā devikā pāpanāśinī \|\| 54 \|\|*

51-54. Lalita said – “I am not at all a jealous woman nor do am blemished woman. All of you are the chaste ladies and are dependent on a single husband. Therefore, all of you are respectable for me. Besides you have the religious inclinations as those of mine. Therefore, you please listen to me, whatever I have to say about the earning of the merit by giving away the lamps in charity. The excellent daughter of Himalaya in the Bhadra country has beautiful limbs and is known by the name of Uma. An excellent river named Devaki also flows there, which had been released by Brahma for the benefit of the people. Have the people not heard of the name of Devaki - the river, which removes all the sins.

## \|\| 3.130.55 \|\|

*tasyāṃ snātvā sakṛnnadyāṃ gāṇapatyamavāpnuyāt \|*  
*tasyāmatha nṛsiṃhākhyaṃ tīrthaṃ kalmaṣanāśanam \|*  
*hariṇā nṛsiṃhavapuṣā yatra snānaṃ kṛtaṃ purā \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. In case one takes a bath in the same even once, he achieves the position of Ganapatya. There is a holy place at the bank of the same river known by Nrsimha-tirtha, which removes all the sins. That is the place, where lord Nrsimha had taken his bath initially.

## \|\| 3.130.56-58 \|\|

*sauvīrarājasya purā maitreyobhūtpurohitaḥ \|*  
*tena cāyatanaṃ viṣṇoḥ kāritaṃ devikātaṭe \|\| 56 \|\|*

*ahanyahani śuśrūṣāṃ puṣpadhūpānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*dīpadānādibhiścaiva cakre tatra sa vai dvijaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*kārttikyāṃ dīpakastatra pradattastena caikadā \|*  
*āsīnnirvāṇabhūyiṣṭho devārcāsu rato niśi \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. This is the place where Sauviraraja is the king and priest Maitreya had built a Viṣṇu temple. The said Brahmana offered the flowers, incense, paste, besides the lamp while worshipping lord Viṣṇu there. Once the same Brahmana, while worshipping lord Viṣṇu there in the month of Kartika, offered a lamp to the lord. But the lamp which was included in the worship of the lord, got extinguished during the night.

## \|\| 3.130.59-61 \|\|

*devatāyatane'vātsaṃ tatrāhamapi mūṣikā \|*  
*pradīpavartiharaṇe kṛtabuddhirvarānanāḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*gṛhītātha mayā vartirvṛkadaṃśo rarāsa ca \|*  
*naṣṭā cāhaṃ tatastasya mārjārasya bhayāturā \|\| 60 \|\|*

*vaktraprāṃtena paśyaṃtyā sa dīpaḥ prerito mayā \|*  
*jajvāla pūrvavaddīptyā tasminnāyatane punaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

59-61. I used to live in the same temple as a mouse. Then I resolved to bring a burning wick from some other place to replace the extinguished one. Accordingly, I carried a burning wick in my mouth, when the dogs started barking. Getting afraid of the cat, pressing the burning wick in my month and with its light, I again went to the temple and placed the burning wick with the extinguished one. Thus I made the lamp to burn as before and it’s started burning as usual.

## \|\| 3.130.62-67 \|\|

*mṛtāhaṃ ca punarjātā vaidarbhe rājakanyakā \|*  
*jātismarā mahīpasya mahiṣī cārudharmaṇaḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*eṣa prabhāvo dīpasya kārttike māsi śobhanaḥ \|*  
*dattasyāyatane viṣṇo ryasyeyaṃ vyuṣṭiruttamā \|\| 63 \|\|*

*asaṃkalpitamadhyasya preraṇaṃ yanmayā kṛtam \|*  
*keśave bāladīpasya tasyedaṃ bhujyate phalam \|\| 64 \|\|*

*etasmātkāra ṇāddīpānahametānaharniśam \|*  
*prayacchāmi harergehe jātamasya mahāphalam \|\| 65 \|\|*

*evamuktvā sapatnīḥ sā dīpadānaparāyaṇā \|*  
*babhūva devadevasya keśava sya gṛhe sadā \|\| 66 \|\|*

*tataḥ kālena mahatā saha rājñā mahātmanā \|*  
*viṣṇulokamanuprāptā paṃcatvaṃ prāya mānadā \|\| 67 \|\|*

62-67. After my death, I was born as a daughter of the king of Vidarbha. Then retaining my earlier memory, I became the chief queen of the king of Kāśī. This is the influence of burning of a lamp in the temple of Viṣṇu, which resulted into bestowing a great merit on me. I had only rekindled a lamp in the temple of the lord, which had been extinguished. I am reaping the excellent reward thereof. Because of the same, I keep on lighting lamps in the temple of the lord throughout the day and night.” Thus speaking to her co-wives, she once again engaged herself in the burning of lamps in the temple. In due course of time, the noble king finally achieved the place of Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 3.130.68 \|\|

*taṃ lokamāsādya nṛpeṇa sārddhaṃ sā rājapatnī kamalābhanetrā \|*  
*reme mahīpālamudā sametā dīpapradānātsakalārtihīnā \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. О Mahipala, Lalita with lotus eyes, being the royal queen, because of the merit of the giving away of lamps, enjoyed the company of the king for long and was freed from all the miseries.

## \|\| 3.130.69 \|\|

*dīpapradānamapi puṇyataraṃ vadaṃti viprāgnigosurakulaikagṛhāṃgaṇeṣu \|*  
*taddānadīptavapuṣātha pathoṃdhakāre gacchannaraḥ patati na skhalate kadācit \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Therefore, for all the respectable learned people, it is quite auspicious to bum lamp in the house of a Brahmana, a cowpen and the temples. It bestows enormous merits, with the giving away of the lamps one achieves illustrious body, as a result of which, a person, while walking in darkness, does not fall.

## Chapter 131. Releasing of the bull

## \|\| 3.131.1-4 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*kārttikyāmatha vā māghyāmayameva yudhiṣṭhira \|\| 1 \|\|*

*caitryāmatha tṛtīyāyāṃ vaiśākhyāṃ dvādaśe'hni vā \|*  
*khaṃḍanīlaṃ śaṃkhapādaṃ sapauṃḍraṃ dhautapuṣpakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*gobhiścaturbhiḥ sahitaṃ sṛjeccaiva vidhiṃ śṛṇu \|*  
*yaduvāca purā gargo gokule'nagha pāṃḍava \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tattehaṃ ca pravakṣyāmi vidhiṃ gargapracoditam \|*  
*mātaraṃ sthāpayitvāgre pūjayetkusumākṣataiḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – On the third moon day of the months of Kartika, Magha and Caitra, besides on the twelfth moon day of the month of Vaisakha, there is a provision of releasing of the four cows and a bull, which should be of blue, Sankhapada, Paundra and white colour. О sinless Pandava, you please listen. The sage Garga in earlier times, once arrived in Gokula and spoke about this process, which is going to be respected by me. After invoking the mothers, same should be worshipped with flowers and the unbroken rice.

## \|\| 3.131.5-12 \|\|

*mātṛśrāddhaṃ tataḥ kuryātsadābhyudayakārakam \|*  
*akālamūlaṃ kalaśamaśvatthadalaśobhitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tatra vidvāñjapitvā tu sthāpayedrudradevatām \|*  
*susamiddhaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā vahnimaṃtrapuraḥsaram \|\| 6 \|\|*

*athainaṃ juhuyātṣaḍbhiḥ pṛthagāhutisaṃjñitaiḥ \|*  
*pauṣyāmaṃtraistataḥ paścāddhutvā vahniṃ yathāvidhi \|\| 7 \|\|*

*ekavarṇaṃ dvivarṇaṃ vā rohitaṃ śvetameva vā \|*  
*jīvadvatsapayasvinyāḥ 'nnaṃ sarvāṃgasundaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

*catasro vatsataryaśca tābhiḥ sārdha malaṃkṛtam \|*  
*tāsāṃ karṇe japedvipraḥ patiṃ vo balinaṃ śubham \|\| 9 \|\|*

*samitāstena sahitāḥ krīḍadhvaṃ hṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|*  
*tato vāme triśūlaṃ ca dakṣiṇe cakramālikhet \|\| 10 \|\|*

*aṃkitaṃ śaṃkhacakrābhyāṃ varṣitaṃ kusumādinā \|*  
*puṣpamālākṛtagrīvaṃ sitavastraiśca cchāditam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*vimuṃcedvatsakābhiśca nīlābhirbalinaṃ vṛṣam \|*  
*devālaye gokule vā nadīnāṃ saṃgame'tha vā \|\| 12 \|\|*

5-12. Thereafter, the Matr-Sraddha should be performed. A pitcher filled with water and decorated with the shoots of the plpala tree, should also be consecrated and the japam for Rudra should be performed. Thereafter, six offering should be made in the fire flames. After that, the homa should be performed appropriately, reciting the mantras and a cow whose calves dose not suffer due to draught, which should be of a single colour, two colours or of red colour, besides a beautiful bull which should be quite well-built with four calves, with decoration, at the time of their free release, the donor should whisper in their ears – “All of you have been given an auspicious husband, which is quite strong besides being auspicious. Therefore, all of you should sport with the same bull with delight.” Thereafter, the bull should be decorated with a trident on the left and a wheel at the right side. The bull which should be decorated with sankha and cakra, together with four new cows, should be set free in a temple, cowpen or at the confluence of the rivers.

## \|\| 3.131.13-14 \|\|

*ityukte gargamuninā vidhānaṃ vṛṣamokṣaṇe \|*  
*svecchāvihāriṇaṃ dṛptaṃ garjaṃtaṃ sundaraṃ gavām \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kakudminaṃ patiṃ yā dhanye vimuñcanti govṛṣam \|*  
*phalaṃ ca tasya vakṣyāmi bruvatāṃ me nibodha tat \|\| 14 \|\|*

13-14. This is the process which has been revealed by the sage Garga. Those who set free the bull which roams at will, eats at will and thunders among the cows, with a raised hump, they indeed are quite graceful. I am going to speak out the merits one gains after releasing such a bull. You please listen.

## \|\| 3.131.15-18 \|\|

*vṛṣotsarge punātyeva daśātītāndaśāparān \|*  
*yatkiṃcitspṛśate toyaṃ samuttīrya jalānmahīm \|\| 15 \|\|*

*vṛṣotsṛṣṭaṃ pitṝṇāṃ tu tadakṣayamudāhṛtam \|*  
*yaiśca yaiśca spṛśettoyaṃ lāṃgūlādibhiraṃtataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sarvaṃ tadakṣayaṃ tasya pitṝṇāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*śṛṅgaiḥ khurairvā yadbhūmimullikhatyaniśaṃ vṛṣaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*madhukulyāḥ pitustasya akṣayāstā bhavaṃti vai \|*  
*sahasratalamātreṇa taḍāgo na yathāśruti \|\| 18 \|\|*

15-18. The completion of the yajna for setting free a bull when performed by a person, redeems the earlier ten generations as well as the following ten generations of the performer. Crossing the river water, when the same bull reaches on the other side and whatever things are touched by the bull, be it water, land or the food, it becomes everlasting for the manes. There is no doubt about it. The land which is always dug by the bull with its horns or the hoofs, it turns into a stream of honey for the manes. According to the provisions of the Srutis, only such a reservoir is known as a lake, which could not be equated by hundreds of pits.

## \|\| 3.131.19 \|\|

*pitṝṇāṃ yā bhavettṛptistāṃ vṛṣastvatiricyate \|*  
*yo dadāti tilairmiśrāṃstilānvā śrāddhakarmaṇi \|*  
*madhu vā nīlakhaṃḍaṃ vā akṣayaṃ sarvameva tat \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A person who pleases the manes well, he is considered to be a praiseworthy bull. During the performing of the Sraddha, when the sesamum seeds and the honey mixed with them besides the nilakhanda is offered to the manes, it becomes everlasting.

## \|\| 3.131.20 \|\|

*eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ putrā yadyeko'pi gayāṃ vrajet \|*  
*yajeta vāśvamedhena nīlaṃ vā vṛṣamutsṛjet \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. Therefore, the birth of several sons is essential, because someone out of them, shall surely perform Sraddha at Gaya, Advamedha-yajna or would release the blue-bull.

## \|\| 3.131.21 \|\|

*na karoti vṛṣotsargaṃ sutīrthe vā jalāñjalim \|*  
*na prayacchati yaḥ putraḥ pituruccāra eva saḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A son who does not release a blue bull, but offers oblations in the sacred tirthas, then it is just useless for the manes.

## \|\| 3.131.22 \|\|

*yadbhūmimālikhati śṛṅgakhuraiḥ prahṛṣṭo yadvā karoti pratimallavṛṣānnirīkṣya \|*  
*khaṇḍaṃ samastamapi tasya vivāhakartuḥ saṃtoṣamāvahati śakrasabhāgatasya \|\| 22 \|\|*

22\. When a bull is digging the earth with its horns or hoofs and at the sight of another bull when the former thunders, the person who sets free the bull, when seated in the court of Indra, feels extremely satisfied for marrying the bull with a cow.

## Chapter 132. Phalguna-Purnima-Vrata

## \|\| 3.132.1-3 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*kimarthaṃ phālgunasyāṃte paurṇamāsyāṃ janārdana \|*  
*utsavo jāyate loke grāmegrāme pure pure \|\| 1 \|\|*

*kimarthaṃ śiśavastasyāṃ gehegehe'tivādinaḥ \|*  
*holikā dīpyate kasmātphālgunāṃte kimucyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*aḍāḍeti ca kā saṃjñā śītoṣṇeti kimucyate \|*  
*ko hyasyāṃ pūjyate devaḥ keneyamavatāritā \|*  
*kimasyāṃ kriyate kṛṣṇa etadvistarato vada \|\| 3 \|\|*

1-3. Yudhisthira said – On the full moon day of the month of Phalguna, festivities are observed in each house of every village, why do the boys utter the vulgar words? When is the Holt burnt? О Kṛṣṇa, what is the meaning of Adada-Samjna and Sitosna or cold and warm? Who is the god to be adored in this case? Who initiated the same? What is the process to be followed in this case? You kindly apprise me of all the details.

## \|\| 3.132.4-5 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*āsītkṛtayuge pārtha raghurnāma narādhipaḥ \|*  
*śūraḥ sarvaguṇopataḥ priyavādī bahuśrutaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*sa sarvāṃ pṛthivīṃ jitvā vaśīkṛtya narādhipān \|*  
*dharmataḥ pālayāmāsa prajāḥ putrānivaurasān \|\| 5 \|\|*

4-5. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О Partha, during the ancient time of Krta-yuga, there ruled a king by the name of Raghu. He was quite strong, possessed all the virtues, with sweet tongue besides being an immensely learned one. He conquered the entire earth and gained control over all the rulers of the earth. He treated the people like his own sons.

## \|\| 3.132.6-7 \|\|

*na durbhikṣaṃ na ca vyādhirnākālamaraṇaṃ tathā \|*  
*nādharmarucayaḥ paurāstasmiñchāsati pārthiva \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tasyaivaṃ śāsato rājyaṃ kṣātradharmaratasya vai \|*  
*paurāḥ sarve samāgamya pāhipāhītyathābruvan \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. During the rule of that king, there were no draughts with the population. People were not interested in the sinful ways, but once the people, during the rule of the same king, reached the royal court and started crying for their protection.

## \|\| 3.132.8-10 \|\|

*paurā ūcuḥ \|*  
*asmākaṃ hi gṛhe kāciḍhḍhauṃḍhā nāmeti rākṣasī \|*  
*divā rātrau samāgamya bālānpīḍayate balāt \|\| 8 \|\|*

*rakṣayā kaṃḍakenāpi bheṣajairvā narādhipa \|*  
*maṃtrajñaiḥ paramācāryaiḥ sā niyaṃtuṃ na śakyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

*paurāṇāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā raghurvismayamāgataḥ \|*  
*vismayāviṣṭahṛdayaḥ purohitamathābravīt \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. The citizens said- A demoness named Dhaundha enters our houses during the day and night and forcibly tortures our children. О king, it has become difficult for us to put on end to her activities for protecting ourselves. At these cries of the people, the king Raghu felt extremely surprised. He at once said to his priest.

## \|\| 3.132.11-12 \|\|

*raghuruvāca \|*  
*ḍhauṃḍheti rākṣasī keyaṃ kiṃprabhāvā dvijottama \|*  
*kathameṣā niyaṃtavyā mayā duṣkṛtakāriṇī \|\| 11 \|\|*

*rakṣaṇātprocyate rājā pṛthivīpālanātpatiḥ \|*  
*arakṣamāṇaḥ pṛthivīṃ rājā bhavati kilbiṣī \|\| 12 \|\|*

11-12. Raghu said – О best of the Brahmanas, who is this Dhaundha demoness? How can I remove her because by protecting the people and well regulating the earth, the kings are known as the lords of earth? In case the king is unable to protect the earth, the king is known as an eunuch.

## \|\| 3.132.13-17 \|\|

*vaśiṣṭha uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu rājanparaṃ guhyaṃ yannākhyātaṃ mayā kvacit \|*  
*ḍhauṃḍhā nāmeti vikhyātā rākṣasī mālinaḥ sutā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tayā cārādhitaḥ śaṃbhurugreṇa tapasā purā \|*  
*prītastāmāha bhagavānvaraṃ varaya suvrate \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yatte manobhilaṣitaṃ taddadāmyavicāritam \|*  
*ḍhauṃḍhā prāha mahādevaṃ yadi tuṣṭaḥ svayaṃ mama \|\| 15 \|\|*

*na ca vadhyāṃ surādīnāṃ manujānāṃ ca śaṃkara \|*  
*māṃ kuru tvaṃ trilokeśa śastrāstrāṇāṃ tathaiva ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*śītoṣṇavarṣāsamaye divā rātrau bahirgṛhe \|*  
*abhayaṃ sarvadā me syāttvatprasādānmaheśvara \|\| 17 \|\|*

13-17. Vasistha said- О king, I am going to narrate to you an extremely secret story, which has not been revealed to anyone so far. You please listen. Dhaundha is the daughter of a demon named Mall who is quite well known. In earlier times, she had performed hard tapas for lord Siva, who getting pleased with her, said to the demoness – “O Suvrata, you ask for a boon you desire. I shall grant you the same, even without thinking for a moment.” On hearing these words of Siva, Phaunda said to lord Mahadeva- “O Sankara, in case you wish to bestow a boon on me, then make me invincible from the gods, humans, besides the weapons of all types. By your grace, I should receive full protection during the heat, winter, rains, during days and nights, within my house or outside it in the open.”

## \|\| 3.132.18-20 \|\|

*śaṃkara uvāca \|*  
*evamastvityathoktvā tāṃ punaḥ provāca śūlabhṛt \|*  
*unmattebhyaḥ śiśubhyaśca bhayaṃ te saṃbhaviṣyati \|*  
*ṛtāvṛtau mahābhāge mā vyathāṃ hṛdaye kṛthāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*evaṃ datvā varaṃ tasyai bhagavānbhaganetrahā \|*  
*svapne labdho yathārthārthastatraivāṃtarhito'bhavat \|\| 19 \|\|*

*evaṃ labdhavarā sā tu rākṣasī kāmarūpiṇī \|*  
*nityaṃ pīḍayate bālānsaṃsmṛtya harabhāṣitam \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. Siva said – The carrier of the trident, in reply to the request, said – “Be it so.” Thereafter, while crying, he again said – “O excellent one, you will always be afraid of the children in al the seasons. Therefore, preserve no danger in your mind. Lord Siva – the snatcher of Bhaga eye, thus granted her the boon and then disappeared. Like the riches earned in a dream, the demoness Dhaundha, getting reminded of the words of lord Siva, started torturing the children daily.

## \|\| 3.132.21-28 \|\|

*aḍāḍayeti gṛhṇāti siddhamaṃtraṃ kuṭuṃbinī \|*  
*gṛheṣu tena sā loke hyaḍāḍetyabhidhīyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

*etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ ḍhauṃḍhāyāścaritaṃ mayā \|*  
*sāṃprataṃ kathayiṣyāmi yenopāyena hanyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

*adya pañcadaśī śuklā phālgunasya narādhipa \|*  
*śītakālo viniṣkrāṃtaḥ prātargrīṣmo bhaviṣyati \|\| 23 \|\|*

*abhayapradānaṃ lokānāṃ dīyatāṃ puruṣottama \|*  
*yathādyāśaṃkitā lokā ramaṃti ca hasaṃti ca \|\| 24 \|\|*

*dārujāni ca khaṃḍāni gṛhītvā samarotsukāḥ \|*  
*yodhā iva viniryāṃtu śiśavaḥ saṃpraharṣitāḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*saṃcayaṃ śuṣkakāṣṭhānāmupalānāṃ ca kārayet \|*  
*tatrāgniṃ vidhivaddhutvā rakṣoghnairmantravistaraiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tataḥ kilakilāśabdaistālaśabdairmanoharaiḥ \|*  
*tamagniṃ triḥ parikramya gāyaṃtu ca hasaṃtu ca \|*  
*jalpaṃtu svecchayā lokā niḥśaṃkā yasya yanmatam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*tena śabdena sā pāpā homena ca nirā kṛtā \|*  
*adṛṣṭaghātairḍiṃbhānāṃ rākṣasī kṣayameṣyati \|\| 28 \|\|*

21-28. While entering the house, she made use of the Adada mantra. Therefore, the said mantra came to be known as Adadya in the world. Thus, I have revealed to you the entire story of the demoness Dhaundha. Now, I am going to speak out the way by which she can be killed You please listen. О king, today is the full moon day of the month of Phalguna. It is the end of the winter season and is the start of summer season. О best of the humans, therefore, you assure protection to the people as a result of which the doubtful people should lead the joyful lives again. The boys, holding playfully the rods in their hands like the warriors anxious to wage the war, getting delightful, should collect the dry wood and the dung cakes and put them to fire. Reciting the mantras for the destruction of the Raksasas, they should pour the offerings of wood and dung cakes in the fire. They should remain delightful clapping their hands and then circumambulate the fire. All the people should arrive there joyfully and should enter into conversation as usual, because with those words as well as the performance of homa, the sinful demoness gets fainted. With the invisible strikes of the boys, the demoness gets destroyed.

## \|\| 3.132.29-30 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*tasyarṣervacanaṃ śrutvā sa nṛpaḥ pāṃḍunadana \|*  
*sarvaṃ cakāra vidhivaduktaṃ tena ca dhīmatā \|\| 29 \|\|*

*gatā sā rākṣasī nāśaṃ tena cogreṇa karmaṇā \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛti loke'sminnaḍāḍā khyātimāgatā \|\| 30 \|\|*
