*ānīya maṇḍape tāni sarvāṇyevādhivāsayet \|*  
*tatastu brāhmaṇaḥ snātaḥ śuklāṃbaradharaḥ śuciḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*oṃkārarapūrvakairmantraistalliṃgairjuhuyād ghṛtam \|*  
*lohanāmābhavatpūrvaṃ dānavastu mahābalaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*sa devaiḥ samare kruddhairbahudhā śakalīkṛtaḥ \|*  
*tadaṃgasambhavaṃ lohaṃ yatsarvaṃ dṛśyate kṣitau \|\| 36 \|\|*

34-36. The performer should be clad in white garments and with utmost purity, a Brahmana should be made to recite the Omkara mantra. Then reciting the Tallinga-mantra, offerings in ghi should be poured in the fire. In earlier times, a powerful Raksasa named Loha was born on earth, who was cut into pieces by the gods in the battlefield. The iron wherever is found, is the part of the limbs of the same demon.

## \|\| 3.138.37-40 \|\|

*śastrāstramantrairhotavyaṃ pāyasaṃ ghṛtasaṃyutam \|*  
*hutaśeṣaṃ turaṃgāṇāṃ gajānāmupahārayet \|\| 37 \|\|*

*lohābhihārikaṃ karma tenaitadṛṣibhiḥ smṛtam \|*  
*baddhapratiśaravyaṃ ca gajāśvasamalaṃkṛtam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*bhrāmayennagare nityaṃ naṃdighoṣapurassaram \|*  
*pratyahaṃ nṛpatiḥ snātvā saṃpūjya pitṛdevatāḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*pūjayedrājacihnāni phalamālyānulepanaiḥ \|*  
*hutaśeṣaṃ pradātavyamaupanāyanike dvije \|\| 40 \|\|*

37-40. Reciting the mantras concerning the weapons, the offerings of ghi, payasam should be dropped. The left out part of the same should be given as the gift to the horses and the elephants. Accordingly, the Ṛṣis have termed it as the Lohabhiharika-karma. Thereafter, the king carrying the bow and arrow, decorating the horses and the elephants, should make an announcement in the city taking round of the city. The king should daily take bath, perform the worship with flowers, garlands, paste etc. and then worship of the weapons as well. Then the homa and the thread ceremony should also be performed. All the articles of homa should be given over to a Brahmana.

## \|\| 3.138.41-43 \|\|

*tasyābhiharaṇādrājño vijayaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*pūjāmaṃtrānpravakṣyāmi purāṇoktānahaṃ tava \|\| 41 \|\|*

*yaiḥ pūjitāḥ prayacchanti kīrtimāyur yaśobalam \|*  
*yathāṃbudaśchādayati śivāyemāṃ vasundharām \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tathācchādaya rājānaṃ vijayārogyavṛddhaye \|*  
*gandharva kulajātastvaṃ mā bhūyāḥ kuladūṣakaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. By accepting this openly or stealthily, the king surely achieves success. I am now speaking out the relevant Pauranic hymns, making use of which the deity bestows long life, glory and strength. As the clouds cover the earth for the welfare of the people, similarly, for the enhancement of victory as well as the achieving of the good health, you cover the king. Uttering the mantra, the umbrella should be given over to the king. “O Turangama, having been horn in the race of the Gandharvas, you don’t bring blemish on the race.

## \|\| 3.138.44-48 \|\|

*brahmaṇaḥ satyavākyena somasya varuṇasya ca \|*  
*prabhāvācca hutāśasya varddhasva tvaṃ turaṃgama \|\| 44 \|\|*

*tejasā caiva sūryasya munīnāṃ tapasā yathā \|*  
*rudrasya brahmacaryeṇa pavanasya balena ca \|\| 45 \|\|*

*smara tvaṃ rājaputro'si kaustubhaṃ ca maṇiṃ smara \|*  
*yāṃ gatiṃ brahmahā gacchetpitṛhā mātṛhā tathā \|\| 46 \|\|*

*bhūmyarthenṛtavādī ca kṣatriyaśca parāṅmukhaḥ \|*  
*sūryācandramasau vāyuḥ pāvakaśca na yatra vai \|\| 47 \|\|*

*vrajecca tāṃ gatiṃ kṣipraṃ tacca pāpaṃ bhavetkila \|*  
*vikṛtiṃ yadi gacchestvaṃ yuddhedhvani turaṃgama \|*  
*ripūnvijitya samare saha bhartrā sukhī bhava \|\| 48 \|\|*

44-48. With the truthful words of Brahma and with the influence of the Moon, Agni and Varuna, besides with the lustre of the Sun, the lustre of the sages, by the grace of the Brahmacarya of lord Rudra and force of the Windgod, let you always achieve the glory. Keep it in mind the fact that you are a prince. Similarly, you also remember about the Kaustubha gem. О Turangama, reaching the battlefield, in case your mind is overpowered with some blemish, then you shall earn the sin of Brahmahatya and the killing of a father. Those who tell a lie for the sake of the land, they achieve the position of those, who flee from the battleground. You also recall such of the sins which are committed at the places where the Sun, the Moon, Wind and the Fire gods have no access. Achieving victory in the battlefield, you enjoy all the comforts with your master. This is known as the Asvattha-mantra.

## \|\| 3.138.49-51 \|\|

*śakraketo mahāvīrya suparṇastvayyupasthitaḥ \|*  
*patatrirāḍvainateyastathā nārāyaṇadhvajaḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

*kāśyapeyo'mṛto jñeyo nāgārirviṣṇuvāhanaḥ \|*  
*aprameyo durādharṣo devaśatruniṣūdanaḥ \|\| 50 \|\|*

*garutmānmārutagatistvayi sannihitaḥ sthitaḥ \|*  
*śastravarmāyudhānyodhānrakṣā smāṃśca ripūndaha \|\| 51 \|\|*

49-51. О immensely valorous Sukra - Ketu, Garuda - the king of the birds is available with you, who adornes the flag of Narayana and is son of Kasyapa. He is the nectar like and the enemy of the Nagas, besides being the vehicle of Viṣṇu. Garuda has the speed of the Windgod, is invincible and destroyer of the enemies of the gods. They are present with you. Therefore, you protect all my warriors who are carrying all the weapons. Destroy the enemy warriors.” This is the mantra for the flag.

## \|\| 3.138.52-56 \|\|

*kumudairāvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpadaṃto'tha vāmanaḥ \|*  
*supratīkoñjano nīla ete'ṣṭau devayonayaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*eteṣāṃ putrapautrāśca balānyaṣṭau samāśritāḥ \|*  
*bhadro mandro mṛgaścaiva gajaḥ saṃkīrṇa eva ca \|*  
*vanevane prasūtāste kariyoniṃ mahāgajāḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*pāṃtu tvāṃ vasavo rudrā ādityāḥ samarudgaṇāḥ \|*  
*bhartāraṃ rakṣa nāgendra samayaṃ pratipālayan \|\| 54 \|\|*

*avāpurhi jayaṃ yuddhe gamane svasti no vraja \|*  
*śrīste somādbalaṃ viṣṇostejaḥ sūryājjavonilāt \|*  
*sthairyaṃ merorjayaṃ rudrādyaśo devātpuraṃdarāt \|\| 55 \|\|*

*yuddhe rakṣaṃtu nāgāstvāṃ diśaśca saha daivataiḥ \|*  
*aśvinau saha gaṃdharvaiḥ pāṃtu tvāṃ sarvataḥ sadā \|\| 56 \|\|*

52-56. There are eight types of the divine yonis (births) which include Kumuda, Airavana, Padma, Puspadanta, Vamana, Supratika, Anjana and Nila. Their sons and grandsons have established eight types of armies. They produced Bhadra, Mandra, Mrga and Gaja. Those elephants produced the elephants of our species in the forests. О Nagendra, because of these, the Vasus, Rudras, Adityas, Marudganas should protect you and as per your own resolve, should protect your master. Only those people become victorious in the battleground. Therefore, you join the march of the chariots, which would bring welfare to you as well as myself. You would gain lustre from the Moon, strength from Vi$nu, shine from the Sun, force from the Windgod, stability from me, japam from Rudra. Indra will also gain the glory from this. Let the serpents and the gods protect you besides all the directions. Similarly, the Gandharvas with Asvinikumaras should protect you from all the sides. This is known as Hasti mantra.

## \|\| 3.138.57-63 \|\|

*hutabhugvasavo rudrā vāyuḥ somo maharṣayaḥ \|*  
*nāgakinnaragandharvayakṣa bhūtagaṇāgrahāḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*pramathāśca sahādityairbhūteśo mātṛbhiḥ saha \|*  
*śakrasenāpatiḥ skando varuṇaścāśritāstvayi \|\| 58 \|\|*

*pradahaṃtu ripūnsarvānrājā vijayamṛcchatu \|*  
*yāni prayuktānyaribhirdūṣaṇāni samaṃtataḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*etāni paraśatrūṇāṃ hatāni tava tejasā \|*  
*kālanemivadhe yuddhe yuddhe tripura ghātane \|\| 60 \|\|*

*hiraṇyakaśiporyuddhe yuddhe devāsure tathā \|*  
*śobhitāsi tathaivādya śobhamānāstu bhūpateḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*nīlāṃ śvetāmimāṃ dṛṣṭvā naśyaṃtvadya nṛpārayaḥ \|*  
*vyādhibhirvividhairghoraiḥ śastraiśca yudhi nirjitāḥ \|\| 62 \|\|*

*sadyaḥ svasthā bhavaṃti sma tvadvātenāpamārjitāḥ \|\| 63 \|\|*

57-63. Agni, Vasus, Rudras, Vayu, the Moon, the Maharsis, Nagas, Kinnaras, Gandharvas, Yaksas, Bhutaganas, the planets, Adityas and the initial Ganas of Lord Siva with Matrkas, Skanda - the commander of Indra and Varuna, all are under your refuge. Let them all destroy the enemies to enable the king to achieve the victory. Let all other blemishes which had been spread by the enemies, also get destroyed. At the time of the killing of the Kalanemi in the battleground, the killing of Tripurasura, Hiranyakasipu besides during the war between the Devas and the Daityas, you always appeared graceful. Similarly, you also display your grace presently, as a result of which with the mere look of your blue and white colour, the enemies get destroyed. My warriors, attracting various ailments in the war, besides those who had been defeated or injured with the terrific weapons, let your blowing wind comfort them and provide soothing touch to them, making them healthy.

## \|\| 3.138.64 \|\|

*pūtanā revatī nāmnā kālarātrīti yā smṛtā \|*  
*dahaṃtvāśu ripūnsarvānpatāke tvāmupāgatāḥ \|\| 64 \|\|*

64\. Similarly, Putana, Revati, Kalaratri, conducting themselves close to you, should destroy all the enemies.

## \|\| 3.138.65-67 \|\|

*asiśca ripuhā khaḍgastīkṣṇakarmā durāsadaḥ \|*  
*śrīgarbho vijayaścaiva dharmadhārastathaiva ca \|\| 65 \|\|*

*ityaṣṭau tava nāmāni svayamuktāni vedhasā \|*  
*nakṣatraṃ kṛttikā tubhyaṃ gururdevo maheśvaraḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*hiraṇyaṃ ca śarīraṃ te dhātā devo janārdanaḥ \|*  
*pitā pitāmaho devastvaṃ māṃ pālaya sarvadā \|\| 67 \|\|*

65-67. This is the mantra meant for the flag. Eight names have been given to the sword by Brahma, which include – Asi, Khadga, Ripu, Tiksnakarma, Durasada, Srigarbha, Vijaya and Dharmadhara. Mahadeva — the preceptor of the world, had allotted Krttika constellation for you. Lord Janardana had given you the body of gold. Therefore, you should always protect me like the father and the grandfather. This is the mantra relating to the sword.

## \|\| 3.138.68 \|\|

*śarmapradastvaṃ samare varma sarvāyaso hyasi \|*  
*rakṣa māṃ rakṣaṇīyo'haṃ tava varmannamo'stu te \|\| 68 \|\|*

68\. 0 Varmadeva, I offer my salutation to you again and again because you always bestow welfare in the battleground and you have the form of iron. Therefore, you protect me. This is called Varma-mantra.

## \|\| 3.138.69-71 \|\|

*dundubhe tvaṃ sapatnānāṃ ghoṣāddhṛdayakampana \|*  
*bhava bhūmipa sainyānāṃ tathā vijayavarddhanaḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*yathā jīmūtaghoṣeṇa hṛṣyaṃti varavāraṇāḥ \|*  
*tathāstu tava śabdena harṣo'smākaṃ mudāvahaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*yathā jīmūtaśabdena strīṇāṃ trāso'bhijāyate \|*  
*tathā ca tava śabdena trasyaṃtvasmaddviṣo raṇe \|\| 71 \|\|*

69-71. О Dundubhi, О large drum, with your deep voice, you always shakes the hearts of the enemy. Therefore, the royal army go on increasing and be victorious. As with the thundering aloud of the clouds, the intoxicated elephants get pleased, similarly, you delight us with your sound. As with the thundering sounds, the ladies get frightened, similarly, you delight us with your thunder and frighten our enemies. This is the Dundubhi mantra.

## \|\| 3.138.72 \|\|

*sarvāyudha mahāmātra sarvadevārisūdana \|*  
*cāpa māṃ sarvadā rakṣa sākaṃ sāyakasattamaiḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

72\. О councilor of all the weapons, you destroy all the enemies of the gods. Therefore, you protect me always with all the devotees. This is the Capa mantra.

## \|\| 3.138.73 \|\|

*puṇyastvaṃ śaṅkha puṣpāṇāṃ maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam \|*  
*viṣṇunā vidhṛto nityaṃ manaḥśāṃtiprado bhava \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. О Sankha, you are the merit of all the merits, besides being welfare of all the welfares and are always owned by lord Viṣṇu. Therefore, you bestow the mental peace on me. This is the mantra for the conch.

## \|\| 3.138.74 \|\|

*śaśāṃkakarasaṃkāśa himaḍiṃḍīrapāṃḍura \|*  
*protsārayāśu duritaṃ cāmarāmaravallabha \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. О flywhisk, you are the beloved of the gods. You were formed of the rays of the Moon, the foam of the oceanic water as well as the mountain snow. You possess the bright lustre. Therefore, you kindly remove all my misfortunes. This is the Camara-mantra.

## \|\| 3.138.75-77 \|\|

*sarvāyudhānāṃ prathamā nirmitā'si pinākinā \|*  
*śūlāyudhādviniṣkṛṣya kṛtvā muṣṭiparigraham \|\| 75 \|\|*

*caṃḍikāyāḥ pradattāsi sarvaduṣṭanibarhiṇi \|*  
*tathā vistāritā cāsi devānāṃ pratipāditā \|\| 76 \|\|*

*sarva sattvāṃgabhūtāsi sarvāśubhanivāriṇi \|*  
*churike rakṣa māṃ nityaṃ śāntiṃ yaccha namo'stu te \|\| 77 \|\|*

75-77. It is the foremost of all the attributes. It was formed by sins, the carrier of the bow named Pinaka. He extracted you out of his trident and bestowed you a body of the size of a fish. For the destruction of the evil people, you have been given over to the goddess Candi. You had also developed in the same way. You have been praised by the gods everywhere. You are the part of all the living beings and you destroy all their evils. Therefore, you protect me always, bestowing peace on me. I offer my salutation to you again and again. This is the Icchurika-mantra.

## \|\| 3.138.78-79 \|\|

*protsāraṇāya duṣṭānāṃ mādhusaṃgrahaṇāya ca \|*  
*brahmaṇā nirmitaścāsi vyavahāraprasiddhaye \|\| 78 \|\|*

*yaśo dehi sukhaṃ dehi jayado bhava bhūpateḥ \|*  
*tāḍayāśu ripūnsarvānhemadaṃḍa namostu te \|\| 79 \|\|*

78-79. You are the dagger, with a handle of gold, for the removal of the evil people and for the protection of the noble people. Besides, you have neutralized the public relations. You were created by Brahma for the same purpose, therefore, you bestow fame to the king, comforts and victory, as result of which let all his enemies vanish. I offer my salutation to you. This is the Kanakadanda-mantra.

## \|\| 3.138.80-83 \|\|

*vijayo jayado jetā ripughātī priyaṃkaraḥ \|*  
*duḥkhahā dharmadaḥ śāṃtaḥ sarvāriṣṭavināśanaḥ \|\| 80 \|\|*

*ete'ṣṭau saṃnidhau yasmāttava siṃhā mahābalā \|*  
*tena siṃhāsaneti tvaṃ viprairvedeṣu gīyase \|\| 81 \|\|*

*tvayi sthitaḥ śivaḥ sākṣāttvayi śakrasureśvaraḥ \|*  
*tvayi sthito harirdevastvadarthaṃ tapyate tapaḥ \|\| 82 \|\|*

*namaste sarvatobhadra bhadrado bhava bhūpateḥ \|*  
*trailokyajayasarvasva siṃhāsana namo'stu te \|\| 83 \|\|*

80-83. You provide victory, destroy the enemies, make one victorious, do pleased things, remove the miseries, make one devoted towards dharma and completely remove all the sufferings and are quite peaceful. The eight lions which are quite strong always guard you. Therefore, the Brahmanas describe the same as Simhasana in the Vedas. Lord Siva, Indra – the god of gods, besides Viṣṇu are always on guard with you. The gods are also performing tapas for you. О Sarvatobhadra (bestower of welfare to all), you be beneficial for the king. Salutation to you. О lion thorns, you are the conqueror of the world, besides being victorious. Therefore, salutation to you again and again. This is the Simhasana mantra.

## \|\| 3.138.84-86 \|\|

*lohābhihārikaṃ karma kṛtvedaṃ maṃtrapūrvakam \|*  
*phalanaivedyakusumairdhūpadīpavilepanaiḥ \|\| 84 \|\|*

*aṣṭamyāṃ dhāvanaṃ kṛtvā pūrvāhne snānamācaret \|\| 85 \|\|*

*durgāṃ kāṃcanamūrtiṃ raupyāṃ vā paittalīṃ vārkṣī caitrīṃ tāmrīṃ vādhibhavataḥ kṛtvā dāruvicitratoraṇavinyastāṃ śobhane sthāne purato vinyastadṛṣṭāṃ vicitragṛhamadhyagāṃ snātāṃ kuṃkumacaṃdanagaṃdhaiścatuḥsamaiścīrapaṭṭaiścarcitagātrāṃ devīṃ kusumairabhyarcya tāṃ bahubhiḥ puṣyamāṇakīrtistairdvi jananairjanitaparitoṣairdivānvito naredraḥ svayaṃ prayacchetpurohitaiḥ sārdhaṃ bilvapatreṇārcanena maṃtreṇānena bhagavatyai \|*  
*jayaṃtī maṃgalā kālī bhadrakālī kapālinī \|*  
*durgā śivā kṣamā dhātrī svāhā svadhā namostu te \|\| 86 \|\|*

84-86. Thus offering the fruits, eatables, incense, lamp and the paste with the reciting of the mantras, the rite of Lohabhiharika should be performed on the eighth moon day, after taking bath in the forenoon. The image of Durga should be made in gold, silver, brass or in painting or of copper and should be established at an auspicious spot, which should have been decorated with beautiful arches, festoon of leaves. After bathing the image in the middle of the courtyard of the temple, the vermilion, sandal paste, fragrance and costumes should be offered. Several Brahmanas should worship the deity offering several types of prayers and the goddess be pleased. Then in the temple, the priest of the king should recite the mantras and the leaves of the wood apple trees should be offered to the goddess, saying- “You are Jayanti, Mangala, Kali Bhadra, Kapalini, Durga, Ksama, Siva, Dhatri, Svaha and Svadha. All of you are being offered salutation by me again and again.’’

## \|\| 3.138.87-93 \|\|

*amṛtodbhavaḥ śrīvṛkṣo mahādevīpriyaḥ sadā \|*  
*bilvapatraṃ prayacchāmi pavitraṃ te sureśvari \|\| 87 \|\|*

*durgā saṃpūjanīyā ca taddināddroṇapuṣpayā \|*  
*sā cābhīṣṭā sureśānyāstathā rūḍhavraṇāyutaḥ \|\| 88 \|\|*

*tataḥ khaḍgaṃ namaskṛtya śatrūṇāṃ mānamarddanam \|*  
*icchetsvavijayaṃ rājyaṃ subhikṣaṃ cātmano nṛpa \|\| 89 \|\|*

*punaḥ punaḥ praṇamyātha dhyāyecca hṛdaye śivām \|*  
*mahiṣaghnīṃ bahubhujāṃ kumārīṃ siṃhavāhinīm \|\| 90 \|\|*

*dānavāṃstarjayatī ca khaḍgoddhatakarāṃ śubhām \|*  
*ghaṃṭākṣasragdharāṃ durgāṃ raṇāraṃbhe vyavasthitām \|\| 91 \|\|*

*tato jayajayākāraiḥ stavaṃ kuryādimaṃ tataḥ \|\| 92 \|\|*

*sarvamaṅgalamāṅgalye śive sarvārthasādhike \|*  
*śaraṇye tryaṃbake gauri nārāyaṇi namo'stu te \|\| 93 \|\|*

87-93. Since the wood apple tree emerged out of the nectar is quite favourite of Mahadevi, О Suresvari, the same wood apple tree leaf is being offered by me. Thereafter, Bhuvanesvari and the goddess Durga should be worshipped with the offering of the auspicious flowers, and then the worship should be concluded and while so doing, on the rear side, beautiful and uninjured seats of other goddesses should also lodged and worshipped. Thereafter, the king should pray for the shattering of the pride of enemies and that he should have plenty of cereals. Thus the goddess, who is the destroyer of the demon Mahisa, possessing multi aims, who is also known as Kumari, Simhavahini, who punishes the evil, holding an auspicious sword in hand, besides holding a bell and rosary, appears ready to rush to the battlefield, one should meditate upon her in one’s mind offering salutation to her again and again. Then he should offer prayer to her uttering these mantras – “O Siva, you are heap of all the welfare, make all the desires successful, provide refuge to the destitute besides possessing three eyes. Therefore, I offer my salutation to Gauri, Narayani again and again.

## \|\| 3.138.94-96 \|\|

*kuṃkumena samālabdhe candanena vilepite \|*  
*bilvapatrakṛtāmāle durge'haṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ \|\| 94 \|\|*

*kṛtvaivamarccāṃ kauravya aṣṭamyāṃ jāgaraṃ niśi \|*  
*naṭanartanagītaiśca kārayettu mahotsavam \|\| 95 \|\|*

*evaṃ hṛṣṭairniśāṃ nītvā prabhāte cāruṇodaye \|*  
*pātayenmahiṣānmeṣānagrato natakandharān \|\| 96 \|\|*

94-96. Her entire body should be plastered with sandal paste mixed with vermilion. She should be decorated with the wood apple leaves and oleander flowers garland and one should say – “I am present before the goddess Durga to serve her.” О son of Kuru race, thus worshipping the goddess on the night of Astami, the music and dance should be carried out during the night, after which the festival should be concluded. When the night is thus spent in delight, at dawn on the next day, the male buffaloes should be sacrificed.

## \|\| 3.138.97-99 \|\|

*śataṃ cāpi śatārdhaṃ vā tadarddhaṃ vā yathecchayā \|*  
*surāsavabhṛtaiḥ kuṃbhaistarpayetparameśvarīm \|\| 97 \|\|*

*kāpālikebhyastaddeyaṃ dāsīdāsajanaistathā \|*  
*vibhajya sarvaṃ kauṃteya suhṛtsaṃbaṃdhibaṃdhuṣu \|\| 98 \|\|*

*tatoparāhṇasamaye navamyāṃ syaṃdane sthitām \|*  
*bhavānīṃ bhrāmayedrāṣṭre svayaṃ rājā sasainyavān \|\| 99 \|\|*

97-99. Their number could be hundred, fifty or half of them as per one’s means. In place of the male buffaloes, the goats and sheep could also be sacrificed. Besides the pitchers filled with beverages should also be distributed, after offering it to the goddess. Thereafter, the male and female servants as well as the relatives should be adequately served with the whole stuff, which should also be given over to Kapalikas, friends, relatives, besides the kiths and kins. In the next forenoon, a chariot should be arranged which should be well decorated. The image of the goddess should be placed over it. The chariot should then be arranged to move round the city in a procession.

## \|\| 3.138.100-102 \|\|

*sahasraiḥ puruṣairvāpi rathayuktaiḥ suśikṣitaiḥ \|*  
*śanaiḥ śanairadhikayā dīptyā prajvaladīpakaiḥ \|\| 100 \|\|*

*ākṛṣṭakhaḍgairvīraiśca dhāturaktairgajaistathā \|*  
*nadadbhiḥ śaṃkhapaṭahairnṛtyadbhi rvārayauvataiḥ \|*  
*alaṃkṛtābhirnārībhirbālakaiḥ suvibhūṣitaiḥ \|\| 101 \|\|*

*bhūtebhyastu baliṃ dadyānmaṃtreṇānena sāmiṣam \|*  
*saraktaṃ sajalaṃ sānnaṃ gandhapuṣpākṣa tairyutam \|\| 102 \|\|*

100-102. During the procession, thousands of the learned people should carry a sword in one hand and a lamp in the other one, together with the domestic elephants and the warriors, producing the sound from the conches and drams, while dancing. The whore should also keep on dancing and singing, together with other ladies clad in beautiful garments and adorned with ornaments. The children should also accompany the ladies. Then for the sake of the goblins, one should make the sacrifice uttering the mantras, which should include blood, water, food, flowers and unbroken rice.

## \|\| 3.138.103-105 \|\|

*trīṃstrīnvārāṃstriśūlena digvidikṣu kṣipedbalim \|*  
*baliṃ gṛhṇantvimaṃ devā ādityā vasavastathā \|\| 103 \|\|*

*maruto'thāśvinau rudrāḥ suparṇā pannagā grahāḥ \|*  
*asurā yātudhānāśca mātaraśca piśācakāḥ \|\| 104 \|\|*

*śākinyo yakṣavetālā yoginyaḥ pūtanāḥ śivāḥ \|*  
*jṛṃbhakāḥ siddhagandharvā vyālā vidyādharā dharāḥ \|\| 105 \|\|*

103-105. These items of sacrifice should be kept thrice on all the four sides. Thereafter, one should pray- “Let all the Gods, Adityas, Vasus, Marudganas, Rudra, Garuda, serpents, the planets, Asuras, demons, Pisacas, the sacred mothers, Sakinis, Yaksas, Vetalas, Putana, Siva, Jambhakas, Siddhas, Gandharvas, the girls and Vidyadharas should accept the offering with pleasure.

## \|\| 3.138.106-107 \|\|

*dikpālā lokapālāśca ye ca vighnavināyakāḥ \|*  
*jagatāṃ śāṃtikartāro brahmādyāśca maharṣayaḥ \|\| 106 \|\|*

*savighnaṃ mama pāpaṃ te śāmyaṃtu paripanthinaḥ \|*  
*saumyā bhavaṃtu tṛptāśca bhūtāḥ pretāḥ sukhāvahāḥ \|\| 107 \|\|*

106-107. Let the Dikpalas, Lokapalas, Vighna-Vinayaka, the gods who maintain peace in the world, Brahma – the creator, Bhutas and Pretas should become benevolent on me, remove my obstacles and sins and make me comfortable.”

## \|\| 3.138.108-111 \|\|

*ityevaṃ bhrāmayedrāṣṭre durgāṃ devī rathe sthitām \|*  
*narayānena vā pārtha tato'vighnaṃ samāpayet \|\| 108 \|\|*

*athotpanneṣu vipreṣu bhūtaśāṃtiṃ samācaret \|*  
*yena vighnā na jāyaṃte yātrā saṃpūrṇatāṃ vrajet \|\| 109 \|\|*

*evaṃ ye kurvate yātrāṃ rājāno'nye'pi mānavāḥ \|*  
*mahānavamyāṃ naṃdāyāṃ putrakā hṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|\| 110 \|\|*

*te sarve pāpanirmuktā yāṃti bhāgavatīṃ purīm \|\| 111 \|\|*

108-111. О Partha, thus the goddess Durga, seated in a chariot, should be taken round in the entire country, and thereby the festival gets concluded without any obstruction. In case, an obstruction is caused, then the Bhuta-santi ceremony should be performed, by which the yatra should be completed without any obstruction. The king or the people who arrange this type of yatra or procession on the day of Mahanavami, they all remain happy with their families and the sons. Getting free from the sins, they achieve the excellent place of the goddess.

## \|\| 3.138.112-114 \|\|

*na teṣāṃ śāvako nāgnirna caurā na vināyakāḥ \|*  
*vighnaṃ kurvanti rājendra yeṣāṃ tuṣṭā maheśvarī \|\| 112 \|\|*

*nīrujaḥ sukhino bhogabhoktāro bhayavarjitāḥ \|*  
*bhavaṃti bhaktāḥ puruṣāḥ bhagavatyāḥ kimucyate \|\| 113 \|\|*

*ityeṣa te samākhyāto durgādevyā mahotsavaḥ \|*  
*paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ caiva sarvāśubhavināśanaḥ \|\| 114 \|\|*

112-114. О Rajendra, a person, on whom the goddess Mahesvari gets pleased, he does not have to face any obstruction from fire, thieves or from Vinayaka. On the other hand, he is freed from the ailments, becomes comfortable, enjoys all the pleasures and becomes the fearless devotee of the goddess. What more could be said on this subject? I have explained to you the method of the performing of the festival of the goddess Bhagavati, with the reading or the listening to of the same, a person is freed from the misfortune.

## \|\| 3.138.115 \|\|

*śūlāgrabhinnamahiṣāsurapṛṣṭhaviṣṭāmṛtkhātakhaḍgarucirāṃgadabāhudaṇḍām \|*  
*abhyarcya paṃcavadanānugatāṃ navamyāṃ durgāṃ sudurgagahanāni taraṃti martyāḥ \|\| 115 \|\|*

115\. In this way, by the worshiping of the goddess Durga on the day of Navami, the people face the horrible and dangerous situations with ease. She has five faces, shatters the body of Mahisasura with tip of the trident. She holds a sword in her raised hand, wears armlets over the arms and is adorned with other ornaments.

## Chapter 139. Indra’s flag festival

## \|\| 3.139.1-4 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*purā devāsure yuddhe brahmādyairamarairnṛpa \|*  
*vijayārthaṃ mahendrasya dhvajayaṣṭiḥ pratiṣṭhitā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*merorupari saṃsthāpya siddhavidyādharoragaiḥ \|*  
*sā devī hyarcitā nityaṃ bhūṣaṇairbhūṣitā svakaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*svacchatraghaṃṭāpiṭakaiḥ kiṃkiṇībaddhabudbudaiḥ \|*  
*tāṃ dṛṣṭvā dānavā naṣṭā bhayādeva raṇe hatāḥ \|*  
*gatā rasātalaṃ daityā devāścāpi divi sthitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tataḥ prabhṛti tāṃ divyāmiṃdrayaṣṭiṃ yajaṃti te \|*  
*devāḥ sarve gaṇāḥ sarve hṛṣṭāstuṣṭā yudhiṣṭhira \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О king, in earlier times, at the time of war between the gods and the demons, all the gods including Brahma and others established a flag for the victory of Indra. The Siddhas, Vidyadharas and the serpents established it over the peak of the Meru mountain and offering the ornaments and other riches to the same, they continued worship of the goddess, in which beautiful umbrellas, bells and small bells were presented in a beautiful vase. At the very sight of the goddess appearing on the scene, many of the demons, out of fright, were killed in the battleground itself. The rest of them fled to the nether world. The gods were again established in the heaven. О Yuddhistira, since that time, all the gods started adoring the Indra pole daily with delight. They all earned enough of merits by so doing.

## \|\| 3.139.5-11 \|\|

*ataḥ svargaṃ gato rājā bhūripuṇyavaśādvasuḥ \|*  
*indraloke mahābhāgo vasudevaiḥ supūjitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tasmai datā mahendreṇa vasuyaṣṭiḥ pragṛhyatām \|*  
*pūjayitvā mahābhāga sarvadaityāpanuttaye \|\| 6 \|\|*

*avatārya varṣāsamaye sarvairnṛpatibhiḥ saha \|*  
*mahyāṃ saṃpūjayāmāsa cakre ceṃdramahaṃ vasuḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*mahena maghavā prīto dadau puṇyaṃ vasorvaram \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yeṣu deśeṣu manujā bhaktibhāvapuraḥsarāḥ \|*  
*pūjayiṣyaṃti varṣānte mayā dattaṃ mahādhvajam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*teṣu deśeṣu muditāḥ prajā rogavivarjitāḥ \|*  
*prabhūtānnā dharmayuktā vṛṣamedhā mahotsavāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyaṃti suveṣāśca subhāṣāśca subhūṣaṇāḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

5-11. The king Vasu then proceeded on to the heaven, where in the divine city of Amaravati, he was honoured by all the gods. Then Mahendra gave away that pole known as Indra-yasti to him. О great one, for the destruction of all the Daityas, the same Indra-yasti was brought down on earth where it was established again. All the rulers of the world then worshipped the same. Thereafter, getting delighted, Indra gave over the same pole to Vasus. In whichever country the said pole (flag) is worshipped by the people with devotion during the rainy season, the people of that country shall always remain delighted, free of ailments, having enough of food grains, religious minded with sharp brains. They shall celebrate many festivals. Their beautiful costumes, praiseworthy speech and beautiful ornaments will impress all.

## \|\| 3.139.12 \|\|

*śrutvaitadvacanaṃ rājā vasurvasumatāṃ varaḥ \|*  
*viśeṣeṇa tataścakre varṣevarṣe mahotsavam \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. On hearing these words, the great king of Vasus started celebrating the festival every year with enthusiasm.

## \|\| 3.139.13-15 \|\|

*śravaṇe sthāpayedyaṣṭiṃ snānavastraiḥ prapūjitām \|*  
*dairghyeṇa viṃśatikarāṃ sāradārumayīṃ śubhām \|\| 13 \|\|*

*indrasthāne puroddiṣṭe indramātṛkasaṃjñake \|*  
*tasminyaṣṭiṃ nṛpo bhoktā svayaṃ yatnena yojayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

*vastrairvicitraiḥ saṃvītāṃ piṭikālaṃkṛtāṃ tathā \|*  
*piṭikānāṃ mahārāja kramaṃ ca kathayāmi te \|\| 15 \|\|*

13-15. The flag should be established in the Sravana constellation. It has then to be bathed. It should then be worshipped offering the costumes in an appropriate manner. An image of twenty cubits length should be made of gold, which should be auspicious looking. Then the place on earth should be selected and the king should himself consecrate the yasti. It should then be covered with an astonishing type of cloth. It should be covered with a large casket. О great king, I shall now speak about the sequence of the caskets.

## \|\| 3.139.16-17 \|\|

*prathamaṃ lokapālākhyaṃ caturasraṃ sakarṇikam \|*  
*yamendradhanadairyuktaṃ varuṇena samaṃ tataḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*vṛttaṃ khaṃḍāsrakaṃ ramyaṃ dvitīyaṃ raktacūrṇitam \|*  
*tṛtīyaṃ śvetakaṃ citramaṣṭāsra piṭakaṃ śubham \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. The first casket is known as that of Lokapala, which is square in shape with a pericarp. Indra, Kubera and Varuna always remain present there on all the four sides. The second casket is round, pleasant and is formed of the red powder. The third casket is of white colour. The third one is octagonal in shape.

## \|\| 3.139.18-19 \|\|

*caturthamindragopālavṛttaṃ mātṛsamāvṛtam \|*  
*pañcamaṃ cāṣṭakoṇaṃ tu śuklaṃ dhātuvicitritam \|\| 18 \|\|*

*kṛṣṇakarṇikayā ṣaṣṭhaṃ vṛttaṃ budbuda śobhitam \|*  
*saptamaṃ cāṣṭakoṇaṃ tu śuddhaṃ vidyādharairyutam \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. The fourth casket is known as Indra-Gopala which is circular and house the Mothers. The fifth casket is of white colour, octagonal in shape. It lacks the use of metals in making it. The sixth casket has a black pericarp, is circular in shape and decorated with small spots. The seventh casket is of white colour, octagonal in shape, in which Vidyadharas are lodged.

## \|\| 3.139.20 \|\|

*aṣṭamaṃ piṭakaṃ vṛttaṃ varatrāsūtraveṣṭitam \|*  
*navagrahayutaṃ dīptaṃ navamaṃ ca sacaṃḍikam \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The eighth casket is circular in shape and the thread is woven around it. The ninth casket houses the nine planets and the goddess Candika in the same.

## \|\| 3.139.21-23 \|\|

*brahmaviṣṇvīśasahitaṃ daśamaṃ śivasaṃsthitam \|*  
*kṛṣṇamekādaśaṃ vṛttaṃ yamayuktaṃ yudhiṣṭhira \|\| 21 \|\|*

*chātraṃ dvādaśamaṃ śuklaṃ dhvajadīrghaṃ trayodaśam \|*  
*sakuśaṃ puṣpasragdāmaghaṃṭācāmaracarcitam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*bandhayitvā candrapādai rajjubhiḥ sthūṇikāṃ naraiḥ \|*  
*śanairutthāpayetpārtha hutvā vaiśvānaraṃ dvijān \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. The tenth casket has Brahma, Viṣṇu and Mahesvara lodged in the same. The eleventh casket is of black colour, is circular in shape and Yama is lodged in it. О Yudhisthira, the casket with a white chatra is the twelfth one. The thirteenth casket has long flags. Making use of the kusa grass, the rosary, bell, flywhisk, decorating the same and making use of the ropes which should be white like the moon rays, they should be bound with the pillars. Thereafter, the Brahmanas should be served with payasam fried cakes.

## \|\| 3.139.24-28 \|\|

*dakṣiṇābhiśca saṃpūjya guḍapāyasapūpakaiḥ \|*  
*kuryānmahotsavaṃ rājā dināni nava sapta vā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*prekṣaṇīyairmahādānairnaṭaigītaiḥ kathānakaiḥ \|*  
*cakradolādharotsargaiḥ karkeṭairmallayodhanaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*veśyāṃganānarairhṛṣṭairdyūtakrīḍāmahotsavaiḥ \|*  
*karpūravastradānaiśca saṃmānaiśca parasparam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*rātrau prajāgaraḥ kāryo rakṣaṇāya prayatnataḥ \|*  
*kākolūkakapotānāṃ yena pāto na vidyate \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kākādbhavati durbhikṣaṃ kauśikānmriyate nṛpaḥ \|*  
*kapotācca prajānāśastato rakṣetsadodyataḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

24-28. They should then be given the daksina. The same should be raised slowly. A king should conclude the festival in seven or nine days, displaying exemplary charities, dancing and music, sports or gambling. Such people are delightfully honoured. There should also be give and take of charities, costumes etc. For the protection of the deities, the people should remain awake making all the efforts in order to avoid the dropping of the crows, pigeons and owls over the flag. Because with the fall of the droppings of the crow, the draught is spread in the kingdom. With the fall of the droppings of the owl, the ruler dies; while with the fall of the droppings of the pigeon, the people have to suffer.

## \|\| 3.139.29-32 \|\|

*śaithilyādgiribhicchakraḥ pramādānnīyate yadi \|*  
*tasmindeśe samutthānamindraketorna kārayet \|\| 29 \|\|*

*yāvattu nīyate sthānādanyasmādaiṃdrato dhvajaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*iṃdradhvajasamutthānaṃ pramādānna kṛtaṃ yadi \|*  
*tato dvādaśame varṣe kartavyaṃ nāṃtare punaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*kathaṃcidyadi vighnaḥ syādvipākaṃ me nibodha vai \|*  
*chatrabhaṃge cchatrabhaṃgo dhvaje rāṣṭraṃ vinaśyati \|\| 32 \|\|*

29-32. Therefore, arrangements should be made for suitable protection of the Indradhvaja. It should not be installed over a place, where it cannot stand firmly. Till such time another Indradhvaja arrives from some other place, till that time the same should be made to stand erect. In case due to some unavoidable reason, it cannot be moved, then it should be moved after complete twelve years and not in the middle. In case some obstruction is caused somehow, then I am speaking about the results thereof. With the breaking of the chatra or with the damage of the flag, the country has to face destruction.

## \|\| 3.139.33-35 \|\|

*mastake mantravicchedo mukhe mukhyabalakṣayaḥ \|*  
*bāhudaṃḍe vadetpīḍāṃ jaṭhare jāṭharaṃ bhayam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*varatrāyāṃ mitranāśaḥ sthūṇikāsu padātayaḥ \|*  
*kṣayaṃ gacchaṃti rājendra tasmādyatnātpuraṃdaram \|\| 34 \|\|*

*utthāpya pūjayedbhaktyā divārātramataṃdritaḥ \|*  
*pramādātpatite bhagne gate cendradhvaje dvidhā \|\| 35 \|\|*

33-35. In case some obstruction is caused, the minister gets destroyed with loss of the face and the army gets destroyed. With the loss of the pole, one develops pain in the arm. By the belly, one develops indigestion; with loss of the costumes, there happens to be the loss of a friend; with the loss of the pillar, the foot soldiers have to meet with death. Therefore, it is essential to protect the flag. О Rajendra, after the Indradhvaja is firmly established, it should be adored daily, during the night and the day. In case due to negligence, it is fallen, or is broken in two pieces, the broken part of it should be replaced with the gold or the silver and it should be raised up completely.

## \|\| 3.139.36-38 \|\|

*sauvarṇaṃ raupyakaṃ kṛtvā pūrṇamutthāpayeddhvajam \|*  
*śāṃtikaṃ pauṣṭikaṃ kṛtvā dvijebhyonnaṃ pradāpayet \|\| 36 \|\|*

*trapusaiḥ karkaṭībhiśca nālikeraiḥ kapitthakaiḥ \|*  
*bījapūraiḥ sanāraṃgairbhakṣyānnairvividhaistathā \|\| 37 \|\|*

*naivedyādibhirabhyarcya maṃtreṇānena toṣayet \|*  
*vajrahasta surārighna bahunetra puraṃdara \|*  
*kṣemārthaṃ sarvalokasya pūjeyaṃ pratigṛhyatām \|\| 38 \|\|*

36-38. Thereafter, performing the Santi and nourishing ceremonies, the food should be given to the Brahmanas, several types of eatables like cucumber, Feroia elephantum, coconut, myrobalan, orange and several other food items, should be given to the Brahmanas. Thereafter, he should offer the prayer with folded hands – “The destroyer of the demons, holding the vajra in hand and having many eyes, О Indra, for the welfare of all the people, you kindly accept the worship offered by me.”

## \|\| 3.139.39-40 \|\|

*śravaṇādbharaṇīṃ yāvatpūjāṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*rātrau visarjayecchakraṃ maṃtreṇānena pāṃḍava \|\| 39 \|\|*

*sārthaṃ surāsuragaṇaiḥ puraṃdaraśatakrato \|*  
*upahāraṃ gṛhītvainaṃ mahendradhvaja gamyatām \|\| 40 \|\|*

39-40. Thus from the Sravana constellation to the Bharana constellation, one should keep on worshipping. One should make the deities depart, reciting the following mantras – O Purandara and Satakratu, in the company of the Suras and Asuras and Mahendradhvaja, you kindly accept the gift now being offered by me.”

## \|\| 3.139.41 \|\|

*evaṃ yaḥ kurute yātrāmindraketoryudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*parjanyaḥ kāmavarṣī syāttasminrāṣṭre na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. O Yudhisthira, when the Indradhvaja is so moved, the clouds drop timely rains in the country. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.139.42 \|\|

*ītayo na pravartaṃte tasmānmṛtyukṛtaṃ bhayam \|*  
*vijitya śatrūnsamare vaśe kṛtvā mahītalam \|*  
*bhuktvā rājyaṃ ciraṃkālamindraloke mahīyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. One does not have to face any danger except the death. He becomes victorious over all the enemies, he exercises his sovereignty over the entire universe and enjoys the royal pleasures for long and ultimately, he is lodged in Indraloka.

## \|\| 3.139.43 \|\|

*rāṣṭre pure ca nagare surarājaketoryatrotsavo nṛpajanaiḥ kriyate sametya \|*  
*duṣṭopasargajanitaṃ paracakrajaṃ vā tasminbhayaṃ bhavati pārtha na kiñcideva \|\| 43 \|\|*

43\. О Partha, in case the Indradhvaja is installed in a country, then after performing the related rites in its cities and towns, the country is freed from the attack of the other countries as well as the wicked people.

## Chapter 140. The Dipavali festival

## \|\| 3.140.1-4 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*purā vāmanarūpeṇa yācayitvā dharāmimām \|*  
*baliyajñe hariḥ sarvaṃ krāṃtavānvikramaistribhiḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*indrāya dattavānrājyaṃ baliṃ pātālavāsinam \|*  
*kṛtvā daityapatervāsamahorātraṃ punarnṛpa \|\| 2 \|\|*

*ekameva hi bhogārthaṃ balirājyeticihnitam \|*  
*sarahasyaṃ tadetatte kathayāmi narottama \|\| 3 \|\|*

*kārttike kṛṣṇapakṣasya pañcadaśyāṃ niśāgame \|*  
*yatheṣṭaceṣṭā daityānāṃ rājyaṃ teṣāṃ mahītale \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О king, in earlier times, lord Viṣṇu taking to the form of Vamana, went to yajna of daitya King Bali, and begged for three feet length of earth and got control over the whole universe. Then lord Viṣṇu gave out the kingship of the heaven to Indra. Thereafter, Bali – the lord of the daityas was permanently lodged in the netherworld. For the use of the daityas only, one symbol was given to the daitya king Bali, which is quite a secret and I am going to reveal the same to you. On the moonless night of the month of Kartika, the daityas rule the earth. All of them fulfill their desires on that particular day.

## \|\| 3.140.5-6 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*niśśeṣeṇa hṛṣīkeśa kaumudīṃ brūhi me prabho \|*  
*kimarthaṃ dīyate dānaṃ tasyāṃ kā devatā bhavet \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kiṃsvittasyai bhaveddeyaṃ kebhyo devaṃ janārdana \|*  
*praharṣaḥ ko'tra nirdiṣṭaḥ krīḍā kātra prakīrtitā \|\| 6 \|\|*

5-6. Yudhisthira said – О lord Hṛṣīkeśa, you kindly let me know in detail about the moonless night. Who are the prominent gods there, and what all is offered to them? What is the cause of so much of enjoyment on that particular day? What types of sports are enjoyed by the people on that particular day?

## \|\| 3.140.7-9 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*kārttike kṛṣṇapakṣe ca caturdaśyāṃ dinodaye \|*  
*avaśyameva kartavyaṃ snānaṃ narakabhīrubhiḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*apāmārgapallavānvā bhrābhayenmastakopari \|*  
*sītāloṣṭasamāyuktasakaṃṭakadalānvitān \|\| 8 \|\|*

*hara pāpamapāmārga bhrāmyamāṇaṃ punaḥpunaḥ \|*  
*āpadaṃ kilbiṣaṃ cāpi mamāpahara sarvaśaḥ \|*  
*apāmārga namastestu śarīraṃ mama śodhaya \|\| 9 \|\|*

7-9. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – On the dark caturdasi of the month of Kartika, the people, who are afraid of the hell, must take the bath. Thereafter, the snake gourd or its leaves should be made round the head, mixed with the sand of the earth dug with the ploughshare full of thorns etc. At that point of time, you should say – “O Apamarga, by repeatedly rotating you around my head, let all my sins be removed. This is the Apamarga bhramana mantra. Let all my sins and miseries be removed and let my body be purified. I offer salutation to you, again and again.”

## \|\| 3.140.10 \|\|

*tataśca tarpaṇaṃ kāryaṃ dharmarājasya nāmabhiḥ \|*  
*yamāya dharmarājāya mṛtyave cāṃtakāya ca \|*  
*vaivasvatāya kālāya sarvabhūtakṣayāya ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. Thereafter, uttering the name of Dharmaraja, the oblation should be offered to him. He should further say that I am offering the oblation, in order to please the gods like – Yama, Dharmaraja, Mrtyu, Antaka, Vaivasvata, Kala and the one who destroys all the living beings.

## \|\| 3.140.11-13 \|\|

*narakāya pradātavyo dīpaḥ saṃpūjya devatāḥ \|*  
*tataḥ pradoṣasamaye dīpāndadyānmanoramān \|\| 11 \|\|*

*brahmaviṣṇuśivādīnāṃ bhavaneṣu maṭheṣu ca \|*  
*kūṭāgāreṣu caityeṣu sabhāsu ca nadīṣu ca \|\| 12 \|\|*

*prākārodyānavāpīṣu pratolīniṣkuṭeṣu ca \|*  
*siddhārhabuddhacāmuṃḍābhairavāyataneṣu ca \|*  
*maṃdurāsu viviktāsu hastiśālāsu caiva hi \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. After adoration of the gods, during the evening time, charities may be given in the temples of Brahma, Viṣṇu, Siva and other gods, besides in the Mathas, the commercial establishments, Caityas, meeting halls, river banks, gorges, orchards, stepwells, drains, the pleasure groves, Siddhas and Buddhas, besides the temples of Bhairava and Camunda, elephants and horse stables. The lamps should be lighted at these places in order to prevent oneself from falling in the hell.

## \|\| 3.140.14-15 \|\|

*evaṃ prabhātasamaye'māvāsyāyāṃ narādhipa \|*  
*snātvā devānpitṝnbhaktyā saṃpūjyātha praṇamya ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*kṛtvā tu pārvaṇaṃ śrāddhaṃ dadhikṣīraghṛtādibhiḥ \|*  
*bhojyairnānāvidhairviprānbhojayitvā kṣamāpya ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. On the moonless night, taking a bath in the early morning, the gods and the manes should be adored, and the Parvana Sraddha should be concluded. Several types of eatables made in milk, curd, ghi etc., should be served to the Brahmanas to please them. Thereafter, one should forgiveness from them.

## \|\| 3.140.16 \|\|

*tato'parāhṇasamaye ghoṣayennagare nṛpaḥ \|*  
*adya rājyaṃ balerlokā yatheṣṭaṃ modyatāmiti \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. During the evening time, the king should make an announcement in the city with the beating of the drums that – “Today is the day of Baliraja, therefore, all the people should enjoy themselves.”

## \|\| 3.140.17-18 \|\|

*lokaścāpi pare hṛṣyetsudhādhavalitājire \|*  
*vṛkṣacandanamālāḍhyaiścarcite ca gṛhegṛhe \|\| 17 \|\|*

*dyūtapānaratodṛptanaranārīmanohare \|*  
*nṛtyavāditrasaṃghuṣṭe samprajvalitadīpake \|\| 18 \|\|*

17-18. Listening to this, the people of the town decorated themselves with the flower plants, with the sandal paste and the flower garlands. Thereafter, in the courtyards of the houses, which look shining, all the men and women got engaged in sports like gambling and others, besides dancing, singing and the welfare sounds. Several lamps were also lighted there.

## \|\| 3.140.19-25 \|\|

*anyonyaprītisaṃhṛṣṭadattalābhena vai jane \|*  
*tāṃbūlahṛṣṭa vadane kuṅkumakṣodacarcite \|\| 19 \|\|*

*dukūlapaṭṭanepathye svarṇamāṇikyabhūṣite \|*  
*adbhutodbhaṭaśṛṃgārapradarśitakutūhale \|\| 20 \|\|*

*yuvatījanasaṃkīrṇavastrojjvalavihāriṇi \|*  
*dīpamālākule ramye vidhvastadhvāṃtasañcaye \|*  
*pradoṣe doṣarahite śastadoṣāgame śubhe \|\| 21 \|\|*

*śaśipūrṇamukhābhiśca kanyābhiḥ kṣiptataṇḍulam \|*  
*nīrājanaṃ prakartavyaṃ vṛkṣaśākhāsu dīpakaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*bhrāmyamāṇo nato mūrghni manujānāṃ janādhipaḥ \|*  
*vṛkṣaśākhāṃtadīpānāṃ nirastāddarśanādvrajet \|*  
*nīrājanaṃ tu teneha procyate vijayapradam \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tasmājjanena kartavyaṃ rakṣodoṣabhayāpaham \|*  
*yātrāvihārasañcāre jayajīveti vādinā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*kṣudropasargarahite rājacaurabhayojjhite \|*  
*mitrasvajanasambandhisuhatpremānuraṃjite \|\| 25 \|\|*

19-25. Filled with utmost devotion and love, the people engaged themselves in the exchange of various types of gifts and presents. They used the betel for chewing it in the mouth. The vermilion was used to decorate the body. Thereafter, clad in astonishing types of costumes and ornaments, the performers in the dancing hall displayed excellent type of acting. The ladies lighted surprising types of lamps. Then during the midnight, in the well lit places, the girls with moon like faces should perform the arati of the trees. At the same time, the king, lowering his head, should accept the arati, should leave the place when the lamps get extinguished. The performing of the arati believes to bestow the victory. For the removal of the blemish of the Raksasas, the people must to perform the arati. At the mid of night, when the slogans of “victory to jiva” are raised, the petty obstructions do not occur. The people are free from the danger from the ruler as well as the thieves. All the friends, relatives and other noble people, remain engaged in pleasant conversation.

## \|\| 3.140.26-28 \|\|

*tato'rddharātrasamaye svayaṃ rājā vrajetpuram \|*  
*avalokayituṃ ramyaṃ padbhyāmeva śanaiḥśanaiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*mahatā tūryaghoṣeṇa jvaladbhirhastadīpakaiḥ \|*  
*kṛtaśobhāṃ purīṃ paśyetkṛtarakṣāṃ svakairnaraiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahadāścaryamṛddhiṃ caivātmanaḥ śubhām \|*  
*balirājyapramodaṃ ca tataḥ svagṛhamāvrajet \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. During the midnight, the king himself, in order to observe the festivities, should move in the city on foot to enjoy the festivities. While walking slowly, the trumpets, cymbals and other musical instruments should be sounded. The lighted lamps should be carried by the royal servants in the well decorated city, which should be astonishingly decorated displaying the grandeur of the king as well. Achieving the delight of the king Bali, he should then return to his palace.

## \|\| 3.140.29 \|\|

*evaṃ gate niśārdhe tu jane nidrārdralocane \|*  
*tāvannagaranārībhiḥ śūrpaḍiṃḍimavādanaiḥ \|*  
*niṣkrāmyate prahṛṣṭābhiralakṣmīḥ svagṛhāṃgaṇāt \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. When the people are fast asleep at the dead of night, the women of the city, playing on the musical instruments, should drive out the Alaksmi or misfortune from the houses, using a winnowing basket.

## \|\| 3.140.30-36 \|\|

*tataḥ prabuddhe sakale jane jātamahotsave \|*  
*mālyadīpakahaste ca snehanirbharalocane \|\| 30 \|\|*

*veśyā vilāsinī sārdhaṃ svasti maṃgalakāriṇī \|*  
*gṛhādgṛhaṃ vrajantī ca pādābhyaṃgapradāyinī \|\| 31 \|\|*

*piṣṭakodvartanapare guruśuśrūṣaṇākule \|*  
*dvijābhivādanapare sukharājyābhivīkṣaṇe \|\| 32 \|\|*

*suvāsinībhyo dāne ca dīyamāne yadṛcchayā \|*  
*yathāprabhātasamaye rājārhamānayejjanam \|\| 33 \|\|*

*sadbhāvenaiva santoṣyā devāḥ satpuruṣā dvijāḥ \|*  
*itare cānnapānena vākpradānena paṃḍitāḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vastraistāṃbūladānaiśca puṣpakarpūrakuṃkumaiḥ \|*  
*bhakṣyairuccāvacairbhojyairantaḥpuravilāsinīḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*grāmairviṣayadānaiśca sāmaṃtanṛpatīndhanaiḥ \|*  
*padātīnaṅgasaṃlagnāngraiveyakaṭakaiḥ svakān \|\| 36 \|\|*

30-36. When the people become alert because of the festivity, holding the lamps as well as the garlands in hands, with the eyes filled with affection, the concubines together with other ladies move from one house to another and offer the red paste to the ladies of the other house which is used over the body, besides serving the preceptors. In that comfortable kingdom, when it is performed, the Brahmanas remain busy in blessing others. The chaste and respectable women should be honoured with gifts of their liking. In the early morning, the king should adore the respectable persons. The gods, noble people and the Brahmanas are pleased by enormous goodwill. The other people should also be served with food, the learned people with the noble words, costumes betel, flowers, camphor, vermilion and excellent eatables, by the noble ladies of the household. The people of high class of the society like ministers, landlords, as well as the foot soldiers should be graced by giving away of riches, the ornaments adorning one’s own body, or the armlets should also be given to the foot soldiers.

## \|\| 3.140.37-42 \|\|

*svayaṃ rājā toṣayetsa janānbhṛtyānpṛthakpṛthak \|*  
*yathārhaṃ toṣayitvā tu tato mallanaṭānbhaṭān \|\| 37 \|\|*

*vṛṣabhānmahiṣāṃścaiva yudhyamānānparaiḥ saha \|*  
*gajānaśvāṃśca yodhāṃśca padātīnsamalaṃkṛtān \|\| 38 \|\|*

*maṃcārūḍhaḥ svayaṃ paśyennaṭanartakacāraṇān \|*  
*kruddhāpayedānayecca gomahiṣyādikaṃ tataḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*diṣṭyā kāryaṃ payojyotiruktipratyuktikā vadet \|*  
*tatoparāhnasamaye pūrvasyāṃ diśi bhārata \|\| 40 \|\|*

*mārgapālīṃ prabadhnīyāttuṃgastaṃbhe'tha pādape \|*  
*kuśakāśamayīṃ divyāṃ saṃbhave bahubhirvṛtām \|\| 41 \|\|*

*pūjayitvā gajānvājīnsārdhe yāmatraye gate \|*  
*gāvo vṛṣāḥ samahiṣā maṃḍitā ghaṭikotkaṭāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

37-42. Thereafter, the king should please all the people individually. Then the sports like the wrestling match, the acrobats and the bull war should be played. The male buffaloes, the horses, elephants and the decorated soldiers should also be honoured. The king then should listen to the songs of the acrobats, dancers, the Caranas as well as the bards, and should distribute the rewards to them with delight. The male buffaloes and the bullocks, who were in rage while fighting in the battlefield, should be neutralized and then honour them saying – “They could be honoured by good luck alone.” These words should be supported. In the forenoon, they should be bound with a tree on the way, which should be made of the kusa grass and should be of several locks. During the third prahara of the day, the elephants and horses should be worshipped and thereafter, the cows, bulls and male buffaloes should be decorated with the bells.

## \|\| 3.140.43-50 \|\|

*kṛte home dvijendraistu gṛhṇīyānmārgapālikām \|*  
*rāṣṭrabhojyena dhārābhiḥ sahasreṇa śatena vā \|\| 43 \|\|*

*svaśaktyapekṣayā vāpi gṛhṇīyādvāmabhojanaiḥ \|*  
*mātuḥ kulaṃ pitṛkulamātmānaṃ sahabaṃdhubhiḥ \|\| 44 \|\|*

*saṃtārayetsa sakalaṃ mārgapālīṃ dadāti yaḥ \|*  
*nīrājanaṃ ca tatraiva kāryaṃ rājñe jayapradam \|\| 45 \|\|*

*mārgapālītalenetthaṃ hayā gāvo gajā vṛṣāḥ \|*  
*rājāno rājaputrāśca brāhmaṇā śūdrajātayaḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*mārgapālīṃ samullaṃghya nīrujaḥ syātsukhī sadā \|*  
*kṛtvaitatsarvameveha rātrau daityapaterbaleḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*pūjāṃ kuryānnaraḥ sākṣādbhūmau maṃḍalake kṛte \|*  
*balimālikhya daityendraṃ varṇakaiḥ paṃcaraṃgakaiḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*sarvābharaṇasaṃpūrṇaṃ viṃdhyāvalyā sahāsitam \|*  
*kūṣmāṃḍabāṇajaṃghorumuradānavasaṃvṛtam \|\| 49 \|\|*

*saṃpūrṇahṛṣṭavadanaṃ kirīṭotkaṭakuṇḍalam \|*  
*dvibhujaṃ daityarājānaṃ kārayitvā nṛpaḥ svayam \|\| 50 \|\|*

43-50. Thereafter, the royal food and Sahasradhara as per one’s means, should be offered to the Brahmanas who have concluded the homa ceremony. The one who provides a pillar, redeems all the people from the father and mother’s side. At the same place, the arati for the king should be offered. The horses, cows, elephants, bulls, the king, the princes, Brahmanas and Sudras should collect under the pillar, for their benefit. On the day of that festival, the night program should be completed and an image of daitya couple Bali should be made and worshipped. In a mandala, the image of Bali should be made in five colours, which should be surrounded by pumpkin, arrows and weapons. The Danava Mura should also be present there. It should prominently display the demon king’s limbs including thighs and knees. The daitya king Bali should have a smiling face. He should be adorned with the kirita crown and should have two arms only.

## \|\| 3.140.51 \|\|

*gṛhasya madhye śālāyāṃ viśālāyāṃ tato'rcayet \|*  
*bhrātṛmaṃtrijanaiḥ sārddhaṃ saṃtuṣṭo vaṃdibhiḥ stutaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. The image of Bali should be kept in the centre of the courtyard. He should be worshipped by the courtiers and relatives. The bards should sing for his glory.

## \|\| 3.140.52-54 \|\|

*kamalaiḥ kumudaiḥ puṣpaiḥ kahlārai raktakotpalaiḥ \|*  
*gandhadhūpānnanaivedyairakṣatairguḍapūpakaiḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

*madyamāṃsasurālehyadīpavartyupahārakaiḥ \|*  
*maṃtreṇānena rājendra samaṃtrī sapurohitaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*balirāja namastubhyaṃ virocanasuta prabho \|*  
*bhaviṣyendrasurārāte pūjeyaṃ pratigṛhyatām \|\| 54 \|\|*

52-54. The lotus flowers, red lotus flowers, fragrance, incense, food, eatables, unbroken rise, raw sugar, fried cakes, beverages, meat, etc. should be given over to the courtiers. In order to please them with other gifts, the mantras should be recited by the priests thus- “O lord, О son of Virocana, О Baliraja, salutation to you. You are the enemy of the future Indra as well. You kindly accept my adoration.”

## \|\| 3.140.55 \|\|

*evaṃ pūjāṃ nṛpaḥ kṛtvā rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ tataḥ \|*  
*kārayetprekṣaṇīyādi naṭakṣatrakathānakaiḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

55\. Thus performing the puja during the night, keeping themselves awake for the whole night, the actors should display the themes of the heroic stories.

## \|\| 3.140.56-58 \|\|

*lokaścāpi gṛhasyāṃte śayyāyāṃ śuklataṃḍulaiḥ \|*  
*saṃsthāpya balirājānaṃ phalaiḥ puṣpaiśca pūjayet \|\| 56 \|\|*

*balimuddiśya dīyaṃte dānāni kurunandana \|*  
*yāni tānyakṣayāṇyāhurmayaivaṃ saṃpradarśitam \|\| 57 \|\|*

*yadasyāṃ dīyate dānaṃ svalpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu \|*  
*tadakṣayaṃ bhavetsarvaṃ viṣṇoḥ prītikaraṃ param \|\| 58 \|\|*

56-58. Similarly, all the people should place the image of the king Bali over a bed in a room spreading the unbroken rice and thus worship it offering the flowers etc. О son of the race of Kuru, the charities which are given for the sake of the king Bali, remain everlasting and I have spoken about the same in an exhaustive manner. Because on the moonless day, whatever little is given in charity, it becomes everlasting and is extremely liked by lord Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 3.140.59-60 \|\|

*viṣṇunā vasudhā labdhā prītena balaye punaḥ \|*  
*upakārakaro dattaścāsurāṇāṃ mahotsavaḥ \|\| 59 \|\|*

*tataḥ prabhṛti rājendra pravṛttā kaumudī punaḥ \|*  
*sarvopadravavidrāvi sarvavighnavināśinī \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. Lord Viṣṇu extracted the land from the daitya king Bali and in return, for the benefit of the asuras, this festival was introduced to them. Since then, this is known as Kaumudi Mahotsava which is being celebrated on earth since then. It subsides all the disturbances and removes all the obstructions.

## \|\| 3.140.61-71 \|\|

*lokaśokaharī kāmyā dhanapuṣṭisukhāvahā \|*  
*kuśabdena mahī jñeyā mudī harṣe tataḥ param \|\| 61 \|\|*

*dhātujñairnaigamajñaiśca tenaiṣā kaumudī smṛtā \|*  
*kau modante janā yasyāṃ nānābhāvaiḥ parasparā \|\| 62 \|\|*

*hṛṣṭāstuṣṭāḥ sukhāyattāstenaiṣā kaumudī smṛtā \|*  
*kumudāni baleryasmāddīyante'syāṃ yudhiṣṭhira \|\| 63 \|\|*

*arthārthe pārtha bhūmau ca tenaiṣā kaumudī smṛtā \|*  
*ekamevamahorātraṃ varṣe varṣe viśāṃpate \|\| 64 \|\|*

*dattaṃ dānavarājasya ādarśamiva bhūtale \|*  
*yaḥ karoti nṛpo rāṣṭraṃ tasya vyādhibhayaṃ kutaḥ \|\| 65 \|\|*

*kuta īti bhayaṃ tatra nāsti mṛtyukṛtaṃ bhayam \|*  
*subhikṣaṃ kṣemamārogyaṃ sarvasampada uttamāḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*nīrujaśca janāḥ sarve sarvopadravavarjitāḥ \|*  
*kaumudīkaraṇādrājanbhavatīha mahītale \|\| 67 \|\|*

*yo yādṛśena bhāvena tiṣṭhatyasyāṃ yudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*harṣadainyādirūpeṇa tasya varṣaṃ prayāti hi \|\| 68 \|\|*

*rudite roditi varṣaṃ hṛṣṭo varṣaṃ prahṛṣyati \|*  
*bhuktau bhoktā bhavedvarṣaṃ svasthaḥ svastho bhavediti \|\| 69 \|\|*

*tasmātprahṛṣṭaistuṣṭaiśca kartavyā kaumudī naraiḥ \|*  
*vaiṣṇavī dānavī ceyaṃ tithiḥ paitrī yudhiṣṭhira \|\| 70 \|\|*

*upaśamitameghanādaṃ prajvalitadaśānanaṃ ramitarāmam \|*  
*rāmāyaṇamiva subhagaṃ dīpadinaṃ haratu vo duritam \|\| 71 \|\|*

61-71. It also removes the grief of the people. It fulfills all the desires and increases riches and is quite comfortable. In the word Kaumudi, ku stands for earth and muda means delight. Therefore, with the conjunction of roots, it is called Kaumudi. On the earth, the way in which the people get extremely delighted, healthy, contented and comfortable, such a situation is called Kaumudi. О Yudhisthira, on that particular day, sacrifice is given for the sake of Bali with delight and as such, it is also called Kaumudi. О Partha, thus during every year, the offerings are made to the king Bali on the earth. It symbolizes the height of the noble feelings for him. A king who performs this, no danger for the spread of the disease or the excess of anything has to be faced. Even the fear of the death becomes rare. On the other hand, there are plenty of cereals and grains in the country, besides spread of happiness and prosperity. The people are freed from ailments, have plenty of wealth with them. The people get free from all the disturbances and are healthy. As a result of the completion of the Kaumudi festival, the people achieve these merits. On the moonless day, whosoever performs this festival with whatever intentions, his whole year is happily spent. In case a person weeps on that day, his whole year will be passed in the same condition. In case that day is spent happily, he remains happy for the whole year. He gets good food, remains healthy throughout the year. Therefore, the people should celebrate the Kaumudi festival with utmost delight. This is also the ancestral tithi for the Vaiṣṇavas and the Danavas. Therefore, this festival should also be celebrated for the sake of father or the ancestors. As in the Ramayana, the end of the great warrior like Meghanada, while Rama is enticed or bewitched and Ravana lost his self control and gets in flames, have been mentioned, let this Dipavali remove all your misfortunes.

## \|\| 3.140.72-73 \|\|

*kūṣmāṇḍādānaramyaṃ kuvalayakhaṇḍaiśca dhātukābhadram \|*  
*śaradiva harigatanidraṃ dīpadinaṃ haratu vo duritam \|\| 72 \|\|*

*dīpotsave janitasarvajanapramodāṃ kurvaṃti ye sumanaso balirājapūjām \|*  
*dānopabhogasukhavṛddhiśatākulānāṃ harṣeṇa varṣamiha pārthiva yāti teṣām \|\| 73 \|\|*

72-73. Having been beautified with giving away of a pumpkin, decorated with the pieces of lotus stalks, in the winter season during which lord Viṣṇu awakes from sleep, let this day of Dipavali brings fortune for you. The people who perform the worship of the daitya king Bali, they achieve hundreds of comforts and the whole year of the noble souls is being spent pleasantly.

## Chapter 141. Navagraha Laksa Homa Vidhi

## \|\| 3.141.1 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*kathayasva mahābhāga sarvajño hyasi yādava \|*  
*sarvakāmāptaye kṛtyaṃ kathaṃ śāṃtikapauṣṭikam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Yudhisthira said – О excellent Yadava, you are omniscient one, for the success of all the desires, how could a peaceful as well as the progressive activity be performed?

## \|\| 3.141.2-6 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*śrīkāmaḥ śāntikāmo vā grahayajñaṃ samārabhet \|*  
*dṛṣṭyāyuḥ puṣṭikāmo vā tathaivābhicaranpunaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sarvaśāstrāṇyanukramya saṃkṣipya granthavistaram \|*  
*grahaśāṃtiṃ pravakṣyāmi purāṇaśrutibhāṣitām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*puṇye'hni viprakathite kṛtvā brāhmaṇavācanam \|*  
*grahāngrahādhidevāṃśca sthāpya homaṃ samārabhet \|\| 4 \|\|*

*grahayajñastridhā proktaḥ purāṇaśrutikovidaiḥ \|*  
*prathamo'yutahomaḥ syāllakṣahomastataḥ param \|\| 5 \|\|*

*tṛtīyaḥ koṭihomastu sarvakāmaphalapradaḥ \|*  
*ayutenāhutīnāṃ ca navagrahamakhaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

2-6. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – For the earning of wealth, desire of having peace, long life, progress and prosperity, yajna should be performed in home. For the success of all the above, he should make efforts constantly. In the sequence of all the scriptures, I shall not expand the book, I shall only say this much in brief which has been exhaustively explained in the Puranas and the Srutis. On an auspicious day as prescribed by a Brahmana, the Svastivacana should be recited by the Brahmanas, consecrating and invoking the planets as well as their chief god. They should be worshipped thereafter. The homa should then be performed. The learned persons who are well-versed in the Srutis and the Puranas, have described the process of this yajna in three ways. The first one is of ten thousand offerings, then the other one is with a lakh of offerings and the third one is for the offering of a crore of ahutis. The homa with the thousand of offerings is known as navagraha yajna.

## \|\| 3.141.7-11 \|\|

*tasya tāvadvidhiṃ vakṣye purāṇaśrutibhāṣitam \|*  
*gartasyottarapūrveṇa vitastidvayavistṛtām \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kuryādvidhānato vediṃ vitastyucchrayasaṃyutām \|*  
*saṃsthāpanāya devānāṃ caturasrāmudakplavām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*agnipraṇayanaṃ kṛtvā tasyāmāvāhayetsurān \|*  
*devānāṃ tatra saṃsthāpyā viṃśatirdvādaśādhikā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*sūryaḥ somo mahīputro budho jīvaḥ sitorkajaḥ \|*  
*rāhuḥ keturiti proktā grahālokahitāvahāḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tāmrakātsphaṭikādraktacandanātsvarṇajāvubhau \|*  
*rajatādāyasāccaiva grahāḥ kāryāḥ kramādamī \|\| 11 \|\|*

7-11. The process of the same is being spoken by me, which you please listen. On the north east of the altar, a pedestal of a cubit in size and suitable height, should be made in an appropriate manner. It should be the square one and water should be poured over it. With the igniting the fire, the gods should be invoked. Thirty two gods including the Sun, the Moon, Mars, Budha, Brhaspati, Sukra, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu and other favourable planets should also be invoked and consecrated. At that point of time, their figures made in copper, crystal, red sandal paste, gold, besides those of irons should be consecrated there.

## \|\| 3.141.12-17 \|\|

*madhye tu bhāskaraṃ vidyāllohitaṃ dakṣiṇena tu \|*  
*uttareṇa guruṃ vidyādbudhaṃ pūrvottareṇa tu \|\| 12 \|\|*

*pūrveṇa bhārgavaṃ vidyātsomaṃ dakṣiṇapūrvake \|*  
*paścimottarataḥ ketuṃ sthāpayecchuklataṃḍulaiḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*rājāmātyānmahārāja taṃḍulaiḥ sthāpayedatha \|*  
*bhāskarasyeśvaraṃ vidyādumāṃ ca śaśinastathā \|\| 14 \|\|*

*skandamaṅgārakasyāpi budhasya ca tathā harim \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ ca gurorvidyācchukrasyāpi śacīpatim \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śanaiścarasya tu yamaṃ rāhoḥ kālaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*ketostu citraguptaṃ tu sarveṣāmeva devatāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*agnirāpaḥ kṣitirviṣṇurindraḥ sauvarṇadevatāḥ \|*  
*prajāpatiśca sūryaśca brahmā pratyadhidevatāḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

12-17. The Sungod should be lodged in the middle of the pedestal; Mangala should be lodged in the south; Brhaspati in the north; Buddha in the north-east, Sukra in the east; the Moon in the south-east; and Ketu besides the king and the ministers should be lodged in north-west, spreading the white unbroken rice. Mahadeva is the supreme lord for the Sun. For Moon, the goddess Uma is supreme. Skanda is the lord of Mangala, while Hari is the lord of Buddha. Brahma is the lord of Brhaspati, while Indra is the lord of Sukra. Yama is the lord of Saturn, Kala is the lord of Rahu, while Citragupta is the lord of Ketu. Similarly, Agni, Varuna, Earth, Viṣṇu, Indra, Sauvarna Prajapati, Surya and Brahma are the additional gods.

## \|\| 3.141.18-20 \|\|

*vināyakaṃ tathā durgāṃ vāyumākāśameva ca \|*  
*sāvitrīṃ ca tathā lakṣmīmumāṃ ca sahabhartṛkām \|\| 18 \|\|*

*āvāhayedvyāhṛtibhistathaivāśvikumārakau \|*  
*saṃsmaredraktamādityamaṃgārakasamanvitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*somaśukrau yathāśvetau budhajīvau ca piṅga lau \|*  
*maṃdarāhū tathā kṛṣṇau dhūmraṃ ketuguṇaṃ viduḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

18-20. After invoking all these gods, Vinayaka, Durga, Vayu, Akasa, Savitri, Laksmi, Uma with Siva, Vyahrtis and Asvinikumaras should also be invoked and worshipped. Surya and Mangala are of red colour; the Moon and Sukra are of white complexions; while Budha is of green colour. Brhaspati is of yellow colour; Sani and Rahu are of black colour; while Ketu is of smoke colour.

## \|\| 3.141.21-22 \|\|

*grahavarṇāni deyāni vāsāṃsi kusumāni ca \|*  
*gaṃdhāśca balayaścaiva dhūpā guggulapūrvakāḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*guḍaudanaṃ raverdadyātsomāya ghṛtapāyasam \|*  
*aṃgārakāya saṃyāvaṃ budhāya kṣīraṣaṣṭikam \|\| 22 \|\|*

21-22. While performing the puja, the planets should be given clothes according to their respective colours. Thereafter, the fragrance, incense, guggulu should also be offered during the worship. The sweet rice should be offered to the Sungod. Moon should be given the payasam mixed with ghi. Mangala should be pleased by offering the pudding. Budha should be pleased with rice mixed with milk.

## \|\| 3.141.23-25 \|\|

*dadhyannaṃ gurave dadyācchakrāya tu ghṛtaudanam \|*  
*śanaiścarāya kṛśaraṃ meṣamāṃsaṃ tu rāhave \|\| 23 \|\|*

*citraudanaṃ ketave ca sarvānbhakṣyairathārcayet \|*  
*prāguttareṇa tasmācca dadhyakṣatavibhūṣitam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*cūta pallavasaṃpannaṃ phalavastrayugānvitam \|*  
*pañcaratnasamāyuktaṃ pañcabhaṃgayutaṃ tathā \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. Brhaspati should be pleased with cooked rice and curd, Sani should be pleased with cooked mixed grains. Rahu should be pleased with the meat of a sheep and Ketu is pleased with Citraudana (rice). Thereafter, all the gods should be delighted with excellent food. Towards the north, an unbroken beautifully decorated pitcher should be established putting the curd, tender shoots of mango tree, fruit, costumes, besides the five types of gems should be kept in it along with the pancagavya.

## \|\| 3.141.26 \|\|

*sthāpayedavraṇaṃ kuṃbhaṃ varuṇaṃ tatra vinyaset \|*  
*gaṃgāyāḥ saritaḥ sarvāḥ samudrāśca sarāṃsi ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. The god Varuna should be consecrated over it. All the rivers like Ganga and oceans should be invoked in the same.

## \|\| 3.141.27 \|\|

*gajāśvarathyāvalmīkātsaṃgamāddhṛdagokulāt \|*  
*mṛdamānīya rājendra sarvauṣadhijalānvitām \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. The dust of elephant stable, horse stable, crossings, white ant hill, confluence of rivers, the tanks, cowpen, together with all the herbs should be poured in pitcher.

## \|\| 3.141.28-32 \|\|

*snānārthaṃ vinyasettatra yajamānasya dharmavit \|*  
*sarve samudrāḥ saritaḥ saraḥ prasravaṇāni ca \|\| 28 \|\|*

*āyāṃtu yajamānasya duritakṣayakārakāḥ \|*  
*evamāvāhayitvā tānsarvānnṛpatisattama \|\| 29 \|\|*

*homaṃ samārabhetsarpiryavavrīhitilādinā \|*  
*arkaḥ palāśakhadirau hyapāmārgo'tha pippalaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*uduṃbara śamīdūrvākuśāśca samidhaḥ kramāt \|*  
*ekaikasya cāṣṭaśatamaṣṭāviṃśati vā punaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*hotavyā madhusarpibhyāṃ dadhnā vā pāyasena vā \|*  
*prādeśamātrā ṛjavo viśākhā viphalāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

28-32. This water could be used for the bathing of the yajamana. О excellent king, then one should pray that – “Let all the oceans, rivers, tanks, reservoirs, springs should arrive here for the removal of the sins of the performer.” All the aforesaid sources of water should be invoked and worshipped. Thereafter, the offerings of barley, wild rice, besides the sesamum seeds should be made. The twigs of swallow wart, catechu, plpala, wild fig tree, Acacia suma, durva and kusa grass, should be used. For the sake of the planets, a hundred or twenty eight offerings should be made with each type of twigs. Thereafter, the offerings of honey, ghi or curd and payasam should also be made. Pradesa, Rja and Visakha are known as auspicious.

## \|\| 3.141.33-36 \|\|

*kalpyaṃte samidhaḥ prājñaiḥ sarvakarmasu sarvadā \|*  
*devānāmapi sarveṣāmupāṃśu paramārthavit \|\| 33 \|\|*

*svena svenaiva maṃtreṇa hotavyāḥ samidhaḥ pṛthak \|*  
*ākṛṣṇena imaṃ devā agnirmūrddhā divaḥ kramāt \|\| 34 \|\|*

*udbudhyasveti bodhyaśca yathāsaṃkhyamudāhṛtāḥ \|*  
*bṛhaspate atiyadastathaivānnātparisutaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*śannodevīti ca kayā ketuṃ kṛṇvannitīti ca \|*  
*hotavyaṃ yadvadājyaṃ caruṃ bhakṣyāṇi vā punaḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

33-36. For the performing of all the religious rites, the use of such twigs have been prescribed by the experts in the field. A learned person who is well-versed in doing good to others, should prescribe different verses for different deities like – “Akrsnena imam deva agnimurddha divah, udrudhyasveti bodhyasca yathasamkhyamudahrta. Brhaspate atiyadaryastithaivannatparisrutah, Sannodevi iti ca kava ketum krnvanniti ca.” Reciting these mantras, the twigs should be poured in the fire as the offerings. Similarly, the offerings of ghi, caru and other eatables should also be poured into the fire flames.

## \|\| 3.141.37-38 \|\|

*maṃtrairdaśāhutīrdattvā homo vyāhṛtibhistataḥ \|*  
*udaṅmukhāḥ prāṅmukhāśca kuryurbrāhmaṇapuṃgavāḥ \|\| 37 \|\|*

*maṃtravaṃtastu kartavyāścaravaḥ pratidaivatam \|*  
*apo rājeti rudrasya balihomaṃ samārabhet \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. Ten offerings of each one of these should be poured into the fire. The homa should then be concluded with the uttering of – “Bhurbhuvah svah” (the vyahrtis). The excellent Brahmanas engaged in this activity should be seated facing the north or the east, while reciting the mantras. Then making the offering of caru or the cooked food in favour of the gods, with the reciting of the mantra- “Ayorajeti’, the offering should be made to Rudra, concluding the homa at the same time.

## \|\| 3.141.39 \|\|

*āpo hiṣṭetyumāyāstu śyeneti svāminastathā \|*  
*viṣṇoridaṃ viṣṇuriti svamiccheti svayaṃbhuvaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

39\. Similarly, uttering the mantra – “Apohisteti”, the offering should be made for Uma. With the mantra – “Syaneti”, the offering should be made to Svami Kartika, and with the mantra – “Visnoridam", the offering should be made to lord Viṣṇu. By uttering – “Svamicheti”, the offering should go to Brahma.

## \|\| 3.141.40-41 \|\|

*indrādidevatānāṃ tu indrāya juhuyātpunaḥ \|*  
*navā yamasyāyaṃ gauścetyevaṃ homaḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*kālasya brahmajajñānamiti maṃtraḥ praśasyate \|*  
*citraguptasya vā jāta paurāṇikā vidurbudhāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

40-41. With the reciting of the mantra – “Indradi”, the offerings should be made to Indra and other gods. Then reciting the mantra – “Gausceti” the offering should be made to Yama and with the mantra – “Brahmajajnamiti”, the offering should be made to Kala. The learned people have ordained that for Citragupta, the offering should be made with the reciting of the Pauranic mantras.

## \|\| 3.141.42-43 \|\|

*agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe iti vahnerudāhṛtaḥ \|*  
*iṃdraṃ yamaṃ varuṇamityayaṃ maṃtraḥ prakīrtitaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*bhūmeḥ pṛthivyaṃtarikṣamiti vedeṣu paṭhyate \|*  
*sahasraśīrṣā puruṣa iti viṣṇorudāhṛtaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

42-43. Then reciting the mantra – “Agnim dutamvrnimahe”, the offering should be made to Agni - the fire god, besides the mantra – “Indram yamam Varunamityayam, Bhumeh prthivyantariksamiti vedesu pathyate”. The “Sahasra-Sirsa Purusa” mantra has to be recited for lord Viṣṇu.

## \|\| 3.141.44-50 \|\|

*varuṇaḥ pavanaścaiva dhanādhyakṣastathā śivaḥ \|*  
*brahmaṇā sahitaḥ śeṣo dikpālāḥ pātu te sadā \|\| 44 \|\|*

*kīrtirlakṣmīrdhṛtirmedhāḥ puṣṭiḥ śraddhā kriyā matiḥ \|*  
*buddhirlajjā śāṃtipuṣṭī kāṃtistuṣṭiśca mātaraḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*etāstvāmabhiṣiṃcaṃtu dharmapatnyaḥ samāgatāḥ \|*  
*ādityaścandramā bhaumo budhajīvasitārkajāḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*grahāstvāmabhiṣiṃcaṃtu rāhuḥ ketuśca tarpitāḥ \|*  
*devadānavagaṃdharvā yakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

*ṛṣayo manavo gāvo devamātara eva ca \|*  
*devapatnyo drumā nāgā daityāścāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ \|\| 48 \|\|*

*astrāṇi sarvaśastrāṇi rājāno vāhanāni ca \|*  
*auṣadhāni ca ratnāni kālasyāvayavāśca ye \|\| 49 \|\|*

*saritaḥ sāgarāḥ śailāstīrthāni jaladā nadāḥ \|*  
*ete tvāmabhiṣiṃcaṃtu sarvakāmārthasiddhaye \|\| 50 \|\|*

44-50. Thereafter, let lord Varuna, the Windgod, Kubera, Siva, Brahma and Dikpalas, protect you. The goddesses like – Kirti, Laksmi, Dhrti, Medha, Pusti, Sraddha, Kriya, Mali, Buddhi, Lajja, Santi, Kanti and Tusti – the mothers and the wives (of gods), should anoint you. Let Surya, Moon, Mangala, Budha, Brhaspati, Sukra, Sani, Rahu and Ketu, and the Gods who are well pleased, Danavas, Yaksas, Gandharvas, Raksasas, Nagas, Ṛṣis, sages, the cows, the divine mothers, the wives of the gods, the moon, serpents, Daityas, Apsaras, all the weapons, the rulers, the vehicles, the heap of herbs, all the gems, the divisions of time (years, months, fortnights, weeks, days), the rivers, the oceans, the mountains, the holy places and the big rivers should come forward and crown you for your achieving success in all the desires.

## \|\| 3.141.51 \|\|

*tataḥ śuklāṃbaradharaḥ śuklagandhānulepanaḥ \|*  
*sarvagandhasamāyuktaḥ snātaḥ śraddhāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

51\. Thereafter, the devotee clad in white garments, plastering the fragrant paste over the body, should then take his bath.

## \|\| 3.141.52 \|\|

*yajamānaḥ sapatnīkānsiddhidāṃstānsamāhitān \|*  
*dakṣiṇābhiḥ prayatnena pūjayedgatavismayaḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

52\. The Yajamana with utmost faith and devotion, accompanied with his wife, should worship all the gods who bestow success.

## \|\| 3.141.53-58 \|\|

*sūryāya kapilāṃ dhenuṃ dadyācchaṃkhaṃ tathendave \|*  
*raktaṃ dhuraṃdharaṃ dadyādbhaumāya kakudādhikam \|\| 53 \|\|*

*budhāya jātarūpaṃ ca gurave pītavāsasī \|*  
*śvetāśvaṃ daityagurave kṛṣṇāṃgāmarkasūnave \|\| 54 \|\|*

*āyasaṃ rāhave dadyātketave cchāgamuttamam \|*  
*suvarṇena samā kāryā yajamānena dakṣiṇā \|\| 55 \|\|*

*sarveṣāmathavā dadyādgururvā yena tuṣyati \|*  
*sumaṃtreṇa pradātavyāḥ sarvāḥ sarvārthadakṣiṇāḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

*kapile sarvadevānāṃ pūjanīyāsi rohiṇī \|*  
*tīrthadevamayī yasmādataḥ śāṃtiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 57 \|\|*

*puṇyastvaṃ śaṃkha puṇyānāṃ maṅgalānāṃ ca maṃgalam \|*  
*viṣṇunā vidhṛto nityamataḥ śāṃtiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 58 \|\|*

53-58. Then becoming alert, a white cow for the Sungod; a conch for the Moon; for Bhima a huge bull with a large hump and of red colour; for Buddha the gold should be given; a pitambara for Brhaspati; a white horse should be given to Sukra; a black cow for the Saturn; For Rahu the iron is to be given; while for Ketu, a female goat should be given with daksina of gold. In case a person is unable to provide charities to all of them, he should give away something which pleases the preceptor the most. After offering the daksina with the reciting of the mantras, one should beg forgiveness – “O Kapila, you are adorable by all the gods, also known as Rohini, you represent all the holy places. You bestow peace on me. О conch, you are the flower of the flowers, besides being welfare of all the welfares, and because of this, you are always carried by lord Viṣṇu. You kindly bestow peace on me.

## \|\| 3.141.59-60 \|\|

*dharma tvaṃ vṛṣarūpeṇa jagadānandakārakaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭamūrteradhiṣṭhānamataḥ śāṃtiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 59 \|\|*

*hiraṇyagarbhagarbhasthaṃ hema bījaṃ vibhāvasoḥ \|*  
*anantapuṇyaphaladamataḥ śāṃtiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 60 \|\|*

59-60. О Dharma, taking to the form of a bull, you bestow delight to the entire universe. Besides you serve as a vehicle to lord Siva having eight forms. Let him bestow peace on me. He is lodged in the golden egg besides being the hemabija of the fire, you bestow the innumerable merits and peace on me.

## \|\| 3.141.61-62 \|\|

*pītavastrayugaṃ dadyādvāsudevasya vallabham \|*  
*pradānāttasya me viṣṇurataḥ śāṃtiṃ prayacchatu \|\| 61 \|\|*

*kapilastvaśvarūpeṇa yasmādamṛtasambhavaḥ \|*  
*candrārkavāhano nityamataḥ śāṃtiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 62 \|\|*

61-62. Lord Vasudeva is offered four yellow garments. Getting pleased with the same, let lord Viṣṇu bestow peace on me. When Kapila took to the form of a horse, the nectar emerged out of him. The same horses became the vehicles of the Sungod as well as the Moon. Let them bestow peace on us.

## \|\| 3.141.63 \|\|

*yasmāttvaṃ pṛthivī sarvā dheno vai kṛṣṇasaṃjñitā \|*  
*sarvapāpaharā nityamataḥ śāṃtiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 63 \|\|*

63\. О cow, you represent the form of the entire earth and are known by the name of Kṛṣṇa and you remove all the sins. Therefore, bestow peace on me always.

## \|\| 3.141.64-65 \|\|

*yasmādāyasa karmāṇi tavādhīnāni sarvadā \|*  
*lāṃgalānyāyudhādīni tasmācchāṃtiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 64 \|\|*

*yasmāttvaṃ chāga yajñānāmaṃgatvena vyavasthitaḥ \|*  
*yonirvibhāvasornityamataḥ śāṃtiṃ prayaccha me \|\| 65 \|\|*

64-65. All the activities related to the iron are all supervised by you. Right from the blade of the plough to the weapons, all are made of iron. Therefore, you bestow peace on me. With the sacrifice of a goat, you are known as Anga and with your combination with the Firegod, you bestow peace on me.

## \|\| 3.141.66 \|\|

*gavāmaṃgeṣu tiṣṭhaṃti bhuvanāni caturdaśa \|*  
*yasmāttasmācchivaṃ me syādiha loke paratra ca \|\| 66 \|\|*

66\. Fourteen lokas are lodged in the parts of the body of the cow. Therefore, bestow peace on me in the present as well as the future lokas.

## \|\| 3.141.67-68 \|\|

*yasmādaśūnyaṃ śayanaṃ keśavasya śivasya ca \|*  
*śayyā mamāpyaśūnyāstu tathā janmani janmani \|\| 67 \|\|*

*yathā ratneṣu sarveṣu sarve devā vyavasthitāḥ \|*  
*tathā śāṃtiṃ prayacchaṃtu ratnadānena me surāḥ \|\| 68 \|\|*

67-68. The one with whom the bed of Kesava as well as Siva is not always vacant (filled) similarly, in each one of my future births, my bed should always have a company. All the gods are always decorated with the gems, because of the giving away of the same gems in charity, let all the gods be pleased with me and bestow peace on me.

## \|\| 3.141.69 \|\|

*yathā bhūmipradānasya kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm \|*  
*dānānyanyāni me śāṃtiṃ bhūmi dānādbhavatyapi \|\| 69 \|\|*

69\. Other charities cannot be compared with a sixteenth part of the donation of land. Therefore, the giving away of the land in charity should bestow peace on me.

## \|\| 3.141.70 \|\|

*evaṃ saṃpūjayedbhaktyā vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*vastrakāñcanaratnaughairmālyagaṃdhānulepanaiḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

70\. Therefore, getting free from the blemish of miserliness, a person should give away the costumes, gold, gems of the ocean, garland, fragrance and the paste for the performing of the worship.

## \|\| 3.141.71-73 \|\|

*grahasvarūpamatulaṃ kathyamānaṃ nibodha me \|*  
*bhaktibhāvaprapannasya kathyamānaṃ virājate \|*  
*padmāsanaḥ padmakaraḥ padmagarbhasamadyutiḥ \|*  
*saptāśvaḥ saptarajjuśca dvibhujaḥ syātsadā raviḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*śvetaḥ śvetāṃbaradharo daśāśvaḥ śvetabhūṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*gadāpāṇirdvibāhuśca kartavyo varadaḥ śaśī \|\| 72 \|\|*

*raktamālyāṃbaradharaḥ karṇikārasamaṃdyutiḥ \|*  
*khaḍgacarmagadāpāṇirvidheyo bhūminaṃdanaḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

71-73. Hereafter, I shall reveal before you the unparallel forms of the planets. You please listen. For the people who take refuge, such words are always graceful. The seven horses should resemble Padmasana, Padmakara and Padmagarbha like lustre. There are seven horses bound with seven ropes which one held in two arms. Their operation has been described. The Moon is supposed to have ten horses of white colour, covered with the white cloth, holding a club in his hand and displaying Varada mudra, Mangala should hold a red rosary and garments, having a glory resembling a pericarp. In his four arms, he should hold a sword, a shield and a club. He is the son of the goddess earth. This is the form of Mangala.

## \|\| 3.141.74 \|\|

*pītamālyāṃbaradharaḥ pītagaṃdhānulepanaḥ \|*  
*kāṃcane ca rathe divye śobhamāno budhaḥ sadā \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. Budha is clad in yellow garments. Yellow paste is applied over his body. He rides a divine chariot of gold.

## \|\| 3.141.75-76 \|\|

*devadaityagurū tadvatpītaśvetau caturbhujau \|*  
*daṃḍinau varadau kāryau sākṣasūtrakamaḍalū \|\| 75 \|\|*

*indranīladyutiḥ śūlī varado gṛdhravāhanaḥ \|*  
*bāṇabāṇāsanadharaḥ kartavyo'rkasutaḥ sadā \|\| 76 \|\|*

75-76. Brhaspati - the preceptor of the gods and fulcra - the preceptor of the demons, are of yellow and white complexion respectively. Both of them hold a danda and are adorned with a yajnopavita each. They also hold in left hands a kamandalu. Sani or the Saturn has the complexion of sapphire gem. He carries a spear and displays Varada mudra. Vultures happen to be his vehicle. He holds a bow and an arrow in his two hands. He is said to be the son of Sun.

## \|\| 3.141.77-78 \|\|

*śārdūlavadanaḥ khaḍgī varmī śūlī varapradaḥ \|*  
*nīlasiṃhāsanasthaśca rāhuratra praśasyate \|\| 77 \|\|*

*dhūmrā dvibāhavaḥ sarve gadino vikṛtānanāḥ \|*  
*gṛdhrāsanaratā nityaṃ ketavaḥ syurvarapradāḥ \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. Rahu has been described having the face of a tiger. He is two armed, having the smoke like complexion. Ketu is two armed and is of smoky complexion. He has a deformed body and is seated over the vulture seat. He displays Varada mudra.

## \|\| 3.141.79-80 \|\|
