15-18. A person who performs this vrata, his seven generations and seven future generations get redeemed of the sins (and reach the heaven). О best of the rulers, I have stated the reward for those who perform this vrata, with a desire. Those who give away the Ghrtadhenu in charity without any desire, they achieve enormous merits, because ghi is the form of fire, Soma, besides representing all the gods. Therefore, a person who donates ghi, the gods get afraid of him.

## \|\| 3.154.19 \|\|

*māyājalaṃ sutakalatramahormimālaṃ lobhogranakraviṣamaṃ bahupuṇyabhājaḥ \|*  
*lagnā nimagnavapuṣo ghṛtadhenupucche saṃsārasāgaramapāramaho taraṃti \|\| 19 \|\|*

19\. A person who gives away the Ghrtadhenu in charity, he crosses the ocean of the universe, which is filled with illusory water, the sons and the wives are the high waves, the hair are like the terrific whirlpools and the crocodiles. Being an auspicious soul, he crosses it with ease, holding the tail of the cow of ghi.

## Chapter 155. Giving away of a cow made of salt

## \|\| 3.155.1-2 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*kṛṣṇakṛṣṇa mahābāho sarvaśāstraviśārada \|*  
*kathayasveha dānānāmuttamaṃ yatprakīrtitam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*yena dattena dānāni sarvāṇyeva bhavaṃtyuta \|*  
*sarvakāmasamṛddhiśca sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Yudhisthira said – О Kṛṣṇa, О Kṛṣṇa, О valorous one, you are well-versed in all the scriptures, you please tell me about such a type of the excellent charity with the performing of which, it should mean that all the charities have been given away. And, the donor gets all his desires fulfilled and all his sins get destroyed. You also speak about the purification after the repentance.

## \|\| 3.155.3-8 \|\|

*prāyaścittaviśuddhiśca tanme kathaya suvrata \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu rājanpravakṣyāmi dānānāmuttamottamam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*khyātaṃ lavaṇadhenvākhyaṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*yāṃ dattvā brahmahā goghnaḥ pitṛhā gurutalpagaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*viśvāsaghātī krūrātmā sarvapāparato'pi vā \|*  
*mucyate nātra saṃdehaḥ śivalokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 5 \|\|*

*subhago dhanasaṃpanno dīrghāyuraparājitaḥ \|*  
*jāyate puruṣo loke sarvakāmasamanvitaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*vidhiṃ vakṣyāmi rājendra lavaṇasyeha kalpanam \|*  
*gomayenopaliptena darbhasaṃstarasaṃsthitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*āvikaṃ carma vinyasya pūrvāśābhimukhaṃ sthitam \|*  
*vastreṇācchāditaṃ kṛtvā dhenuṃ kurvīta buddhimān \|\| 8 \|\|*

3-8. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – I am speaking to you about the Lavana-dana or the giving away of the salt in charity, which fulfills all the desires of a person. With the performing of which, one is relieved of all the grave sins like the killing of the cow, Brāhmaṇa and others, the betrayer of the faith, one who enjoys sex with the wife of the preceptor, who is cruel by nature and the one who is an absolutely sinful person. There is no doubt about it. After his rebirth in this world, such a person becomes quite well off, rich, having long-life, invincible, getting all his desires fulfilled. О king, I am going to speak about the Lavana-dhenu. The kusa grass should be spread over the earth plastered with the cowdung. A skin of sheep should be spread over it, which should be covered with a cloth. Thereafter, a j cow of salt should be made over it.

## \|\| 3.155.9-11 \|\|

*āḍhakenaiva kurvīta vahuvitto'lpavittavān \|*  
*svarṇaśṛṅgīṃ raupyakhurāmikṣupādāṃ phalastanīm \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kāryā śarkarayā jihvā gandhaprāṇavatī tathā \|*  
*samudrodaraje śuktī karṇau tasyāḥ prakalpayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kaṃbalaṃ paṭṭasūtreṇa grīvāyāṃ ghaṇṭikāṃ tathā \|*  
*śṛṃge candanakāṣṭhābhyāṃ mauktike cākṣiṇī ubhe \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. A person with wisdom, irrespective of his being a rich or a poor person, the cow should be made by him in adhaka measure. The horns should be made of gold, while the hoofs should be made of the silver. The udder should be made of the fruits, the tongue should be made of the sugar, besides the nose. The ears should be made of the mother of pearls, the frills of the neck should be made of the cotton cloth. The sandalwood should be used in the making of the horns. The beads should be used in making the eyes.

## \|\| 3.155.12-14 \|\|

*kapolau saktupiṇḍābhyāṃ yavānāsye pradāpayet \|*  
*tilānpārśve prakurvīta godhūmāścaiva bhaktitaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*evaṃ vai saptadhānyāni yathālābhaṃ prakalpayet \|*  
*pṛṣṭhe vai tāmrapātraṃ tu apāne guḍa piṃḍikām \|\| 13 \|\|*

*lāṃgūle kaṃbalaṃ dadyāddrākṣāṃ kṣīrapradeśataḥ \|*  
*yonipradeśe ca madhu sarvavastuphalānvitam \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. The barley powder should be used in the making of the pindas, which should decorate the cheeks of the cow. The mouth should be made of barley. The sesamum seeds and wheat should be used for the making of the back of the cow. Besides the seven grains should be used for the making of the several parts of the cow. The cow should thus be made with devotion. The copper vase should be placed over the back, a sugarcane cake should be placed at anus, blanket over the tail and grapes should be placed near udder. At the place of yoni, fruits and honey should be kept.

## \|\| 3.155.15-16 \|\|

*evaṃ samyakparisthāpya rasarasyamayīṃ ca gām \|*  
*sthāpayedvatsamekaṃ ca caturbhāgena mānavaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*evaṃ dhenuṃ samabhyarcya mālyavastravibhūṣaṇaiḥ \|*  
*snātvā devārcanaṃ kṛtvā brāhmaṇānabhipūjya ca \|*  
*kṛtvā pradakṣiṇāṃ gāṃ tu putrabhāryāsamanvitaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. When the salt cow is thus made, a person should also create a calf with one fourth of the material used for the making of the cow. Thereafter, both the husband and the wife should take their bath and then adore the cow offering the garland, costumes and ornaments. The gods and the Brāhmaṇas should also be worshipped. The donor couple should then go round the cow of salt.

## \|\| 3.155.17-22 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāya suśīlāya vṛttayuktāya vai nṛpa \|*  
*dadyātparvasu sarveṣu mantrapūrvaṃ subhaktitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*lavaṇe vai rasāḥ sarve lavaṇe sarvadevatāḥ \|*  
*sarvadevamaye devi lavaṇākhye namo'stu te \|\| 18 \|\|*

*evamuccārya maṃtrāṃ te viprāya pratipādayet \|*  
*samyakpradakṣiṇāṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇāsahitāṃ nṛpa \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pradakṣiṇā mahī tena kṛtā bhavati bhārata \|*  
*sarvadānāni dattāni sarvakratuphalāni ca \|\| 20 \|\|*

*sarve rasāḥ sarvamannaṃ sarvaṃ ca sacarācaram \|*  
*saubhāgyaṃ paramā buddhirārogyaṃ sarvasaṃpadaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*bhavati dattvā nṛṇāṃ tu rasadhenuṃ na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*svarge ca niyatā vāso yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 22 \|\|*

17-22. О king, the cow should then be given over to a celebrated Brāhmaṇa with the reciting of the mantras, on the festive occasions. While so giving the charity, the donor should say – “All the juices are lodged in the salt, therefore, I offer my salutation to the salt cow, who represents all the gods, again and again.” Thus reciting the mantra, one should go round the cow. Thereafter, the salt-cow should be given over to a Brahmana after going round of the salt cow. Reciting the mantras, the same should be given over to a Brahmana with the daksina. When a person takes a round of the salt-cow, it amounts to the circumambulating the entire earth. The performer, while so doing, earns the merits of all the yajnas, all the rasas, all the food grains, fortunes, excellent wisdom, good health and all the riches are achieved by him. There is no doubt about it. He also dwells in the heaven till the time of great dissolution.

## \|\| 3.155.23 \|\|

*parṇaurṇakaṃbalagalāṃ lavaṇāḍhakena kṛtvā phalastanavatīmapi lāvaṇākhyām \|*  
*dattvā dvijāya vidhivadrasadhenumenāṃ lokaṃ gavāṃ sakalasaukhyayuto viśetsaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

23\. Thus, with the giving away of a salt cow to a Brāhmaṇa in an appropriate manner, whose frills of neck are made of wool, with the salt measuring an adhaka being used in the making of her body and other limbs, besides the udder of fruits, the donor achieves the heaven with all the comforts and the Goloka.

## Chapter 156. Giving away of a golden cow in charity

## \|\| 3.156.1-5 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi rājankāñcanadhenukām \|*  
*yāṃ dattvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

*surāpo brahmahā goghno bhīrurbhagnavrato'pi vā \|*  
*gurughātī svasṛgāmī paradārarataśca yaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*mucyate pātakaiḥ sarvairdattvā kāñcanadhenukām \|*  
*saṃśuddhasya suvarṇasya paṃcāśatpalikāṃ śubhām \|\| 3 \|\|*

*arddhena vā prakurvīta śaktyā vā nṛpasattama \|*  
*ukhāṃ paścimabhāge tu dṛṣṭakukṣipayodharām \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vibhaktāṅgīṃ sujaghanāṃ sumanoharakarṇikām \|*  
*sarvaratnavicitrāṅgīṃ kārayetkapilāṃ śubhām \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О king, I am now speaking about the cow of gold, with the giving away of which in charity, a person is relieved of all the sins. There is no doubt about it. The sins of a drunkard, the killers of a Brahmana and a cow, a coward, at the breaking of the fast, the killer of the preceptor, having illicit relations with sister and one who enjoys other’s wife, get washed out with the giving away of the golden cow in charity. О best of the kings, making use of the pure gold weighing fifty or twenty five palas (a measurement of weight) or as per one’s means, a Kapila cow should be made. The limbs of the rear side like the belly, udder etc. should be well proportioned. The hips should be excellently made and the ears should be charming, decorated with gems.

## \|\| 3.156.6-7 \|\|

*caturthena tu bhāgena vatsaṃ tasyāḥ prakalpayet \|*  
*raupyaghaṭāṃ ca dattvā tu kauśeyaparivāritām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tāmraśṛṃgīṃ tathā kuryādvaiḍūryamayakaṃbalām \|*  
*muktāphalamaye netre vaidrumī rasanā tathā \|\| 7 \|\|*

6-7. The calf should be made of a quarter of the above weight. A bell of silver should be tied in the neck of the cow. A silken cloth should be spread over the body of the cow. The horns should be made of copper. The frills below her neck should be made of sapphire. The eyes should be made of beads, while the tongue should be made of coral tree.

## \|\| 3.156.8-11 \|\|

*kṛṣṇājine guḍaprasthaṃ tatrasthāṃ kārayecchubhām \|*  
*kuṃbhāṣṭakasamopetāṃ nānā phalasamanvitām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tathāṣṭādaśa dhānyātapatropānadyugānvitām \|*  
*bhājanaṃ vasanaṃ caiva tāmradohanakaṃ tathā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dīpakānnādilavaṇaśarkarādhānyakānvitām \|*  
*pradadyādbrāhmaṇaṃ pūjya vastrairābharaṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*snātaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya dhenuṃ sarvāṅgasaṃyutām \|*  
*guḍadhenūktamaṃtraiśca āvāhya pratipūjya ca \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. Placing sugarcane balls over the skin of a black buck, the same should be placed over the cow. It should have eight kalasas, besides various types of fruits, eighteen types of grains, umbrella, a pair of shoes, costumes, milk pot of copper, the lamp, food, salt, sugar and cereals should also be placed there. After worshipping a Brahmana, offering the costumes and ornaments to him, one should go round the cow of gold and with the reciting of the Gudadhenu mantras, should give over the same to the Brahmana.

## \|\| 3.156.12-13 \|\|

*tvaṃ sarvadevagaṇamandirabhūṣaṇāsi viśveśvaratripathagodadhiparvatānām \|*  
*śraddhāmbutīkṣṇaśakalīkṛtapātakaughaḥ prāpnoti nirvṛtimatīva parāṃ namāmi \|\| 12 \|\|*

*loke yathepsitaphalārthavidhāyinī tvāmāsādya ko hi bhayabhāgbhavatīha martyaḥ \|*  
*saṃsāraduḥkhaśamanāya yatastvakāmāstvāṃ kāmadhenumiti vedavido vadaṃti \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. At the time of the giving away of the cow, he should say – “Let you be the ornament for Visvesvara, Viṣṇu, the Ganga, besides the gods in the temples, over the oceans, the mountains.” With the giving away of a golden cow in charity, all the sins get destroyed and a person earns enormous peace. Therefore, I offer my salutation to you. You bestow all the merits in this world, and by getting you, who will be the person who would not be fearless and fortunate? For the subjugation of the miseries, the persons well-versed in the Vedas call you as Kamadhenu and this is quite appropriate.

## \|\| 3.156.14-15 \|\|

*evamāmantrya tāṃ dhenuṃ viprāya pratipādayet \|*  
*sadakṣiṇopaskarāṃ ca praṇipatya kṣamāpayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

*dānakāle tu ye devāstīrthāni manavastathā \|*  
*śarīre nivasaṃtyasyāstāñchṛṇuṣva narādhipa \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Thus involving her, the cow with all the materials, besides the daksina should be given over to a Brahmana. At the time of giving away the cow in charity, whatever is the number of gods, tirtha, Manus and others in the body of the cow, same is being spoken by me. You please listen.

## \|\| 3.156.16-18 \|\|

*netrayoḥ sūryaśaśinau jihvāyāṃ tu sarasvatī \|*  
*daṃteṣu maruto devāḥ karṇayośca tathāśvinau \|\| 16 \|\|*

*śṛṃgāgragau sadā cāsyā devau rudrapitāmahau \|*  
*gaṃdharvāpsarasaścaiva kakuddeśaṃ pratiṣṭhitāḥ \|*  
*kukṣau samudrāśca tvāro yonau tripathagāminī \|\| 17 \|\|*

*ṛṣayo romakūpeṣu apāne vasudhā sthitā \|*  
*antreṣu nāgā vijñeyāḥ parvatāścāsthiṣu sthitāḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

16-18. The sun and the moon reside in her eyes, while Sarasvati dwells over the tongue. The mountain Meru lives in the teeth; Asvini kumaras in the ears; Rudra and Pitamaha (the grandsire) at the tip of the horns; Apsaras and the Gandharvas in the hump; all the four oceans in the belly; the Ganga in the yoni; the Ṛṣis in the hair pits; Vasudha in the anus; the serpents in the veins; the mountains in the bones.

## \|\| 3.156.19-21 \|\|

*dharmakāmārthamokṣāstu pādeṣu parisaṃsthitāḥ \|*  
*huṃkāre ca caturvedāḥ kaṃṭhe rudrāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pṛṣṭhabhāge sthito merurviṣṇuḥ sarvaśarīragaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ sarvamayī devī pāvanī viśvarūpiṇī \|\| 20 \|\|*

*kāñcanena kṛtā dhenuḥ sarvadevamayī smṛtā \|*  
*yo dadyāttādṛśīṃ dhenuṃ sarvadānaprado hi saḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. The artha, kama, moksa and humkara are lodged in the hoofs. The Rudras are lodged in the neck; Meru over the back; Viṣṇu in all the limbs. Thus, an auspicious cow representing the universe and made of gold, when given in charity to a Brahmana, it is believed that he had done everything.

## \|\| 3.156.22-23 \|\|

*karmabhūmau hi martyānāṃ dānametatsudurlabham \|*  
*tasmāddeyamidaṃ śaktyā sarvakalmaṣanāśanam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*pāvanaṃ tāraṇaṃ caiva kīrtidaṃ śāṃtidaṃ tathā \|*  
*varṣakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ svargaloke gato naraḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Though this type of charity is difficult to be performed in this world, still a person should do so as per his means, for the washing out of all the sins. This charity is quite auspicious and bestows glory besides the peace. It also provides an excellent place in the heaven.

## \|\| 3.156.24-26 \|\|

*nārī vā pūjyate devairvimānavaramāsthitā \|*  
*gaṃdharvaigīyamānastu puṣpairmālāvibhūṣitaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

*sarvābharaṇasaṃpannaḥ sarvadvaṃdvavivarjitaḥ \|*  
*svarge sthitvā ciraṃ kālaṃ tato martye'bhijāyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

*ādhi vyādhi vinirmukto rūpavānpriyadarśanaḥ \|*  
*evaṃ naro vā nārī vā dattvā dānamidaṃ bhuvi \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti jāyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. A woman who performs this charity, she getting graceful in the excellent plane, is adorned with the flower garlands and is adored by the gods and the Gandharvas. A person performing this charity is honoured in the heaven for a long time and is reborn on earth without a liability or the ailment, with a beautiful body, besides being quite good looking. With the influence of this vrata, the men and the women both are born on earth again and again and get all their desires fulfilled.

## \|\| 3.156.27 \|\|

*āmantrya sādhukulaśīlaguṇānvitāya viprāya yaḥ kanakadhenumimāṃ pradadyāt \|*  
*prāpnoti siddhamunikinnaradevajuṣṭaṃ kanyāśataiḥ parivṛtaṃ padamindumauleḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

27\. When the golden cow is given over to a noble person of high virtues, the person is served by the Siddhas, Munis, Kinnaras, besides the gods. He is pleased by the hundreds of girls and finally achieves the place of Indra.

## Chapter 157. Giving away of a cow of gems

## \|\| 3.157.1-2 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi dānamanyatsudurllabham \|*  
*ratnadhenviti vikhyātaṃ golokaphaladaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 1 \|\|*

*puṇyaṃ dinamathāsādya gomayenopalepanam \|*  
*kṛtvā bhūmau mahārāja tatra dhenuṃ prakalpayet \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – I am now speaking to you about the giving away of the charity of the cow of gems, which is rarely found on earth. This bestows the people with the merit of achieving the Goloka. On an auspicious day, the earth should be plastered with the cowdung and the cow of gems should be created over the same.

## \|\| 3.157.3-8 \|\|

*dhenuṃ ratnamayīṃ kuryāttattatsaṃkalpapūrvikām \|*  
*sthāpayetpadmarāgāṇāmekāśītiṃ mukhe budhaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*puṣparāgaśataṃ dhenoḥ pādayoḥ parikalpayet \|*  
*lalāṭe hematilakaṃ muktāphalaśataṃ dṛśoḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*bhrūyuge vidrumaśataṃ śuktī karṇadvaye smṛte \|*  
*kāñcanāni ca śṛṅgāṇi śirovajraśatātmakam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*grīvāyāṃ netrapuṭake gomedakaśataṃ tathā \|*  
*indranīlaśataṃ pṛṣṭhe vaidūryaśata pārśvake \|\| 6 \|\|*

*sphāṭikairudaraṃ kāryaṃ saugandhikaśataṃ kaṭau \|*  
*khurā hemamayā kāryāḥ pucchaṃ muktāvalīmayam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*sūryakāntendukāntau ca ghrāṇe karpūracandanaiḥ \|*  
*kuṃkumena ca romāṇi raupyaṃ nābhiṃ ca kārayet \|\| 8 \|\|*

3-8. A learned person should then utter a samkalpa and each one of the limbs of the cow should be created. Making use of the eighty one rubies, the face of the cow should be formed. With a hundred topaz gems, her hoofs should be formed. The forehead should be made of tilakam of gold. The eyes should be made of a hundred beads. The eyebrows should be made with a hundred corals. Making use of the m other of pearls, both the ears should be made, the horns should be made of gold. The head should comprise of diamonds, the neck should be made of a hundred gomedakas. A hundred sapphires should be used for making back of the cow. The back portion should be made of a hundred lapiz lazuli gems. The belly should be made of crystal gems. The waist should be made of a hundred Saugandhika gems, the hoofs should be made of the gold, while the tail should comprise of the gems. The nose should be made of moon stone and camphor should be used for the making of a tail; the nose should be made of sandalwood. The hair on the body should be made of vermilion. The navel should be made of silver.

## \|\| 3.157.9-11 \|\|

*gārutmataśataṃ tadvadapāne parikalpayet \|*  
*tathānyāni ca ratnāni sthāpayetsarvasaṃdhiṣu \|\| 9 \|\|*

*kuryāccharkarayā jihvāṃ gomayaṃ ca guḍātmakam \|*  
*gomūtramājyena tathā dadhidugdhasvarūpataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*pucchāgre cāmaraṃ dadyātstanayostāmradohanam \|*  
*kārayedevamevaṃ tu caturthāṃśena vatsakam \|\| 11 \|\|*

9-11. The anus should be made of garutmat. All the joints should be made of the gems. The tongue should be made of sugar, the sugarcane cakes should be used as the cowdung. The ghi, curd, milk can be conceived to be the cow’s urine. The flywhisk should be used as a tail. The udder should be made of the copper. After making the cow in this fashion, a quarter of the aforesaid material should be used for the making of a calf of the cow.

## \|\| 3.157.12-13 \|\|

*nānāphalāni pārśveṣu kṛtvā pūjāṃ prayatnataḥ \|*  
*guḍadhenuvadāvāhya idaṃ codāharettataḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*tvāṃ sarvadevagaṇavāsamiti stuvaṃti rudrendracandrakamalāsanavāsudevāḥ \|*  
*tasmātsamastabhuvanatrayadehayuktā māṃ pāhi devi bhavasāgara magnamāsu \|\| 13 \|\|*

12-13. After preparing thus, the cow should be invoked reciting several mantras and then worshipped. She should be conceived to be the abode of all the gods, including Indra, Rudra, Moon, Brahmā and lord Vāsudeva. Thereafter, she should be praised, saying – “Your body is the abode of all the bhuvanas. Therefore, you protect me, because I am drowning in the ocean of the universe.”

## \|\| 3.157.14-15 \|\|

*evamāmantrya tāṃ dhenuṃ viprāya pratipādayet \|*  
*saṃpūjya vastrābharaṇairvidhijñaṃ vedapāragam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tataśca dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā praṇipatya kṣamāpayet \|*  
*evaṃ yaḥ kurute pārtha tasya puṇyaphalaṃ śṛṇu \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. Thus speaking, the cow should then be given over to a Brahmana. Thereafter, a Brahmana who is well-versed in the Vedas should be given over the cow with daksipa. Then offering his salutation to him, he should beg forgiveness from the Brahmana. О Partha, a person who gives away the cow in charity in this way, the details of the merits earned by him are being spoken by me. You please listen.

## \|\| 3.157.16-17 \|\|

*kalpakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ śivaloke sukhaṃ vaset \|*  
*tataḥ kāle bahutithe rājarājo bhavediha \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sarvakāmasamṛddhaśca śatrupakṣakṣayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. After dwelling in the Sivaloka for a long period, the donor enjoying all the pleasures, is reborn on earth as an emperor whose all the desires are fulfilled, besides being the destroyer of the enemies.

## \|\| 3.157.18 \|\|

*iti sakalavidhijño ratnadhenupradānaṃ vitarati sa vimānaṃ prāpya dedīpyamānam \|*  
*sakala kaluṣamukto baṃdhubhiḥ putrapautraiḥ sa hi madanasarūpaḥ sthānamabhyeti śaṃbhoḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Thus with the giving away of the cow of gems, the fortunate person possesses an illustrious plane. He is relieved of all the sins. He then achieving the sons and grandsons, becomes a courtier of lord Siva.

## Chapter 158. Giving away of a pregnant cow in charity

## \|\| 3.158.1 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*prasūyamānā dātavyā dhenurbrāhmaṇapuṅgave \|*  
*vidhinā kena dharmajñaṃ dāne tasyāśca kiṃ phalam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Yudhisthira said – О lord well-versed in dharma, you had told earlier that only a pregnant cow should be given to a Brahmana. You kindly tell the method of doing so and the related reward.

## \|\| 3.158.2-5 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*prasūyamānātipuṇyaiḥ prāpyate gaurnṛpottama \|*  
*prāpnuvaṃti narāḥ kecitpuṇyasaṃbhāravistarāḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yāvatpādau yonigatau śiraścaiva pradṛśyate \|*  
*tāvadgauḥ pṛthivī jñeyā yāvadgarbhaṃ na muṃcati \|\| 3 \|\|*

*gauryāvaddvimukhī caiva yadā bhavati bhārata \|*  
*tadāsau pṛthivī jñeyā saśailavanakānanā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*dattvobhayamukhīṃ rājanyatpuṇyaṃ prāpyate nṛbhiḥ \|*  
*na tadvarṇayituṃ yāti mukhenaikena kenacit \|\| 5 \|\|*

2-5. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О best of the humans, one gets a pregnant cow as a result of some auspicious deeds. Therefore, a person having enormous merits to his credit, can have such a cow and none else. During the pregnancy, when the calf comes out of the womb of the cow, she is called the earth. When the cow is pregnant, she should be taken to the earth. Therefore, by giving away a cow in charity, the height of merit so earned by a donor is difficult to be brought out or rather it is impossible.

## \|\| 3.158.6-9 \|\|

*kimiṣṭairbahubhiryajñairdānairdattaiśca sattama \|*  
*prasūyamānāṃ gāmekāṃ dehi kiṃ bahunā tava \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ekaiva pāti narakātsukhamekaiva kārayet \|*  
*ekāpi dvimukhī dattā gaurgaurbhavati bhārata \|\| 7 \|\|*

*svarṇaśṛṃgīṃ raupyakhurāṃ muktālāṅgūlabhūṣitām \|*  
*kāṃsyopadohanāṃ rājannalaṃkṛtya dvijottame \|*  
*prasūyamānāṃ gāṃ dattvā mahatpuṇyaphalaṃ labhet \|\| 8 \|\|*

*yāvaṃti dhenuromāṇi vatsasyāpi narādhipa \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. Leaving aside the performing of the several yajnas, you give away a pregnant cow in charity, because a single cow could save a person from falling in the hell and bestows comforts. So much so, that with the giving away in charity of a single pregnant cow, it is considered to be the real charity. The horns should be covered with gold, the hoofs should be covered with silver and the tail should be decorated with beads. She should then be given to a Brahmana with a milk vase of bell-metal (bronze). With the giving away of a pregnant cow in charity, one earns enormous merit. О king, whatever be the number of the hair on the body of the cow and the calf, the donor enjoys all the pleasures in the heaven for thousands of years.

## \|\| 3.158.10-12 \|\|

*pitṝnpitāmahāṃścaiva tathaiva prapitāmahān \|*  
*samuddharatyasaṃdigdhaṃ narakādbhūridakṣiṇaḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ghṛtakṣīravahā nadyo dadhipāyasakardamāḥ \|*  
*tatra te yāṃti yatrāsti drumaścepsitakāmadaḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yo dadāti suvarṇena bahunā saha bhāvinīm \|*  
*golokaḥ sulabhastasya brahmalokaśca pārthiva \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. The person who donates a cow with enough of dakfiijd redeems his father, the grandfather and the great grandfather with many generations, from the hell. There is no doubt about it. The country in which the milk and ghi flow in the rivers instead of water and instead of mud, one finds the curd and payasam (in tanks), the donor of the pregnant cow achieves the same place. While giving away the pregnant cow as charity, the donor achieves Goloka and Brahmaloka quite easily.

## \|\| 3.158.13 \|\|

*na deyā durbalā rājandhenurnaivālpadakṣiṇā \|*  
*kāmyo'yaṃ vidhiruddiṣṭaḥ phalado vidhinā kṛtaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. A weak cow and a meagre daksina should never be given, because this process has been prescribed by Brahma himself.

## \|\| 3.158.14 \|\|

*striyaśca ta caṃdrasamānavaktrāḥ prataptajāṃbūnadatulyavarṇāḥ \|*  
*mahānitaṃbāstanuvṛttamadhyāḥ sevaṃtyajasraṃ nalinābhanetrāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Such a donor is served by the ladies with moon like faces, having the bodies with golden complexion, developed buttocks, slender waist and the lotus like eyes.

## Chapter 159. Giving of a thousand cows of ghi in charity

## \|\| 3.159.1 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*gosahasravidhānaṃ ca kathayasva janārdana \|*  
*kasminkāle pradātavyaṃ kathaṃ deyaṃ ca tadbhavet \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Yudhisthira said – What is the process of giving away of a thousand cows? When should it be given and to whom should it be given? You kindly tell me.

## \|\| 3.159.2-4 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*gāvaḥ pavitrā lokānāṃ gāva eva parāyaṇam \|*  
*brahmaṇā sṛjatā lokānvṛttihetoḥ prajeśvara \|*  
*gāvaḥ prathamataḥ sṛṣṭāstrailokya hitakāmyayā \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yāsāṃ mūtrapurīṣeṇa devatāyatanānyapi \|*  
*śucīni samajāyaṃta kiṃbhūtamadhikaṃ tataḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*mūlaṃ yajñasya kāmyasya sarvadevamayāḥ śubhāḥ \|*  
*gomaye vasate lakṣmīḥ paryāptaṃ tannidarśanam \|\| 4 \|\|*

2-4. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О Prajesvara, the cow is always auspicious and parayana should be performed for the same. Therefore, while creating the universe for the welfare of all the three lokas, the cow was created first of all by Brahma. With the urine and dung of the cow, even the temples are purified. What more could be said about it? The cows are the basic cause of the yajnas performed with a definite purpose, because of being divine and sacred. Laksmi resides in her dung and this is enough of direction for her.

## \|\| 3.159.5 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāścaiva gāvaśca kulamekaṃ dvidhā kṛtam \|*  
*ekatra maṃtrāstiṣṭhanti haviranyatra tiṣṭhati \|\| 5 \|\|*

5\. Brahmana and the cow are of the same race, but have been separated into two parts, in which Brahmanas received the Vedic hymns, while the havi went to the share of the cows.

## \|\| 3.159.6-9 \|\|

*yāsāṃ putrairdhṛtā lokā dhāritāḥ sarvadevatāḥ \|*  
*tāsāṃ dānavidhānaṃ ca śṛṇu tatpṛthivīpate \|\| 6 \|\|*

*ekā'pi gaurguṇopetā kṛtsnaṃ tārayate kulam \|*  
*surūpā śīlasaṃpannā yuvatiḥ supayasvinī \|\| 7 \|\|*

*suvatsā suduhā caiva pāparogavivarjitā \|*  
*vidhivattādṛśā dattā kṛtsnaṃ tārayate kulam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kiṃ punardaśa yo dadyācchataṃ vā vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*sahasraṃ tu punardadyāttasya vai kimihocyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. О lord of the earth, the one whose sons have held the gods and all the lokas, I am going to speak to you the process of giving them in charity. You please listen. Even a single virtuous, docile and milk giving cow, when given in charity, becomes competent enough to redeem the entire family. When a cow with a beautiful calf, yielding milk, devoid of all the ailments, is given away in charity, she redeems the entire family, but a person, who gives away ten, a hundred or a thousand cows in charity, what could be spoken about him?

## \|\| 3.159.10-12 \|\|

*gosahasraṃ purā dattaṃ nahuṣeṇa mahībhṛtā \|*  
*sa gato brahmaṇaḥ sthānaṃ yayātiśca mahāmatiḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*gaṃgātīre mahaddattamadityā putrakāmyayā \|*  
*lebhe putraṃ trilokeśaṃ nārāyaṇamakalmaṣam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*śrūyate pitṛbhirgītā gāthāstāḥ śṛṇu bhūpate \|\| 12 \|\|*

10-12. In earlier times, the king Nahusa and the immensely intelligent Yayati had given a thousand cows in charity, as a result of which they achieved the Brahmaloka. Similarly, with the desire of having a son, Aditi had performed the charity of a cow over the bank of the river Ganga, who got spotless Narayana as her son. О king, there is a song of the pitrs (manes), the story of which is being narrated by me. You please listen.

## \|\| 3.159.13-18 \|\|

*yadi kaścitkule'smākaṃ gosahasraṃ pradāpayet \|*  
*yāsyāmaḥ paramāṃ siddhiṃ kāritāṃ puṇyakarmaṇā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*duhitā vā kule kācidgosahasrapradāyinī \|*  
*sopānaḥ sugatirdatto bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi yajñaṃ vai sarvakāmikam \|*  
*gosahasraṃ tadā dadyācchāstroktavidhivannaraḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tīrthe goṣṭhe gṛhe vāpi maṃḍapaṃ kārayecchubham \|*  
*daśadvādaśahastaṃ vā caturvaktraṃ satoraṇam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tanmadhye kārayedvediṃ caturhastāmanūpamām \|*  
*hastamātrapramāṇena hastena samalaṃkṛtām \|\| 17 \|\|*

*pūrvottare'thadigbhāge grahavediṃ prakalpayet \|*  
*grahayajñavidhānena grahāṃstatra kramādyajet \|\| 18 \|\|*

13-18. In case a person, in our race, gives away a thousand cows in charity, then by so doing, he certainly achieves the supreme success. In case, a girl (in her parent’s home) gives away a thousand cows in charity, then she provides not only the salvation or beautitude, but also the stairs to the heaven. There is no doubt about it. Thereafter, I am going to speak about a Go-yajna as prescribed in the scriptures and keeping it in view, a person should perform this yajna and charity. One should make a square pedestal of twelve cubits, creating a pavilion at the same time in a house or a cow- pen. In the centre of the same, a vedi of four cubits should be built which should be fully decorated. In its north-east, Grahavedi should be built and the planets should be consecrated there, according to the provision of the Graha-yajna. The worship should then start.

## \|\| 3.159.19-21 \|\|

*brahmā viṣṇuśca rudraśca pūjyāḥ prathamameva hi \|*  
*ṛtvijaḥ parikartavyā ṣoḍaśāṣṭau ca śobhanāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*catvāro vā mahārāja upādhyāyaśca paṃcamaḥ \|*  
*sarvābharaṇasaṃpannāḥ karṇaveṣṭāṃgulīyakaiḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*śobhitāśchatrasaṃpannāstāmrapātradvayānvitāḥ \|*  
*grahayajñoktavidhinā homaṃ havyaṃ samācaret \|\| 21 \|\|*

19-21. Initially, Brahma, Rudra and Viṣṇu should be worshipped. Thereafter, four, eight or sixteen yajna priests should be established. Then, one should touch the feet of Upadhyaya, who should be adorned with all the ornaments including the finger ring. He should also be given an umbrella and two vases of copper. He should then perform the homa of havya according to the sacrificial practices.

## \|\| 3.159.22-23 \|\|

*vedyāḥ pūrvottare bhāge śivakuṃḍaṃ niyojayet \|*  
*kuṃbhadvayaṃ ca dvāreṣu paṃcaratnaṃ sapallavam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kāryaṃ kurukulaśreṣṭha tato homaṃ samārabhet \|*  
*lokapālabaliṃ dadyāttulāpuruṣadānavat \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. О best of the Kuru race, to the north-east of the pedestal, altar of Siva should be made. At each one of the gates, two pitchers filled with water and tender tree leaves, besides the pancaratna should be established. The homa, the giving away in charity and the tula-purusa (or weighing one’s body against corn, gold, silver etc.) should be performed. The offerings to the Lokapalas should be made thereafter.

## \|\| 3.159.24-26 \|\|

*gosahasrādviniṣkṛṣya savatsaṃ daśakaṃ gavām \|*  
*gosahasrādbahiṣkuryādvastramālyavibhūṣaṇam \|*  
*ataḥ praveśya daśakaṃ vastrairmālyaiśca pūjayet \|\| 24 \|\|*

*suvarṇaghaṃṭikāyuktaṃ tāmradohanakānvitam \|*  
*suvarṇatilakopetaṃ khurai raupyairalaṃkṛtaiḥ \|*  
*hemaratnamayaiḥ śṛṃgaiścāmaraiścopaśobhitam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*munayaḥ kecidicchanti kāṃcanaṃ naṃdikeśvaram \|*  
*lavaṇadroṇaśikhare bhaktyā tamapi kārayet \|\| 26 \|\|*

24-26. It should include a hundred calves of buffalos and ten cows, which should be separated and decorated with costumes and garlands. Besides the bells of gold should be hung around their necks. The milk-pots should be of copper. The heads should be decorated with tilakam of gold. The hoofs should be decorated with silver, the horns should be of gold with tips of gems. The flywhisks should also be used for decoration. Some of the ascetics are of the opinions that an image of Nandikesava should also be made in gold and it should be lodged over the heap of salt.

## \|\| 3.159.27-28 \|\|

*ekā pratyakṣaṛṣabhe keṣāṃciddānamiṣyate \|*  
*grahānsurāṃśca saṃpūjya mālyavastraphalākṣataiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*patākābhiralaṃkṛtya devatāyatanāni ca \|*  
*gośate'pi daśāṃśena sarvametatprakalpayet \|\| 28 \|\|*

27-28. When there is only one bull, a single cow should be given in charity, this is also the opinion of some people. While worshipping the other gods, the garlands, costumes, fruits, cereals etc. should be offered to them as well as the planets and while so doing, the temples should also be decorated with flags. Similar process is to be followed for giving away o f a hundred or ten cows.

## \|\| 3.159.29 \|\|

*yadi sarvā na vidyante gāvaḥ sarvaguṇottamāḥ \|*  
*daśakaṃ pūjya yatnena itaraḥ parikalpayet \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In case all the cows do not possess all the virtues, then in that case, only ten cows should be worshipped initially and the rest should only be imagined.

## \|\| 3.159.30 \|\|

*puṣpakālamatho vādyagītamaṃgalanisvanaiḥ \|*  
*sarvauṣadhyudakasnātaḥ snapito dvijapuṃga vaiḥ \|*  
*imamuccārayenmaṃtraṃ gṛhītakusumāṃjaliḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. At an auspicious time, the performance of singing with music should be carried out and the donor should have a welfare bath with the water mixed with herbs and with the chanting of the mantras by the Brahmanas. Thereafter, holding the flowers in the hand-cups, the mantras should be chanted.

## \|\| 3.159.31-34 \|\|

*namo vo viśvamūrtibhyo viśvamātṛbhya eva ca \|*  
*lokādhivāsinībhyastu rohiṇībhyo namo namaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*gavāmaṃgeṣu tiṣṭhanti bhuvanānyekaviṃśatiḥ \|*  
*brahmādayastathā devā rohiṇyaḥ pāṃtu mātaraḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*gāvo mamāgrataḥ saṃtu gāvo me saṃtu pṛṣṭhataḥ \|*  
*gāvo me sarvataḥ saṃtu gavāṃ madhye vasāmyaham \|\| 33 \|\|*

*yasmāttvaṃ vṛṣarūpeṇa dharmaścaiva sanātanaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭamūrtteradhiṣṭhānamataḥ pāhi sanātanaḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

31-34. Salutation to Visvamurti (universal form) and the mother of the universe. Salutation to the controller of the universe and Rohini. Twenty one bhuvanas are lodged in the limbs of the cow, besides Brahma and other gods. Therefore, let all the Rohini mothers protect me. Since the cows are present around me as also at my back, therefore, I actually live among the cows. Taking to the form of a bull, you represent Dharma as well as the Astamurti Siva. Being the eternal form, you please protect me.

## \|\| 3.159.35-38 \|\|

*ityāmantrya tato dayādgurave naṃdikeśvaram \|*  
*sarvopaskaraṇopetaṃ goyutaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*gavāṃ śatamathaikaikaṃ tadardhaṃ cāpi viṃśatiḥ \|*  
*daśa pañcaśataṃ dadyādbahubhyastadanujñayā \|\| 36 \|\|*

*naikā bahubhyo dātavyā dātā doṣakaro bhavet \|*  
*bahvyastvekasya dātavyāḥ śrīmadārogyavṛddhaye \|\| 37 \|\|*

*payovratastatastiṣṭhedekāhaṃ gosahasradaḥ \|*  
*tathaiva brahmacārī syādya icchedvipulāṃ śriyam \|\| 38 \|\|*

35-38. Reciting in this way, the donor should give away a bull also with the cows, at the feet of the preceptor. Thereafter, the cow should be distributed to each one of the Brahmanas, giving them a hundred, fifty, ten or five each, as per the command of the preceptor. In case a hundred cows each are given to several Brahmanas, the donor earns benefits. But for the achieving of the fortunes and good health, one person should be given many cows. Thereafter, the donor of a thousand cows, being desirous of getting enormous wealth, should spend that particular day observing Brahmacarya and consuming milk alone.

## \|\| 3.159.39-43 \|\|

*na deyā durbalā dhenurnālpakṣīrā na rogiṇī \|*  
*na jīrṇā jīrṇavastrā vā nāpatyagatacetanā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*anena vidhinā yastu gosahasraprado bhavet \|*  
*sarvapāpavinirmuktaḥ siddhacāraṇasevitaḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

*vimānenārkavarṇena kiṃkiṇījālamālinā \|*  
*sarveṣāṃ lokapālānāṃ loke saṃpūjyate suraiḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*saptāvarānsapta parānsapta caiva parāvarān \|*  
*puruṣānuddhareddattvā gosahasraṃ vidhānataḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*svargalokāccyuto vātha nārī vā satparāyaṇā \|*  
*sapta janmāni rājñī syātstūyamānā punaḥpunaḥ \|\| 43 \|\|*

39-43. A cow which is quite lean and thin, yielding little of milk, an old one or whose calves die, should not be given in charity. With the following of this process, the donor of a thousand cows, getting relieved of all the sins, is served by the Caranas as well as the Siddhas and is made to board a plane decorated with the small bells, having a lustre of the Sun, and is adored in the place of the Lokapalas and tire gods. One who gives the cows in charity, redeems the seven earlier and the seven future generations. After falling from the heaven, in due course of time, he again becomes a king. In case, he is born as a woman, she leads the life of chastity for seven births, who is praised by the people daily.

## \|\| 3.159.44-45 \|\|

*na tvevedaṃ dānamātraṃ praśastaṃ pātraṃ kālo goviśeṣo vighiśca \|*  
*tasmādetāḥ sarvabhūṣāsametāḥ pātre kāle kṣīravatyo vidhānāt \|\| 44 \|\|*

*ekāpi gaurbahuguṇā guṇine pradattā dātuḥ kulaṃ tripuruṣaṃ vidhivatpunāti \|*  
*yaḥ śraddhayā vitaratīha gavāṃ sahasraṃ śakyaṃ phalaṃ na nṛpate'sya mayābhidhātum \|\| 45 \|\|*

44-45. Thus not only the charity is praised, but the performer, the time, the excellent cow, besides the process is also equally praised. Therefore, at an opportune time, a virtuous cow alone should be given away in charity to a virtuous Brāhmaṇa. One who does so, he purifies his three generations. However, if a person gives away a thousand cows in charity, I am unable to speak out the merits so earned by him.

## Chapter 160. Giving away of a bull in charity

## \|\| 3.160.1-2 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*yuṣmadvākyāmṛtamidaṃ śṛṇvānāha janārdana \|*  
*na tṛptimadhigacchāmi jātaṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me \|\| 1 \|\|*

*gopatiḥ kila govindastriṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ \|*  
*govṛṣasya pradānena trailokyamabhinaṃdati \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Yudhisthira said – О Janardana, I do not feet contented with the listening of your nectar like words and rather becoming more and more anxious to hear further. О Acyuta, it is well known that Gopati is Govinda. This is well known in the three worlds. With the donating of a bull, the three worlds get delighted. Therefore, you speak to me about the merit of donating a bull.

## \|\| 3.160.3-9 \|\|

*tadgovṛṣabhadānasya phalaṃ me kathāyācyuta \|*  
*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*vṛṣadānaphalaṃ puṇyaṃ śṛṇuṣva kathayāmi te \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pavitraṃ pāvanaṃ caiva sarvadānottamottamam \|*  
*daśadhenusamo'naḍvānekaścaikadhuraṃdharaḥ \|*  
*daśadhenupradānāddhi sa evaiko viśiṣyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yo hṛṣṭaścātipuṣṭāṃgo hyarogaḥ pāṃḍunandana \|*  
*yuvā bhadraḥ suśīlaśca sarvadoṣavivarjitaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*dhuraṃdharaḥ sthāpayate eka eva kulaṃ mahat \|*  
*trātā bhavati saṃsāre nātra kāryā vicāraṇā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*alaṃkṛtya vṛṣaṃ śāṃtaṃ puṇyakāla upasthite \|*  
*raupyalāṃgūlasaṃyuktaṃ brāhmaṇāya nivedayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

*maṃtreṇānena rājendra taṃ śṛṇuṣva vadāmi te \|\| 8 \|\|*

*dharmastvaṃ vṛṣarūpeṇa jagadānandakārakaḥ \|*  
*aṣṭamūrteradhiṣṭhānamataḥ pāhi sanātana \|\| 9 \|\|*

3-9. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – I am going to speak about the merit of donating a bull, which is quite auspicious and excellent. You please listen. A powerful bull is considered to be equivalent to the ten cows, which is enough. О son of Pandu, a young well built, healthy, docile and unblemished bull establishes a powerful race in the world. He is the protector as well. There is no controversy about the same. A t some auspicious time, a peaceful bull should be well decorated, having the tail decorated with silver. I am going to tell you the mantra reciting which the bull should be given away in charity. You please listen. О Rajendra, the donor at that time should say - “As a bull, you are the form of Dharma. You also serve lord Siva as his vehicle. You also delight the world. Therefore, you protect me.”

## \|\| 3.160.10-14 \|\|

*dattvaivaṃ dakṣiṇāyuktaṃ praṇipatya visarjayet \|*  
*saptajanmakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ vāṅmanaḥ kāyakarmaṇām \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ vilayaṃ yāti godānasukṛtena ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

*yānaṃ vṛṣabhasaṃyuktaṃ dīpyamānaṃ suśobhanam \|*  
*āruhya kāmagaṃ divyaṃ svalokamadhirohati \|\| 11 \|\|*

*yāvaṃti tasya romāṇi govṛṣasya mahīpate \|*  
*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi gavāṃ loke mahīyate \|\| 12 \|\|*

*golokādavatīrṇastu iha loke dvijo bhavet \|*  
*yajñayājī mahātejāḥ sarvabrāhmaṇapūjitaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yathoktaṃ te mahārāja kasya deyo vṛṣottamaḥ \|*  
*tadahaṃ te pravakṣyāmi pātraṃ trāṇapadaṃ nṛṇām \|\| 14 \|\|*

10-14. Thus giving the bull in charity and offering salutation, the same should be sent off. With the giving away o f a cow in charity, the sins committed in the past seven births get washed out. The donor along with the bull achieves the heaven, mounting over a plane, having enormous lustre. The number of hairs that are there on the body of the bull, the donor enjoys the pleasures of the heaven for the period of thousands of years for each hair. After having been worshipped in Goloka for a long time, he is reborn in a Brāhmaṇa family in which the yajnas are performed. He becomes illustrious and adored by all the Brahmanas. О king, whatever has been spoken by you, as to whom the bull should be given over, therefore, I am giving the answer.

## \|\| 3.160.15-16 \|\|

*ye kṣāṃtadāṃtāḥ śrutipūrṇakarṇā jiteṃdriyāḥ prāṇivadhānnivṛttāḥ \|*  
*pratigrahe saṃkucitā gṛhasthāste brāhmaṇāstārayituṃ samarthāḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*ūrjasvinaṃ bharasahaṃ dṛḍhakaṃdharaṃ ca yacchaṃti ye vṛṣamaśeṣaguṇopapannam \|*  
*dattena yadbhavati godaśakena puṇyaṃ satyaṃ bhavaṃti bhuvi tatphalabhāginaste \|\| 16 \|\|*

15-16. It should be given to a Brahmana, who is the performer of the yajna, who is quite illustrious and is adored by all the Brāhmaṇas, who is devoid of terror, peaceful, well-versed in the Vedas, is hesitant to accept donations and is competent to redeem others. Such a Brāhmaṇa earns the merit of donating ten cows.

## Chapter 161. Glory of giving away the Kapila cow

## \|\| 3.161.1 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*kapilādānamāhātmyaṃ kathayasva jagatpate \|*  
*puṇyaṃ yatsarvadānānāṃ sarvapātakanāśanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Yudhisthira said- О lord of the universe, you kindly tell me the glory of giving away of a Kapila cow in chanty, which yields enormous merit and destroys all the sins,

## \|\| 3.161.2 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*tatte'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi vinatāśvena yatpurā \|*  
*kathitaṃ kapilādānaṃ tacchṛṇuṣva mahāmate \|\| 2 \|\|*

2\. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О learned one, in earlier times, whatever Vinatasva had spoken in this connection, is being repeated by me. I am speaking about the importance of the giving away a Kapila cow in charity. You please listen.

## \|\| 3.161.3 \|\|

*vinatāśva uvāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ mahārājobhayamukhyāḥ samāsataḥ \|*  
*vidhānaṃ yadvarāheṇa dharaṇyai kathitaṃ purā \|\| 3 \|\|*

3\. The Earth goddess said – О lord, you have initially sanctified the name of Kapila. It is the source of Homa-dhenu, besides being the place of incarnation for the merit and sacrifice. You kindly tell me about the day on which it should be given over to a Brāhmaṇa and the procedure of doing so, since it has been praised by Brahma himself. Several types of Kapila cows have been defined with different symptoms. О Madhava, О Madhusudana, by giving away the Kapila cow in charity making all the efforts and the related merits earned by a person, I would like to know about the same. Therefore, you kindly describe the same exhaustively.

## \|\| 3.161.4-7 \|\|

*tadahaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi navapuṇyaphalaṃ ca yat \|*  
*dharaṇyuvāca \|*  
*yattvayā kapilā nāma pūrvamutpāvitā prabho \|\| 4 \|\|*

*homadhenuḥ sadā puṇyā dhenuryajñāvatārabhūḥ \|*  
*sā kathaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo hi deyā kasmindine'pi ca \|\| 5 \|\|*

*kīdṛśāya ca viprāya dātavyā puṇyalakṣaṇā \|*  
*kati vā kapilāḥ proktāḥ svayameva svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 6 \|\|*

*tāsāṃ prayatnāddānena kiṃ puṇyaṃ syācca mādhava \|*  
*etadicchāmyahaṃ śrotuṃ vistarānmadhusūdana \|\| 7 \|\|*

4-7. Varaha said – О noble one, I am going to reveal before you the excellent glory of the same which destroys the sins together with its essence and with the performing of which, a person is relieved of all the sins. There is no doubt about it, you please listen. О excellent lady, in earlier times, Brahma collected all the lustres and created fire, homa as well as the cow named Kapila, for the purpose of yajna. Because of this reason, the cow Kapila is considered to be the most auspicious one, the highest welfare of all the welfares, besides being the most sacred one of all the highly sacred elements. In case the same cow Kapila is given away in charity, she represents the best of the dhyana of all the meditations, the best vrata of all the vratas, the best of tapas of all the tapas, the best of charity of all the charities, which remains everlasting.

## \|\| 3.161.8-11 \|\|

*varāha uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇuṣva bhadre tattvena pavitraṃ pāpanāśanam \|*  
*kṛtvā yatsarvapāpebhyo mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*kapilā agnihotrārthaṃ yajñārthe ca varānane \|*  
*uddhṛtya sarvatejāṃsi brahmaṇā nirmitā purā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*pavitrāṇāṃ pavitraṃ ca maṅgalānāṃ ca maṃgalam \|*  
*puṇyānāṃ paramaṃ puṇyaṃ kapilā ca varānane \|\| 10 \|\|*

*tapasastapa evāgryaṃ vratānāmuttamaṃ vrataṃ \|*  
*dānānāmuttamaṃ dānaṃ vidhinā hyetadakṣayam \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. She happens to be best of all the holy places, besides being a temple. Because of all these facts and qualities, she is considered to be of excellent holy form, besides being auspicious. Making use of the ghi, milk etc. of the cow, the Brahmana perform the homas in the morning as well as in the evening. A person who performs the homa making use of different types of cereals and adores all the guests with devotion, he achieves the highest position, boarding the planes issuing enormous lustre. Accordingly, in earlier times, the cow known as Kapila was created by Brahma. О excellent lady (the earth goddess), at the command of Brahma — the Grandsire, all the holy places reside in the head and neck of the Kapila cow. The water which falls from the head and the neck of the cow Kapila, those people who pour it over their heads, they earn great merits and with the influence of which they also get relieved of all their sins. Their sine earned for the past thirty years are burnt out instantaneously like the burning wood.

## \|\| 3.161.12-18 \|\|

*pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni guhyānyāyatanāni ca \|*  
*pavitrāṇi ca puṇyāni sarvaloke vasundhare \|\| 12 \|\|*

*hotavyānyagnihotrāṇi sāyaṃ prātardvijātibhiḥ \|*  
*kapilāyā ghṛteneha daśa kṣīreṇa vā punaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

*yajaṃte ye'gnihotrāṇi annaiśca vividhaiḥ sadā \|*  
*pūjayantyatithīṃścaiva parāṃ bhaktimupāgatāḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*teṣāṃ tvādityavarṇaiśca vimānairjāyate gatiḥ \|*  
*sūryamaṇḍalamadhye ca brahmaṇā nirmitā purā \|\| 15 \|\|*

*kapilāyāḥ śiro grīvāṃ sarva tīrthāni bhāmini \|*  
*pitāmahaniyogācca nivasaṃti hi nityaśaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*prātarutthāya yo martyaḥ kapilā galamastakāt \|*  
*cyutaṃ tu bhaktyā pānīyaṃ śirasā dhārayennaraḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sa tena puṇyenopetastatkṣaṇādgatakilviṣaḥ \|*  
*viṃśadvarṣakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ dahatyagnirivendhanam \|\| 18 \|\|*

12-18. О earth goddess, getting up early in the morning, a person who goes round the Kapila cow, he earns the merit of circumambulating the entire world. О Vasundhara, by going round the cow Kapila once only, the sins accumulated by a person during the past ten years get destroyed. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.161.19-20 \|\|

*kalya utthāya yo martyaḥ kuryāttāsāṃ pradakṣiṇam \|*  
*pradakṣiṇīkṛtā tena pṛthivī syādvasundhare \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pradakṣiṇāyāṃ caikāyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ ca vasundhare \|*  
*daśavarṣakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ naśyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. One who uses the urine of the Kapila cow for the purpose of bathing, he is equated with a person who takes his bath in the Gangs.

## \|\| 3.161.21-23 \|\|

*kapilāyāstu mūtreṇa snāyādvai yaḥ śucivrataḥ \|*  
*sa gaṅgādyeṣu tīrtheṣu snāto bhavati mānavaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*yena snānena caikena bhavamukto bhavennaraḥ \|*  
*yāvajjīvakṛtātpāpāttatkṣaṇādeva mucyate \|\| 22 \|\|*

*gosahasraṃ ca yo dadyādekāṃ vā kapilāṃ naraḥ \|*  
*samametatpurā prāha brahmaloke pitāmahaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. Because using the cow’s urine for a bath, it relieves a person of the worldly attractions and all his sins collected during the whole life get destroyed. A person who gives away a hundred cows, the merit earned by him equates with the merits achieved by a person who gives away a Kapila cow in charity. This had been revealed by Brahma in the Brahmaloka.

## \|\| 3.161.24 \|\|

*yaścaikāṃ kapilāṃ hanyānnaro rajjukaro yadi \|*  
*gosahasraṃ hataṃ tena bhavatīha na saṃśayaḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

24\. In case, a person holding a rope in his hands kills a Kapila cow, he earns the sin of killing a thousand cows. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.161.25-27 \|\|

*gavāṃ sthitiṃ kalpayeta ghṛtaṃ gavyaṃ na dūṣayet \|*  
*yāvaddhi varddhate gavyaṃ tāvatpāpaistu pūyate \|\| 25 \|\|*

*gavāṃ kaṃḍūyanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tathā ca pratipālanam \|*  
*tulyaṃ goghṛtadānasya bhayarogādipālanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tṛṇādibhakṣaṇārthaṃ ca gavāṃ dadyāddharādikam \|*  
*svargavāsaphalaṃ divyaṃ labhate mānavottamaḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

25-27. Therefore, one should think pleasantly about the cows in order to avoid the attracting of blemish in milk and ghi. Till such time the ghi remains in the vase, the person remains purified free from the sins. Rubbing the limbs of the cows and feeding them up is said to be highly rewarding. It also protects from danger and it amounts to the giving away of ghi in charity. One who gives the green grass as fodder to the cows, he earns the merit of living in the heaven.

## \|\| 3.161.28-29 \|\|

*daśeha kapilāḥ proktāḥ svayameva svayaṃbhuvā \|*  
*yo dadyācchrotriyasyaiva svargaṃ gatvā sa mānavaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*vimānairvividhairdivyairdivyakanyābhirarcitaḥ \|*  
*sevyamānastu gaṃdharvairdīpyamānā yathāgnayaḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

28-29. The self-born Brahma has spoken about the ten forms of Kapila cows. In case, a Kapila cow is given over to a Brahmana well-versed in the Vedas, the donor earns his stay in the heaven, where he reaches boarding various types of planes and is served by the divine damsels as well as the Gandharvas.

## \|\| 3.161.30-32 \|\|

*suvarṇakapilā pūrvā dvitīyā gaurapiṅgalā \|*  
*āśā caiva tṛtīyā syādagnijvālā caturthikā \|\| 30 \|\|*

*paṃcamī juhuvarṇā syātṣaṣṭhī tu ghṛtapiṅgalā \|*  
*saptamī śvetapiṅgā syādaṣṭamī kṣīrapiṅgalā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*navamī pāṭalā jñeyā daśamī puṣpapiṅgalā \|*  
*etā daśa samākhyātāḥ kapilāśca vasuṃdhare \|\| 32 \|\|*

30-32. Out of the ten Kapila cows, first one is known as Suvarna-Kapila; the second one is known as Gaurapingala; the third one is known as Asa\\ the fourth one is Agnijvala; the fifth one is Juhuvarna; the sixth one is Ghrtapingala; the seventh one is Svetapingala; the eighth one is Ksirapingala; the ninth one is known as Patala\\ and the tenth one is known as Puspapingala. О Vasudhara, these are the ten types of Kapila cows.

## \|\| 3.161.33-37 \|\|

*sarvā hyetā mahābhāgāstārayaṃti na saṃśayaḥ \|*  
*saṃgameṣu praśastāśca sarvapāpapraṇāśanāḥ \|\| 33 \|\|*

*evametāstu kapilāḥ pāpaghnyaśca vasundhare \|*  
*āśā caiva tu yā proktā agnigarbhānalaprabhā \|\| 34 \|\|*

*agnijvālojjvalaiḥ śṛṃgaiḥ pradīptāṃgāralocanā \|*  
*agnipuṣpā agnilomā tathānyā cānalaprabhā \|\| 35 \|\|*

*tāmāgneyyāṃ sadā dadyādbrāhmaṇāyetaraiḥ sadā \|*  
*gṛhītvā kapilāṃ śūdraḥ kāmatastatpayaḥ pibet \|\| 36 \|\|*

*patitaśca bhavennityaṃ caṃḍālasadṛśaḥ pumān \|*  
*tasmānna pratigṛhṇīyācchabalāṃ gāṃ kathaṃcana \|\| 37 \|\|*

33-37. All these auspicious cows redeem the human beings. There is no doubt about it. Of all the cows on earth, the Kapila cow is considered to be quite praiseworthy and the destroyer of all the sins. The third type of the Kapila cow is known as Asa, while the one known as Agnigarbha illuminates like the fire. Agnijvala has the bright horns and the eyes like the burning fire. The others known as Agnipuspa and Agnihoma possess the lustre of fire. These types of Kapila cows having the lustre of the fire, should be given over by the people to the Brahmana in charity with utmost respect. Keeping a Kapild cow in his house, a Sudra should not drink her milk of his own accord and one who does so, attains the position of a Candala. Therefore, he should not keep a Kapila cow with him.

## \|\| 3.161.38-40 \|\|

*dvārāṃte parihartavyā kapilā gaurdvijetaraiḥ \|*  
*lokeṣu te mṛḍhatamāḥ kapilākṣīrabhojanāḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*asaṃbhāṣyāśca patitāḥ śūdrāste pāpakarmiṇaḥ \|*  
*pibaṃti yāvatkapilāṃ tāvatteṣāṃ pitāmahāḥ \|*  
*amedhyaṃ bhuñjate'tastāṃ nopajīveddvijetaraḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*tāsāṃ ghṛtaṃ ca kṣīraṃ vā navanītamathāpi vā \|*  
*upajīvaṃti ye śūdrāste prayāṃti yamālayam \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. Except a Brahmana, Ksatriya or a Vaisya, a Sudra should remove a Kapila cow from his house. A Sudra, who consumes the milk of a Kapila cow in the world, is considered to be extremely foolish. Such a Sudra, having fallen is not fit to be talked. The days upto which Sudra consumes the milk of the Kapila cow, for the same number of days, his manes have to take prohibited food. Therefore, a Sudra should not earn his livings from the same source. A Sudra who consumes the milk, ghi or butter of the Kapila cow, has to proceed to the place of Yama.

## \|\| 3.161.41-43 \|\|

*kapilājīvinaḥ śūdrāḥ sarve gacchaṃti rauravam \|*  
*raurave bhuñjate duḥkhaṃ varṣakoṭi śatoṣitāḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tato vimuktāḥ kālena jāyaṃte śvānayoniṣu \|*  
*śvānayonervimuktāste viṣṭhāyāṃ kṛmiyonigāḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*viṣṭhāsveva ca pāpiṣṭhā durgaṃdheṣu ca nityaśaḥ \|*  
*bhūyo'pi jāyamānāste tatrottāro na vidyate \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. A Sudra who earns his living from a Kapila cow, falls in a terrific hell and has to face misery for a hundred crores of years. Getting relieved of the hell in due course of time, he is reborn as a dog and from there, he becomes the worm of the refuse. Thus, all such sinners are born and die in refuse alone and they cannot be redeemed in anyway.

## \|\| 3.161.44-47 \|\|

*brāhmaṇaścaiva yo devi kuryātteṣāṃ pratigraham \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛtyamedhyāyāṃ pitarastasya śerate \|\| 44 \|\|*

*taṃ vipraṃ nānubhāṣeta na cāpyekāsane viśet \|*  
*sa nityaṃ varjanīyo vai dūrāttu brāhmaṇādhamaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*yastena saha bhāṣeta prāyaścittī bhave ddvijaḥ \|*  
*ekasya gopradānasya sahasrāṃśo na pūryate \|\| 46 \|\|*

*kimanyairbahubhirdānaiḥ koṭisaṃkhyātavistaraiḥ \|\| 47 \|\|*

44-47. Besides the cows, a Brahmana who accepts the chanty of the Madras is also treated as the degraded one. His manes also sleep in an impure manner. Therefore, one should neither talk to him nor should anyone share seat with him. He should be discarded from a distance for all times to come, because a Brahmana who talks to such people, has to perform repentance. When a thousandth part of the merit of giving a cow in charity cannot be completed, then what is the use of the donation of the crores? A person who gives away in charity a Kapila cow to a mendicant, the poor but noble, besides a Brahmana who performs homa, is relieved of all the sins.

## \|\| 3.161.48-49 \|\|

*śrotriyāya daridrāya suvṛttāyāhitāgnaye \|*  
*dattvaikāṃ kapilāṃ dhenuṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate \|\| 48 \|\|*

*māse prasavinīṃ dhenuṃ dānārthī pratipālayet \|*  
*ātmārthe na prapālyā hi sadā narakabhīrubhiḥ \|\| 49 \|\|*

48-49. During the last days of her pregnancy, for the sake of the charity, the cow-donor actually makes the receiver as the benefactor and not himself, because by so doing one has to fall in the hell. When the pregnancy of a Kapila cow reaches the middle, only then she should be given in charity to a Brahmana, till the face of the calf becomes visible in the womb.

## \|\| 3.161.50-52 \|\|

*kapilā'rdhaprasūtā ca dātavyā hi dvijanmane \|*  
*jāyamānasya vatsasya mukhaṃ yonyāṃ pradṛśyate \|\| 50 \|\|*

*tāvatsā pṛthivī jñeyā yāvadgarbhaṃ na muṃcati \|\| 51 \|\|*

*dhenoryāvaṃti romāṇi savatsāyā vasundhare \|*  
*bhūmyāṃ tu pāṃsavo yāvadyāvannakṣatratārakāḥ \|\| 52 \|\|*

50-52. Till such time the cow does not litter the calf, upto that time she should be known as Prthivi. О Earth, the number of hair the cow with calf have on their bodies, or the dust particles, besides the number of stars and the constellations, each one of them when multiplied with a thousand years, the donor enjoys his stay for an equivalent number of years in Brahmaloka. The donor of a Kapila cow is adored by Brahma and Viṣṇu and lives there with comfort.

## \|\| 3.161.53-56 \|\|

*tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi brahmeśādibhirarcitaḥ \|*  
*brahmaloke nivasati yaścaikakapilāpradaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*suvarṇaśṛṅgīṃ yaḥ kṛtvā khurai raupyaiḥ samarcitām \|*  
*brāhmaṇasya kare dattvā suvarṇaṃ raupyameva ca \|\| 54 \|\|*

*kapilāyāstadā putraṃ brāhmaṇasya kare nyaset \|*  
*udakaṃ ca kare dattvā vācayeta svaśaktitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*suvarṇaistu caturbhiśca tribhirdvābhyāmathāpi vā \|*  
*ekahīnā na dātavyā yadīcchecchubhamātmanaḥ \|\| 56 \|\|*

53-56. A person should give away to a Brahmana, a cow with the horns decorated with gold and the hoofs with silver. At the same time, the calf of Kapila should be given over to the Brahmana in his hand. Thereafter, the water should be poured in his hand and an appropriate samkalpa should be chanted. At that point of time, two, three or four gold coins should surely be given. There should not be less than a gold coin, because by failing to do so, some obstructions could be created in the welfare of the donor. After thus performing, it would be construed that the ocean, the forest, the mountains, the castles and the entire earth filled with diamonds has been given over in charity. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.161.57-60 \|\|

*sa samudravanopetā saśailavanakānanā \|*  
*ratnapūrṇā bhaveddattā pṛthivī nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*pṛthivīdānatulyena dānenaitena vai naraḥ \|*  
*tārito yāti pitṛbhirvaiṣṇavaṃ yatpadaṃ param \|\| 58 \|\|*

*brahmasvaharaṇo goghno bhrūṇahā brahmaghātakaḥ \|*  
*pāpakṛccobhayamukhīṃ dadyātsatkanakānvitām \|*  
*taddinaṃ ca payobhojī saṃyataścātivāhayet \|\| 59 \|\|*

*gomayenopalipyātha maṇḍalaṃ vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*svaśākhoktena maṃtreṇa homayettu vicakṣaṇaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

57-60. With the influence of this charity which equates with the giving away of the land, the manes are freed and achieve the supreme Vaisnava position. A person, having committed the sin of snatching away of the livelihood of a Brahmana, killing of the cow, abortion, killing of a Brahmana, must give away a pregnant cow in charity together with gold, observing fast on that particular day. A pavilion should be made over the earth plastered with the cowdung. Then reciting the hymns as prescribed in the scriptures, the intelligent donor should perform the homa as well.

## \|\| 3.161.61-64 \|\|

*vyāhṛtyā homayetpūrvaṃ paṃcavāruṇakaṃ tathā \|*  
*irāvatī dhenumatī devasya tveti vā punaḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*syonā pṛthivi maṃtreṇa gaurvatsasahitā navā \|*  
*nikāmaphaladā dhenuḥ sā syātsurabhinaṃdinī \|\| 62 \|\|*

*yā te sarasvatī devī viṣṇunā ca tathā mahī \|*  
*gaurī viṣṇupadaṃ coktvā śāṃtikarmaṇi vācayet \|\| 63 \|\|*

*yāvadvatsasyadvau pādau śiraścaiva pradṛśyate \|*  
*tāvadvai pṛthivī jñeyā yāvadgarbhaṃ na muñcati \|*  
*tasminkāle pradātavyā brāhmaṇāya vasuṃdhare \|\| 64 \|\|*

61-64. Initially making use of the vyahrtis (i.e., bhur, bhuvah, svah), Pancavaruni homa should be performed and the hymn – “Iravati Dhenumati Devasya Tvam Syona Prthivi” should be recited. Then a cow with a calf, who is also known as Surabhi, Nandini, Dhenu, bestow the desireless merit. For the sake of peace, one should utter the hymn of Sarasvati Devi, Viṣṇumahi, Gauri and Viṣṇupada. Till such time the hoofs and the head of the calf emerge out of the womb of the cow and unless the calf emerges out of the womb completely, the cow should be known as Prthivi and the same should be given to a Brāhmaṇa in charity.

## \|\| 3.161.65-67 \|\|

*suvarṇaśṛṃgīṃ raupyakhurāṃ kāsyadohāṃ satāmrakām \|*  
*savastraghaṃṭābharaṇāṃ gaṃdhapuṣpairalaṃkṛtām \|*  
*vastrākṣataiḥ samabhyarcya brāhmaṇāya samarpayet \|\| 65 \|\|*

*suvarṇasya sahasreṇa tadardhenāpi bhāmini \|*  
*tasyāpyardhena śaktyā'tha tasyāpyarddhena vā punaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*yathā śaktyā pradātavyā vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaiḥ \|*  
*kare dattvā suvarṇaṃ ca athavā rūpyameva ca \|\| 67 \|\|*

65-67. The horns should be decorated with gold, while the hoofs should be decorated with silver and the milk pot should be made of bronze or the bell. metal. Besides the fragrance, costumes, a bell, ornament and flowers should also be given to the Brāhmaṇa with the cow. A thousand cows of gold or half of that or still half of that or as per one’s means should be given over to the Brāhmaṇa. One should not at all be miserly at that point of time. In the absence of the gold, the silver can be used while giving away the cow in charity.

## \|\| 3.161.68-70 \|\|

*gṛhāṇemāṃ mahādhenuṃ bhava bhrātā mamāśu vai \|*  
*sarvapāpakṣayaṃ kṛtvā sadā svastikaro bhava \|\| 68 \|\|*

*irāvatī dhenumatī jāhnavī tadanantaram \|*  
*pratidāsyāmi te dhenuṃ kuṭumbārthe viśeṣataḥ \|\| 69 \|\|*

*bhavatātsvasti me nityaṃ sukhaṃ cānuttamaṃ tathā \|*  
*dattā tu pṛthivī devī tvayeyaṃ pratigṛhyatām \|\| 70 \|\|*

68-70. At that time, the donor should say – “O Brahmana, accepting this cow in donation, you kindly remove all my sins as my brother and bestow welfare on me. Thereafter, for the sake of your family, I shall give away the cows known as Iravati, Dhenumati and Jahnvi. You kindly bestow all the comforts to me regularly. I am giving over this cow as the earth. You kindly accept the same.”

## \|\| 3.161.71-72 \|\|

*ko'dāditi ca vai maṃtro japitavyo dvijena ca \|*  
*visṛjya brāhmaṇaṃ so'pi tāṃ dhenuṃ svagṛhaṃ nayet \|\| 71 \|\|*

*evaṃ prasūyamānāṃ gāṃ yo dadāti vasundhare \|*  
*sā samudravanopetā saśailavanakānanā \|*  
*ratnapūrṇā bhaveddattā pṛthivī nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 72 \|\|*

71-72. At that point of time, the Brahmana should also chant the mantra— “ко ’dati” The receiver Brahmana should also take the cow to his home. О earth, the pregnant cow is thus given in charity. One who does so, he is deemed to have donated the entire earth with ocean, forest, besides the forts etc., filled with gems. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.161.73 \|\|

*prataptajāṃbūnadatulyavarṇāṃ mahānitaṃbāṃ tanuvṛttamadhyām \|*  
*arddhaprasūtāṃ dvimukhīṃ suśīlāṃ sevantyajasraṃ kapilāṃ hi devāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

73\. Even the gods serve the pregnant cow Kapila who is double-faced, with developed rear part and having slender waist.

## \|\| 3.161.74-76 \|\|

*prātarutthāya yo bhaktyā dhenukalpaṃ naro bhuvi \|*  
*jitendriyaḥ śucirbhūtvā paṭhedbhaktyā samanvitaḥ \|\| 74 \|\|*

*trikālaṃ paṭhate yastu pāpaṃ varṣaśatodbhavam \|*  
*naśyatyekakṣaṇādeva vāyunā pāṃsavo yathā \|\| 75 \|\|*

*śrāddhakāle paṭhedyastu idaṃ pāvanamuttamam \|*  
*tasyānnaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ tadvai pitaro'śnaṃti dhīmataḥ \|\| 76 \|\|*

74-76. Getting up early in the morning, a person who with utmost devotion and discipline, purifying himself, chants the auspicious Dhenukalpa during all the three kalas, his all sins of hundred years are washed out. During the Sraddha time, recitation of Dhenukalpa is most beneficial. Then the learned manes accept with delight the food cooked by him on the earth.

## \|\| 3.161.77-78 \|\|

*amāvāsyāṃ ca yo vidvāndvijānāmagrataḥ paṭhet \|*  
*pitarastasya tuṣyaṃti varṣāṇāṃ śatameva ca \|\| 77 \|\|*

*yaścaitatchṛṇuyātpuṇyaṃ tadgatenāṃtarātmanā \|*  
*saṃvatsarakṛtātpāpāttatkṣaṇādeva mucyate \|\| 78 \|\|*

77-78. Similarly, on the moonless day, a learned person when recites it before the learned Brāhmaṇas, his manes live with comfort for a hundred years. Those who attentively listen to its recitation, their sins committed during a year are all washed out.

## \|\| 3.161.79 \|\|

*idaṃ rahasyaṃ rājendra varāhamukhanirgatam \|*  
*dharaṇyai kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|\| 79 \|\|*

79\. This I have revealed to you the secret which was revealed by lord Varaha to the earth goddess, which destroys all the sins.

## Chapter 162. Giving of a buffalo in charity

## \|\| 3.162.1-6 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*mahiṣīdānamāhātmyaṃ kathayāmi yudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*puṇyaṃ pāpavināśaṃ ca āyuṣyaṃ sarvakāmadam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*candrasūryagrahe puṇye kārttikyāmayane tathā \|*  
*śuklapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ sūryasaṃkrāntivāsare \|\| 2 \|\|*

*yadā vā jāyate cittaṃ vittaṃ ca kurunandana \|*  
*tadaiva deyā mahiṣī saṃsārabhayabhīruṇā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*supayodharaśobhāḍhyā suśṛṃgī sukhurā tathā \|*  
*prathamaprasūtā taruṇī suśīlā doṣavarjitā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*suvarṇaśṛṅgatilakā ghaṃṭābharaṇabhūṣitā \|*  
*raktavastrāvṛtā ramyā kāṃsyadohanakānvitā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*piṇyākapiṭikopetā sahiraṇyā ca śaktitaḥ \|*  
*saptadhānyayutā deyā brāhmaṇe vedapārage \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О Yudhisthira, now I am going to speak about the merit of giving away a buffalo in donation, which fulfills all the desires. О son of the Kuru race, at the time of the lunar or the solar eclipse, on the full moon day of the month of Kartika, or change of half year, or on the fourteenth bright moon day, or on the first day of the month or an any other auspicious day, when an idea develops in one’s mind to give away a buffalo in charity, the person is quite afraid of the way of the world about giving away a buffalo in charity. She should have a beautiful udder, besides the horns and the hoofs and should have littered for the fast time. She should be quite young, unblemished, with horns of beautiful colour, adorned with a bell in the neck and should be covered with the red cloth. She should have a beautiful form and the milk vase of bronze metal should be given with the buffalo together with the fodder. With the gold as per one’s means, the seven grains and the buffalo should be given over to a learned Brahmana, who is well-versed in the Vedas.

## \|\| 3.162.7-10 \|\|

*purāṇapāṭhake tadvajjyotiḥśāstravide tathā \|*  
*deyā na vedarahite na ca kuvratine kvacit \|\| 7 \|\|*

*dravyairebhiḥ samāyuktāṃ puṇye'hni vidhipūrvakam \|*  
*dadyānmaṃtreṇa rājendra purāṇapaṭhitena tu \|\| 8 \|\|*

*indrādilokapālānāṃ yā rājamahiṣī śubhā \|*  
*mahiṣī dānamāhātmyātsāstu me sarvakāmadā \|\| 9 \|\|*

*dharmarājasya sāhāyye yasyāḥ putraḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ \|*  
*mahiṣāsurasya jananī yā sāstu varadā mama \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. A Brahmana who is well-versed in the Puranas or an astrologer or a Brahmana who is devoid of the Vedic knowledge should not be given the buffalo in charity. О Rajendra, the buffalo with the aforesaid materials should be given on an auspicious occasion in an appropriate manner, while saying – “Let the royal queen of Indra and Lokapalas, with the influence of the charity of the donating a buffalo, arriving here in this form, should fulfill all my desires, whose son has been established for the help of Dharmaraja and who is the mother of Mahisasura. She arriving here in this form, should bestow boon on me.”

## \|\| 3.162.11-15 \|\|

*dadyātpradakṣiṇīkṛtya brāhmaṇe tāṃ payasvinīm \|*  
*pratigrahaḥ smṛtastasyāḥ pṛṣṭhadeśe svayaṃbhuvā \|\| 11 \|\|*

*evaṃ dattvā vidhānena brāhmaṇasya gṛhaṃ nayet \|*  
*vastrairābharaṇaiḥ pūjya bhaktyā ca kurunandana \|\| 12 \|\|*

*saṃpāditā mayā tubhyaṃ saṃtuṣṭo me bhava dvija \|\| 13 \|\|*

*anena vidhinā dattvā mahiṣīṃ dvijapuṅgave \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti iha loke paratra ca \|\| 14 \|\|*

*yā sā dadāti mahiṣīṃ sā rājamahiṣī bhavet \|*  
*mahārājaḥ pumānrājanvyāsasya vacanaṃ yathā \|\| 15 \|\|*

11-15. Thus chanting this mantra, the milk giving buffalo should be given over to the Brahmana. The self-born Brahma, at the time of accepting her, had desired that the rear side of the buffalo should be patted. О son of Kuru race, thus decorating the buffalo with the best of costumes and ornaments, it should be sent off to the house of a Brahmana with a message – “O Brahmana, I have given over the buffalo to you, therefore, you keep her well fed.” In case, the buffalo is thus given over to a noble Brahmana, all the desires of the present as well as the future worlds are fulfilled. According to the words of Vyasa, a woman who gives away a buffalo in charity, she becomes a queen and the man becomes a king.

## \|\| 3.162.16-17 \|\|

*yajñayājī bhavedvipraḥ kṣatriyo vijayī bhavet \|*  
*bhavedvaiśyastu dhanavāñchūdraḥ sarvārthasaṃyutaḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tasmānnareṇa dātavyā mahiṣī vibhave sati \|*  
*putrapautraprapautrārthamātmanaḥ śubhamicchatā \|\| 17 \|\|*

16-17. Similarly, a Brahmana becomes the performer of yajna, a Ksatriya becomes victorious; a Vaisya earns riches and a Sudra gets all his desires fulfilled, in case he gives away a buffalo in charity. Therefore, for the benefit of sons, grandsons, great grandsons and himself, a person should give away a buffalo in an appropriate manner.

## \|\| 3.162.18-19 \|\|

*daśadhenusamāṃ rājanmahiṣīṃ nārado'bravīt \|*  
*viṃśatigosamāṃ vyāsaḥ sarvadānottamaṃ raviḥ \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sagareṇa kakutsthena dhuṃdhumāreṇa gādhinā \|*  
*dattāḥ saṃpūjya viprebhyo mahiṣyaḥ sarvakāmadāḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. О king, Narada had equated giving away of a buffalo in charity to the giving away of ten cows in charity. Vyasa had equated a buffalo with twenty cows. Ravi had described this to be the best of all the charities. The king Sagara in earlier times, besides Dhundhumara and Gadhi gave away a buffalo each to a Brahmana, which fulfills all the desires.

## \|\| 3.162.20 \|\|

*mahiṣī dānamāhātmyaṃ yaḥ śṛṇoti sadā naraḥ \|*  
*sa sarvapāpanirmuktaḥ śivaloke mahīyate \|\| 20 \|\|*

20\. The merit of donating a buffalo is when heard by a person, he getting relieved of all the sins, is respected in the Sivaloka.

## \|\| 3.162.21 \|\|

*dugdhādhikāṃ hi mahiṣīṃ jalameghavarṇāṃ sapuṣṭapaṭṭakavatīṃ jaghanābhirāmām \|*  
*dattvā suvarṇatilakāṃ dvijapuṃgavāya lokadvayaṃ vijayate kimu tatra citram \|\| 21 \|\|*

21\. A buffalo which yields much milk, having the colour of the clouds with filled water, adorned with badge, with beautiful legs, decorated with a gold tilakam, when given to an excellent Brāhmaṇa, the donor becomes victorious in both the worlds.

## Chapter 163. Donation of a sheep

## \|\| 3.163.1-6 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*śṛṇu pārtha paraṃ dānaṃ sarvakilbiṣanāśanam \|*  
*yaddattvā trividhaṃ pāpaṃ sadyo vilayamṛcchati \|\| 1 \|\|*

*suvarṇaromāṃ sauvarṇīṃ pratyakṣaṃ vā suśobhanām \|*  
*suvarṇatilakopetāṃ sarvālaṃkārabhūṣitām \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kauśeyaparidhānāṃ ca divyacaṃdanabhūṣitām \|*  
*divyapuṣpopahārāṃ ca sarvadhāturasairyutām \|*  
*saptadhānyasamāyuktāṃ phalapuṣpavatīṃ tathā \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śatena kārayettāṃ ca suvarṇasya prayatnataḥ \|*  
*yathā śaktyātha vā kuryādvittaśāṭhyaṃ na kārayeta \|\| 4 \|\|*

*ayane viṣuve caiva grahaṇe śaśisūryayoḥ \|*  
*duḥsvapnadarśane caiva janmarkṣe pitṛsaṃkṣaye \|\| 5 \|\|*

*yadā vā jāyate vittaṃ cittaṃ śraddhāsamanvitam \|*  
*tadaiva dānakālaḥ syādyato'nityaṃ hi jīvitam \|\| 6 \|\|*

1-6. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – I am going to speak to you about another excellent type of charity, which destroys all the sins, besides the three types of crimes. You please listen. Irrespective of its being real or a figure of it made of gold, it should be adorned with a tilakam of gold, besides all the ornaments and covered with a silken cloth. It should also be adorned with gold ornaments and possessing all the rasas as well as the dhatu or metals, together with the seven cereals. It should be further decorated with the flower garlands. It should be given over to a Brāhmaṇa with high respect. The gold image of the sheep should be made of thirty tolas or as per the means of the donor. But while doing so, miserliness should never be shown. At the time of the change of half year, some festival of Viṣṇu, solar or lunar eclipses, on the day of birth constellation, on witnessing an evil dream, last day of pitrpaksa or whenever an idea to perform such a type of charity develops in the mind of a person, at the same time, with one’s heart having been filled with devotion, a sheep should be given away in charity, because the life is unpredictable.

## \|\| 3.163.7-12 \|\|

*dadyāttīrthe gṛhe vāpi yatra vā ramate manaḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

*tatra saṃsthāpya deveśamumayā saha śaṃkaram \|*  
*brahmāṇaṃ saha gāyatryā saśrīkaṃ śrīdharaṃ tathā \|\| 8 \|\|*

*ratyā saha tathānaṃgaṃ lokapālāngrahānapi \|*  
*saṃpūjya ca vidhānena gaṃdhapuṣpanivedanaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*tadagre kārayeddhomaṃ tilājyena mahīpate \|*  
*alaṃkṛtya dvijaṃ śāṃtaṃ vāsobhiḥ pratipūjya ca \|\| 10 \|\|*

*talliṅgamaṃtrairhomaśca kartavyo jvalite'nale \|*  
*tatastāṃ tilakuṃbhasthāṃ lavaṇāntamupasthitām \|\| 11 \|\|*

*pūjayitvā vidhānena mantrametamudīrayet \|*  
*romatvaṅmāṃsamajjādyaiḥ sarvopakaraṇaiḥ sadā \|*  
*jagataḥ saṃpravṛddhāsi tvāmataḥ prārthaye sthitām \|\| 12 \|\|*

7-12. At one’s own house or at a holy place, wherever one thinks, the images of Uma with Siva, Brahma with Gayatri, Sri with Sridhara, Rati with Kamadeva, besides Lokapalas and the planets should be established. Thereafter, all of them should be worshipped offering sandal paste, flowers etc. in an appropriate manner. Thereafter, the homa with ghi and sesamum seeds should be performed. Then, the sheep should be given over to a peaceful Brāhmaṇa offering him the costumes, with the reciting of the mantras and making the offerings in the fire flames. Thereafter, the image should be properly worshipped. A prayer should then be offered, chanting the following mantra – “O sheep, you are good to the entire world with your wool, skin, marrow and flesh, therefore, I am offering my prayer to you.

## \|\| 3.163.13-16 \|\|

*vāṅmanaḥkāyajanitaṃ yatkiñcinmama duṣkṛtam \|*  
*tatsarvaṃ vilayaṃ yātu tava dānātprasevitam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*evamuccārya tāṃ dadyādbrāhmaṇāya kuṭumbine \|*  
*nābhibhāṣeta taṃ dattvā mukhaṃ ca nāvalokayet \|\| 14 \|\|*

*duṣṭapratigrahahato vipro bhavati pātakī \|\| 15 \|\|*

*no dadyāddakṣiṇāhīnāṃ dātavyā sā vidhānataḥ \|*  
*dakṣiṇāvidhinā hīnā duḥkhaśokāvahā bhavet \|\| 16 \|\|*

13-16. Let all my evil designs drawn mentally, by speech or physically, be washed with the performing of this charity.” Thus speaking, the donor should handover the sheep to a Brāhmaṇa with family. At that point of time, he should not talk to him, nor should be look at his face. Because in case, the Brāhmaṇa is hurt with the wicked donation, it is considered to be sinful. The donor should not give away the charity without giving daksina which should not be improper. In case, charity is not given in a proper manner or is given without daksina, the donation of the sheep in that case causes the grief.

## \|\| 3.163.17-19 \|\|

*purā dattamidaṃ dānaṃ gauryā śaṃkarakāmyayā \|*  
*tena śaṃbhuḥ patirlabdhaḥ sarvadevanamaskṛtaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*indrāṇyā svarṇaromāṇāṃ śataṃ dattaṃ vidhānataḥ \|*  
*sarvadevapatiṃ prāpya patiṃ sādyāpi modate \|\| 18 \|\|*

*nalena dattametaddhi rājyaṃ kṛtvā divaṃ gataḥ \|*  
*rukmiṇyāhaṃ patirlabdhaḥ saubhāgyamatulaṃ tathā \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. This type of charity was performed by Gauri to get Siva as her husband, as a result of which she got Siva as her husband who became adorable by all the gods. Indrani also gave away a hundred sheep with gold like wool in charity in a proper manner, as a result of which she got Indra – the lord of all the gods as her husband and remains delightful even today. With the influence of this charity, she enjoyed the royal pleasures besides the heaven. Similarly, with the influence of this vrata, Rukmini got me as her husband as well as enormous fortunes.

## \|\| 3.163.20-22 \|\|

*dānasyāsya prabhāveṇa putrā bahubalānvitāḥ \|*  
*aputro labhate putramadhano labhate dhanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*dattvā dānaṃ śubhāṃ kāṃtiṃ vipulāṃ ca tathā śriyam \|*  
*ya imaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ dānakalpamanuttamam \|*  
*ahorātrakṛtātpāpānmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*meṣī viśeṣakaluṣāpaharātiśastā dāne sadaiva rasadhātuyutā sadhānyā \|*  
*tāmādareṇa kurunandana dehi dattvā yenāstapāpatimiraḥ saviteva bhāsi \|\| 22 \|\|*

20-22. Those desirous of having sons, get the sons; the poor people get the riches, pleasant lustre and enormous wealth. A person who listens to this kalpakatha, his sins for the day and night are removed instantaneously. О son of the race of Kuru, therefore, you must give away in charity the sheep with sapta-dhatu, seven grains, because it surely removes all the sins and has been conceived as praiseworthy. By giving away a sheep in charity, a person getting relieved of the sins, shines like the sun.

## Chapter 164. Donation of land

## \|\| 3.164.1-4 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*bhūmidānamato vakṣye sarvapāpapraṇāśanam \|*  
*ye prayacchaṃti viprebhyo bhūmidānaṃ sadakṣiṇam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*śrotriyāya daridrāya agnihotraratāya ca \|*  
*sa sarvakāmatṛptātmā sarvaratnairvibhūṣitaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*sarvapāpavinirmukto dīpyamāno raviryathā \|*  
*bālasūryaprabhābhāsairvāditradhvajaśobhitaiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*vimānairbhāsvarairdivyairviṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati \|\| 4 \|\|*

1-4. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – I am now going to speak about the process of donating land, which removes all the sins. When the land is given in charity with daksina to a Brahmana well-versed in the Vedas, a poor, or a Brahmana who performs the homa, then getting all his desires fulfilled, the donor is further decorated with the gems. Getting relieved of all the sins, he shines like the sun and ultimately, boarding a divine plane, getting adorned with the lustre of the rising sun, has his flag always rising, illuminating at the same time and reaches Viṣṇuloka.

## \|\| 3.164.5-7 \|\|

*tatra divyāṃganābhiśca sevyamāno yathāsukham \|*  
*kāmagaḥ kāmarūpī ca krīḍatyānaṃdamakṣayam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*yāvaddhārayate lokānbhūraṃkurasamudbhavā \|*  
*tāvadbhūmipradaḥ kāmaṃ viṣṇuloke mahīyate \|\| 6 \|\|*

*nahi bhūmipradānādvai dānamanyadviśiṣyate \|*  
*diśo daśānugṛhṇāti hartā tā daśa haṃti ca \|\| 7 \|\|*

5-7. There he is served by the divine damsels, enjoys all the desired pleasures and sports of various nature, achieving the eternal bliss. Till such time the land accommodates all the lokas, for the same length of period, the donor of the land is honoured in the Viṣṇuloka. There is no other charity comparable with the donation of land. Therefore, the donor of the land receives all the ten directions and a person who usurps the same, he destroys all the ten directions.

## \|\| 3.164.8-9 \|\|

*dānānyanyāni kṣīyaṃte kālena puruṣarṣabha \|*  
*bhūmipradānapuṇyasya kṣayo naivopapadyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sarvapāpāni kṣīyaṃte kālayogakrameṇa tu \|*  
*bhūmihartuśca rājeṃdra duḥkhasyāṃto na vidyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

8-9. О best of the humans, all other types of charities get lost in due course of time, but the merit of donating the land never gets destroyed. О Rajendra, according to the sequence of Kalayoga, all the sins get declined, but a person who usurps the land, there is no end to his miseries.

## \|\| 3.164.10 \|\|

*brāhmaṇāya suśīlāya bhūmiṃ dattvā tu yo naraḥ \|*  
*na hi tāmupajīvedyaḥ sa mahatpuṇyamāpnuyāt \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. A person, who donating the land to a noble Brahmana and after so doing never makes use of the same land, he earns enormous merit.

## \|\| 3.164.11-14 \|\|

*halakṛṣṭāṃ mahīṃ kṛtvā sabījāṃ sasyamālinīm \|*  
*yāvatsūryakṛtā lokastāvatsvarge mahīyate \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca ratnānyābharaṇāni ca \|*
