*sarvadānāni rājeṃdra dadāti vasudhāṃ dadat \|\| 12 \|\|*

*sāgarānsaritaḥ śailānsamāni viṣamāṇi ca \|*  
*sarvagaṃdharasānsnehāndadāti vasudhāṃ dadat \|\| 13 \|\|*

*oṣadhīḥ kṣīrasaṃpannā nānāpuṣpaphalopagāḥ \|*  
*kamalotpalakhaṃḍāṃśca dadāti vasudhāṃ dadat \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. After ploughing the land and then sowing the seeds in the same, the seeds get sprouted, spreading greenery everywhere. Similarly, a person, who gives the land with greenery grown over it or the fields, illumines in the heaven with respect upto the end of the universe. О Rajendra, a person donating the land is actually also donating wealth, food grains, ornaments of gold studded with gems, together with all the oceans, rivers, the high mountains, all the rasas, juices with fragrance, all the herbs which always remain flowering, besides the red lotus flowers are also donated by him.

## \|\| 3.164.15-17 \|\|

*agniṣṭomādibhiryajñairye yajaṃti sadakṣiṇaiḥ \|*  
*prāpnuvaṃti ca tatpuṇyaṃ bhūmidānādyadāpyate \|\| 15 \|\|*

*śrotriyāya mahīṃ dattvā ye haraṃti na mānavāḥ \|*  
*tāvatteṣāṃ bhavetsvargo yāvallokā pratiṣṭhitāḥ \|\| 16 \|\|*

*sasyapūrṇāṃ mahīṃ yastu śrotriyāya prayacchati \|*  
*pitarastasya tuṣyaṃti yāvadābhūtasaṃplavam \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. The donor of land earns enormous merit, which one earns with the performing of the Agnistoma homas with enormous daksina. By giving away the land to a Srotriya Brāhmaṇa and not getting it back in return, the person is honoured in the heaven till the time of dissolution. Similarly, when the land of green fields is given over to a Srotriya Brāhmaṇa, the manes of the donor remain satisfied till the time of dissolution.

## \|\| 3.164.18-19 \|\|

*yatkiṃcitkurute pāpaṃ puruṣo vṛttikarśitaḥ \|*  
*api gocarmamātreṇa bhūmidānena śudhyati \|\| 18 \|\|*

*suvarṇānāṃ sahasreṇa yatpuṇyaṃ samudāhṛtam \|*  
*bhūmi gocarmamātreṇa tatphalaṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

18-19. Whatever sins are committed by a person under compulsion of earning livelihood, the same are washed out with the donating of the land equivalent to the hide of a cow. The merit one earns with the giving away of a thousand gold coins in charity, the same merit could be achieved with the donation of a piece of land of the size of a hide of the cow.

## \|\| 3.164.20-21 \|\|

*kapilānāṃ sahasrebhyo yaddatte'nnaṃ narottama \|*  
*bhūmigocarmamātreṇa tatphalaṃ labhate naraḥ \|\| 20 \|\|*

*madhyamasya manuṣyasya vyāsena parisaṃkhyayā \|*  
*triṃśaddaṃḍāṃśca gocarma dattvā svarge mahīyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

20-21. О best of the humans, by giving away in charity a hundred of Kapila cows, the merit which is earned by a person, the same merit is earned by donating the land, equal to the size of the hide of cow. According to the words of Vyasa, a cow’s hide is said to be as big as the thirty dandas. Therefore, by giving away the same stretch of land, the person is adored in the heaven in the middle category.

## \|\| 3.164.22-23 \|\|

*bahubhirvasudhā bhuktā rājabhiḥ sagarādibhiḥ \|*  
*yasya yasya yadā bhūmistasyatasya tadā phalam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*kiṃkarā mṛtyudaṃḍāśca asipatravanādayaḥ \|*  
*ghorāśca vāruṇāḥ pāśā nopasarpaṃti bhūmidam \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. Several kings like Sagara and others have made use of the charity of the land. Therefore, whosoever donated the land at any stage, he achieved the merit at the same time. The attendants of Yama, his rod of death or the sword like leaves, cannot touch the person who has donated the land.

## \|\| 3.164.24-27 \|\|

*nirayā rauravādyāśca kuṃbhīpākaḥ suduḥsahaḥ \|*  
*tathā ca yātanāḥ kaṣṭā nopasarpaṃti bhūmidam \|\| 24 \|\|*

*citraguptaśca kālaśca kṛtāṃto mṛtyureva ca \|*  
*yamaścāpi svayaṃ rājā saṃpūjayati bhūmidam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*rudraḥ prajāpatiḥ śakro devāsuragaṇāstathā \|*  
*ahaṃ ca paramaprītyā pūjayāmīha bhūmidam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ṣaṭkarmakṛtsuvṛttāya kṛśāya ca priyārthine \|*  
*bhūmirdeyā naravyāghra sannidhiścākṣayo bhavet \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. The terrific and awful hells like Raurava and others, besides the unbearable Kumbhipaka hell and the horrible tortures of that place can never even approach the donor of the land. Even Citragupta, Kala, Yama and Mrtyu personally worship the donor of the land. Similarly, Rudra, Prajapati Indra and all the gods and even myself, worship the donors of the land personally. Those who perform the six duties of their own family tradition, the noble ones, the poor and the loveable Brahmanas should be given away the land in charity to enable him to earn him the everlasting merit.

## \|\| 3.164.28 \|\|

*sīdamānakuṭuṃbāya śrotriyāyāhitāgnaye \|*  
*vṛttasthāya daridrāya bhūmirdeyā nareśvara \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. О Naresvara, the Brahmana with a family or the one who is poor, reciter of the Vedas, performer of the homa, who earns his livelihood by fair and noble means, should be given the land in donation.

## \|\| 3.164.29 \|\|

*yathā janitrī kṣīreṇa putraṃ saṃvarddhayetsadā \|*  
*tathā bhūmipradaṃ bhūmiḥ sarvakāmaistu tarpati \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. As a lady after giving birth to a child feeds the same with the milk of her own breast, similarly, the land makes all the desires of the donor successful, and makes him delightful.

## \|\| 3.164.30 \|\|

*yathā gaurbharate vatsa kṣīreṇa kṣīramutsṛjet \|*  
*tathā sarvarasopetā bhūmirbharati bhūmidam \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Like a cow, which feeds her calf with her milk, similarly, the earth possessing all the rasas, also feeds the donor in many ways.

## \|\| 3.164.31 \|\|

*yathā bījāni rohaṃti jalasiktāni bhūtale \|*  
*tathā kāmāḥ prarohaṃti bhūmidasya dinedine \|\| 31 \|\|*

31\. As the seed sprouts with irrigating the water to the same, similarly, the donor of the land has all his desires fulfilled gradually.

## \|\| 3.164.32-34 \|\|

*yathodayansahasrāṃśustamaḥ sarvaṃ vyapohati \|*  
*tathā bhūmipradānaṃ tu sarvapāpaṃ vyapohati \|\| 32 \|\|*

*para dattāṃ tu yo bhūmimupahiṃsetkadācana \|*  
*sa baddho vāruṇaiḥ pāśaiḥ kṣipyate pūyaśoṇite \|\| 33 \|\|*

*svadattāṃ paradattāṃ vā yo hareta vasuṃdharām \|*  
*sa naro narake ghore kliśyatyāpralayāṃtikam \|\| 34 \|\|*

32-34. As the rising sun removes all the darkness, similarly, die donating of the land relieves the donor of all the sins. A person, who destroys the land donated by others, he is bound with the noose of Varuna and is thrown in the altar of blood and puss. One who usurps the land donated by him, himself or by others, he falls in the awful hell, where he remains till the time of dissolution.

## \|\| 3.164.35-37 \|\|

*rudatāṃ vṛttināśena ye pataṃtyaśrubiṃdavaḥ \|*  
*tādvarṣasahasrāṇi narake pacyate tu saḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇānāṃ hṛte kṣetre hartustripuruṣaṃ kulam \|*  
*dattvā bhūmiṃ tu viprāya upahiṃsedyadā punaḥ \|*  
*adhomukhaśca duṣṭātmā kuṃbhīpāke sa pacyate \|\| 36 \|\|*

*divyavarṣasahasrāṃte kuṃbhīpākādviniḥsṛtaḥ \|*  
*iha loke bhavecchā vai sapta janmāni pārthiva \|\| 37 \|\|*

35-37. A person who shatters or usurps the land of other and when he weeps and the tears fall on the ground, the one who so usurped the land of other, he has to spend his life in the hell for a thousand years against a single drop of tear. One who usurps the field of a Brāhmaṇa, he destroys his three generations. When a Brahmana is given the land in donation, one who destroys it again, he is hung upside down in the kumbhipaka hell. After his release from the kumbhipaka hell, for seven births he has to be born as a dog or a Candala.

## \|\| 3.164.38-40 \|\|

*svadattāṃ paradattāṃ vā yatnādrakṣedyudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*mahīṃ mahībhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha dānācchreyonupālanam \|\| 38 \|\|*

*toyahīneṣvaraṇyeṣu śuṣkakoṭaravāsinaḥ \|*  
*kṛṣṇāhvayobhijāyaṃte narā brahmasvahāriṇaḥ \|\| 39 \|\|*

*evaṃ dattvā mahīṃ rājanprahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā \|*  
*sarvānkāmānavāpnoti manasā ciṃtitānnaraḥ \|\| 40 \|\|*

38-40. О Yudhisthira, one should protect his own land as well as that belonging to others making all the efforts, because as compared to the other excellent charities by the kings, the protection of the land has been considered to be more meritorious. A person who usurps the earnings of the Brahmana, is born as a black Cobra and lives in the hollow of a tree in the forest. By donating the earth with a delightful mind, all the desires of a person get fulfilled.

## \|\| 3.164.41 \|\|

*bhūmidānātparaṃ nāsti sukhaṃ vāmuṣmikaṃ mahat \|*  
*na cāpi bhūmiharaṇādanyatpātakamucyate \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. In this, as well as in the future world, there is no other thing more comfortable than the giving away of land in charity. Similarly, there is no other sin greater than the usurping of the land of others.

## \|\| 3.164.42 \|\|

*yacchaṃti ye dvijavarāya mahīṃ sukṛṣṭāṃ te yāṃti śakrasadanaṃ suviśuddhadehāḥ \|*  
*ye lopayaṃtyatibalādatha kāmalobhātte rauravātigahanānna samuttaraṃti \|\| 42 \|\|*

42\. Ploughing the field properly, when the green field is given over to a Brāhmaṇa by a person, he getting his soul purified, achieves the place of Indra, and the one who destroys the same, can never be relieved of the terrific hell.

## Chapter 165. Donating the Image of Earth goddess

## \|\| 3.165.1-2 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*bhūmidānaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ nānyeṣāmupapadyate \|*  
*te hyupārjayituṃ śaktā dātuṃ pālayituṃ yathā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*bhūmidānasamaṃ kiṃcidanyatkathaya yādava \|*  
*saṃprāptavittairyacchakyaṃ saṃsārabhayabhīrubhiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Yudhisthira said - It is possible for the Ksatriyas to donate the land, because they alone are competent enough to acquire it, donate it as well as preserve it. Therefore, you also speak about another charity equivalent to the donation of the land by which other persons are also able to perform the same vrata, with the spending of their wealth.

## \|\| 3.165.3-9 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*sauvarṇāṃ vidhivatkṛtvā sādridrumavatīṃ śubhām \|*  
*mahīṃ prayaccha viprāṇāṃ tattulyā sā nigadyate \|\| 3 \|\|*

*śṛṇuṣvaikamanā bhūtvā mahādānaṃ narottama \|*  
*savidhānaṃ pravakṣyāmi phalaṃ yatnena yadbhavet \|\| 4 \|\|*

*caṃdrasūryoparāge ca janmarkṣe viṣuve tathā \|*  
*yugādiṣu ca dātavyamayane ca vidhānataḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*anyeṣvapi ca kāleṣu praśaste dhanasaṃcaye \|*  
*pāpakṣayāya dātavyaṃ yaśo'rthe vā narairbhuvi \|\| 6 \|\|*

*hemnaḥ palaśatenoktā tadardhenāpi śaktitaḥ \|*  
*kuryātpaṃcapalādūrdhvamasamartho'pi bhaktimān \|\| 7 \|\|*

*kārayetpṛthivīṃ haimīṃ jaṃbudvīpānukāriṇīm \|*  
*maryādāparvatavatīṃ madhye merusamanvitām \|\| 8 \|\|*

*lokapālāṣṭakopetāṃ brahmaviśveśasaṃyutām \|*  
*nānāparvatapūrṇāṃ ca ratnābharaṇabhūṣitām \|\| 9 \|\|*

3-9. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – Making a gold image of the goddess earth in which the mountains and forests should be displayed and then giving it to the Brahmanas is equated with the giving of land in donation. Therefore, I am speaking about the great charity and the reward thereof. You please listen with apt attention. On the day of lunar or solar eclipse, or the birth constellation or at the time of equinox, or on the eve of half year, the image should be given in an appropriate manner. When the wealth is sufficiently available with a person, then for the washing out of the sins, or for the earning of the glory, the people should give away this type of charity on earth. The image of the earth goddess should be made of a hundred palas or as per the means of the donor. But in case a person is filled with devotion (having little means or resources), he can make the image of five palas also. The image of the goddess Earth should be made according to Jambudvipa, in which the traditions, the mountains with Meru mountain in the centre, together with Siva, Brahma and other gods should also be shown. It should also be filled with mountains, the eight Dikpalas and others.

## \|\| 3.165.10-13 \|\|

*sarvasasyavicitrāṃgīṃ sarvagaṃdhādhivāsitām \|*  
*īdṛśīṃ tu mahīṃ kṛtvā kārayenmaṃḍapaṃ tataḥ \|\| 10 \|\|*

*daśadvādaśahastaṃ ca caturvaktra satoraṇam \|*  
*madhye ca vedikāṃ kuryāddhanurhastāṃ pramāṇataḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*aiśānyāṃ surasaṃsthānamāgneyyāṃ kuṃḍameva ca \|*  
*patākābhiralaṃkṛtya devatāyatanānyatha \|\| 12 \|\|*

*lokapālā grahāścaiva pūjyā mālyavilepanaiḥ \|*  
*homaṃ kuryurdvijāḥ śāṃtāścātuścaraṇikāḥ śubhāḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

10-13. It should have all the food grains, other different limbs, besides the fragrance and scents. Making an image of this type, thereafter, a mandapa of ten or twelve cubits should be made with toranas or arches. A pedestal of the size of a bow should be made in the middle of the mandapa and in the north east of which the places for the gods should be made. The fire altar should be made in the south-east comer, and the temples of Lokapalas and the planets should be made. After worshipping the gods offering the garlands to them, the peaceful Brahmanas should be made to perform the homa.

## \|\| 3.165.14-18 \|\|

*sālaṃkārā savastrāśca mālyacaṃdanabhūṣitāḥ \|*  
*agnisaṃsthāpanaṃ tatra kṛtvā pūrvaṃ tato mahīm \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ānayeyurdvijā rājanbrahmaghoṣapuraḥsaram \|*  
*śaṃkhatūryaninādaiśca geyamaṃgalanisvanaiḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*tilaiḥ pracchāditāṃ vediṃ kṛtvā tatrādhivāsayet \|*  
*athāṣṭādaśadhānyāni rasāṃśca lavaṇādikān \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tathāṣṭau pūrṇakalaśānsamaṃtātsthāpayecchubhān \|*  
*vitānakaṃ ca kauśeyaṃ phalāni vividhāni ca \|\| 17 \|\|*

*aṃśukāni vicitrāṇi śrīkhaṃḍaśakalāni ca \|*  
*ityevaṃ racayitvā tāmadhivāsanapūrvakam \|\| 18 \|\|*

14-18. The Brahmanas adorned with ornaments, costumes, garlands, sandal paste etc., should initially consecrate the fire and then the conches, trumpets and other welfare sounds should be produced. Thereafter, the image of the earth goddess should be brought there and should be consecrated over the pedestal, over which the sesamum seeds should be spread. Thereafter, the eighteen types of food grains, all the rasas, salt etc., besides the four pitchers filled with water should be consecrated an all the four sides. Then, a canopy of the silken cloth should be raised and several types of fruits, different coloured costumes and the pieces of sandalwood should be used for decorating the place. Making such a type of the creation, the adhivdsana rite of the image should be performed.

## \|\| 3.165.19-22 \|\|

*tato homāvasāneṣu niṣpanne sarvaśāṃtike \|*  
*śuklamālyāṃbaradharo yajamānaḥ svayaṃ tataḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ pṛthvīṃ gṛhītvā kusumāṃjalim \|*  
*puṇyakālamathāsādya maṃtrānetānudīrayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

*namaste sarvadevānāṃ tvameva bhavanaṃ yataḥ \|*  
*dhātrī tvamasi bhūtānāmataḥ pāhi vasuṃdhare \|\| 21 \|\|*

*vasu dhārayase yasmātsarvasaukhyapradāyakam \|*  
*vasuṃdharā tato jātā tasmātpāhi bhayādalam \|\| 22 \|\|*

19-22. While performing the homa and other Santi rites, the donor should be clad in white garments and the garland. Then carrying the flowers in hand-cups, he should go round the earth goddess. On that auspicious occasion, a prayer should be offered reciting the mantras – “O Vasundhara, you are the abode of all the gods. Therefore, salutation to you again and again. You contain all the jivas, therefore, you please protect me.

## \|\| 3.165.23-25 \|\|

*caturmukho'pi no gacchedyasmādaṃtaṃ tavācale \|*  
*anaṃtāyai namastubhyaṃ pāhi saṃsārakardamāt \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tvameva lakṣmīrgovide śive gaurīti saṃsthitā \|*  
*gāyatrī brahmaṇaḥ pārśve jyotsnā caṃdre ravau prabhā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*buddhirbṛhaspatau khyātā medhā muniṣu saṃsthitā \|*  
*viśvaṃ prāpya sthitā yasmāttato viśvaṃbharā matā \|\| 25 \|\|*

23-25. You have the Vasus who bestow comforts and because of which you are called as Vasundhara. Being fearless, you kindly protect me. О immovable one, even the four-faced Brahma could not know the end of you. You are limitless, you kindly protect me from the worldly swamp or mud. I offer my salutation to you again and again. You happen to be Laksmi of Govinda, Gayatri for Brahma, the moonlight for the Moon, besides the lustre of the Sun. Similarly, you are the wisdom with Brhaspati, Medha with the ascetics. You serve as a feeder for the universe and as such you are called Visvambhara.

## \|\| 3.165.26 \|\|

*dhṛtiḥ kṣitiḥ kṣamā kṣoṇī pṛthivī vasudhā mahī \|*  
*etābhirmūrtibhiḥ pāhi devi saṃsārasāgarāt \|\| 26 \|\|*

26\. О Goddess, you are Dhrti (the patience), Ksiti (the welling place), Ksama (forgiveness), Ksoni (the earth), Prthivi (earth), Vasudha, Mahi and with several other forms, you protect, me in this world.”

## \|\| 3.165.27-30 \|\|

*evamuccārya tāṃ devīṃ brāhmaṇebhyo niveda yet \|*  
*dharārddhaṃ vā caturbhāgaṃ gurave pratipādayet \|\| 27 \|\|*

*anena vidhinā yastu dadyāddevīṃ dharāṃ budhaḥ \|*  
*puṇyakāle ca saṃprāpte sa padaṃ yāti vaiṣṇavam \|\| 28 \|\|*

*yadi kartuṃ na śaknoti puṇyehni bahuvistaram \|*  
*saṃsthāpya śobhane sthāne mahīmeva pradāpayet \|\| 29 \|\|*

*vimānenārkavarṇena kiṃkiṇījāla mālinā \|*  
*nārāyaṇapuraṃ gatvā kalpatrayamathāvaset \|\| 30 \|\|*

27-30. After thus offering the prayer, the image should be given over to the Brahmana. Thereafter, the half or a quarter of the part of the earth should be given over to the preceptor. Following this process, a person who donates the earth goddess, he achieves the Vaiṣṇava position (Viṣṇuloka) at an auspicious time. In case a person is unable to give away the earth goddess in charity at an auspicious occasion in an exhaustive manner, then he can give away the image alone of the earth goddess at some sacred place and by so doing, the donor reaches the place of Narayana in a beautiful plane decorated with the net of bells, where he stays for three kalpas.

## \|\| 3.165.31-33 \|\|

*kṣīṇapuṇya ihābhyetya rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ \|*  
*vijayī śatrudamano bahubhṛtyaparicchadaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*śatakoṭyadhipaḥ śūraścakravartī mahābalaḥ \|*  
*sapta janmāni dānasya māhātmyādrājyamāpnuyāt \|\| 32 \|\|*

*dvīpāvikarṣaviṣamāṃ vidhivadvidhāya haimīṃ mahīṃ suramahīmiva vindhyamadhyām \|*  
*lokeśaśaṃbhuśivakeśavasaṃyutāṃ ca prāyaccha pārtha tava kiṃ bahunoditena \|\| 33 \|\|*

31-33. After the decline of his merits, he is reborn on earth as a king, who gets victorious over all his enemies, besides having a large number of attendants. He rules over the earth for more than a hundred of years, because of influence of the giving away of the gold image of the earth goddess in charity. Therefore, you should give away in charity a gold image of the earth goddess in an appropriate manner. This type of charity is equivalent to all the charities given in past seven births. What is the use of speaking much? О Partha, one who has two feet, Vindhya in the middle, besides Lokapalas, Siva and Kesava, such an earth goddess of gold should be given in charity.

## Chapter 166. Giving in charity of the line of plough

## \|\| 3.166.1-2 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi dānamatyadbhutaṃ tava \|*  
*yena dattena rājendra sarvadānaprado bhavet \|\| 1 \|\|*

*sarvapāpapraśamanaṃ sarvasaukhyapradāyakam \|*  
*prayuktaṃ halapaṃktyā ca sarvadānaphalapradam \|\| 2 \|\|*

1-2. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О Rajendra, I am now speaking to you about an astonishing type of charity. It is known as Halapankti, which removes all the sins and bestows the entire merit of the charity.

## \|\| 3.166.3-8 \|\|

*paṃktirdaśahalā proktā halaṃ syāttu caturgavam \|*  
*sāradārumayānyāhurhalāni daśa paṃḍitāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*sauvarṇapaṭṭasaṃnaddha ratnavaṃti śubhāni ca \|*  
*yūnaśca balino bhavyānvyaṃgahīnānsvalaṃkṛtān \|\| 4 \|\|*

*vastrakāṃcanapuṣpaiśca caṃdanairdigdhamastakān \|*  
*abhagnānyojayetteṣu lāṃgaleṣu vṛṣāñchubhān \|\| 5 \|\|*

*yoktrāṇi yugalagnāni savṛṣāṇi ca kārayet \|*  
*pratodakīlakābaṃdhasarvopakaraṇānvitām \|\| 6 \|\|*

*evaṃvidha halaiḥ kuryāttaṃ yuktāṃ halapaṃktikām \|*  
*karkaṭaṃ kheṭakaṃ cāpi grāmaṃ vā sasyamālinam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*nivartanaśataṃ vāpi tadarddhaṃ vā prakalpayet \|*  
*evaṃvidhāṃ parvakāle dadyātprayatamānasaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

3-8. The learned Brāhmaṇas have prescribed the plough to be made of the best of wood. The collection of ten ploughs make a pankti or a line. Four bullocks are yoked in the same. All these combined are called a plough. There should be a badge of gold over it, which should be studded with gems. This is treated as quite auspicious. The young and powerful bullocks should be yoked for the purpose. These bullocks should be unblemished, well decorated. Their foreheads should be well decorated with costumes, gold, flowers, besides the sandal paste. The auspicious bulls should be brought before the plough and the yoke should be placed over their necks with ropes quite securely. There should be a whip also which should be free from the nails. A line of plough is formed. These ploughs and the bullocks are driven with crabs and long staff or the green cereals or grams and should be given over in charity at an auspicious occasion.

## \|\| 3.166.9-10 \|\|

*kārtikyāṃ cātha vaiśākhyāmuttare vā'yane tathā \|*  
*janmarkṣe grahaṇe vāpi viṣuve vā pradāpayet \|\| 9 \|\|*

*brāhmaṇānvedasaṃpannānvyaṃgahīnānalaṃkṛtān \|*  
*śrotriyāṃśca vinītāṃśca halasaṃkhyānnimaṃtrayet \|\| 10 \|\|*

9-10. This could be done on the full moon day of the month of Kartika or Vaisakha, when the same is in the Uttarayana, during the constellation of birth, on the day of solar or the lunar eclipse, besides at the time of equinox, the plough should be given over to the Brahmanas who should be noble without ornaments, well-versed in the Vedas, docile and should have been invited for the purpose.

## \|\| 3.166.11-13 \|\|

*daśahastapramāṇena maṃḍapaṃ kārayedbudhaḥ \|*  
*pūrve dvikuḍamekaṃ vā hastamātraṃ suśobhanam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*tatra vyāhṛtibhirhomaṃ kuryuste dvijasattamāḥ \|*  
*parjanyādityarudrebhyaḥ pāyasena yajedbudhaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*pālāśyaḥ samidhastatra sājyaṃ kṛṣṇāstilāstathā \|*  
*adhivāsya ca tāṃ paṃktiṃ dhānyamadhyagatāṃ śubhām \|\| 13 \|\|*

11-13. A pavilion of ten cubits should be prepared. To the east of it, one or two beautiful altars should be made in which the offerings of payasam should be made for the clouds, Aditya and Rudra. The twigs of palasa tree should be used together with the black sesamum seeds and ghi. This auspicious pankti should be established among the grains.

## \|\| 3.166.14-17 \|\|

*tataḥ sarvasamīpe tu snātaḥ śuklāṃbaraḥ śuciḥ \|*  
*halapaṃktiṃ yojayitvā yajamānaḥ samāhitaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*tūryaśaṃkhaninādaiśca brahmaghoṣaiḥ supuṣkalaiḥ \|*  
*imamuccārayenmaṃtraṃ gṛhītakusumāṃjaliḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

*yasmāddevagaṇāḥ sarve hale tiṣṭhaṃti sarvadā \|*  
*vṛṣaskaṃdhe saṃnihitāstasmādbhaktiḥ śivestu me \|\| 16 \|\|*

*yasmācca bhūmidānasya kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm \|*  
*dānānyanyāni me bhaktirdharme cāstu dṛḍhā sadā \|\| 17 \|\|*

14-17. Then the donor taking his bath, should put on the white garments. Then keeping on the purity, the donor should go over to line of plough and should tie up the same. Then playing on the musical instruments, he should recite the mantras carrying the flowers in his handcups – “The purpose for which the gods reside in the plough which is placed over the neck of the bullocks, similarly, the devotion of Siva should remain with me forever. As the other charities cannot be compared with one sixteenth part of. the donations of land, similarly, the devotion in Dharma should remain with me for all times to come and remain firm.”

## \|\| 3.166.18-21 \|\|

*evamukte tataḥ paṃktiṃ prerayeyurdvijottamāḥ \|*  
*bījāni sarvaratnāni suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tathā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*svayaṃ paścāddhale lagno viprahasteṣu nirvapet \|*  
*yāyānnivartanaṃ yāvattatastu viramedbudhaḥ \|\| 19 \|\|*

*pradakṣiṇaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā viprāṇāṃ pratipādya ca \|*  
*sadakṣiṇāṃ vidhānena praṇipatya visarjayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

*anena vidhinā yastu dānametatprayacchati \|*  
*ekaviṃśatkulopetaḥ svargaloke mahīyate \|\| 21 \|\|*

18-21. After thus speaking, moving by those fines or panktis with seeds and the gems, as well as the gold, one should follow the plough and the Brahmanas should be made to sow the seeds. Till such time the process of sowing continues, (others) should wait. After circumambulating, the donor should give them away in charity to the Brahmanas, who should be sent off with respect. By following this process, when a person donates the hala-pankti, he is respected in the heaven with his twenty one generations.

## \|\| 3.166.22-23 \|\|

*saptajanmasu dāridryaṃ daurbhāgyaṃ vyādhayastathā \|*  
*na paśyati ca bhūmestu tathaivādhipatirbhavet \|\| 22 \|\|*

*dṛṣṭvā taddīyamānaṃ tu dānametadyudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*ājanmanaḥ kṛtātpāpānmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ \|\| 23 \|\|*

22-23. During the seven future births, he does not have to face poverty, misfortunes and the ailments. Rather, he becomes the lord of the land. О Yudhisthira, while giving away the charity, when another person observes it from a distance, he is also relieved of his sins for whole life. There is no doubt about it.

## \|\| 3.166.24-27 \|\|

*dānametatpradattaṃ hi dilīpena yayātinā \|*  
*śibinā niminā caiva bharatena ca dhīmatā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*te'dyāpi divi modaṃte dānasyāsya prabhāvataḥ \|*  
*tasmātsarvaprayatnena dānametannṛpottama \|\| 25 \|\|*

*dātavyaṃ bhaktiyuktena striyā vā puruṣeṇa vā \|*  
*yadi paṃktirna vidyeta paṃca vā caturo'tha vā \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ekamapyuktavidhinā halaṃ deyaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. The great kings like Dilipa, Sivi, Nimi and the intelligent king Bharata, all had performed this charitable exercise as a result of which, they are enjoying in the heaven till date. Therefore, all the men and the women must perform this charity. In case due to some reason, a person is unable to perform the charity of pankti, then he can resort to the giving away of five or four or even one plough, definitely.

## \|\| 3.166.28 \|\|

*ye saṃti lāṃgalamukhottharajovikārā yāvaṃti tadgatadhuraṃdhara romakāṇi \|*  
*tāvaṃti śaṃkarapure triyugāni tiṣṭhetpaṃktipradānamiha yatkurute manuṣyaḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. The earth which is dug with the ploughshare, the number of the particles of that dust with the number of the hair over the body of each one of the bulls, for the same number of years, the donor dwells in the abode of Siva.

## \|\| 3.166.29 \|\|

*yuktāṃ vṛṣairatibalairhalapaṃktimetāṃ puṇyehni bhaktisahitāndvijapuṃgavebhyaḥ \|*  
*yacchaṃti ye sukṛtino vasudhāsametāṃ te bhūbhujo bhuvamupetya bhavaṃti bhavyāḥ \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. Thus a donor, who gives away the hala-pankti with plough and the bullocks at an auspicious time to the excellent Brahmanas, he becomes a noble soul and becomes a great king on earth.

## Chapter 167. Giving away of an earthen vase in charity

## \|\| 3.167.1 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*tanme kathaya deveśa yena dattena mānavaḥ \|*  
*bahuputro bahudhano bahubhṛtyaśca jāyate \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Yudhisthira said- О Devesa, you kindly speak about a charity, by giving which, a person achieves enough of sons, enormous wealth and several servants or attendants.

## \|\| 3.167.2-5 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*purā bhārata vaṃśesminrājāsīddhavyavāhanaḥ \|*  
*pitṛpaitāmahaṃ tena prāptaṃ rājya makaṃṭakam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*na tasya rājye vidhvaṃso na vairijanitaṃ bhayam \|*  
*śarīrotthamahāvyādhirna caivāṃtaradāyakaḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*tasyaivaṃ kurvato rājyaṃ pūrvakarmārjitāśubhāt \|*  
*nāsti bhṛtyo bhārasahaḥ sarvarājyadhuraṃdharaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*na putraḥ priyakṛtkaścinna maṃtrī madhurākṣaraḥ \|*  
*na mitraṃ kāryakaraṇe samartho na suhṛttathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

2-5. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О Bhārata, in ancient times, there had been a king named Havyavahana in his race, who inherited his kingdom from his father and ruled the country without any obstruction. During the time of his rule, no destruction could be found, nor was there any danger because of the mutual enmity. There had been no ailments at all. Although, he was ruling without any obstruction for long, but because of his earlier misdeeds, he had no dependable servant who could share his burden or descend him. There was no son with him nor was there any dependable courtier or minister. Besides there was no competent friend or the well-wisher with him.

## \|\| 3.167.6-9 \|\|

*na bhojyasamaye prāpte bhojanaṃ sārvakāmikam \|*  
*na pūgaphalasaṃyuktaṃ tāṃbūlaṃ vasanaṃ na ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*na dhanaṃ janasaṃbandhakārako ratnasaṃcayaḥ \|*  
*tasyaivaṃ kurvato rājyamavyāhatamaceṣṭitam \|\| 7 \|\|*

*athaikasmindine vipraḥ pippalādo'tiviśrutaḥ \|*  
*ājagāma mahāyogī rājñaḥ pārśvaṃ mahādyutiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tamāgataṃ muniṃ dṛṣṭvā rājapatnī śubhāvatī \|*  
*pādyārghyāsanadānena sarvathā tamapūjayat \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. He also could not get food of his liking. He could not get the good quality of betel leaves or betel nuts, nor did he have the collection of gems. Thus, he kept on ruling unwillingly for long, when once Ṛṣi Pippalada arrived there. Finding the arrival of the great Ṛṣi in her kingdom, the chief queen known by the name of Subhavati, welcomed the Ṛṣi offering customary padya and arghya to him.

## \|\| 3.167.10-11 \|\|

*tataḥ kathāṃte kasmiṃścittamuvāca śubhāvatī \|*  
*bhagavanrājyametannaḥ sarvabādhāvivarjitam \|\| 10 \|\|*

*kasmānna bhṛtyāḥ putrā vā maṃtrimitrādikaṃ dvija \|*  
*bhogāvāptirna ca tathā sarvalokātiśāyinī \|\| 11 \|\|*

10-11. After finishing of the discourse, the queen said to the sage – “O lord, though in my kingdom, no obstruction is found, still we have no reliable servant, sons, courtiers or the friends. And, the enjoying of pleasures is also not quite praiseworthy.

## \|\| 3.167.12-14 \|\|

*pippalāda uvāca \|*  
*yadyena pūrvavihitaṃ tadasau prākṛte phalam \|*  
*karmabhūmiriyaṃ rājñi nātaḥ śocitumarhasi \|\| 12 \|\|*

*na tatkurvaṃti rājāno na dāyādā na śatravaḥ \|*  
*na bāṃdhavā na mitrāṇi yadyena na purā kṛtam \|\| 13 \|\|*

*tasmādbhavadbhiyarddattaṃ prāptaṃ tadrājyamuttamam \|*  
*bhṛtyamitrādisaṃbaṃdho na dattaḥ prāpyate kutaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

12-14. Pippalada said – О queen, whatever has been done by a person in the earlier birth, he reaps the reward for the same. Since this is the land of activity, therefore, one should not grieve about it in anyway. A person who did not care for his relatives and friends in his earlier births, that they do not care few him in the present birth. Therefore, whatever the noble deeds were performed by you in die earlier births, you have achieved the vast kingdom as a result of the same. When you had not cared for the servants (in the past birth), how can you get the same from them in the present birth?

## \|\| 3.167.15-19 \|\|

*śubhāvatyuvāca \|*  
*idānīmeva viprarṣe kasmāttannopadiśyate \|*  
*yena me bahavaḥ putrā dhanaṃ bhṛtyā bhavaṃti vai \|\| 15 \|\|*

*maṃtro vā siddhayogo vā vrataṃ dānamupoṣitam \|*  
*kathayasvāmalamate yena saṃpadyate sukham \|\| 16 \|\|*

*tataḥ sa kathayāmāsa pippalādo dvijottamaḥ \|*  
*āpākākhyaṃ mahādānaṃ sarvasaṃpatpradāyakam \|\| 17 \|\|*

*śraddhayā kuruśārdūla nārī vāpyatha vā pumān \|*  
*yena dattena bhāgyānāṃ bahūnāṃ bhājanaṃ bhavet \|\| 18 \|\|*

*tacchrutvā sa dadau rājā'pākākhyaṃ dānamuttamam \|*  
*lebhe putrānpaśūnbhṛtyānmaṃtrimitrasuhṛjjanān \|\| 19 \|\|*

15-19. Subhavati said – “Why don’t you deliver us the discourses, by which we could relieve us from many sins, have enormous wealth, besides the servants. О sage of spotless wisdom , in case there be any mantras, fasts, siddhayoga, vrata, or charities to be performed, then you kindly speak out the same to us.” Thereafter, Pippalada – the best of the Ṛṣis, revealed to them about a charity known as Apaka-dana, which bestows all types of prosperity. O lion among the race of Kurus, a man or a woman, whosoever performs this vrata, he or she attains several types of fortunes. On hearing this, the king performed the Apaka-dana in an appropriate way as a result of which, the king got a son, animals, the servants, courtiers, friends as well as the well-wishers.

## \|\| 3.167.20-24 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*āpākākhyaṃ mahādānaṃ kathayāmi yudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*dattena yena kāmānāṃ pumānbhavati bhājanam \|\| 20 \|\|*

*grahatārābalaṃ labdhvā bhārgavaṃ pūjayecchubham \|*  
*vāsobhirbhūṣaṇaiścaiva puṣpairagarucaṃdanaiḥ \|\| 21 \|\|*

*kuryāttathaiva sammānaṃ yathā tuṣṭo'bhijāyate \|*  
*kuruṣva tvaṃ me bhāṃḍāni gurūṇi ca laghūni ca \|\| 22 \|\|*

*maṇikādīni śubhrāṇi sthālyaśca sumanoharāḥ \|*  
*ghaṭakāḥ karakāścaiva galaṃtyaḥ kuṃḍalāni ca \|\| 23 \|\|*

*śarāvādīni pātrāṇi bhāṃḍamuccāvacaṃ bahu \|*  
*saṃpādaya mahābhāga viśvakarmā tvameva hi \|\| 24 \|\|*

20-24. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – I am now speaking about the Apaka-dana, with the performing of which a person can have all his desires fulfilled. Observing the strength of the stars, besides the auspicious time, one should worship them offering costumes, ornaments, flowers, agaru, sandal paste etc. and please them. Thereafter, he should say- “For my sake, you kindly arrange for the making of the big and small clay utensils, besides bright beads, pleasant plates, spouted jug and vase for drinking wine. О great soul, you are Visvakarma, therefore, you must perform this task.”

## \|\| 3.167.25-29 \|\|

*bhārgavo'pi prayatnena nānā bhāṃḍānvitaṃ śubham \|*  
*āpākaṃ kalpayeddivyaṃ vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā \|\| 25 \|\|*

*sahasramekaṃ bhāṃḍānāṃ sthāpayitvā vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*saṃdhyākāle jvalitvā tu dadyāccāpi hutāśanam \|\| 26 \|\|*

*rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kuryādgītamaṅgalanisvanaiḥ \|*  
*tataḥ prabhāte vimale jñātvā nirvāpitaṃ śanaiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*raktavastraiḥ samācchādya puṣpamālābhirarcayet \|*  
*yajamānastataḥ snātvā śuklāṃbaradharaḥ śuciḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

*hemaraupyāṇi bhāṃḍāni tāmralohamayāni ca \|*  
*paritaḥ sthāpayitvā ca svaśaktyā tāni ṣoḍaśa \|\| 29 \|\|*

25-29. Making all the efforts, the potter should also make several types of auspicious vases of auspicious clay. Thereafter, in the evening, these vases should be baked in fire. The night should then be spent by singing and dancing. But at the spotless dawn time, taking the vases which have been baked, covering them with the red colour, one should worship them with the offering of the flowers. The donor should take his bath and should then wear the white clothes. The ornaments should be made of gold, silver, copper or iron as per his means. These sixteen vases should be spread on all the four sides.

## \|\| 3.167.30-33 \|\|

*pūjayitvā prayatnena kṛtvā cāru pradakṣiṇām \|*  
*brāhmaṇānpūjayitvā ca bhārgavaṃ pūjya yatnataḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*nāryaścāvidhavāstatra samānīya prapūjya ca \|*  
*pradakṣiṇaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā maṃtreṇānena pūjayet \|\| 31 \|\|*

*āpākabrahmarūposi bhāṃḍānīmāni jaṃtavaḥ \|*  
*pradānātte prajāpuṣṭiḥ svargaścāstu mamākṣayaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*bhāṃḍarūpāṇi yānyatra kalpitāni mayā kila \|*  
*bhūtvā satpātrarūpāṇi upatiṣṭhaṃtu tāni me \|\| 33 \|\|*

30-33. Thereafter, the potter and the Brāhmaṇa should be worshipped. The married women with their husbands alive, should also be invited to participate in the rituals. Circumambulating and praying with the reciting of a mantra, he should say – “O Apaka, you are the form of Brahman. The creatures are like the earthen vases. By worshipping you, let me achieve the heaven. The vases, which have been conceived by me, they should be achieved by me as the auspicious vases.” This is the charity mantra.

## \|\| 3.167.34-36 \|\|

*yā ca yadbhāṃḍamādatte tasyaitaddāpayettataḥ \|*  
*svecchayā caiva gṛhṇātu na nivāryāstu kāścana \|\| 34 \|\|*

*anena vidhinā yastu dānametatprayacchati \|*  
*viśvakarmā bhavettuṣṭastasya janmatrayaṃ nṛpa \|\| 35 \|\|*

*nārī ca dattvā saubhāgyamatulaṃ pratipadyate \|*  
*gṛhaṃ sarvaguṇopetaṃ bhṛtyamitrajanairvṛtam \|\| 36 \|\|*

34-36. Thereafter, whichever vase is selected by a woman, she should be given over the same. He (the donor) should allow all the ladies the vase of their choice. By following this process, a person who performs the ceremony of the giving of charity, Visvakarma gets pleased with him. As a result of this, even the lady remains virtuous after three births with enormous fortunes. She possesses all the meritorious servants, besides the friends who are the real well-wishers.

## \|\| 3.167.37-38 \|\|

*aviyogaṃ sadā bhartrā rūpaṃ cānuttamaṃ labhet \|*  
*bhūdānametannirdiṣṭaṃ prakāreṇa tavānagha \|*  
*bhidyate bahubhirbhedairbhūmireṣā nareśvara \|\| 37 \|\|*

*niṣpādya bhāṃḍanicayoccataraṃ prayatnādāpākadānamiha yā kurute varastrī \|*  
*sā putrapautrapaśuvṛddhimukhāni bhuktvā pretya svabhartṛsahitā sukhinī sadāste \|\| 38 \|\|*

37-38. The lady receives an excellent husband, and gains the final beautitude. О Naresvara, by various manners, I have told you the merit of the giving away of the earth in charity. This is said to have been divided in several parts. Therefore, the earthen vases should be made making all the efforts. A lady who performs the donation of Apaka, she achieves the sons, grandsons, animals, progress etc., besides other comforts. She always remains comfortable with her husband.

## Chapter 168. Giving of a house in charity

## \|\| 3.168.1 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*sarvaśāstrārthatattvajña jñānavijñānapāraga \|*  
*gṛhadānasya māhātmyaṃ vidhiṃ vada vidāṃvara \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Yudhisthira said – О best of the learned one’s, you are well aware of the tattvas of all the scriptures and possess the enormous knowledge of worldly matters as well as the spiritual aspects. Therefore, you kindly enlighten me about the importance of the giving away of a house in charity.

## \|\| 3.168.2-7 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*na gārhasthayātparo dharmo nāsti dānaṃ gṛhātparam \|*  
*nānṛtādadhikaṃ pāpaṃ na pūjyo brāhmaṇātparaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*dhanadhānyasamāyuktaṃ kalatrāpatyasaṃkulam \|\| 3 \|\|*

*gogajāśvagaṇākīrṇaṃ gṛhaṃ svargādviśiṣyate \|*  
*yathā mātaramāśritya sarve jīvaṃti jaṃtavaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*evaṃ gṛhasthamāśritya vartayaṃtītarāśramāḥ \|*  
*dharmaścārthaśca kāmaśca mitrāṇi prathitaṃ yaśaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*prāptakāmairnaraiḥ pārtha sadā sevyo gṛhāśramaḥ \|*  
*na gṛheṇa vinā dharmo nārthakāmau sukhaṃ na ca \|\| 6 \|\|*

*na loka paṃktirna yaśaḥ prāpyate tridaśairapi \|*  
*na tatsvarge nāpavarge na tatkenopamīyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

2-7. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – There is no other dharma of a householder, there is no charity bigger than giving away of a house, there is no other sin greater than the speaking of the untruth and none is more adorable than a Brahmana. A person with house, having enough of riches, food grains, sons, family, besides the cows, elephants and the horses, is far better than the heaven. As all the living beings feel comfortable with the mother, similarly, those, getting shelter in a household, also feel comfortable. О Partha, by living in a house, a person achieves dharma, artha, ката, friends, besides the enormous glory. Therefore, a person for the success of his desires, should always live in the household. Because, without a house, even the gods cannot achieve dharma, artha, kama, comforts, loka-pankti and the fame. Therefore, there is no comparison of the same in the heaven as well as the liberation.

## \|\| 3.168.8-10 \|\|

*prasārya pādau yadrātrau svagṛhe svapatāṃ sukham \|*  
*dināni nāsya gaṇyaṃte nainamāhurmahāśanam \|\| 8 \|\|*

*api śākaṃ pacānasya svagṛhe paramaṃ sukham \|*  
*iti matvā mahārāja kārayitvā suśobhanam \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bhavanaṃ brāhmaṇe deyaṃ bhavyabhūtimabhīpsatā \|*  
*kārayitvā dṛḍhastaṃbhaṃ śubhapakveṣṭakāmayam \|\| 10 \|\|*

8-10. The people who sleep comfortable in the house spreading their feet, the same could never be gained in other asramas. Even the days of comfort in the Grhastha-asrama can never be counted. Also, the person in this asrama cannot be said to be a great eater as well, because even by consuming the ordinary vegetables in the house, he feels extremely comfortable. Thus realizing, a person desirous of enormous pleasures, should get a beautiful house constructed and then give over to a Brahmana in charity, which should be made of burnt bricks as well as the solid pillars.

## \|\| 3.168.11-19 \|\|

*śubhaṃ kamaṭhapṛṣṭhābhaṃ bhābhāsitadigaṃtaram \|*  
*sudhānuliptaṃ guptaṃ ca sukhaśālāvirājitam \|\| 11 \|\|*

*dadyādanaṃtaphaladaṃ śaivavaiṣṇavayoginām \|*  
*pratiśraye tu vistīrṇe kārite sajale ghane \|\| 12 \|\|*

*dīnānāthajalārthāya kṛtaṃ kiṃ na kṛtaṃ bhavet \|*  
*kārayitvā gṛhānpaścādṛtvigrudrārkasaṃkhyayā \|\| 13 \|\|*

*kuḍhyastaṃbhagavākṣāḍhayānvicitrānbahubhūmikān \|*  
*saprākārapratolīkānkapāṭārgalayaṃtritān \|\| 14 \|\|*

*sudhādhavalitānramyānvistīrṇāṃgaṇavāṭikān \|*  
*praveśanirgamayutānsamāsannajalāśayān \|\| 15 \|\|*

*lohopaskarasaṃpūrṇāṃstā mropaskarasaṃyutān \|*  
*svarṇopaskaraśobhāḍhyānraupyopaskarasaṃkulān \|\| 16 \|\|*

*ratnopaskarasaṃyuktānkāṃsyopaskaramaṃḍitān \|*  
*ārakūṭatrapusīsadā nopaskaravarjitān \|\| 17 \|\|*

*vaṃśopaskarasaṃkīrṇānkāṣṭhopaskara bṛṃhitān \|*  
*mṛnmayopaskarākīrṇānvastropakaraṇānvitān \|\| 18 \|\|*

*dharmopaskarasaṃbhāraśaṇavalkalarājitān \|*  
*rājitāṃstṛṇapāṣāṇaiḥ sarvopaskarabhūṣitān \|\| 19 \|\|*

11-19. It should be auspicious, resembling the back of the tortoise, looking graceful and painted with lime wash. It should have a secret and comfortable space. By giving away such of the house in charity one who does so, he enjoys enormous merits like the great Vaisnavas, Sarvas as well as the Yogins. Escaping the fury of the fall of the rains of fresh clouds, for the benefit of the poor and the downtrodden people, the house should be built with spacious rooms. For giving to the Brahmanas eleven and for the sake of the Sungod, twelve houses should be built in a secure manner with walls, pillars, windows or ventilators. Maximum part of the land should be kept plain. There should be beautiful boundary walls around the same, besides roads and the side lanes, the doors, the bolts for the securing of the doors, white washed, pleasant, with vast courtyard. There should also be a garden attached to it. There should be convenient exit and entry arrangements, the step-wells, besides the wells. The iron and copper should be freely used in construction of the house. The gold, silver, the gems should be used in the construction work, besides the bronze, brass and lead etc. At places, the bamboo and the wood should also be used, besides the mud or clay. The cloth, the resources for Dharma, the ropes, the hay and the stones should also be used in the construction work.

## \|\| 3.168.20-24 \|\|

*saptadhātumayaṃ bhāṃḍaṃ yattadratnasamudbhavam \|*  
*carmakāṣṭhamahābhāṃḍaṃ navavastumayaṃ tathā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*gomahiṣyaśvavṛṣabhapreṣyaveśyāgaṇānvitān \|*  
*kṣetrārāmajalāsannānkāmyānharmyavarāñchubhān \|\| 21 \|\|*

*saṃpūrṇānsarvadhānyaistu ghṛtatailaguḍādibhiḥ \|*  
*tilataṃdulaśālīkṣumudgagodhūmasarṣapaiḥ \|\| 22 \|\|*

*niṣpāvāḍhakyacaṇakakulatthāṇumasūrakaiḥ \|*  
*kaṃgumāṣayavādyāḍhyāñchākavṛṃtākapūritān \|\| 23 \|\|*

*lavaṇārdrakakharjūradrākṣājīrakadhānyakaiḥ \|*  
*hiṃgukuṃkumakarpūrasnānadravyaiḥ sacaṃdanaiḥ \|\| 24 \|\|*

20-24. There should be vases of all the seven metals in the house, besides those of gems, wood and other fresh material. The domestic animals like the cows, buffalos, horse, bulls, the messengers and the concubines should also be there. There should be fields, orchards and beautifully designed rooms. There should also be enough of grains, ghi, oil, raw sugar, sesamum seeds, rice, wild rice, green grams, mustard, winnowing baskets, pulse, citrus, arhara, gram, cereals, horse bean, anu, lentil, course grain, black gram, barley etc. Vegetables, brinjal, salt etc., besides there should be palm, grapes, cumin, coriander, asafetida, vermilion, camphor, sandal paste etc. should also be there.

## \|\| 3.168.25-28 \|\|

*dhūpopaskaraparyuptatūlīgaṇḍopadhānakaiḥ \|*  
*cullīcchedanamaṃthānabhadrāsanakagucchakaiḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*piṭharolūkhalasthālīśūrpadarpaṇapatrakaiḥ \|*  
*muśalāsikṛpāṇīṣudaṃḍakodaṃḍamudgaraiḥ \|\| 26 \|\|*

*gṛhāṭavāṭakādarvīdṛṣalloṣṭakahastakaiḥ \|*  
*cātrakāṃśukalohādi dīptamaṃthanikādibhiḥ \|\| 27 \|\|*

*kaṃḍaṇī peṣaṇī cullī udakumbhī pramārjanī \|*  
*maṃjūṣākoṣṭhakāsaṃdī kaṃbalaistanurāṃkavaiḥ \|\| 28 \|\|*

25-28. Besides the incense, cushions, pillow, hearth, kitchen knife, churning rod, a beautiful seat, bunch of flowers, mortar and pestle, vase for water, mirror, sword, dagger, bow and arrow, rod, club, kitchen garden, big spoon, stone grinder, churning rod, flour grinder, pedestal, broom, casket, besides the furniture inside the room like the chairs, wooden blankets and other essential articles in the house should be given over to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 3.168.29-33 \|\|

*ityevamādibhiḥ pūrṇāngṛhāndadyāddvijātiṣu \|*  
*kartuścaṃdrabalopete sthiranakṣatrasaṃyute \|\| 29 \|\|*

*śubhe'hni viprakathite dānakālaḥ praśasyate \|*  
*evaṃ saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāro yajamānaḥ svayaṃ dvijān \|\| 30 \|\|*

*kulaśīlasamāyuktāngṛhasaṃkhyānnimaṃtrayet \|*  
*adhītavedāñchāstrajñānpurāṇasmṛtipāragān \|\| 31 \|\|*

*gṛhasthadharmaniratāñchāṃtāndāṃtāñjiteṃdriyān \|*  
*alaṃkṛtya sapatnīkānvāsobhiratha pūjayet \|\| 32 \|\|*

*sugaṃdhisragdharānkṛtvā śāṃtikarmaṇi yojayet \|*  
*gṛhāṃgaṇe kārayitvā kuṃḍamekaṃ samekhalam \|\| 33 \|\|*

29-33. During the strength of the moon, together with his stable constellation, carrying such a great responsibility, the donor should invite the number of Brahmanas equal to the number of the houses. These Brahmanas should be of noble families, full of humility, well-versed in the Vedas and other scriptures besides the Puranas, excellent householders, peaceful as well disciplined. All the Brahmanas should initially be worshipped with their wives, offering the flower garlands etc., and should resort to Santi-karma. The donor should make an altar in his courtyard, with a chain.

## \|\| 3.168.34-35 \|\|

*grahayajñaḥ prakartavyastuṣṭipuṣṭikaraḥ sadā \|*  
*rākṣoghnāni ca sūktāni paṭheyurbrāhmaṇāstataḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

*vāstupūjā prakartavyā dikṣu bhūtabaliṃ kṣipet \|*  
*tataḥ puṇyāhaghoṣeṇa brāhmaṇāṃsteṣu veśmasu \|\| 35 \|\|*

34-35. The yajna for the planets, which is the cause of prosperity, should be performed. At that point of time, the Brahmanas should chant the mantras or hymns, relating to the destruction of the Raksasas. With the Vastu-puja and making offerings to the. directions, the welfare and auspicious ceremonies should be performed.

## \|\| 3.168.36-40 \|\|

*praveśayitvā śayyāsu sabhāryānupaveśayet \|*  
*yajamānastataḥ prājñaḥ śuklāṃbaradharaḥ śuciḥ \|\| 36 \|\|*

*yadyasya vihitaṃ pūrvaṃ tattasya pratipādayet \|*  
*idaṃ gṛhaṃ gṛhāṇa tvaṃ sarvopaskarasaṃyutam \|\| 37 \|\|*

*tava vipra prasādena mamāstvabhimataṃ phalam \|*  
*evamekaikaśo dattvā praṇipatya kṣamāpayet \|\| 38 \|\|*

*svastīti brāhmaṇairvācyaṃ kodāditi ca pūjitaiḥ \|*  
*gṛhopakaraṇaistulyā dakṣiṇā bhavanaṃ vinā \|\| 39 \|\|*

*upadeṣṭāramāpṛcchettanmūlatvānmaharṣayaḥ \|*  
*svayaṃ tānpūjayitvā tu tataḥ svabhavanaṃ vrajet \|\| 40 \|\|*

36-40. The donors should then make the Brahmanas to enter the houses with their wives and then make them sit over the beds. The learned donor should then clad himself in white costumes and should hand over each one of the houses to the Brahmanas for whom the same was built. “O Brahmana, the house with all the amenities may please be accepted by you, as a result of which, my desire could be fulfilled.” Thus speaking, the charity should be given to each one of the Brahmanas and the donor should beg forgiveness. The Brahmanas should chant the Vedic hymns and should utter the word Svasti (Be it so). Then uttering the mantras— “Grhopakaranai, upadesta”, great Ṛṣis should be worshipped by him, himself. Thereafter, he should proceed to his abode.

## \|\| 3.168.41 \|\|

*dadyādanena vidhinā gṛhamekaṃ bahūnapi \|*  
*na saṃkhyāniyamaḥ kāryaḥ śaktiratra niyāmikā \|\| 41 \|\|*

41\. With the following of this process, the donor should donate one or more than one houses. No particular limits for the donation of the houses have been prescribed. The donor has to do so, as per his means.

## \|\| 3.168.42-44 \|\|

*śītavātātapaharaṃ dattvā tṛṇakuṭīrakam \|*  
*iṣṭānkāmānavāpnoti pretya svarge mahīyate \|\| 42 \|\|*

*kiṃ punarbahunoktena sarvopaskarabhūṣitām \|*  
*atyaṃtasukhalubdhena dattvā brahmapurīṃ priyām \|\| 43 \|\|*

*gobhūhiraṇyadānāni yamāḥ saniyamāstathā \|*  
*gṛhadānasya kauṃteya kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm \|\| 44 \|\|*

42-44. A person with the giving away of a thatched hut is respected in the heaven, getting all his desires fulfilled. Then, what could be said about a person who donates a house with all the amenities and the equipments? O son of Kunti, the donations of a cow, gold and the land, besides performing all the austerities do not equate with even one sixteenth part of the merit earned by donating a house.

## \|\| 3.168.45 \|\|

*yaḥ kārayetsudṛḍhaharmyavatī mahārhā satsevitāṃ dvijapurīṃ sujanopabhogyām \|*  
*divyāpsarobhirabhi naṃditacittavṛttiḥ prāpnotyasāvanavamaṃ padamiṃdumauleḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

45\. When the fully furnished houses in the towns with well built rooms are used by the people of nobility, the donor enjoying the company of the Apsaras and all the pleasures, earns the eternal place of lord Siva with the moon digit decorating his head.

## Chapter 169. Merit of giving away of the food

## \|\| 3.169.1-5 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*annadānasya māhātmyaṃ kathayāmi tavānagha \|*  
*yatproktamṛṣibhiḥ pūrvaṃ tadihaikamanāḥ śṛṇu \|\| 1 \|\|*

*dadasvānnaṃ dadasvānnaṃ dadasvānnaṃ yudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*sadyastuṣṭikaraṃ loke kiṃ dattena pareṇa te \|\| 2 \|\|*

*rāmeṇa daśarathinā vanasthena nijānujaḥ \|*  
*nirvedādyatpurā proktastadahaṃ prabravīmi te \|\| 3 \|\|*

*pṛthivyāmannapūrṇāyāṃ vayamannasya kāṃkṣiṇaḥ \|*  
*saumitre nūnamasmābhirna brāhmaṇamukhe hutam \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yaducyate karmabījaṃ tasyāvaśyaṃ phalaṃ naraiḥ \|*  
*prāpyate lakṣmaṇāsmābhirnānnaṃ vipramukhe hutam \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О sinless one, I am now speaking to you about the glory of giving away the food in charity, you please listen. By giving away of the food in charity, a person derives enormous benefit, therefore, I repeat it thrice that this type of charity please a person instantly. Sri Rama, while in exile, had spoken to his younger brother Laksmana about the merit of the same, which is going to be repeated by me before you. In earlier times, Sri Rama said – “By living over the earth, which serves food for all, all of us are desirous of having the food. As will be the seed of karmas, the resultant fruit that he will receive will be also like that. Therefore, it is certain that in earlier times, once the food had not been served to the Brahmanas.

## \|\| 3.169.6-8 \|\|

*yatra prāpyaṃ tadaprāpyaṃ vidyayā pauruṣeṇa vā \|*  
*satyo lokapravādo'yaṃ nādattamupatiṣṭhati \|\| 6 \|\|*

*bhakṣopayogādannasya dānaṃ śreyaskaraṃ param \|\| 7 \|\|*

*prakārāṃtarabhojyāni dānānyanyāni bhārata \|*  
*annameva paraṃ dānaṃ satyavākyaṃ paraṃ padam \|\| 8 \|\|*

6-8. Whatever could not be achieved by learnings or by making efforts, (it is because of the past karmas only.) Therefore, the hearsay is correct – “That which has never been given, can never be achieved.” Because of its use in eating (or filling the belly of a hungry person), the giving away of the food has been treated to be quite beneficial. О Bharata, though the other types of the charities are also quite useful, but the giving away of the food is the best. It is the true expression besides being the supreme position.

## \|\| 3.169.9-13 \|\|

*buddhiścārthātparo lobhaḥ santoṣaḥ paramaṃ sukham \|*  
*snātānāmanuliptānāṃ bhūṣitānāṃ ca bhūṣaṇaiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*na sukhaṃ na ca santoṣo bhavedannādṛte nṛṇām \|*  
*śveto nāma mahīpālaḥ sārvabhaumo'bhavatpurā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*teneṣṭaṃ bahubhiryajñaiḥ saṃgrāmā bahavo jitāḥ \|*  
*dānāni ca pradattāni dharmataḥ pālitā mahī \|\| 11 \|\|*

*bhuktā bhogāḥ suvipulā śatrūṇāṃ mūrdhani sthitam \|*  
*vānaprasthena vidhinā tyaktvā rājaśriyaṃ nṛpa \|\| 12 \|\|*

*svargaṃ jagāma bhuktvā tu pūjyamāno marudgaṇaiḥ \|*  
*vimānamarkapratimaṃ pratipede mudā yutaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

9-13. The meaning which is derived by one’s own intelligence always has the touch of greed in it, but contentment is the best of the comforts. By taking bath, applying paste over the body and with the wearing of the ornaments, a person does not attain as much satisfaction as he achieves by taking the food. In earlier times, there had been a great king known by the name of Sveta, who had performed several yajnas and became victorious in many wars, gave away several of the charities, ruled the earth as per the provisions of dharma, enjoyed enormous comforts and always ruled over the heads of the enemies. О king, at the end of his life, according to the rules of the vanaprastha (forest dweller), he discarded the royal riches, and then proceeded on to the heaven, where he reached delightfully boarding an illumining plane and was welcomed by all Marudganas.

## \|\| 3.169.14-15 \|\|

*tatrāste ramamāṇo'sau sākaṃ vidyādharaiḥ sukham \|*  
*prasiddhaiḥ stūyate siddhaiḥ sevyate'psarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

*gaṃdharvairgīyate hṛṣṭaiḥ śakreṇāpyanugamyate \|*  
*divyamālyāṃbaradharo divyābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ \|\| 15 \|\|*

14-15. The Vidyadharas made him comfortable while he lived there. The well known Siddhas offered prayer to him, while the nymphs served him well. The delightful Gandharvas pleased him variously and Indra followed him. He was adorned with divine garlands, garments and the ornaments.

## \|\| 3.169.16 \|\|

*sa ca nityaṃ vitānāgryādavatīrya mahītalam \|*  
*svamāṃsānyatti kauṃteya pūrvaṃ tyaktvā kalevaram \|\| 16 \|\|*

16\. But inspite of all that, the same powerful king daily went to the earth in a plane and used to eat flesh from his own dead body, which he has left on earth after his death.

## \|\| 3.169.17-19 \|\|

*taccharīraṃ tathaivāste rakṣitaṃ pūrvakarmabhiḥ \|*  
*sa kadācitsureśānaṃ brahmāṇaṃ samupasthitaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*praṇamya prāṃjalirbhūtvā nirvedādidamabravīt \|*  
*bhagavaṃstvatprasādena prāptaṃ svargasukhaṃ mayā \|\| 18 \|\|*

*sarveṣāmapi saṃpūjyaḥ surāṇāṃ surapuṃgava \|*  
*kiṃ tu kṣudbādhate'tyarthaṃ svargasthasyāpi me prabho \|\| 19 \|\|*

17-19. Because of his earlier deeds, his body was preserved. Once he went to the self-born Brahma and with his folded hands, offered his salutation to him. With his agonized mind, he said to Brahma – “O lord, by your grace, I had the chance of enjoying all the comforts of the heaven and have been adored by all the gods. But in spite of my stay in the heaven, I suffer badly from hunger as a result of which I have to eat the flesh of my own dead body.”

## \|\| 3.169.20-25 \|\|

*yayā māṃsānyahaṃ svasya bhakṣyayāmyaśanaṃ vinā \|*  
*brahmovāca \|*  
*śvetābhijanasaṃpanna śveta śṛṇu vaco mama \|\| 20 \|\|*

*tvayādhītaṃ hutaṃ dattaṃ guravaḥ paritoṣitāḥ \|*  
*nāśanaṃ bhavatā dattaṃ yaddvijebhyo narādhipa \|\| 21 \|\|*

*anannadānasya phalaṃ tvayedamupabhujyate \|*  
*tarhyannadānato nānyaccharīrārogyakārakam \|\| 22 \|\|*

*nānyadannādṛte puṃsāṃ kiñcitsañjīvanauṣadham \|*  
*mahīṃ gatvā mahārāja kuruṣva vacanaṃ mama \|\| 23 \|\|*

*tapaḥ svādhyāyasaṃpanne śāstrajñe saṃjitendriye \|*  
*yena saṃpadyate tṛptirakṣayā kṣmāṃpate tava \|\| 24 \|\|*

*viriṃcervacanādgatvā tvarāyukto mahītalam \|*  
*agastyaṃ bhojayāmāsa bhaktyā bharatasattama \|\| 25 \|\|*

20-25. Brahma said – “O king born in the Sveta family, I am going to enlighten you about the cause for the same. You had pleased your preceptor, studied well the Vedas, well performed the yajnas, charities, as well as the preceptors, besides all other noble deeds. But you never served food to Brahmanas or the hungry people. Because of your failure to serve food to the hungry people, you have to suffer this misery. Therefore, there is no other charity bigger than the giving of food. Besides that, there is no other life saving drug better than the giving away of the food to the poor or hungry in charity. Accepting my words, you should go to earth and feed a noble Brahmana well-versed in the Vedas, which would yield for you the extreme satisfaction.” At the command of lord Brahma, the said king descended on earth and served food to Maharsi Agastya.

## \|\| 3.169.26-28 \|\|

*bhojayitvā tataḥ prādāddakṣiṇāṃ kṣīṇakalmaṣaḥ \|*  
*ekāvaliṃ svakātkaṇṭhātsamuttārya samujjvalām \|\| 26 \|\|*

*tato dundubhighoṣeṇa pūjitaḥ surasattamaiḥ \|*  
*śvetastṛpto gataḥ svargaṃ dattvānnaṃ dakṣiṇāyutam \|\| 27 \|\|*

*paulastye nihate paścāddevadānavasaṃkaṭe \|*  
*rāmāyaikāvaliṃ prādādagastyaḥ parayā mudā \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. Thereafter, the king removed the neck ornament from his body and gave away the same to the Ṛṣi in daksina. Observing that, the gods started playing on the musical instruments and then adored the king, who feeling contented with the giving of the food and the daksina, reverted to the heaven. The same neck ornament was given over by the sage Agastya to Sri Rama with delight, after the killing of Ravana and other daityas by Sri Rama.

## \|\| 3.169.29-35 \|\|

*etadannasya māhātmyaṃ kathayāmyaparaṃ ca te \|*  
*na cānnādaparaṃ kiñcitsatyaṃ tava mayoditam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*annaṃ vai prāṇināṃ prāṇā annamojo balaṃ sukham \|*  
*etasmātkāraṇātsadbhirannadaḥ prāṇadaḥ smṛtaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*sudūrādāśayā yasya gṛhaṃ prāptā bubhukṣitāḥ \|*  
*tṛptāḥ pratinivartaṃte ko'nyastatsadṛśaḥ pumān \|\| 31 \|\|*

*dīkṣitaḥ kapilā satrī rājā bhikṣurmahodadhiḥ \|*  
*dṛṣṭamātrā punaṃtyete tasmātpaśyaṃti nityaśaḥ \|\| 32 \|\|*

*ekasyāpyatitherannaṃ yaḥ pradātumaśaktimān \|*  
*tasyā'rambhaiḥ parikleśairvasataḥ kiṃ phalaṃ gṛhe \|\| 33 \|\|*

*śakyate duṣkare'pyarthe cirarātrāya jīvitum \|*  
*na tvāhāravihīnena śakyaṃ vartayituṃ ciram \|\| 34 \|\|*

*bhuktvā gṛhe gṛhasthasya maithunaṃ yaśca sevate \|*  
*yasyānnaṃ tasya te putrā iti prāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ \|\| 35 \|\|*

29-35. Besides this, I am also revealing before you another glory of the giving away of the food in charity, because it is true that there is no other chanty greater than the giving away of the food, which serves as the strength, life and comforts. Therefore, the noble people say – “The giver of the food is the giver of life.” A person with a high hope, when arrives at the abode of householder and returns alter taking food with satisfaction, who else can equate with such a donor? With the mere sight of the one who performs sacrifice, the Kapila cow, a king, a beggar, the ocean, they always remain observing. What it the use of a person in a householder, who cannot serve food to a guest? Therefore, all his activities become painful. In case, some great efforts by a person do not become successful, one does not feel encouraged. In case a guest produces a child in a household, the same shall be treated to belong to the householder, because of the food consumed by the guest.

## \|\| 3.169.36-40 \|\|

*duṣkṛtaṃ hi manuṣyāṇāmannamāśritya tiṣṭhati \|*  
*yo yasyānnaṃ samaśnāti sa tasyāśnāti duṣkṛtam \|\| 36 \|\|*

*vanaspatigate some parānnaṃ yastu bhuṃjati \|*  
*tasya māsakṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ dātāramupagacchati \|\| 37 \|\|*

*kasmānna dīyate nityaṃ kasmādannaṃ na dīyate \|*  
*yasyedṛśī phalāvāptiḥ kathitā pūrvasūribhiḥ \|\| 38 \|\|*

*bhikṣāṃ vā puṣkalāṃ vāpi haṃtakāraṃ dvijātaye \|*  
*bhojanaṃ vā yathālābhamadattvāśnāti kilbiṣam \|\| 39 \|\|*

*yenāyutaṃ sahasraṃ vā bhojitaṃ syāddvijanmanām \|*  
*tena brahmagṛhāsannaṃ nūnaṃ baddhaṃ kuṭīrakam \|\| 40 \|\|*

36-40. All the evils of a person are lodged in his food. Therefore, a person who consumes the food of a person, also consumes the evils of the householder. Since Vanaspati is derived from Soma, the person who consumes the food from the householder, the merits of the consumer of the food for a month, goes to the householder. Therefore, according to the ancient sages, when the giving of food yields such results, then why should me not give away the food in charity? A person who takes food, without giving food to the Brahmanas or giving alms to the beggars, then it becomes sinful. A person who serves food to ten thousand Brahmana’s, he surely makes his hut close to the abode of Brahma.

## \|\| 3.169.41-43 \|\|

*vārāṇasyāṃ purā pārtha vaṇigāpaṇajīvanaḥ \|*  
*dhaneśvara iti khyāto devabrāhmaṇapūjakaḥ \|\| 41 \|\|*

*tasyāpaṇaikadeśe tu muktvāṃḍaṃ pāṃḍuracchavi \|*  
*sasarpa sarpastaddeśādvaṇigdṛṣṭvā viśaṃkitaḥ \|\| 42 \|\|*

*tadaṃḍaṃ vaṇijā tena dṛṣṭaṃ kāruṇyabuddhinā \|*  
*tataḥ prabhṛtyanudinaṃ rarakṣa ca puṣoṣa ca \|\| 43 \|\|*

41-43. О Partha, once there lived an efficient trader in the city of Varanasi who was known by the name of Dhanesvara. He always served the gods as well as the Brahmanas. Once a serpent laid an egg in the comer of the shop of the shopkeeper. The trader spotted the egg with a doubtful eye. Still he, out of compassion, did not disturb the egg, rather he started taking care of it daily.

## \|\| 3.169.44-47 \|\|

*nirjagāma dinaiḥ kaiścidbhitvāṃḍaṃ sarpapotakaḥ \|*  
*taṃ vaṇikkṣīrapānādyairupacārairavardhayat \|\| 44 \|\|*

*lilihe ghṛtabhāṃḍāni jighre ca gaṃdhasaṃcayān \|*  
*luloṭha pāṃsuprakare cacāra vārimadhyagaḥ \|\| 45 \|\|*

*vaṇijā rakṣyamāṇaḥ sa snehāccāharahaḥ punaḥ \|*  
*jagāma sumahānkālo'bhavadeṣa bhayaṃkaraḥ \|\| 46 \|\|*

*athaikasmindine gaṃgāṃ gataḥ snātuṃ trilokagām \|*  
*vaṇigāpaṇe paṇyavidaṃ sthāpayitvā sutaṃ matam \|\| 47 \|\|*

44-47. After a few days, a young one of the snake emerged out of the egg, by breaking it. The trader served milk to the young one of the snake. The young one of the snake developed a taste for the ghi and also developed a liking for other scents. It started crawling in dust as well as in water. But out of affection and for protecting it, the trader helped it in growing. In a short time, it became a terrific serpent. Once the trader left the shop to the care of his son and he himself went to the Ganga for the taking of the bath.

## \|\| 3.169.48-52 \|\|

*vyavahartuṃ samārabdhaṃ vaṇikputreṇa dhīmatā \|*  
*dadāti pratigṛhṇāti ghṛtatailayavaikṣavam \|\| 48 \|\|*

*vyavahārākulatayā pādayoraṃtareṇa saḥ \|*  
*sarpaścacāla cāpalyādvaṇigvikṣepamabhyagāt \|\| 49 \|\|*

*jānannapi tadvṛttāṃtaṃ nidāne niyatervaśāt \|*  
*trāsātsaṃtarjayāmāsa balena padacāriṇam \|\| 50 \|\|*

*sa mahītaḥ samutthāya mūrddhānamavaruhya ca \|*  
*uvāca dāruṇataraṃ vacanaṃ pannagādhamaḥ \|\| 51 \|\|*

*śaraṇāgataṃ poṣitaṃ ca tava pitrā priyaṃkaram \|*  
*kasmānmāṃ haṃsi duṣṭātmankathaṃ jīvanvimokṣyase \|\| 52 \|\|*

48-52. The trader’ son started selling and purchasing of several commodities like ghi, oil, barley and raw sugar etc. While he was busy in the business of the shop, the serpent once passed through his feet. Feeling panicky, the son crushed the snake, well aware of its birth in the shop itself. Then the snake suddenly got up and coiled itself around the neck of the trader’s son and spoke in harsh words – “Because I took refuge with your father, he took good care of me and has brought me up. Therefore, О wicked one, why do you intend to kill me?”

## \|\| 3.169.53-56 \|\|

*anaṃtaraṃ kalakalaḥ saṃjāto rodatāṃ nṛṇām \|*  
*dhaneśvarasuto daṣṭaḥ sarpeṇāpi bhṛśākulaḥ \|\| 53 \|\|*

*acyutānaṃta goviṃda kṛṣṇakṛṣṇetyudīrayan \|*  
*dhaneśvaropyanuprāptaḥ provācākulayā girā \|\| 54 \|\|*

*kiṃ kṛtaṃ mama putreṇa tava pavraga vipriyam \|*  
*yadayaṃ bhavatā mūrdhni svabhogenābhiveṣṭitaḥ \|\| 55 \|\|*

*mūrkha mitraṃ susaṃbaṃdhaṃ hīnajātijano hi yaḥ \|*  
*yaḥ karotyabuthoṃgārānsa svahastena karṣati \|\| 56 \|\|*

53-56. Thereafter, a crowd of crying people collected there and there were commotions everywhere. The people started saying – “Dhanesvara’s son has been bitten by the snake, as a result of which he has been fainted.” At the same time, reciting the name of Acyuta, Ananta, Govinda and Kṛṣṇa, Dhanesvara also reached there and feeling upset, said – “O serpent, what wrong had my son done to you? Why are you coiling around his neck?” When a person of a high race develops contact with a person of lower race out of his foolishness, such a foolish person picks up the burning coal with his own hands.

## \|\| 3.169.57-58 \|\|

*tamuvāca ca sarpo'sau vāṣpagadgadayā girā \|*  
*niraparādho bhavataḥ putreṇāhaṃ samāhataḥ \|\| 57 \|\|*

*tadahaṃ paśyataste'dya daśāmyenaṃ narādhipa \|*  
*yathā na bhūyo bhūtānāṃ bhavedasmātkvacidbhayam \|\| 58 \|\|*

57-58. Thereafter, the serpent, with his choked voice and eyes full of tears, spoke to the merchant – “Your son has beaten an innocent being like me. Therefore, I am going to bite him in your presence in order to save other creatures from danger.”

## \|\| 3.169.59-65 \|\|

*dhaneśvara uvāca \|*  
*upakāraṃ vrataṃ bhaktyā snehapāro na yasya ca \|*  
*satāṃ mārgamapākramya prayātaḥ kena vāryate \|\| 59 \|\|*

*kṣaṇamātraṃ pratīkṣasva yāvadeva śiśurmama \|*  
*aurdhvadehikakarmāṇi karoti svayamātmanaḥ \|\| 60 \|\|*

*evamuktā gṛhaṃ gatvā yatīnāṃ brahmacāriṇām \|*  
*sahasraṃ bhojayāmāsa ghṛtapāyasabhojanaiḥ \|\| 61 \|\|*

*samutthāya tataḥ sarve brāhmaṇā hṛṣṭamānasāḥ \|*  
*vaṇikputrasyottamāṃge cikṣipuḥ kusumākṣatān \|\| 62 \|\|*

*vaṇikputra ciraṃ jīva naśyaṃtu tava śatravaḥ \|*  
*abhīṣṭaphalasaṃsiddhirastu te brāhmaṇājñayā \|\| 63 \|\|*

*tataḥ sa duṣṭaprakṛtirvipra vāgvajratāḍitaḥ \|*  
*pannago nagasaṃkāśaḥ papāta ca mamāra ca \|\| 64 \|\|*

*vipannaṃ pannagaṃ dṛṣṭvā trastacakṣurdhaneśvaraḥ \|*  
*āḥ kimetaditi procya viṣādamagamatparam \|\| 65 \|\|*

59-65. Dhanesvara said – “A person who is devoid of devotion, who has neither done good to others nor had he performed any vrata. besides the one having no bondage of love, leaving the path of the noble people follows an evil path, then who can stop him from so doing. Therefore, you stop for a moment, wait for some time till my son completes the rites pertaining to the obsequious of a deceased person.” Thus speaking, the trader went to his home and served thousands of yatis and Brahmacaris with payasam mixed with food. Thereafter, with a delightful mind, the merchant returned to his son with many Brāhmaṇas, who pouring flowers over the son of the merchant, said- “Let the son of the merchant have long life and his enemies should get destroyed. At the command of the Brāhmaṇas, you should have your task established.” At these words spoken by the Brahmanas, the serpent, which was quite a wicked one and appeared terrific, fell down dead. Finding the dead serpent, the merchant Dhanesvara exclaimed in surprise- “What is all this, that has happened?”

## \|\| 3.169.66-69 \|\|

*poṣito'yaṃ mayā bālaḥ pālito lālitastathā \|*  
*mamāpacārātpaṃcatvamāpannaḥ pavanāśanaḥ \|\| 66 \|\|*

*upakāriṣu yaḥ sādhuḥ sādhutve tasya ko guṇaḥ \|*  
*apakāriṣu yaḥ sādhuḥ sa sādhuḥ sadbhiriṣyate \|\| 67 \|\|*

*ityevamavadhāryāsau duḥkhasaṃtaptamānasaḥ \|*  
*bubhuje nākulatayā na ca suṣvāpa tāṃ niśām \|\| 68 \|\|*

*tataḥ prabhāte gaṃgāyāṃ snātvā saṃtarpya devatāḥ \|*  
*sahasraṃ bhojayāmāsa punareva dvijanmanām \|\| 69 \|\|*

66-69. Thus speaking, he felt extremely painful and said – “I had brought up that serpent, but the same has been killed due to me. When a person does good to the people who had done good to him, then it is of no consequence. In case, a noble person behaves with in a gentle manner, only he is considered to be really a gentle person. These are the words cited by the noble people.” Thus thinking, the merchant felt aggrieved at heart and the trader could neither take food nor sleep on that particular night. On the next morning, he got up early and after performing oblation to the gods and the manes, again served food to a thousand Brahmanas.

## \|\| 3.169.70-73 \|\|

*tairbhuktairiṣṭasaṃsiddhairbrāhmaṇai ranumoditaḥ \|*  
*vaṇikprāha mamābhīṣṭaṃ saṃjīvatveṣa pannagaḥ \|\| 70 \|\|*

*tato dvijavaronmuktairaṃbubhiḥ pariṣiṃcitaḥ \|*  
*udatiṣṭhadahīnāṃgaḥ sahasā hi mahākulaḥ \|\| 71 \|\|*

*praharṣamatulaṃ lebhe dṛṣṭvā taṃ purataḥ sthitam \|*  
*pratyagrāvayavaṃ dṛṣṭvā sṛkkiṇīparileliham \|\| 72 \|\|*

*sādhuvādo mahāñjātaḥ praśaśaṃsurdhaneśvaram \|*  
*purīnivāsinaḥ sarve vismayotphullalocanāḥ \|\| 73 \|\|*

70-73. Feeling contented with the excellent food served to them, the Brahmanas asked the merchant to express his desire. The merchant desired that the serpent should get back his life. On hearing these words, the Brahmanas poured the water over the dead serpent, as a result of which, the serpent regained its lost life. At the survival of the serpent, the merchant was immensely pleased and the people present there started shouting the slogans of “well done”. Thereafter, the merchant Dhanedvara was praised everywhere.

## \|\| 3.169.74 \|\|

*sahasrabhojyamāhātmyaṃ kathitaṃ te yudhiṣṭhira \|*  
*samyakchraddhāprayuktasya kimanyatkathayāmi te \|\| 74 \|\|*

74\. О Yudhisthira, having been forced with your devotion, I have narrated to you the glory of feeding a thousand people. What more should I say?

## \|\| 3.169.75 \|\|

*yacchaṃti ye'nudivasaṃ dvijapuṃgavānāmannaṃ viśuddhamanaso bhṛśamāgatānām \|*  
*martye vihṛtya suciraṃ sasuhṛjjanāste pretya prayāṃti bhavanaṃ muditā murāreḥ \|\| 75 \|\|*

75\. With a purified heart, such of the persons, who serve well the food to the persons who arrive as the guests, they enjoy all the comforts on earth and then proceed to the abode of lord Kṛṣṇa.

## Chapter 170. Giving away of a cooling vase

## \|\| 3.170.1-7 \|\|

*yudhiṣṭhira uvāca \|*  
*annadānaprasaṃgena mamāpi smṛtimāgatam \|*  
*tatte'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi śrutaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ ca yanmayā \|\| 1 \|\|*

*akṣadyūtena bhagavandhanaṃ rājyaṃ ca no hṛtam \|*  
*āhūya niṣkṛtiprājñaiḥ kitavairakṣakovidaiḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*vanaṃ prasthāpitāḥ sarve valkalājinavāsasaḥ \|*  
*draupadyā sahitāḥ kṛṣṇa karṇaduryo dhanādibhiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*jñātvā vanagatānasmānbrāhmaṇāḥ saṃjiteṃdriyāḥ \|*  
*draṣṭumabhyāyayuḥ sarve paurāścāpyanujagmire \|\| 4 \|\|*

*asmānsnehātkliśyamānā dṛṣṭvā brāhmaṇasattamāḥ \|*  
*paurānkarmakarāṃścaiva nirvedādidamabruvan \|\| 5 \|\|*

*jīvato yasya jīvaṃti viprā mitrāṇi bāṃdhavāḥ \|*  
*jīvanaṃ tasya saphalamātmārthe ko na jīvati \|\| 6 \|\|*

*abhyāgataṃ suhṛdvargaṃ kuṭuṃbamapahāya ca \|*  
*jīvannapi mṛtaḥ pāpaḥ kevalaṃ svodaraṃbhariḥ \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Yudhisthira said – In the story related to the giving away in charity of the cooked food, I have also been reminded of some events, which had been observed by me. I am going to place them before you. You kindly listen to the same. By inviting the shrewd and wicked gamblers, Karna, Duryodhana and others usurped our wealth, kingdom, after which all of us together with Draupadi, were clad in embark garments and drove us out in exile. О Kṛṣṇa, learning of our having become the forest dwellers, the disciplined Brahmanas arrived in the forest in order to meet us, together who the other people, who had been devoted to us. Observing the misery of the villagers, the Brahmanas said to me – “Only such a person is said to be living alive, by whose means, the Brahmanas, friends and the relatives remains alive with their families. But when a person, who disowning his own family and friends, remains alive filling his own belly, such a sinful person is considered to be dead even when he is alive.”

## \|\| 3.170.8-11 \|\|

*ityevamavadhāryāhaṃ tānṛṣīnpunarabruvam \|*  
*bhavaṃtaḥ sarva evātra trikālajñā maharṣayaḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*samāgatā matpriyārthaṃ jñānavijñānapāragāḥ \|*  
*brūta kaṃcidupāyaṃ me bhavaṃtobhijanaṃ prati \|\| 9 \|\|*

*bhavadbhiḥ sahitāḥ sarve bhṛtyairbhrātṛbhireva ca \|*  
*nirgaccheyaṃ vane śūnye dvādaśemāḥ samā yathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*māmuvācātha maitreyaḥ śṛṇu kauṃteya madvacaḥ \|*  
*pūrvavṛttaṃ pravakṣyāmi dṛṣṭaṃ divyena cakṣuṣā \|\| 11 \|\|*

8-11. On hearing this, I said to the Maharsis – “O great Ṛṣis, all of you are well aware of the past, present and future. You possess all the sacred knowledge. You have been kind enough to appear here for my benefit. Therefore, you kindly enlighten the Pandavas, for the procuring of the food, by which I should be able to serve food to all of you together with the relatives, in this lonely forest. I should be able to spend twelve years of exile.” At this, the great sage Maitreya said – “O son of Kunti, you listen to me attentively. I would like to repeat the same event, which had been witnessed by me in earlier times with my divine sight.

## \|\| 3.170.12-15 \|\|

*āsīttapovane kācidbrāhmaṇī brahmacāriṇī \|*  
*durbhagā durgatā duḥkhādārādhayati sā dvijān \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śaucena tuṣṭā munayaḥ praśrayeṇa damena ca \|*  
*procurvada viśālākṣi kiṃ kurmastava suvrate \|\| 13 \|\|*

*sā tānuvāca kiṃ tanme vrataṃ dānamathāpi vā \|*  
*kathayadhvaṃ bhaveyaṃ vai yena śrīsukhabhāginī \|\| 14 \|\|*

*ādhārabhūtā bhūtānāṃ bahvapatyā patipriyā \|*  
*spṛhaṇīyā trijagatāṃ trivargaphalabhāginī \|\| 15 \|\|*

12-15. In this tapovana, there once lived a Brāhmaṇa woman who was quite chaste, who had fallen to misfortune and was facing misery. Facing the enormous miserable condition, she still served the Brāhmaṇas. Getting pleased with her discipline, way of life, the chastity, love and devotion, the sages said to her – “O broad-eyed one, auspicious one, what type of good can be done by us for your sake?” On hearing this, she said – “Instead of talking about the vratas, you tell me the way out, by which I could be able to enjoy, get some comfort and be able to do something good of the living beings. I should also have children, a nice husband and also enjoy the pleasure of dharma, artha and kama in three worlds.”

## \|\| 3.170.16-21 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhastāmuvācātha śṛṇuṣva kathayāmi te \|*  
*dānaṃ mānakaraṃ puṃsāṃ sarvakāmapradāyakam \|\| 16 \|\|*

*kṛtvā tāmramayīṃ sthālīṃ palānāṃ pañcabhiḥ śataiḥ \|*  
*aśaktastu tadarddhena caturthāṃśena vā punaḥ \|\| 17 \|\|*

*sarvaśaktivihīnastu mṛnmayīmapi kārayet \|*  
*sugaṃbhīrodaradarīdṛḍhadaṇḍakuṭuṃbakām \|\| 18 \|\|*

*mudgataṃdulaniṣpannasusvinnakṣiprapūritām \|*  
*upadaṃśodakayutāṃ ghṛtapātrasamanvitām \|\| 19 \|\|*

*dhautapārśvāṃ dhautakarṇāṃ carcitāṃ candanena ca \|*  
*sthāpya maṃḍalake vastraiḥ puṣpadhūpairathārcayet \|\| 20 \|\|*

*āditye'hani saṃkrāṃtau caturdaśyaṣṭamīṣu vā \|*  
*ekādaśyāṃ tṛtīyāyāṃ viprāya pratipādayet \|\| 21 \|\|*

16-21. At this, Vasistha said – “I am speaking to you about a charity, which brings respect to the people, besides fulfilling all the human desires. As per one’s means, a cooling vase of five hundreds palas of gold or half of it or a quarter of the same, or of copper and in case a person is unable to even arrange for the same, an earthen vase which should be quite strong, should be made. It should be filled with the mixture of green gram and rice, besides a radish and ghi should be dropped therein. Its rear part as well as the neck should be clean. It should be pasted with sandal paste, and then consecrated in a mandala. It should be adored with costumes and flowers. It should then be given over to the Brahmanas on Sunday, first day of the month, on the eighth, eleventh, thirteenth or fourteenth day of the month.

## \|\| 3.170.22-25 \|\|

*jvalajjvalanapārśvasthaistaṃḍulaiḥ sajalairapi \|*  
*na bhavedbhojyasaṃsiddhirbhūtānāṃ piṭharīṃ vinā \|\| 22 \|\|*

*tvaṃ siddhiḥ siddhikāmānāṃ tvaṃ puṣṭiḥ puṣṭimicchatām \|*  
*atastvāṃ praṇamāmyāśu satyaṃ kuru vaco mama \|\| 23 \|\|*

*jñātibaṃdhusuhṛdvarge vipre preṣyajane tathā \|*  
*abhuktavati nāśnīyāttathā bhava varapradā \|\| 24 \|\|*

*ityuccārya pradātavyā haṃḍikā dvijapuṃgave \|*  
*tuṣṭipuṣṭipradā puṃsāṃ sarvānkāmānabhīpsatā \|\| 25 \|\|*

22-25. Without a vase, the food, the burning fire and rice with water cannot be given to the people. You are success for the people desirous of success and growth for the people desirous of growth, therefore, I offer my salutation to you. You make my desire truthful or successful. I offer my salutation to you. On that particular day, food should be served to all, and none of the friends, relatives, Brahmanas and the servants should miss the food. To ensure all these, you bestow a boon on me.” Thus speaking, the vase should be given over to a Brāhmaṇa. The said vase brings contentment and growth, besides fulfilling all the desires.

## \|\| 3.170.26-28 \|\|

*vasiṣṭhavacanaṃ śrutvā sā cakāra tathaiva tu \|*  
*prādātsthālīṃ brāhmaṇāya bahūnāṃ bahudakṣiṇām \|\| 26 \|\|*

*sā caiṣā draupadī pārtha bhavadbhāryā'bhavatpriyā \|*  
*tena dānaprabhāveṇa bhavitā'śūnyapāṇikā \|\| 27 \|\|*

*eṣā satī śacī svāhā sāvitrī bhūraruṃdhatī \|*  
*śrīreṣā yatra vasati na kiṃcittatra durlabham \|\| 28 \|\|*

26-28. Listening to the words of Vasistha, the Brahmana woman gave away the pottery vase to a Brahmana with daksina. With the influence of the same charity, Draupadi has become your wife, whose womb was never without a son. The same vrata was performed by the chaste Indrani, Svaha, Savitri, Bhu and Arundhati, wherever she dwells in whichever form, no shortage of any sort remains there.

## \|\| 3.170.29-32 \|\|

*anayā yā bhṛtā sthālī tayā sarvamidaṃ jagat \|*  
*bhojayiṣyasi kauṃteya kimato brāhmaṇā amī \|\| 29 \|\|*

*maitreyāttadupaśrutya tatra saṃhṛṣṭamānasaḥ \|*  
*pūrvaṃ bhojitavānasmi bahuviprajanā vane \|\| 30 \|\|*

*annadānaprasaṃgena sthālīdānamidaṃ mayā \|*  
*kathitaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa kṣaṃtavyamanasūyayā \|\| 31 \|\|*

*sthālīṃ viśālavadanāṃ ca sataṃḍulāṃ ca yacchaṃti ye madhuraśulbamayīṃ dvijebhyaḥ \|*  
*teṣāṃ suhṛtsvajanaviprajanena bhojyaṃ saṃbhujyamānamapi kṛṣṇa na yāti nāśam \|\| 32 \|\|*

29-32. О son of Kunti, when that vase is filled with food, the entire universe could be served with food out of the same vase, what to speak of these Brahmanas.” Listening to the words of Vasistha, I served food to many Brahmanas in that lonely forest. О lord with lotus like eyes, in the context of the giving away of food in charity, I have spoken about the giving away of an earthen vase in charity, for which I beg forgiveness. О Kṛṣṇa, such a vase of large size which could be made in copper as well, filled with rice, when given to a Brahmana by a person, the vase never becomes empty even after serving food to the Brāhmaṇas, the friends, the relatives. It never gets empty.

## Chapter 171. Giving away of a slave girl

## \|\| 3.171.1-7 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*dāsīdānamahaṃ te'dya pravakṣyāmyarisūdana \|*  
*bhaktyā snehācca bhavato yatroktaṃ kenacitkvacit \|\| 1 \|\|*

*caturṇāmāśramāṇāṃ hi gṛhasthaḥ śreṣṭha ucyate \|*  
*gṛhasthācca gṛhaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ gṛhācchreṣṭhā varāḥ striyaḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*pūrṇeṃdubiṃbavadanāḥ pīnonnatapayodharāḥ \|*  
*tadgṛhaṃ yatra dṛśyaṃte yoṣitaḥ śīlamaṃḍanāḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*jāmayo yatra pūjyaṃte ramante tatra devatāḥ \|*  
*yatraitāstu na pūjyaṃte vinaṃkṣyatyāśu tadgṛham \|\| 4 \|\|*

*jāmayo yāni gehāni śapaṃtyapratipūjitāḥ \|*  
*tāni kṛtyāhatānīva sadyo yāṃti parābhavam \|\| 5 \|\|*

*amṛtasyeva kuṇḍāni sukhānāmiva rāśayaḥ \|*  
*rateriva nidhānāni yoṣitaḥ kena nirmitāḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*śyāmā maṃtharagāminyaḥ pīnonnatapayodharāḥ \|*  
*mahiṣyo varanāryaśca na bhavaṃti gṛhegṛhe \|\| 7 \|\|*

1-7. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О killer of the enemies, because of your affection and devotion for me, I am speaking to you about the giving away of slave girls in charity, which is not known to anyone else anywhere. The grhastha-asrama is conceived to be the best of all the asramas and the ladies are said to be the best in a household. Only that place is said to be a house, in which the ladies having faces resembling the full moon and with developed breasts, live. The house in which the noble damsels live, the gods live there as well and the house in which they are not honoured, it gets destroyed in no time. The house in which there develops dissent, the ladies of the family getting humiliated pronounce a curse and the house is destroyed by the krtyas. This is because the ladies are the altar of nectar, besides being the source of the love sports. Therefore, it is essential to know about them. The damsels like Syama of sixteen years of age, move gracefully, with developed breasts and are considered to be the best, the buffaloes are not found in every house.

## \|\| 3.171.8-13 \|\|

*ahiraṇyamadāsīkamalpānnājyamagorasam \|*  
*gṛhaṃ kṛpaṇavṛttīnāṃ narakasyāparo vidhiḥ \|\| 8 \|\|*

*adaṇḍapāśikaṃ grāmamadāsīkaṃ ca yadgṛham \|*  
*anājyaṃ bhojanaṃ yacca vṛthā taditi me matiḥ \|\| 9 \|\|*

*vibhavābharaṇā dāsyo yadgṛhaṃ samupāsate \|*  
*tatrāste paṃkajakarā lakṣmīḥ kṣīrodavāsinī \|\| 10 \|\|*

*na yatrāsti gṛhe śaucaṃ na sukhaṃ vyavahārajam \|*  
*yatra vā nāsti dāsyekā tatsadaivānavasthitam \|\| 11 \|\|*
