О Bharata, after shaving of the head, after enjoying intercourse with a woman, with the touch of the earth, one should take bath with the clothes on.

## \|\| 3.205.129-132 \|\|

*guroḥ pativratānāṃ ca tathā yajñatapasvinām \|*  
*parivādaṃ na kurvīta parihāse'pi bhārata \|\| 129 \|\|*

*yugapajjalamagniṃ ca bibhṛyānna vicakṣaṇaḥ \|*  
*guruṃ devānprati tathā na ca pādau prasārayet \|\| 130 \|\|*

*nācakṣīta dhayaṃtīṃ gāṃ jalaṃ nāṃjalinā pibet \|*  
*vātātapau na seveta anutāpaṃ ca varjayet \|\| 131 \|\|*

*dāsaṃ śapenna vai kruddhaḥ sarvabandhūnamatsarī \|*  
*bhītāśvāsanakṛtsādhuḥ svargastasyāvyayaṃ phalam \|\| 132 \|\|*

129-132. O Bharata. in the presence of the preceptors, devoted ladies and tapasvis, one should not speak anything facing them. One should not spread his legs in front of the preceptor or gods and should not disrespect the fire lighting in the altar. One should not drink water in handcups in front of cows drinking water. One should stop repenting. It would not be improper to scold a servant, but one should not do so in anger. If one follows all these, he definitely achieves heaven.

## \|\| 3.205.133-134 \|\|

*nordhvaṃ tu pattanadvāraṃ nirīkṣya paryaṭennaraḥ \|*  
*yugamātraṃ mahīpṛṣṭhe naro gacchedvilokayan \|\| 133 \|\|*

*śeṣāhe tvapi śeṣāṃśca vaśyātmā yo nirasyati \|*  
*tasya dharmārthakāmānāṃ hānirnālpāpi jāyate \|\| 134 \|\|*

133-134. One should not walk looking at the entrance gate of someone’s else house. A person should walk with a great care. A person, who even after standing before the serpent Sesa discards his six enemies, his dharma, artha and kama never decline.

## \|\| 3.205.135-138 \|\|

*vṛthā māṃsaṃ na khādeta pṛṣṭhamāṃsaṃ tathaiva ca \|*  
*ākrośaṃ ca vivādaṃ ca paiśunyaṃ ca vivarjayet \|\| 135 \|\|*

*saṃyāvaṃ kṛśaraṃ māṃsaṃ śaṣkulīpāyasaṃ tathā \|*  
*ātmārthe na prakartavyaṃ devatānāṃ prakalpayet \|\| 136 \|\|*

*ajāśca nāvakarṣeta tā bahirdhārayaṃti ca \|*  
*raktamālyaṃ na dhāryaṃ syācchuklaṃ dhāryaṃ tu paṃḍitaiḥ \|\| 137 \|\|*

*varjayitvātra kamalaṃ tathā kuvalayaṃ vibho \|*  
*raktaṃ śirasi dhāryaṃ ca tathā pāneyamityapi \|\| 138 \|\|*

135-138. Eating of flesh or meat is of no consequence, similarly, one should keep himself away from denouncing others, controversies and back-biting. The pudding, the cooked mixed grains, meat, fried cakes and payasam should be prepared for the sake of the divinities and for self. A Brāhmaṇa should not hold the rope of a female goat, besides the garland of red flowers. He should wear a garland of white flowers alone. Besides the lily flowers, the red lotus flowers and paneya should be worn over the head.

## \|\| 3.205.139-141 \|\|

*kāṃcanīyāpi yā mālā sā na duṣyati karhicit \|*  
*anyadeva bhavedvāsaḥ śayanīye narottama \|\| 139 \|\|*

*anyadarcāsu devānāmanyaddhāryaṃ sabhāsu ca \|*  
*pippalaṃ ca vaṭaṃ caiva śīrṇaśleṣmāṃtakaṃ tathā \|\| 140 \|\|*

*udubaraṃ na khādeta bhavārthī puruṣottamaḥ \|*  
*patitaiśca kathāṃte ca cchedanaṃ ca vivarjayet \|\| 141 \|\|*

139-141. The garland of gold can never be polluted. О best of the humans, a person should wear other clothes at the time of sleep, while separate clothes should be worn at the time of the worship of the gods. Similarly, while attending the assemblies, one should wear different clothes. A person, who is desirous of comforts in the world, should not consume the fruits of pipala, vata, slesa and udumbara trees. At the end of the revelation or the narrating of the stories, one should avoid contact with the fallen people.

## \|\| 3.205.142-145 \|\|

*patitaḥ syānnaro rājanpatitaistu sahācaran \|*  
*vṛddho jñātistathā mitraṃ daridro yo bhavediha \|\| 142 \|\|*

*gṛhe vā saṃsthāpitāste gṛhavṛddhimabhīpsatā \|*  
*gṛhe pārāvatā dhanyāḥ śukāśca sahasārikāḥ \|\| 143 \|\|*

*bhavaṃtyete tathā pāpāstathā vai tilapāyikāḥ \|*  
*ājokṣā caṃdanaṃ vīṇā ādarśo madhusarpiṣī \|\| 144 \|\|*

*jalāgnī caiva bibhṛyādgṛhe nityamiti sthitiḥ \|*  
*dhanurvede ca satataṃ yatnaḥ kāryo narādhipa \|\| 145 \|\|*

142-145. The company of the fallen people makes a person himself fallen. One who is interested in the expansion of the house despite of being an elderly person, a person belonging to his own caste, some friend or a poor person, incharge of the store house, the birds like pigeons, parrots and the cuckoos, are said to be graceful, inspite of their being sinful and consumer of sesamum seeds. The sandalwood, vina, a mirror, honey, water and fire should always remain in the house. О king, one should always take steps for the training in archery and the practice of the same.

## \|\| 3.205.146-148 \|\|

*hastipṛṣṭhe'śvapṛṣṭhe ca rathacaryāsu caiva hi \|*  
*yatnavānbhava rājendra nayavānsukhamedhate \|\| 146 \|\|*

*prajāpālana yuktaśca na kṣāṃtiṃ labhate nṛpa \|*  
*yajñaśāstraṃ ca vijñāya śabdaśāstraṃ ca bhārata \|\| 147 \|\|*

*gāṃdharvaśāstraṃ vijñeyaṃ kalā jñeyāśca bhārata \|*  
*purāṇamitihāsaṃ ca tathākhyānāni yāni ca \|\| 148 \|\|*

146-148. While riding over the back of the elephant as well as the horse besides in a chariot, one should always remain careful and alert, because an alert person alone remains comfortable. О king, a ruler who rules the country, cannot practice forgiveness always. О Bharata, one should have fair knowledge of yajha-sastra, grammar, archery, the sixty form of arts, the Puranas, history and all the ancient stories.

## \|\| 3.205.149-151 \|\|

*eṣa te lakṣaṇoddeśa ācārasya prakīrtitaḥ \|*  
*śeṣāśca vedyā vṛddhebhyaḥ pratyāhāryā narādhipa \|\| 149 \|\|*

*ācāro bhūtijanana ācāraḥ kīrtivardhanaḥ \|*  
*ācārādvardhate hyāyurācāro haṃtyalakṣaṇam \|\| 150 \|\|*

*āgamānāṃ hi sarveṣāmācāraḥ śreṣṭha ucyata \|*  
*ācāraḥ paramo dharma ācārādvardhate dhanam \|\| 151 \|\|*

149-151. О king, I have spoken to you the symptoms of the good conduct, besides the purpose for the same. Rest of the information could be collected from the old people. One earns enormous riches and that further increases with the practice of the good conduct. It also enhances the age and removes the blemishes. The good conduct has been described to be the best in the entire Agama literature, which has also been described to be the supreme dharma.

## \|\| 3.205.152 \|\|

*puṇyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ svargyaṃ svastyayanaṃ mahat \|*  
*sarvavarṇānukaṃpārthaṃ mayaitatsamudāhṛtam \|\| 152 \|\|*

152\. It also enhances the wealth and leads to the path of the heaven. It bestows enormous welfare. I have narrated to you the merits of the good conduct for the welfare and the benefit of all the varnas.

## \|\| 3.205.153 \|\|

*ācāra eva narapuṃgava sevyamāno dharmārthakāmaphalado bhavatīha puṃsām \|*  
*tasmātsadaiva viduṣāvahitena rājañchāstrodito hyanudinaṃ paripālanīyaḥ \|\| 153 \|\|*

153\. О lion among the humans, with the following of the good conduct, all the desires of a person related to dharma, artha and kama get successful. Therefore, the learned people, well-versed in the sastras or scriptures, must follow the good conduct.

## Chapter 206. Rohini-Candra Vrata

## \|\| 3.206.1 \|\|

*nārada uvāca \|*  
*dīrghāyurārogyakulādivṛddhiyuktaḥ pumānyena guṇānvitaḥ syāt \|*  
*muhurmuhurjanmani yena samyagvrataṃ mama brūhi tadiṃdumauleḥ \|\| 1 \|\|*

1\. Narada said— You kindly tell me about the vrata of the crescent-headed Siva, with the listening of which a person achieves long age, healthy body, expansion of the race, besides remaining delightful in all his future births.

## \|\| 3.206.2-6 \|\|

*śrībhagavānuvāca \|*  
*tvayā pṛṣṭamidaṃ samyagamutrākṣayakārakam \|*  
*rahasyaṃ te pravakṣyāmi yatpurāṇavido viduḥ \|\| 2 \|\|*

*rohiṇīcandraśayanaṃ nāma vratamihottamam \|*  
*tasminnārāyaṇasyārccāmarccayediṃdunāmabhiḥ \|\| 3 \|\|*

*yadā somadinayuktā bhavetpaṃcadaśī kvacit \|*  
*atha vā brahmanakṣatraṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ prajāyate \|\| 4 \|\|*

*tadā snānaṃ naraḥ kuryātpaṃcagavyaṃ ca sarṣapaiḥ \|*  
*āpyāyasveti ca japedvidvānaṣṭaśataṃ punaḥ \|\| 5 \|\|*

*śūdro'pi parayā bhaktyā pākhaṃḍālāpavarjitaḥ \|*  
*somāya varadāyātha viṣṇave ca namonamaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

2-6. The Lord said – You have put me an excellent question which bestows everlasting merit in this as well as the future world and has been well described by the people well-versed in the Puranas. The same is being repeated by me before you. You please listen. There is a vrata known as Rohini-candra-sayana which is considered to be an excellent one. In this vrata, Lord Narayana is adored reciting various names of the lord. When the moon day falls on Monday or when Brahma constellation falls on the full moon day, one should take bath with mustard mixed water and pancagavya, reciting the mantra- “Apyayasveti a hundred and eight times. This can be done even by a Sudra, who gets himself relieved of the falsehood by offering salutation to the Moon (as Viṣṇu) who bestows the boon as Viṣṇu, again and again.

## \|\| 3.206.7-10 \|\|

*kṛtajapyaḥ svabhavanamāgatya madhusūdanam \|*  
*pūjayetphalapuṣpaiśca somanāmāni kīrtayet \|\| 7 \|\|*

*somāya śāṃtāya namo'stu pādāvanaṃtanāmne hyanujānu jaṃghe \|*  
*ūrudvayaṃ cāpi vṛkodarāya saṃpūjayenmeḍhramanaṃgabāhave \|\| 8 \|\|*

*namonamaḥ kāmasukhapradāya kaṭiḥ śaśāṃkasya samarcanīyā \|*  
*tathodaraṃ cāpyamṛtodarāya nābhiḥ supūjyā vidhilocanāya \|\| 9 \|\|*

*namo'stu candrāya mukhaṃ prapūjya hanurdvijānāmadhipāya pūjyā \|*  
*āsyaṃ namaścaṃdramasebhipūjyamoṣṭhau kumutkhaṃḍavanapriyāya \|\| 10 \|\|*

7-10. This mantra should be muttered for some time. Thereafter, the devotee should worship lord Madhusudana, uttering the names of the moon, saying – “Salutation to Soma”. Saying this, he should touch the feet; saying salutation to Ananta, the knees and thighs should be touched. Saying salutation to Vrkodara, both the thighs should be touched. Saying salutation to Anangabahu, the penis should be touched. Saying salutation to the one who makes us enjoy the sex pleasures, the waist should be touched; saying salutation to Anrtadara, the belly should be touched. Saying salutation to Vidhilocana, the naval is to be touched; saying salutation to Dvijanama, the chin should be touched; saying salutation to Candra, cheeks should be touched; saying salutation to Kumuda – the khandana vana’s delight, the lips should be touched.

## \|\| 3.206.11-14 \|\|

*nāsā ca nāthāya vanauṣadhīnāṃ hyānaṃndadāyātha punarbhruvośca \|*  
*netradvayaṃ nīlakumutpriyāya ceṃdīvaraśyāmakarāya coraḥ \|\| 11 \|\|*

*namaḥ samastādhvaravaṃditāya karṇadvayaṃ daityaniṣūdanāya \|*  
*lalāṭamiṃdorudadhipriyāya keśā suṣumṇādhipateḥ prapūjyāḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

*śiraḥ śaśāṃkāya namo'surārerviśveśvarāyeti namaḥ kirīṭam \|*  
*padmapriye rohiṇi nāma lakṣmi saubhāgyasaukhyāmṛtatārakāyai \|\| 13 \|\|*

*devīṃ ca saṃpūjya sugandhadhūpanevadyapuṣpādibhiriṃdupatnīm \|*  
*prapūjya bhūmau punarutthitena snātvā ca viprāya haviṣyayuktaḥ \|\| 14 \|\|*

11-14. Saying salutation to the lord of Vanausadhis, the nose should be touched; saying salutation to Anandadaya, both the eyebrows should be touched. Then saying salutation to the one to whom the blue lotus flowers are dear, both the eyes should be touched; saying salutation to Aindivarasyama, the ear has to be touched; saying salutation to the one who is adored by all the yajnas, both the ears should be touched. Saying salutation to the killer of the daityas, the forehead is to be touched. Saying salutation to Susumnadhipati, the hair should be touched. Saying salutation to Sasanka, the head should be touched; saying salutation to Visvesvara - the enemy of asuras, the kirita crown should be adored. Then he should pray- “O Laksmi - lodged over the lotus, besides the goddess who bestows the fortunes and the goddess Amrta-taraka, salutation to her.”

## \|\| 3.206.15-17 \|\|

*deyaḥ prabhāte sa hiraṇyavārikuṃbho manaḥpāpavināśanāya \|*  
*saṃprāśya gomūtramamāṃsamannamakṣāramaṣṭāvatha viṃśatiṃ ca \|\| 15 \|\|*

*grāsānpayaḥ sarpiyutānupoṣya bhuktvetihāsaṃ śṛṇuyānmuhūrtam \|*  
*kadaṃbanīlotpalaketakāni jātī sarojaṃ śatapatrikā ca \|\| 16 \|\|*

*amlānakubjānatha siṃduvārapuṣpaṃ punarnārada mallikāyāḥ \|*  
*muktaṃ ca viṣṇoḥ karavīrapuṣpaṃ śrīcaṃpakaṃ caṃdramasaśca deyam \|\| 17 \|\|*

15-17. Thus speaking, the fragrant flowers, universe, eatables, besides the flowers etc. should be worshipped along with the goddess, who is the spouse of the Moongod, Thereafter, taking bath in the early morning, a gold kalasa filled with water, should be given over to a Brāhmaṇa, for the removal of the mental sins. Thereafter, sipping the cow’s urine, one should take saltless food, without meat. They should be cooked in ghi and milk. Then twenty eight morsels of the food should be eaten and the donor should listen to the ancient scriptures. Similarly, the flowers like the blue lotus, jasmine, lotus, satapatrika, kubja, nutmeg etc., should be offered to Viṣṇu, while the flowers of oleander and campaka should be offered to the Moon.

## \|\| 3.206.18 \|\|

*śrāvaṇādiṣu māseṣu kramādetāni sarvadā \|*  
*yasminmāse vratādiḥ syātpuṣpairabhyarcayeddharim \|\| 18 \|\|*

18\. Whatever procedure has been laid down for whichever month, the flowers so prescribed to be offered to each one of the deities, should be offered to them, while adoring them.

## \|\| 3.206.19-20 \|\|

*ekasaṃvatsaraṃ yāvadupoṣya vidhivannaraḥ \|*  
*vratāṃte śayanaṃ dadyāddarpaṇopaskarānvitam \|\| 19 \|\|*

*rohiṇacaṃdramithunaṃ kārayitvā tu kāṃcanam \|*  
*caṃdraḥ ṣaḍaṃgulaḥ kāryo rohiṇī caturaṃgulā \|\| 20 \|\|*

19-20. Thus observing the fasting for a year in an appropriate way, the bed, Rohini and the Moon’s golden image should be made. The image of Rohini should be of four angulas in height, while that of the moon should be of six angulas in height.

## \|\| 3.206.21-23 \|\|

*muktāphalāṣṭakayutaṃ sitanetrapaṭāvṛtam \|*  
*kṣīrakuṃbhopari puna. kāṃsyapātrākṣatānvitam \|\| 21 \|\|*

*dadyānmaṃtreṇe pūrvāhne śālīkṣuphalasaṃyutam \|*  
*śvetāmatha suvarṇāsyāṃ raupyakhurasamanvitām \|\| 22 \|\|*

*savastrabhājanāṃ dhenuṃ tathā śaṃkhaṃ ca śobhanam \|*  
*bhūṣaṇairdvijadāṃpatyamalaṃkṛtya guṇānvitam \|\| 23 \|\|*

21-23. Eight white pearls should be used as the eyes. The images should be covered with clothes. They should be placed over a pitcher filled with milk and covered with cloth, which should be placed over the bronze vase, in which the rice should be spread. All these items should be given away in the forenoon to a Brāhmaṇa couple, together with a white cow whose face has been decorated with gold, the hoof with silver along with costumes and food. The Brāhmaṇa couple should be adorned with all the ornaments.

## \|\| 3.206.24-27 \|\|

*caṃdro'yaṃ dvijarūpeṇa sabhārya iti kalpayet \|*  
*yathā na rohiṇī kṛṣṇa śayanaṃ tyajya gacchati \|\| 24 \|\|*

*somarūpasya te tadvanmamābhedo'stu mūrtibhiḥ \|*  
*yathā tvameva sarveṣāṃ paramānaṃdamuktidaḥ \|\| 25 \|\|*

*bhuktirmuktistathā bhaktistvayi yajñe'stu me dṛḍhā \|*  
*iti saṃsārabhītasya muktikāmasya cānagha \|\| 26 \|\|*

*rūpārogyāyuṣāmetadvidhāyakamanuttamam \|*  
*idameva pitṝṇāṃ ca sarvadā vallabhaṃ mune \|\| 27 \|\|*

24-27. The donor should then conceive the Brahmana couple as the form in which the Moongod exists and pray to them – “O Kṛṣṇa, as Rohini never leaves you, similarly, you – the form of moon, never leaves me and let my mind remains devoted to you as well as the yajna. Let you always grant everlasting happiness to me.” О sinless one, a person desirous of beatitude, by performing this worship, he attains beauty, long life and healthy body. О sage, this vrata is also favourite with the manes.

## \|\| 3.206.28 \|\|

*trailokyādhipatirbhūtvā śatakalpaśatatrayam \|*  
*caṃdralokamavāpnoti punarāvṛttidurlabham \|\| 28 \|\|*

28\. With the performing of this vrata, a person enjoys the sovereignty of the three worlds for three hundred kalpas, after which he gets lodged in the place of Moon and reaching that place, one does not have to reborn.

## \|\| 3.206.29 \|\|

*nārī vā rohiṇī caṃdraśayanaṃ vā samācaret \|*  
*sā'pi tatphalamāpnoti punarāvṛttidurlabham \|\| 29 \|\|*

29\. In case the Rohini-candra-sayana vrata is performed by a lady, then she also earns the same reward. She also does not have to take rebirth.

## \|\| 3.206.30 \|\|

*iti paṭhati śṛṇoti vā ya itthaṃ madhumathanārcanamiṃdukīrtanena \|*  
*matimapi ca dadāti so'pi śaurerbhavanagataḥ paripūjyate'maraughaiḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

30\. Thus the story of the vrata in which lord Madhusudana is adored with the name of the moon, when one reads or listens to the one who supports the same, he surely achieves the place of Viṣṇu.

## Chapter 207. Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s return to Dvaraka

## \|\| 3.207.1-5 \|\|

*śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca \|*  
*vrataṃ dānamatho rājaṃstava dharmāḥ prakāśitāḥ \|*  
*dharmamūlaṃ yataścedaṃ tasmāddharmaparo bhava \|\| 1 \|\|*

*jānatā'pi mayā pārtha kāmārthau na prakāśito \|*  
*yataḥ svayaṃ pravṛttotra lokaḥ kimanuvarṇyate \|\| 2 \|\|*

*kāmino varṇayankāmāṃllobhaṃ lubdhasya varṇayan \|*  
*naraḥ kiṃ phalamāpnoti kūpeṃ'dhamiva pātayan \|\| 3 \|\|*

*bhaviṣyottarametatte kathitaṃ pāṃḍunaṃdana \|*  
*sadācāravatāṃ puṃsāṃ vratadānasamuccayaḥ \|\| 4 \|\|*

*yaddṛṣṭamitihāseṣu purāṇeṣu ca bhārata \|*  
*vedavedāṃgasaṃbaddhaṃ tatsarvamiha darśitam \|\| 5 \|\|*

1-5. Śrī Kṛṣṇa said – О king, I have spoken to you about the dharma in relation to the vratas, fasting and charities. These are the pillars of the dharma. Therefore, you should always be firm in your religious beliefs. I have deliberately avoided discussions about Kama and Artha, because what is the use of discussing over the subjects in which the people are directly involved? Like pushing a blind person in a well, what is the use of discussing about Kama with a lustful person, or about the wealth to a greedy person? О son of Pandu, in this way, the later part of the Bhavisya Purana has been narrated by me to you, in which, for the people of good conduct, the giving away of charities and performing of the vratas have been fully described. О Bharata, whatever has been visualized by me in the ancient historical treatises besides the Puranas, which form the part of the Vedas and Vedangas, have been narrated before you.

## \|\| 3.207.6-9 \|\|

*lokavedaviruddhaṃ yatkathyate manujottama \|*  
*na tatrāsthā prakartavyā vipralāpo hi sa smṛtaḥ \|\| 6 \|\|*

*atisnehena bhavato mamaitatsamudāhṛtam \|*  
*ṛṣīṇāṃ purataḥ pārtha kuṃṭhā bhavati bhāratī \|\| 7 \|\|*

*naitatprakāśanīyaṃ hi dāṃbhikāya śaṭhāya vā \|*  
*nāstikāyānyamanase kutarkopahatāya ca \|\| 8 \|\|*

*sādhuvṛttāya dāṃtāya satyārjavaratāya ca \|*  
*etadākhyāyamānaṃ hi śubhāmutpādayedgatim \|\| 9 \|\|*

6-9. О best of the humans, whatever is seen in this world contrary to the provision of the Vedas, should not be taken seriously and should be considered as the simple dialogue of the Brāhmaṇa alone. Feeling overwhelmed with your affection. I have revealed these facts, because one feels hesitant to discourse in the presence of the Ṛṣis. The deceitful, wicked, ill-mannered or unmindful and those indulging in false arguments, such people should not be apprised of the subject. This matter should be discussed with the people who possess good conduct, are auspicious and truthful. The reciting of the Bhavisya Purana earns beatitude for a person.

## \|\| 3.207.10 \|\|

*sāmānyametatsurasattamānāṃ varṇāśramāṇāṃ ca nareṃdracandra \|*  
*khyātaṃ bhaviṣyottaranāmadheyaṃ mayā purāṇaṃ tava sauhṛdena \|\| 10 \|\|*

10\. О Narendra, because of my attachment with you, this Bhaisyottara Purana, in which the subjects like varnasrama and the best of the stories of the deities have been discussed, has been narrated by me.

## \|\| 3.207.11 \|\|

*dharmaḥ svayaṃ pārtha bhavāniha tvaṃ dharmārthaviddṛṣṭaparāvaraśca \|*  
*pṛṣṭo'smyato dharmamahaṃ ca vacmi śraddheyametatsutarāṃ janasya \|\| 11 \|\|*

11\. O Partha, you yourself are the form of dharma, because of your being well-versed in the essence of dharma. Since you are away from the feelings of the high and low, on your request, I have discussed about dharma.

## \|\| 3.207.12 \|\|

*yāsyāmyahaṃ dvāravatīṃ punaśca yajñaṃ sameṣyāmi mahotsave ca \|*  
*kālasya sarvaṃ hi vaśe viditvā naivānutāpo bhavatātra kāryaḥ \|\| 12 \|\|*

12\. I shall now proceed to the city of Dvaraka and shall try to attain the auspicious festivities with you, including the performing of the yajnas.

## \|\| 3.207.13 \|\|

*ityuktavānyātukāmaḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ saṃpūjitaḥ pāṃḍusutairmahātmā \|*  
*pṛṣṭvā suhṛjjjñātijanaṃ hi sarvaṃ jagāma viprānpraṇipatya kṛṣṇaḥ \|\| 13 \|\|*

13\. Considering everything under the command of Kala, you should not grieve in any way. Thus speaking, Lord Kṛṣṇa, with the desire to return, was adored even by the enemies of the Pandavas. With the delight of his friends and relatives and with their permission, he took leave of them, offering his salutation to all and proceeded on to Dvaraka.

## \|\| 3.207.14 \|\|

*yadyājñavalkyamuninā bhagavānvaśiṣṭhaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ kilottaramuvāca bahuprakāram \|*  
*kṛṣṇena pāṃḍutanayasya ca yatpradiṣṭaṃ vyāsena tatkṛtamaho munipuṃgavena \|\| 14 \|\|*

14\. Thus after questioning the sage Yajnavalkya, whatever had been stated in reply by the great Maharsi Vasistha, and whatever discourse had been delivered before Yudhisthira – the son of Pandu, the same has been composed by the sage Vyasa in the form of this Purana.

## \|\| 3.207.15 \|\|

*jayati parāśarasūnuḥ satyavatīhṛdayanaṃdano vyāsaḥ \|*  
*yasyāsyakamalagalita vāṅmadhupuṇyaṃ jagatpibati \|\| 15 \|\|*

15\. Vyasa is the son of the sage Parasara and loving son of Satyavati. Victory to him. He is the one from whose lotus like mouth emerged the nectar like words, which are enjoyed by the people of the world.

## Chapter 208. The table of Contents

## \|\| 3.208.1-13 \|\|

*vyāsānugamanaṃ pūrvaṃ brahmāṃḍasya samudbhavaḥ \|*  
*māyā ca vaiṣṇavī yasmātsaṃsāre doṣakīrtanam \|\| 1 \|\|*

*pāpabhedastatastasmācchubhāśubhavinirṇayaḥ \|*  
*śakaṭavratamāhātmyaṃ tilakavratakīrtanam \|\| 2 \|\|*

*aśokakaravīrākhyaṃ vrataṃ tasmācca kokilam \|*  
*bṛhattapovrataṃ nāma rudropoṣaṇameva ca \|\| 3 \|\|*

*dvitīyāvratamāhātmyamaśūnya śayanaṃ tathā \|*  
*kāmākhyā tu tṛtīyā ca meghapālīvrataṃ tathā \|\| 4 \|\|*

*paṃcāgnisādhanā ramyā tṛtīyāvratamuttamam \|*  
*trirātraṃ goṣpadaṃ nāma harakālī vrataṃ tathā \|\| 5 \|\|*

*lalitākhyā tṛtīyā ca yogākhyā ca tathāparā \|*  
*umāmaheśvaraṃ nāma tathā raṃbhātṛtīyakam \|\| 6 \|\|*

*saubhāgyākhyā tṛtīyā ca ārdrānaṃdakarī thā \|*  
*caitre bhādrapade māghe tṛtīyāvratamucyate \|\| 7 \|\|*

*anaṃtarī tṛtīyā ca gaṇaśāṃtivrataṃ tathā \|*  
*sārasvatavrataṃ nāma paṃcamīvrata mucyate \|\| 8 \|\|*

*tathā śrīpaṃcamī nāma ṣaṣṭhī śokapraṇāśinī \|*  
*phalaṣaṣṭhī ca maṃdāraṣaṣṭhīvratamathocyate \|\| 9 \|\|*

*lalitāvrataṣaṣṭhī ca ṣaṣṭhī kārtikasaṃjñitā \|*  
*mahattapaḥ saptamī ca vibhūṣā saptamī tathā \|\| 10 \|\|*

*ādityamaṃḍapavidhistrayodaśīti saptamī \|*  
*kṛkavākuplavaṅgā ca tathaivābhayasaptamī \|\| 11 \|\|*

*kalyāṇasaptamī nāma śarkarāsaptamīvratam \|*  
*saptamī kamalākhyā ca tathānyā śubhasaptamī \|\| 12 \|\|*

*snapanavratasaptamyau tathaivācala saptamī \|*  
*budhāṣṭamīvrataṃ nāma tathā janmāṣṭamīvratam \|\| 13 \|\|*

1-13. (Narrative) This Purāṇa starts with the salutation to the sage Vyāsa, then comes the creation of the cosmos or the universe followed by the description of the Māyā (illusion of Viṣṇu) according to which the universe is full of blemishes. The definition of the sins has been described and the earning of the merits and demerits from the same; then there is the mention of the glory of Śakaṭa-vrata, Tilaka-vrata, the vrata of Aśoka-karavīra, the Kokila-vrata, the great Tapo-vrata, the Rudra-vrata, the glory of the Dvitīyā-vrata, Aśūnya-śayana-vrata, Kāmākhyā-tṛtīyā, Meghapūlī-vrata, Ramyā-tṛtīyā-vrata, Gopada-vrata lasting for three nights, Harakālī-vrata, Lalitā-tṛtīyā-vrata, Rambhā-tṛtīyā-vrata of Umā-Maheśvara, Saubhāgya-tṛtīyā-vrata, Ardrā-nandakarī-tṛtīyā, tṛtīyā vratas of Caitra, Bhadrapada and Māgha, Gapa-śānti-vrata, Sārasvata-vrata, Pañcamī-vrata, Śrī-Pañcamī-vrata, Śoka-pūrṇādinī-ṣaṣṭhī, Phala-ṣaṣṭhī, Mandāra-ṣaṣṭhī, Mahat-tapaḥ, Saptamī, Vibhāḍā-saptamī, Kalyāṇī-saptamī, Śarkarā-saptamī, Kamalā-saptamī, Śubha-saptamī, Snāna-vrata-saptamī, Acalā-saptamī, Buddhatamī and Janmāṣṭamī are described.

## \|\| 3.208.14-34 \|\|

*dūrvākṛṣṇāṣṭamī proktā anayāvratamaṣṭamī \|*  
*aṣṭamyarkāṣṭamī cātha vṛkṣanavamīvratam \|\| 14 \|\|*

*dhvajākhyā navamī caiva ulkākhyā navamī tathā \|*  
*daśāvatāravratakaṃ tathāśādaśamīvratam \|\| 15 \|\|*

*rohiṇīṃhariśaṃbhubrahmasūryāviyogakam \|*  
*govatsadvādaśīnāma vratamuktaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 16 \|\|*

*nīrājanadvādaśī ca bhīṣmapaṃcakameva ca \|*  
*mallikākhyā dvādaśī ca bhīmā dvādaśikottamā \|\| 17 \|\|*

*śravaṇadvādaśī nāma saṃprāptidvādaśīvratam \|*  
*govindadvādaśīnāma vratamuktaṃ tataḥ param \|\| 18 \|\|*

*akhaṃḍadvādaśīnāma tiladvādaśyataḥ param \|*  
*sukṛtadvādaśī nāma dharaṇīvratameva ca \|\| 19 \|\|*

*viśokadvādaśī nāma vibhūtidvādaśīvratam \|*  
*puṣyarkṣadvādaśī caiva dvādaśī śravaṇarkṣagā \|\| 20 \|\|*

*anaṃgadvādaśī caiva aṅgapādavrataṃ tathā \|*  
*nimbārkakaravīrātha yamā darśatrayodaśī \|*  
*anaṃgadvādaśī cāpi pālirambhāvrate tathā \|\| 21 \|\|*

*caturdaśīvrataṃ proktaṃ tato'nantacaturdaśī \|*  
*śrāvaṇīvratanaktaṃ ca caturdaśyaṣṭamīdine \|\| 22 \|\|*

*vrataṃ śivacaturdaśyāṃ phalatyāgacaturdaśī \|*  
*vaiśākhī kārtikī māghī vratametadanaṃtaran \|\| 23 \|\|*

*kārtikyāṃ kṛttikāyoge kṛttikāvratamīritam \|*  
*phālgune pūrṇimāyāṃ tu vrataṃ pūrṇamanoratham \|\| 24 \|\|*

*aśokapūrṇimā nāma anaṃtavratameva ca \|*  
*vrataṃ hi sāṃbharāyiṇyaṃ nakṣatrapuruṣavratam \|\| 25 \|\|*

*śivanakṣatrapuruṣaṃ saṃpūrṇaṃ yena mucyate \|*  
*kāmadānavrataṃ nāma vṛntākavidhireva ca \|\| 26 \|\|*

*ādityasya dine naktaṃ saṃkrātyudyāpane phalam \|*  
*bhadrāvratamagastyārgho navacandrārkameva ca \|\| 27 \|\|*

*arghaḥ śukrabṛhaspatyoḥ paṃcāśīti vratāni ca \|*  
*māghasnānaṃ nityasnānaṃ rudrastānavidhistathā \|\| 28 \|\|*

*caṃdrārkagrahaṇe snānaṃ vidhiścānnāśane tathā \|*  
*vāpīkūpataḍāgānāmutsargo vṛkṣayājanam \|\| 29 \|\|*

*devapūjādīpadānavṛṣotsargavidhistathā \|*  
*phālgunyutsavakaṃ nāma tathānyaḥ sadanotsavaḥ \|\| 30 \|\|*

*bhūtamātā ca śrāvaṇyāṃ rakṣābaṃdhavidhistathā \|*  
*vidhistathā navamyāstu tathā candramahotsavaḥ \|\| 31 \|\|*

*dīpālikāyāṃ tu homo lakṣahomavidhistathā \|*  
*koṭihomo mahāśītirgaṇanāthasya śātikā \|\| 32 \|\|*

*tathā nakṣatrahomotha godānavidhireva ca \|*  
*guḍadhenughṛtadhenutiladhenuvrataṃ tathā \|\| 33 \|\|*

*jaladhenuvidhiḥ prokto lavaṇasya tathā parā \|*  
*dhenuḥ kāryāsamaṃjñātvā navanītasya cāparā \|*  
*suvarṇadhenuśca tathā devakāryaṃ cikīrṣubhiḥ \|\| 34 \|\|*

14-34. Similarly, Dhruva-kṛṣṇāṣṭamī, Anayaṣṭamī-vrata, Arkāṣṭamī-vrata, Śrī-vṛkṣa-navamī, Dhvaja-navamī, Ulkā-navamī, Daśāvatāra-vrata, Aṣṭā-daśamī-vrata, Rohiṇī, Indra, Hari, Sambhu, Brahma and Sūrya-viyoga vrata, Govatsa-dvādaśī-vrata, Nīrājana-dvādaśī-vrata, Bhīṣmapañcaka-vrata, Mallikā-dvādaśī, Bhīma-dvādaśī, Śravaṇa-dvādaśī, Saṃprāpti-dvādaśī, Govinda-dvādaśī, Akhaṇḍa-dvādaśī, Tila-dvādaśī, Sukṛta-dvādaśī, Dhāraṇī-vrata, Viśoka-dvādaśī, Vibhūti-dvādaśī, Pūrva-nakṣatra-dvādaśī, Śravaṇā-nakṣatra-dvādaśī, Anaṅga-dvādaśī, Aṅkapāda-vrata, Nimbārka-karavīra and Yama-trayodaśī, Pāli-rambhā-vrata, Anaṅga-dvādaśī, Caturdaśī-vrata, Ananta-caturdaśī, Śrāvaṇī-vrata, Śiva-caturdaśī, Phalatyāga-caturdaśī, Kārttika-Māgha-pūrṇimā-vrata, Kṛttikā-vrata, Manoratha-vrata during full moon day of Phālguna, Aśoka-pūrṇimā, Sāmbhārdyaṇī-vrata, Nakṣatra-puruṣa-vrata, Śiva-nakṣatra-vrata, Kāmadāna-vrata, Vṛttārikā-viddhi, Nakta-vrata of Āditya, merit of Saṅkrānti-vrata, Bhadra-vrata, Nava-candrārka-vrata, eighty five vratas of Śukra and Bṛhaspati, daily bath, method of Rudrasnāna, Māghasnāna, bath during solar and lunar eclipses, rites of tasting of the food, making of step wells and tanks, planting of trees, Devapūjā, Dīpadāna and Vṛkṣotsarga, the festival during the month of Phālguna, Sadānotsava, worship of Mother earth, Rakṣābandhana in the month of Śrāvaṇa, rites of Navamī, Candra-mahotsava, Dīpālikā, the performing of homa, Lalāṭa-homa, Koṭi-homa, Mahāśānti-vrata, Gaṇanātha-homa, Nakṣatra-homa, method of giving away a cow in charity, Gudadhenu, Ghṛta-dhenu, Tila-dhenu, Jala-dhenu, Lavana-dhenu, Navanīta-dhenu and Suvarṇa-dhenu is to be given away in charity by the people engaged in the worship of the Devas.
